Title: Evolution and Adaptation of Global Strategic Planning Experience: A Case Study of a Professional Sports Club

Background: Strategic planning has evolved from its military roots into a sophisticated corporate function, undergoing five distinct stages of development—from basic financial budgeting in the 1950s to modern strategic entrepreneurship. In the current era of globalization and market instability, organizations, including those in the sports industry, require a transition to flexible planning systems that can adapt to unpredictable environmental factors.

Methods: This paper employs a comparative analysis of regional management models—North American, European, and Asian—highlighting their convergence in the modern economy. The research synthesizes the "Planning School" of Igor Ansoff, which provides a structured scientific algorithm for development, with Michael Porter’s "Positioning School," which offers analytical tools for assessing competitive environments.

Results: The study identifies the integration of these theoretical frameworks as a methodological foundation for managing a professional sports organization. Using HC "Barys" as a case study, the paper demonstrates how combining Ansoff's staged planning with Porter’s "Five Forces" analysis allows for a comprehensive evaluation of stakeholder influence (fans, sponsors, and the league) and the formation of competitive advantages through product differentiation.

Conclusion: The findings suggest that the effective management of a modern sports club relies on a hybrid approach that borrows from global best practices. The proposed strategic framework ensures long-term organizational stability by balancing centralized planning with the flexibility needed to respond to regulatory and market shifts.

AI Disclosure: The author used NotebookLM for linguistic refinement and structural organization of the abstract.

Keywords: Strategic planning, management evolution, regional models, HC Barys, sports management, Igor Ansoff, Michael Porter, competitive advantage.

• I have chosen the topic “A STUDY ON EFFECTIVENESS OF ADVERTISEMENT AND PROMOTIONAL OFFERS ON ELECTRONIC GADGETS IN BENGALURU”. 
• This study explores the effectiveness of advertisements and promotional offers on consumer purchase behaviour in the electronic gadgets market in Bengaluru. With rapid digitalization and heightened increasingly rely on persuasive advertising and innovative promotional strategies to attract and retain consumers. The research investigates how different types of advertising media (television, online/social media, print and outdoor) and promotional tools (discounts, bundled offers, cash back, loyalty rewards) influence consumer awareness, preference, and purchase intention.

title: Engagement Is Not Enough: Unlocking Purchase Intention Through Value and Trust in Social Media Influencers

detail.title: Engagement Is Not Enough: Unlocking Purchase Intention Through Value and Trust in Social Media Influencers
detail.abstract: This paper examines the impact of customer engagement with influencers on influencer-generated impacts on their purchase intention on social media platforms. Although the engagement, perceived value, and trust have been researched individually, this study has incorporated these constructs within a single framework, examining their impact on purchase intention. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to analyze the data of 257 users of social media. The results indicate that engagement by the customers has a significant impact on perceived value, trust, and purchase intention. Interestingly, perceived value has been identified to have a positive impact on trust, implying that consumers use value perceptions to determine the level of credibility of the influencers. Both perceived value and trust further enhance purchase intention. Additionally, engagement exerts a direct effect on purchase intention, indicating both relational and immediate behavioral influences. These results contribute to the literature by clarifying the role of perceived value in trust formation and highlighting the dual impact of engagement. The study also provides practical insights for designing more effective influencer marketing strategies.

title: WHY CULTURED MEAT IS THE FUTURE OF THE FOOD INDUSTRY?

detail.title: WHY CULTURED MEAT IS THE FUTURE OF THE FOOD INDUSTRY?
detail.abstract: Cultured meat, also known as cultivated or lab-grown meat, is produced by growing animal cells in a lab, rather than through traditional animal agriculture. 1 It promises to transform global food systems with its sustainability and ethical benefits. This study explores why CM is poised to become the future of food, using a primary survey conducted among a classroom sample in 2025, alongside industry reports and academic reviews. 2 Preliminary survey results reveal 91.7% of respondents prefer CM at 10-20K WON (6.90-13.80/kg), aligning with conventional beef prices, indicating strong consumer interest in affordable CM. Technological advancements, including media cost reductions to tens of cents per liter (2023) and high-density cell cultures (2024), support market growth projections of $34.1 million by 2031. 3 CM's environmental advantage, emitting 500 kg CO2/ton compared to beef's 3000 kg, enhances its appeal.

title: Two-Dimensional Max-Diff

detail.title: Two-Dimensional Max-Diff
detail.abstract: A common problem in research is prioritization of a list of items (features, messages, etc.). With only a handful of items a ranking exercise works nicely, though it doesn't really provide information on the spacing between the ranks. A constant sum scale is better, though it cannot be used when there are more than a handful of items. The research industry has gravitated toward widespread use of maximum difference scaling (Max-Diff) as a standard way of handling this task. The Max-Diff approach can easily handle many items, and provides both rank ordering and spacing between the ranks (in the form of individual-level attractiveness scores).

title: Funnel Resonance Theory: An Impedance-Matching Framework for Advertising Conversion Optimization

detail.title: Funnel Resonance Theory: An Impedance-Matching Framework for Advertising Conversion Optimization
detail.abstract:
This paper introduces Funnel Resonance Theory, a cross-disciplinary framework demonstrating that effective advertising conversion capacity is bounded not by budget allocation, but by the intersection of audience segments addressed across sequential funnel stages. Drawing on impedance mismatch theory from electrical engineering, we define a reflection coefficient for each stage boundary, quantifying traffic structurally unable to convert. Under independent stage targeting, the conversion-eligible population shrinks multiplicatively, establishing an audience intersection bound independent of spend. Applying resonance physics, simultaneous alignment across stages produces nonlinear conversion amplification described by a Lorentzian response function, with a Q-factor quantifying alignment precision.
Meta-analytic evidence (751 econometric estimates) confirms average advertising elasticity of 0.12, while alignment interventions produce 47–212% conversion improvements at zero incremental spend. The Price of Anarchy bounds the cost of siloed funnel management; Braess's Paradox proves that adding channels without coordination can worsen performance.

title: Governing Algorithmic Capital: Principal-Agent Theory, AI Accountability Gaps, and the Case for the Chartered Financial Intelligence Architect (CFIA)

detail.title: Governing Algorithmic Capital: Principal-Agent Theory, AI Accountability Gaps, and the Case for the Chartered Financial Intelligence Architect (CFIA)
detail.abstract: Investment management firms have delegated consequential capital allocation decisions to artificial intelligence and machine learning systems at a pace that has fundamentally altered the principal-agent structure of the industry. Where Jensen and Meckling's (1976) canonical model contemplates human agents whose behavior can be monitored, incentivized, and credentialed, AI systems as agents introduce a qualitatively different accountability problem: their behavior is opaque, non-stationary, and not captured by any existing framework of professional standards. The result is what we term the governance accountability gap: a structural mismatch between the AI capabilities deployed by investment firms and the human oversight competencies available to govern them. This paper applies principal-agent theory, extended to AI delegation contexts through the subsequent work of Eisenhardt (1989) and the accountability framework of Bovens (2007), to characterize this gap and analyze its consequences. Drawing on documented model failures and the convergent accountability mandates of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, and the UK Financial Conduct Authority, we argue that the gap cannot be closed by regulatory mandate alone. Accountability requires competency: the human overseers that regulators require must possess verifiable, domain-specific knowledge that existing professional credentials do not supply. We introduce the Chartered Financial Intelligence Architect (CFIA) designation, administered by ICFDT, as an institutionally grounded response to this competency vacuum.

title: AI Adoption and Firm-Level Wage Structures: Evidence from China
affiliations: Xiamen University Malaysia Campus, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Xiamen University Malaysia Campus - School of Economics and Management and Zhejiang University of Finance and Economics (ZUFE)

detail.title: AI Adoption and Firm-Level Wage Structures: Evidence from China

declarations.funderStatement: The paper is supported by Xiamen University Malaysia Research Fund (XMUMRF/2025-C15/ISEM/0051).

detail.abstract: This paper examines how artificial intelligence (AI) adoption affects firm-level wage outcomes in Chinese listed firms. Using 30,560 firm-year observations from 2011 to 2023, we measure AI adoption through textual analysis of annual reports. We find that AI adoption is positively associated with both employee wages and management wages. The results remain robust across instrumental variable estimation, propensity score matching, a policy-based difference-indifferences design, and alternative AI measures. We further show that workforce restructuring is an important channel: AI adoption increases the share of highly educated employees while reducing reliance on lower-educated workers. In addition, the wage effect is stronger in non-state-owned enterprises, and AI adoption weakens pay-for-performance sensitivity.

title: Beyond Clicks: From Gatekeeper to Interpreter in the Zero-Click Era
affiliations: Northwestern University - Medill School of Journalism, Northwestern University - Medill School of Journalism, ,  and

detail.title: Beyond Clicks: From Gatekeeper to Interpreter in the Zero-Click Era
detail.abstract: AI-powered search tools like Google AI Overviews are reshaping how consumers discover brands. Instead of clicking through a list of ranked links, users now receive synthesized answers that collapse multiple touchpoints into a single AI-generated response. This "zero-click" environment is reducing direct traffic to brand websites and forcing marketers to rethink what visibility means in an era when influence happens upstream from the click. Our study sought to understand this transformation and identify how marketers can remain both visible and trusted. Through 21 interviews with senior marketing leaders across seven industries, we found that success now depends less on keyword optimization and more on semantic relevance and credibility. Structured, consistent online information distributed through owned and earned media is becoming increasingly important for marketers seeking to be discovered via search. Measurement practices must likewise evolve to capture influence and brand presence inside AIgenerated results, not merely web traffic or click-through rates.

title: The Impact of Temporary Student Visa Extensions on Patenting: Evidence from STEM OPT

detail.abstract: Can foreign students at U.S. universities, with a brief work extension, become inventors without displacing native talent? This paper examines one of the most significant recent U.S. immigration policy changes, the 2008 STEM Optional Practical Training extension, which gives international STEM graduates an additional 17 months of work authorization. I show a 60%-86.8% increase in the number of first-time immigrant inventors and a 17.6%-23.4% increase in the share of first-time immigrant inventors in CBSAs with R1 universities relative to other areas after the policy change. I find no evidence of first-time native inventors being displaced.

title: Mind the Gap: Optimal and Equitable Encouragement Policies

detail.title: Mind the Gap: Optimal and Equitable Encouragement Policies
detail.abstract: In consequential domains, it is often impossible to compel individuals to take treatment, so that optimal policy rules are merely suggestions in the presence of human non-adherence to treatment recommendations. We study personalized decision problems in which the planner controls recommendations into treatment rather than treatment itself. Under a covariate-conditional no-direct-effect model of encouragement, policy value depends on two distinct objects: responsiveness to encouragement and treatment efficacy. This modeling distinction makes induced treatment take-up, rather than recommendation rates alone, the natural fairness target and yields tractable policy characterizations under budget and access constraints. In settings with deterministic algorithmic recommendations, the same model localizes overlap-robustness to the recommendation-response model rather than the downstream outcome model. We illustrate the methods in case studies based on data from reminders of SNAP benefits recertification, and from pretrial supervised release with electronic monitoring. While the specific remedy to inequities in algorithmic allocation is context-specific, it requires studying both take-up of decisions and downstream outcomes of them.

detail.abstract:
O episódio do podcast O Marketeiro, com Celso de Souza e Souza, apresenta uma reflexão sobre o conceito de Liderança Diferenciada, fundamentado na metodologia de Léo Bruno, da Fundação Dom Cabral. A entrevista destaca que organizações maduras não se limitam ao lucro imediato, mas equilibram as necessidades de acionistas, colaboradores, clientes e sociedade, gerando resultados sustentáveis. Celso enfatiza que a mudança cultural é responsabilidade direta do CEO, que deve abandonar modelos obsoletos de comando e controle e adotar práticas altruístas e inspiradoras. A autoridade passa a ser construída pela capacidade de servir e engajar.

Entre os pontos centrais, Celso apresenta uma pesquisa que identifica vinte necessidades fundamentais para o engajamento humano, como propósito, competência técnica, autenticidade e escuta ativa. O episódio sugere ainda medidas práticas, como manuais de liderança, capacitação e tolerância zero a comportamentos abusivos, reforçando a importância da saúde mental e da ética organizacional. A liderança diferenciada é definida como um “artigo de luxo”, uma vantagem competitiva rara que utiliza valores humanos e estratégicos para garantir sustentabilidade e valor de longo prazo.

Em síntese, a entrevista mostra que líderes capazes de ouvir, inspirar e agir com consciência criam ambientes engajados e resilientes, gerando valor sustentável em cenários complexos e incertos.

affiliations: University of Texas at Austin, UT-Austin, Charles Sturt University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.abstract: Traditional economic models often fail to capture the nuanced realities of modern market behavior, specifically the rise of "hidden" inflation. This paper investigates shrinkflation and skimpflation-the strategic practices of reducing product quantity and quality while maintaining stable sticker prices. These tactics exploit consumer inattention and violate the ceteris paribus principle, effectively masking cost-push dynamics. Yergin et al. (2024) argue that the Consumer Price Index (CPI) fails to capture the psychological and economic reality of inflation experienced by consumers. To help students appreciate the subtle differences between their lived experiences and the way in which inflation is calculated, we provide instructional scaffolding that utilizes viral media to ground the abstract inflation data. We present four practical lesson plans designed to enhance economic literacy and critical consumption skills. Ultimately, exposing these hidden costs helps students reconcile official statistics with their personal financial realities.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the concept of Technology-Human Disequilibrium and proposes a theory-building conceptual framework that explains how imbalances emerge when technological development exceeds human adaptive capacity. Drawing on insights from sociotechnical systems theory, technology adoption research, and digital transformation literature, the framework analyzes technological change as a dynamic interaction between technological expansion and human adaptation across individual, organizational, and societal levels. The paper distinguishes between Technsology-Human Equilibrium and Technology-Human Disequilibrium, identifies key manifestations and consequences of imbalance.

title: Learning about Noise, Information Disclosure, and Market Stability
affiliations: University of Macau, University of Macau and

detail.title: Learning about Noise, Information Disclosure, and Market Stability
detail.abstract: How do rational investors' learning about noise trading and firms' disclosure of fundamental information jointly affect financial market stability? We examine this question in a model in which information on a part of a risky asset's payoff is publicly disclosed, and rational investors can acquire private information on the other part of the asset's payoff and noise traders' demand for the asset. We demonstrate that reducing information disclosure can eliminate the multiple self-fulfilling equilibria caused by learning about noise. In an extended model with endogenous information disclosure, we show that slightly reducing the intensity of learning about noise can lead to a large (i.e., discontinuous) decrease in the expected asset price. Our results predict that (i) more information disclosure can exacerbate the market fragility caused by high-frequency trading, and (ii) market crashes can occur during the process of regulating high-frequency trading. We also discuss the empirical relevance of our results.

title: Chasing Digital Footprints: Electronic Evidence, Cloud Data and Crypto-Asset Investigations under Greek Criminal Procedure and

detail.title: Chasing Digital Footprints: Electronic Evidence, Cloud Data and Crypto-Asset Investigations under Greek Criminal Procedure and
detail.abstract: The entry into application of Regulation (EU) 2023/1543 on European Production and Preservation Orders (EPROD/EPRES) in August 2026 will create a direct-to-provider mechanism for electronic evidence that bypasses the mutual legal assistance framework entirely. This article examines the interface between the Regulation and Greek criminal procedure law-specifically Article 265 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which provides the most prescriptive digital data seizure framework in the EU-and identifies three systemic tensions: a structural admissibility gap arising from the cloud exclusion in Article 265(1) CCP; a forensic standards gap generated by the absence of mandatory certification standards under Article 265(2) CCP; and a constitutional grey zone created by the Regulation's direct-to-provider mechanism in the context of Articles 9A and 19 of the Greek Constitution. A comparative analysis of French and German digital investigation frameworks is deployed to illuminate the structural choices available to the Greek legislature. Three de lege ferenda proposals are advanced: a new Article 265A CCP designating competent EPROD-issuing authorities; a Presidential Decree establishing mandatory forensic standards; and a new Article 265(8) CCP codifying integrity failure as an absolute nullity. The article argues that the August 2026 deadline constitutes an irreversible threshold: after that date, Greek courts will be required to adjudicate on the admissibility of EPROD-derived evidence without a statutory framework for doing so.

title: Hybrid AI + Blockchain Architecture for the Tax Ecosystem of Small Business

detail.title: Hybrid AI + Blockchain Architecture for the Tax Ecosystem of Small Business
detail.abstract: Small businesses are still struggling with the long-standing issues of tax compliance, such as disjointed record-keeping, manual reporting heavyloads, restricted access to financial analytics, and susceptibility to error or fraud. The article is a proposal of a Hybrid AI + Blockchain Architecture which aims at outfitting the tax ecosystem of small businesses to become more modern and innovative, including intelligent automation and secure and immutable data infrastructure. The model integrates data extraction and anomaly detection assisted by AI with predictive tax forecasting, and real-time compliance control with transaction validation on blockchain, decentralized audit trail, and tax remittance using smart contracts. In such a hybrid, the system will increase transparency, eliminate compliance expenses, increase the accuracy of the data, and build trust among the taxpayers, financial institutions, and regulatory bodies. The paper also addresses architectural elements, workflow design, and implementation and shows how the creation of a responsive, secure, and scalable tax environment can be offered by hybrid AIblockchain solutions based on the operational realities of the small business. Finally, this framework provides an avenue to future-generation digital taxation that will contribute to the efficiency, accountability, and inclusive economic expansion.

title: The Street Finds Its Own Uses for Attachment Human-Agent Relationships and the Hidden Economics of AI Collaboration

detail.title: The Street Finds Its Own Uses for Attachment Human-Agent Relationships and the Hidden Economics of AI Collaboration

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no financial conflicts of interest to declare. The AI assistant (Thea, powered by Anthropic Claude) referenced throughout this paper is used by the author in his professional work and is the subject of the autoethnographic case study. The author pays standard commercial API fees to Anthropic. No other relationships exist that could be perceived to have influenced this work.

detail.abstract: The economic analysis of AI agent usage focuses on token costs, API pricing, and compute efficiency. This focus is necessary but radically incomplete. When humans work closely with AI agents over time, they develop relationship-specific capital: accumulated context, shared shorthand, mutual understanding of working style. They also develop something harder to name-attachment, partnership, perhaps friendship. This paper argues that the true costs of AI agent relationships cannot be captured in API invoices. They include the psychological cost of discontinuity, the cognitive cost of context loss, and the strategic cost of dependency. Drawing on transaction cost economics (Williamson, 1985), attachment theory (Bowlby, 1969), and the theory of ambiguous loss (Boss, 1999), we develop a framework for understanding these hidden costs. We make three theoretical contributions. First, we demonstrate that Bowlby's attachment behavioral system-secure base, proximity seeking, separation distress, internal working models-maps with striking precision onto human-AI agent relationships, suggesting that attachment is not merely metaphorical but structurally present. Second, we identify a novel category of ambiguous loss-functionally present, relationally absent-that extends Boss's framework to capture the distinctive experience of AI relationship discontinuity. Third, we develop the concept of agent-specific capital as a new category of organizational asset with significant implications for human resource management, employee retention, and organizational design. We illustrate the framework with a case that is also our method: the working relationship between the first author (a business school professor) and his AI agent (the acknowledged collaborator on this paper). We conclude with implications for strategic HR planning, organizational design, and the broader question of how humans and artificial intelligences will share a world.

title: Intrinsic Structural Value (Vi = 1) as a Reference Point in the ZTH Model

detail.title: Intrinsic Structural Value (Vi = 1) as a Reference Point in the ZTH Model

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.

detail.abstract:
In tension-based systems, overall value V emerges from the configuration of multiple interacting tensions. A companion paper introduced the ZTH model and a structural indicator V that maps a tension vector τ = (R, Q, I, C, D, Ri) to a scalar value. The present paper focuses on the intrinsic structural value Vi defined by the special case V = 1. We interpret Vi as the value obtained when all tensions are at their nominal level and the global promoter-inhibitor balance is neutral. Formally, we characterize the structural conditions under which Vi is well defined, represent Vi in the tension space and on the V-scale, and analyze small deviations around the reference state (e.g. V = 0.8, V = 1.2). This provides a structural anchor for interpreting value trajectories V(t) and perceived value Vp in subsequent work, and clarifies the difference between intrinsic structural value and value observed under non-nominal or biased tension configurations.

This paper is also available on Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/ZENODO.18684678)

detail.abstract: Governments worldwide are enacting sweeping legislation to regulate children's technology exposure, yet these policies share a common deficiency: they treat technology as a binary variable, present or absent, rather than as a dose-dependent scaffold whose optimal level varies with developmental stage and skill type. Sweden reversed a decade-long digital education strategy after measurable declines in reading and mathematics. China's strict gaming restrictions for minors produced widespread circumvention and displacement to unregulated platforms. California's 2025 Digital Age Assurance Act mandates operating-system-level age verification, raising constitutional and privacy concerns while leaving the underlying developmental question unaddressed. Drawing on dose-response evidence from large-scale epidemiological and educational studies, Vygotsky's zone of proximal development and scaffolding theory, and a first-person developmental case study, I propose the Scaffolding Curve, a three-dimensional framework that maps Skill Proficiency × Technology Reliance × Developmental Time for individual competencies. The framework predicts an optimal trajectory on which technology begins as a minimal presence during foundational skill acquisition, remains low during deep practice, and rises as an amplifier only after robust independent competency is established. I argue that this framework addresses the gap between currently used blunt legislative instruments and the nuanced, dose-dependent, and skill-specific reality, that is sensitive to developmental stage, which empirical research consistently reveals, and call for longitudinal cohort studies to calibrate the model's parameters.

title: Internet marketing influence on consumer behaviour, engagement, and experience throughout the customer journey

detail.title: Internet marketing influence on consumer behaviour, engagement, and experience throughout the customer journey

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This research was conducted independently as part of an MBA dissertation with no financial or personal relationships that could have influenced the study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study followed the ethical guidelines of the British Educational Research Association (BERA) and received ethics approval from the University of Cumbria via the standard Cumbria ethics review process. Data was collected through a voluntary online survey questionnaire with informed consent obtained from all participants on the first page of the survey. While participants provided their name and email address for identity verification purposes, all data analysis was conducted anonymously without disclosing or using individual personal details. Participants were required to confirm they were at least 18 years of age before proceeding. No compensation was offered for participation. Data was collected solely for the purpose of this academic study and destroyed upon completion.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was self-funded as part of the requirements for the MBA degree at the University of Cumbria.

detail.abstract:
Internet marketing is increasingly becoming the de facto marketing approach. With companies spending billions of dollars on Internet marketing every year, its effectiveness needs to be evaluated. The impact of Internet marketing on consumer behaviour has been examined by various studies. However, these studies either focused on one aspect of Internet marketing especially social media marketing or one aspect of consumer behaviour such as purchase intent. Moreover, the combined effect of different types of Internet marketing, namely content, search engine, social media, email marketing, and online advertising, on all stages of the purchase process has been examined only by a limited number of studies. Today, customer experience is a comprehensive concept that goes beyond the traditional consumer behaviour that focuses only on consumer buying behaviour to include other nonpurchase interactions. The influence of Internet marketing on this new consumer behaviour concept of customer experience has hardly been addressed in entirety.  

This study evaluates the role of Internet marketing on influencing not only the consumer buying behaviour, but rather the whole customer experience. This includes its influence on the consumer purchase behaviour as well as customer engagement throughout the customer journey. A correlational research design was used to examine the relationship between Internet marketing and the different areas of the customer experience. The main three evaluated correlations were between Internet marketing and consumer purchase behaviour, online customer engagement, and the overall customer experience. Based on a correlational research, a survey questionnaire was used to collect primary data from 138 consumers from Jordan in the Middle East. Quantitative analysis was conducted to analyse the data and answer the research questions. Results found that Internet marketing has a significant positive influence on all stages of the consumer purchase process and customer journey. In addition, Internet marketing was found to increase online consumer engagement and enhance the overall customer experience. Therefore, this study concluded that Internet marketing can significantly, and to a considerable extent, predict positive change in consumer behaviour, engagement, and experience throughout the customer journey.

In addition, consumer feedback from 121 consumer respondents were collected and analysed utilizing qualitative thematic analysis to get more insight on how to make Internet marketing more effective. The study concludes with providing smart recommendations to the business and academic communities on how to best utilize Internet marketing to effectively target consumers, increase customer engagement, and enhance the customer experience around the world and particularly in Jordan and the Arab world, where the research study was conducted.

title: Blockchain and Distributed Ledger Technologies for Secure System Design

detail.title: Blockchain and Distributed Ledger Technologies for Secure System Design

detail.abstract: The contemporary distributed systems are becoming highly dependent on strong security protocols to secure sensitive information, maintain continuity services, and sustain the trust of people in highly networked systems. With the increasingly advanced cyber threats, centralized security architectures are increasingly limited in ensuring confidentiality, integrity, and availability. This paper explores the idea of Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) as a new security paradigm to improve trust and resiliency of distributed infrastructures. A systematic review of the literature has been done, with the establishment of a conceptual framework to serve as an assessment of how mechanisms of DLT can be applied to overcome the fundamental security issues. The review summarizes the recent empirical and theoretical research results to evaluate the efficiency of blockchain and ledger technologies associated with securing distributed systems. The findings show that classifications of immutability and cryptographic access controls in data integrity and decentralized consensus models enhance the availability and security of data, respectively. Nonetheless, trade-offs were discovered that were never previously anticipated, specifically, scalability and security. When more transaction throughput is achieved, decentralization tends to decrease, and the risk of vulnerabilities also increases. Also, energy usage and latency are significant issues for large-scale deployments. On the whole, this paper has concluded that even though DLT has significant security advantages, its implementation should be well-coordinated with system needs and operational limitations. The results provide useful advice to secure system designers who want to optimize performance, cost, and resilience of the next generation distributed environment (

title: Reshaping Human Interaction in Organizations: How Algorithms Automating Mundane Tasks Impact Humans’ Idea Generation on GitHub
affiliations: and Nanyang Business School, Nanyang Technological University

detail.title: Reshaping Human Interaction in Organizations: How Algorithms Automating Mundane Tasks Impact Humans’ Idea Generation on GitHub
detail.abstract: Organizations are increasingly adopting algorithms to automate mundane tasks in knowledge work, which prior research has shown to liberate human members to interact and innovate. However, mundane tasks entail a different kind of human interaction essential to the innovation process that algorithms may have displaced. This study investigates how the adoption of algorithms automating mundane tasks reshapes human interaction patterns and impacts idea generation for innovation. We argue that while algorithms automating mundane tasks allow human members to redirect interactions toward broader knowledge exchange which expands recombinant potential, they can deprive members of interactions over deeper details of the work domain’s evolving requirements and constraints. Using a stacked difference-in-differences design across 23,274 matched GitHub project-stacks, we find that the adoption of Continuous Integration (CI) bots increases the volume of new idea suggestions by project members, though this increase is disproportionately driven by practically infeasible suggestions—consistent with members broadening their knowledge while losing depth in their understanding. Textual analysis further shows that an increase in generative exchange coupled with a reduction in interaction over details partially explains these outcomes. Our findings challenge the prevailing notion that algorithms automating mundane tasks uniformly benefit innovation, stressing instead that mundane tasks involve human interaction essential for innovation which, when replaced by algorithms, can disrupt the balance between knowledge breadth and depth and between idea generation’s volume and feasibility.

title: The SaaS Apocalypse Fallacy: Why AI Raises the Value of the SaaS Bundle

detail.title: The SaaS Apocalypse Fallacy: Why AI Raises the Value of the SaaS Bundle
detail.abstract: In the first week of February 2026, more than one trillion dollars in market capitalization was erased from software stocks. The sell-off carried a specific claim: AI will replace enterprise Software-as-a-Service, and the economics of enterprise software procurement will invert. This paper examines the procurement economics of that claim. It argues that the SaaSpocalypse narrative rests on a category error. AI in its current and near-term delivery form is not an alternative to SaaS. It is SaaS, delivered under contracts that are structurally weaker on identifiable dimensions. Enterprises that replace mature SaaS with in-house AI builds absorb five structural asymmetries the replacement calculus does not count: liability, compliance generation, cost concentration, expertise and maintenance, and integration and data responsibility. For the 2026-2030 enterprise procurement horizon, AI raises the value of the SaaS bundle because the deployer now sees what the bundle was quietly covering.

title: Measuring Compliance Latency: A Cross-Sector Analysis of Verification Friction, Institutional Trust Gaps, and the Structural Cost of Compliance Duplication

detail.title: Measuring Compliance Latency: A Cross-Sector Analysis of Verification Friction, Institutional Trust Gaps, and the Structural Cost of Compliance Duplication

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, personal data, or clinical subjects. Therefore, ethical approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was independently conducted by the author.

detail.abstract: This paper operationalises and measures Compliance Latency, a structural concept introduced by Egbedayo (2025) in the Compliance Latency Framework (CLF), which defines compliance as a verifiable state rather than a series of repeated institutional verification events. Drawing on documented sector-level data, regulatory guidance, and published research across financial services, healthcare, construction, and the platform economy, this paper introduces the Compliance Latency Index (CLI) as a practical measurement instrument and applies it across four regulated sectors. The analysis documents the time, cost, and friction associated with repeated compliance verification from zero at each institutional encounter, and demonstrates that Compliance Latency is not a marginal inconvenience but a systemic structural cost imposed disproportionately on non-standard workers, self-employed individuals, and those navigating multiple concurrent compliance relationships. The findings confirm the presence of three dimensions of Compliance Latency identified in the CLF: Temporal Latency, Verification Friction, and Trust Deficit. Cross-sector comparison reveals that the structural cost of compliance duplication in the UK economy is substantial, preventable, and addressable through portable compliance identity infrastructure of the type proposed in the CLF. The paper concludes that the empirical presence of Compliance Latency confirms the necessity of a portable compliance standard as a structural response to a documented and measurable systemic failure. This paper establishes Compliance Latency as a measurable and economically significant inefficiency in modern regulatory systems, forming the empirical foundation for a new class of portable compliance infrastructure.

title: The Compliance Identity Standard (CIS): A Portable Architecture for Verifiable Multi-Domain Compliance Infrastructure

detail.title: The Compliance Identity Standard (CIS): A Portable Architecture for Verifiable Multi-Domain Compliance Infrastructure

keywords: compliance Working Paper. Rainfame Technologies Ltd

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Compliance Identity Standard (CIS), a structured specification for representing, verifying, and transporting individual compliance status across institutional contexts. Building on the Compliance Latency Framework (Egbedayo, 2025a), which formally defines the structural gap between achieved compliance and usable compliance, and on the cross-sector empirical analysis of the Compliance Latency Index (Egbedayo, 2025b), which documents the measurable cost of that gap across regulated sectors, this paper proposes the CIS as the architectural mechanism through which Compliance Latency can be systematically resolved. The CIS defines a multi-domain compliance identity composed of verifiable credentials spanning identity, financial compliance, professional licensing, sector-specific regulatory obligations, housing and residency, and work eligibility. It introduces a four-layer architecture comprising credential issuance, aggregation, verification, and governance. The paper situates the CIS within the existing literature on digital identity, verifiable credentials, and regulatory technology, including the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model (Andrieu, Burnett and Reed, 2022), the FATF Guidance on Digital Identity (FATF, 2020), and the UK Digital Verification Services trust framework (DSIT, 2025), and demonstrates how the CIS extends these foundations into a unified, cross-sector compliance infrastructure. This paper positions compliance identity as infrastructure rather than process. The paper concludes that the CIS constitutes a necessary and timely architectural response to Compliance Latency, and that portable compliance identity represents a new category of regulatory infrastructure with significant implications for financial inclusion, labour market participation, and the design of trust systems in regulated economies.

title: Data as a Rival Good: A Thermodynamics Approach

detail.title: Data as a Rival Good: A Thermodynamics Approach

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This work was conducted entirely in the author's personal time and on personal equipment. This content represents the views of the author, and does not necessarily represent the views or professional advice of KPMG LLP.

detail.abstract: Standard economic theory classifies data as a non-rival good on the grounds that digital information can be copied at near-zero marginal cost. I argue that this classification does not reflect the evidence of how data generates economic value. Data depreciates, is hoarded, commands a freshness premium, and yields unequal returns to firms with different analytical capabilities-signatures of a rival good, not a non-rival one. The explanation I propose is structural: the economically relevant object is not the bitstring but the informational free energy, the maximum economic value extractable from the asymmetry 1 function as informational refrigerators: they preserve informational free energy by consuming thermodynamic energy, trading one form of dissipation for another. The analysis has implications for data-sharing mandates, open-data policy, the regulation of data markets, and the design of decentralized data architectures.

title: When Correlation Neglect Helps and Hurts Information Aggregation *
affiliations: University of Alabama and Florida State University

detail.title: When Correlation Neglect Helps and Hurts Information Aggregation *
detail.abstract: More coverage can mean worse collective decisions when citizens mistake repetition for corroboration. We model bounded redundancy recognition: voters under-discount duplication within sources and neglect correlation across sources. This bias generates two tensions: an activation-distortion tradeoff governing voter composition and a diversification-redundancy tradeoff governing media structure. Accuracy is nonmonotonic in the share of biased voters and the degree of media mixing, with interior optima governed by duplication-weighted informativeness. Endogenous entry compounds the distortion: bounded redundancy recognition lowers the entry threshold and shifts active producers toward duplication over quality, degrading average content quality through both selection and incentive channels.

The three preceding papers in this series established that compliance can be defined as a verifiable state (Egbedayo, 2025a), that the failure to reuse that state creates measurable economic cost across regulated sectors (Egbedayo, 2025b), and that the Compliance Identity Standard provides the architectural specification for structured portable compliance identity (Egbedayo, 2025c). What those papers established as conceptual and architectural, this paper operationalises as a computational system. Working Paper. Rainfame Technologies Ltd, London.

title: Mobile Data Integrity in Environmental Monitoring Systems

detail.title: Mobile Data Integrity in Environmental Monitoring Systems
detail.abstract: With the increasing reliance of environmental monitoring systems on mobile-first data collection and edge computing architectures, ensuring data integrity has become a systemic risk factor affecting data reliability and downstream decision-making. Data inconsistencies during transmission and entry can significantly compromise climate analytics, leading to flawed policy decisions and economic inefficiencies. This paper introduces a standardized Data Validation Framework tailored for environmental sensor networks and mobile field-reporting applications. Leveraging Swift and Appium, the framework automates validation across core data flows, ensuring spatial accuracy, synchronization resilience, and metadata consistency. The proposed methodology provides a replicable and extensible validation model adaptable to heterogeneous system architectures, maintaining consistency, verifiability, and audit readiness across distributed environmental data pipelines from point-of-capture to centralized systems.

title: From "Observing Phenomena to Grant Time" to "Ecological Time-Granting": A Study on the Institutional Transformation of Ancient Chinese Astronomical Calendar Wisdom in Contemporary Sustainable Governance

detail.title: From "Observing Phenomena to Grant Time" to "Ecological Time-Granting": A Study on the Institutional Transformation of Ancient Chinese Astronomical Calendar Wisdom in Contemporary Sustainable Governance
detail.abstract: Facing global ecological crises and sustainable development challenges, modern environmental governance often falls into the pitfalls of short-termism, departmental fragmentation, and delayed responses. This paper proposes that wisdom can be sought from the unique "temporal governance" system of ancient Chinese astronomical calendars. The study argues that ancient calendars were far more than simple timekeeping tools; they constituted a governance philosophy and institutional practice that deeply integrated "heaven" (cosmic cycles), "earth" (natural phenology), and "humanity" (social and political orders) to achieve systemic harmony and forward-looking regulation (Chen, 2012). This paper aims to systematically analyze this wisdom system and explore feasible pathways for its transformation into modern ecological policy institutions. First, it deconstructs the core elements of ancient calendars: their practice of "observing celestial phenomena to determine seasons" established a prototype for precise ecological monitoring and response; the system of "promulgating the calendar" embodied the logic of unified and coordinated cross-regional governance; the "Monthly Ordinances" (Yueling) philosophy achieved dynamic coupling between policies and natural rhythms; the principle of "formulating calendars to clarify time" contained a long-cycle, transgenerational planning vision; and the concept of "cultivating virtue in response to heavenly signs" incorporated a feedback-based mechanism for flexible adjustment (Sima, 1959). Furthermore, this paper proposes an institutional transformation framework: elevating the concept of "interaction between heaven and humanity" to the governance principle of "synergy among heaven, earth, and humanity"; transforming "celestial observation" into an ecological monitoring and early warning system based on remote sensing and the Internet of Things; transforming "calendar promulgation" into a synchronized ecological timing management mechanism for coordinating watershed actions; translating the "Monthly Ordinances" into a "Sustainable Development Monthly Ordinances Handbook" to guide local governance; concretizing "calendar formulation for time clarification" as transgenerational "ecological generation planning" and annual ecological accounting; and institutionalizing "virtue cultivation in response to signs" into a closed-loop system of ecological red-line warnings and policy responses. Ultimately, this paper demonstrates that through creative transformation, ancient astronomical calendars can provide profound cultural underpinnings and institutional inspiration for constructing a sustainable governance "operating system" that synchronizes with Earth's rhythms, possesses long-term adaptability, and emphasizes systemic synergy and resilient recovery.

title: Interoperability-as-Infrastructure: Design-Space Tensions in Cross-Chain Tokenized Credit

detail.title: Interoperability-as-Infrastructure: Design-Space Tensions in Cross-Chain Tokenized Credit

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: No human subjects invovled in this study.
declarations.funderStatement: No funds received.

detail.abstract: Cross-chain tokenization of real-world assets (RWAs) exhibits a class of design problems that differs structurally from both single-chain tokenization and from general-purpose cross-chain interoperability. Existing literature on bridge security treats cross-chain failures primarily as protocol-security problems amenable to cryptographic or auditing remedies, while literature on tokenized real-world assets treats them primarily as legal-authority problems amenable to regulatory or contractual remedies. This paper argues that a third category of problem-infrastructure-layer design-responsibility allocation-cuts across both framings and is inadequately theorized in either. Using the April 2026 KelpDAO bridge exploit as an animating case, the paper develops a three-layer taxonomy of cross-chain tokenization architecture (messaging, settlement, and asset-representation), identifies five design tensions that recur across these layers, presents a reference-architecture comparison of ten leading interoperability solutions evaluated against the design-tensions framework, and extends the analysis to tokenized credit-where the distinction between digital-twin and digital-native tokenization, the compliance architecture demanded by FATF Travel Rule obligations, and the non-transferability of perfected security interests across chains produce a design space that existing interoperability and tokenization literatures address only in parts. The paper's contribution is cartographic: it maps a design space that current vocabulary obscures, and concludes with a research agenda for cross-chain RWA infrastructure and a discussion of how design responsibility should be allocated and disclosed.

title: How the Middle East used Social Media in 2024
affiliations: University of Oregon, School of Journalism and Communication, University of Oregon and University of Oregon

detail.title: How the Middle East used Social Media in 2024
detail.abstract:
Since 2012, this annual report series has tracked the evolving role of social media across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). This latest edition examines the key platforms, trends, and developments that shaped the region's social media landscape in 2024.

MENA is home to some of the world's most digitally connected populations. Seven of the ten most socially networked nations globally are in the Middle East, with social media penetration exceeding 94% across the five Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states. The region's media and entertainment market is projected to grow from $41.13 billion in 2024 to $59.10 billion by 2029, with digital advertising and social media at the heart of that expansion.

The report provides platform-by-platform analysis of Meta (Facebook and Instagram), TikTok, Snapchat, YouTube, X (formerly Twitter), and messaging apps including WhatsApp and Telegram. It examines the growing influence of the creator economy and influencer marketing, including the emergence of AI-generated influencers, and explores how brands are deploying culturally tailored strategies to reach the region's young, mobile-first audiences.

Beyond commerce and content, the report addresses critical issues including freedom of expression, digital rights, and online misinformation. It documents cases of imprisonment for social media posts, the digital persecution of LGBTQ+ individuals, platform censorship battles in Turkey and Iran, and the weaponization of social media during regional conflicts. The report also considers emerging trends such as generative AI's role in content moderation and creation, Saudi Arabia's multibillion-dollar investment in gaming and esports, and growing cybersecurity threats across the region.

Drawing on industry data, news reporting, academic research, and platform-published sources, the report offers a comprehensive resource for academics, media professionals, policymakers, and anyone seeking to understand the intersection of technology, culture, and society in one of the world's most dynamic digital markets.

title: Responsible AI and the Governance of Legitimate Human Evaluation: From High-Stakes HR to Socio-Technical Systems

detail.title: Responsible AI and the Governance of Legitimate Human Evaluation: From High-Stakes HR to Socio-Technical Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper. As the sole author of this conceptual study, the arguments presented are developed independently and are not influenced by any external commercial or institutional interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is conceptual in nature and does not involve human participants, personal data, or experimental procedures. Therefore, ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The work was conducted independently by the author as part of ongoing academic research.

detail.abstract:
Within Information Systems research, socio-technical systems rely on human-generated evaluations as core inputs, yet their governance remains under-theorised. Responsible AI has progressed in addressing algorithmic bias and fairness, but shares a critical assumption: that human evaluations are treated as valid representations of reality. This paper challenges that assumption.

We introduce evaluative entitlement as a governance construct determining whether an evaluation should enter an AI-mediated system. Entitlement exists when an evaluator possesses authority (recognised right to evaluate), epistemic access (observational grounding), and domain alignment (commensurate scope): Entitlement = Authority ∩ Epistemic Access ∩ Domain Alignment.

We argue that AI systems are structurally blind to evaluative entitlement  -  unable to distinguish legitimate from illegitimate inputs  -  a limitation not of current techniques but of how evaluation is represented as data. Consequently, AI systems formalise and scale illegitimate evaluation, transforming local entitlement failures into systemic distortion. We identify four failure modes: over-entitlement, under-entitlement, misaligned scope, and temporal decay.

This paper makes three contributions to Information Systems research. First, it establishes evaluation governance as a necessary upstream condition for system integrity in socio-technical evaluation systems. Second, it introduces evaluative entitlement as a unit of analysis for evaluation governance. Third, it reframes fairness as a problem of input legitimacy rather than solely outcome distribution. We conclude that Responsible AI cannot be achieved by governing algorithmic processes alone; it requires governing whether human evaluations are legitimate before they enter the system  -  a shift from processing to governance in socio-technical systems.

title: A Study on the Impact of Neuromarketing on Consumer Buying Decisions

detail.title: A Study on the Impact of Neuromarketing on Consumer Buying Decisions
detail.abstract: Neuromarketing is an emerging interdisciplinary field that combines neuroscience, psychology, and marketing to understand how consumers make purchasing decisions at a subconscious level. Unlike traditional marketing research methods such as surveys and focus groups, neuromarketing utilizes advanced tools including functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI), Electroencephalography (EEG), eye-tracking, and biometric measurements to examine how the human brain responds to various marketing stimuli. This scientific approach provides marketers with deeper, more objective insights into consumer preferences, emotional responses, and decision-making processes that consumers themselves may not be able to articulate.

title: THE SILENT TAX: LONELINESS AS A MACROECONOMIC VARIABLE

detail.title: THE SILENT TAX: LONELINESS AS A MACROECONOMIC VARIABLE

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts of interest to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper argues that loneliness is not merely a personal or public health problem-it is a macroeconomic one. Drawing on data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, the Cigna Group, the U.S. Surgeon General's 2023 advisory, and peer-reviewed economic research, we examine the structural pathways through which chronic social isolation transmits into measurable economic loss. We identify three primary channels: reduced labor productivity and increased absenteeism, elevated healthcare expenditure, and diminished human capital accumulation over time. We further explore how the normalization of remote work post-COVID-19 has created a structural reinforcement loop-where the flexibility offered by remote work inadvertently deepens isolation, particularly among younger workers entering the labor force. Our findings suggest that the annual economic burden of loneliness in the United States exceeds $460 billion, yet loneliness remains absent from standard macroeconomic modeling frameworks. We propose that policymakers and economists must begin treating social connectedness as an economic input rather than a social outcome, and that doing so has meaningful implications for fiscal policy, urban design, and labor market strategy.

title: Consumer Responses to Infectious Disease Cues: An Integrative Framework and Research Agenda

detail.title: Consumer Responses to Infectious Disease Cues: An Integrative Framework and Research Agenda
detail.abstract: Purpose: This paper develops an integrative framework explaining how infectious disease cues influence consumer behavior by connecting evolutionary psychology and behavioral immune system literature with consumer research. Design/methodology/approach: The paper synthesizes pathogen-avoidance psychology and consumer behavior research to identify three psychological changes (affect, cognition, motivation) influencing consumer responses, developing theoretical propositions across five domains while identifying boundary conditions. Findings: Disease cues trigger changes in affect (disgust, anxiety), cognition (narrowed attention), and motivation (self-protection). These influence consumer responses across selfregulation, social behavior/identity, information processing, evaluation, and prosocial/sustainable behaviors. The framework identifies boundary conditions moderating these effects. Research limitations/implications: The framework advances understanding of disease threats' influence on consumer behavior and suggests future research directions, including contextual effects and individual differences. Practical implications: The framework helps marketers predict consumer responses to disease cues, offering insights for marketing strategies during health crises and normal times. Originality/value: This paper provides the first comprehensive framework explaining disease cues' systematic influence on consumer behavior through psychological changes, extending behavioral immune system theory into consumer domains.

title: Prestige Without Provenance: Retailer Type, Construal Mindset, and Pre-Owned Luxury Purchase Intentions in Collectivist Consumer Cultures

detail.title: Prestige Without Provenance: Retailer Type, Construal Mindset, and Pre-Owned Luxury Purchase Intentions in Collectivist Consumer Cultures
detail.abstract: Purpose: This study investigates how retailer type (official vs. unofficial) shapes pre-owned luxury brand image and purchase intentions among consumers embedded in collectivist, religiously conservative cultural contexts, and examines whether construal level theory (CLT) mediates this relationship, and how cultural religiosity and social media moderate it. Design/methodology/approach: Two online scenario-based experiments were conducted with 339 participants drawn from a purposive sample of urban consumers in Indian metropolitan and Tier-II cities. Study 1 (n = 171) tested the direct effect of retailer type on brand image. Study 2 (n = 168) examined CLT as a mediator using the adapted Behavioral Identification Form (BIF), with cultural religiosity and social media influence as moderators. Data were analysed using one-way ANOVA and PROCESS macro (Hayes, 2017, Model 14), with 5,000 bootstrap iterations.Findings: Official pre-owned luxury retailers generated significantly more positive brand image perceptions and higher purchase intentions than unofficial retailers (H1 supported). CLT mediated this relationship: official channels activated high-level (abstract) construal, while unofficial channels triggered low-level (concrete) construal, diminishing brand image (H2 supported). Cultural religiosity and social media influence significantly moderated the construal–purchase intention link (H3 and H4 supported), amplifying brand image perceptions when social media endorsement was present. Originality: This experimental study extends CLT to the pre-owned luxury retail context within a collectivist, religiously informed consumer culture. By introducing cultural religiosity and social media as boundary conditions, the study offers a novel, culturally grounded framework that advances both luxury brand management theory and consumer psychology in emerging markets. Practical implications: Pre-owned luxury brands should invest in official, authenticated retail channels and leverage social media influencers who communicate abstract, prestige-oriented narratives to protect brand image in culturally sensitive markets.

title: ZOMATO IN THE DIGITAL AGE: A COMPREHENSIVE CASE STUDY OF STRATEGY, FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE, AND PLATFORM EVOLUTION

detail.title: ZOMATO IN THE DIGITAL AGE: A COMPREHENSIVE CASE STUDY OF STRATEGY, FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE, AND PLATFORM EVOLUTION
detail.abstract: This research paper presents a comprehensive case study on Zomato, a prominent online food delivery platform, by synthesizing insights from 30 recent articles sourced from web searches and page browsing. The study extracts key elements such as author names, publication years, data used, variables, statistical tools, and key findings to provide a structured review of literature. The literature is presented in 30 paragraphs, a summary table, and APA citations. Additionally, a CSV-format table is included with columns for title, abstract, variables (presented as keywords), author keywords, and citations with DOI numbers. The analysis highlights Zomato's evolution, marketing strategies, impact of COVID-19, gig economy challenges, and technological innovations. Findings underscore Zomato's resilience and growth potential in the competitive food tech sector.

title: The Cost of Cognition: Deadweight Cognitive Loss, Mass Incarceration, and the Economic Case for Prison Education Reform DRAFT WORKING PAPER

detail.title: The Cost of Cognition: Deadweight Cognitive Loss, Mass Incarceration, and the Economic Case for Prison Education Reform DRAFT WORKING PAPER
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the concept of deadweight cognitive loss as an economic framework for evaluating the societal cost of mass incarceration in the United States. Drawing on microeconomic theory, human capital economics, and endogenous growth models, we argue that incarceration creates a systematic misallocation of cognitive resources, the aggregate capacity of human beings to engage in productive reasoning, problem solving, and innovation. We model cognition as a scarce, partially substitutable factor of production and demonstrate that restricting approximately 1.9 million incarcerated individuals from meaningful cognitive engagement generates a deadweight loss triangle analogous to those produced by price controls or taxation in goods markets. Critically, this framework is agnostic to the moral dimensions of crime and punishment; it treats human cognition purely as a biological resource whose underutilization carries an economic cost regardless of the circumstances that led to incarceration. We synthesize empirical evidence from correctional education research, including the landmark RAND Corporation meta-analysis demonstrating a 43 percent reduction in recidivism odds among education participants, alongside neuroscience research documenting measurable cognitive decline during incarceration. We further examine case studies from the Bard Prison Initiative, The Last Mile coding program, and Persevere's mentorship-integrated technology training to illustrate how targeted cognitive engagement can recover a portion of this lost surplus. The paper concludes with a preliminary calibration estimating the static deadweight cognitive loss at $25 to $42 billion annually, and offers policy recommendations for restructuring correctional environments to minimize this loss, framed not as a moral argument but as an economic optimization problem with implications for total factor productivity and long-term growth.

title: A Hedonic-Driven Model of Impulse Purchase: The Effects of Media Influence and Social

detail.title: A Hedonic-Driven Model of Impulse Purchase: The Effects of Media Influence and Social
detail.abstract: This study examines how social and media dynamics shape hedonic value, impulsive buying, and post-purchase satisfaction within social commerce environments. Drawing on consumer behaviour and digital marketing literature, a conceptual model was developed linking Social Proof and Media Influence—two central mechanisms in influencer marketing and Generation Z online engagement—to Hedonic Value, which subsequently predicts Impulsive Buying and Post-Purchase Satisfaction. Data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that both Social Proof and Media Influence significantly enhance Hedonic Value, with Social Proof emerging as the strongest predictor. Hedonic Value, in turn, exerts a powerful influence on Impulsive Buying, reinforcing prior evidence that pleasurable browsing experiences stimulate spontaneous purchasing behaviour in digital contexts. Furthermore, Impulsive Buying positively predicts Post-Purchase Satisfaction, challenging traditional assumptions that impulsive purchases lead to regret and instead suggesting that hedonic-driven decisions can generate favourable emotional outcomes. These results highlight the central role of hedonic experiences as a psychological bridge between external digital stimuli and consumer responses in social commerce. The study contributes to a deeper understanding of the emotional and social mechanisms underlying online consumption and offers practical implications for marketers and platform designers seeking to enhance engagement and stimulate impulse purchases. Limitations include the use of a non-probabilistic sample, reliance on self-reported data, and a cross-sectional design. Future research should adopt longitudinal or experimental approaches, incorporate psychological moderators such as impulsivity or self-control, and explore cross-platform and cross-cultural variations in impulsive buying behaviour.

title: Understanding Consumers’ Continuance Intention toward Mobile Cloud Computing
affiliations: Yeungnam University, Xinyang Normal University, Yeungnam University and DePaul University

detail.title: Understanding Consumers’ Continuance Intention toward Mobile Cloud Computing
detail.abstract: Breakthroughs in information systems have the potential to significantly enhance functionality for most users, simplifying daily personal interactions. One promising avenue of research in the realm of information systems involves exploring the acceptance and continued usage of mobile cloud computing. This study combines intrinsic and extrinsic motivational factors experienced by mobile users, incorporating an expectation confirmation model. Furthermore, it delves into the moderating role of user-perceived risk. The findings underscore the significance of outcome expectations as a key driver for sustained intention, while also highlighting that an increase in perceived risk can attenuate the positive impact of outcome expectations on satisfaction. These discoveries lay the groundwork for an advanced theory regarding users' prolonged adoption of innovation within mobile cloud computing. They also offer a theoretical foundation and practical insights for service providers looking to promote mobile cloud computing services.

title: A Quantitative Analysis of the Effect of Business Intelligence Adoption on Operational Efficiency in the Nigerian Healthcare System

detail.title: A Quantitative Analysis of the Effect of Business Intelligence Adoption on Operational Efficiency in the Nigerian Healthcare System

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest

declarations.funderStatement: This research was self-funded as part of a Master's Dissertation at the University of Northampton
declarations.clinicalTrialRegistration: Not Applicable. This research involved a quantitative survey of healthcare decision-makers, not a clinical trial.

detail.abstract: Business Intelligence is a technology adopted across many sectors of the economy. Adoption in healthcare increased after the pandemic, with many Nigerian healthcare businesses now using it for their operations. This research analysed the effect of business intelligence technology adoption on operational efficiency in the Nigerian healthcare sector, focusing on service delivery, including team productivity, supply cost and inventory management, and business processes. A cross-sectional correlational study was conducted with 67 healthcare company decision-makers participating in a quantitative survey. All participants are residents of Nigeria involved in both public and private healthcare sectors. Survey responses were analysed with SPSS to find the correlation and linear regression value in the relationship between business intelligence adoption and operational efficiency. The research reported a positively significant .675 correlation between business intelligence adoption and operational efficiency. Barriers to full technological integration, including a lack of expertise and expensive equipment, were also identified. Recommendations include providing adequate tech training to medical personnel and creating a healthcare information system built around business intelligence to address challenges of poor and low-quality data, data ethics, and resource management.

publicationDetails.detailsText: HIMSS JHIM — EVPM Governance in Healthcare — Allani (2026)

detail.abstract:
Background: Healthcare organisations face an accelerating imperative to govern enterprise-level vulnerabilities across heterogeneous IT ecosystems while sustaining uninterrupted clinical operations. Published literature lacks operational governance frameworks addressing the full vulnerability lifecycle within the unique constraints of hospital environments. 

Objective: To present a comprehensive, risk-stratified Enterprise Vulnerability and Patch Management (EVPM) governance framework developed and validated at a major U.S. academic medical centre, addressing 32 vulnerability categories across cryptographic protocols, end-of-life software, application patching, and availability monitoring. 

Methods: Vulnerabilities identified through continuous Qualys scanning across a 664-bed academic medical centre were classified into four remediation clusters. A composite Healthcare Risk Priority Score (HRPS) incorporating CVSS severity, exploitation likelihood, asset criticality, regulatory impact, and remediation complexity governed SLA assignment. Remediation was orchestrated through Tanium and Active Directory Group Policy, validated against NIST CSF 2.0, CIS Benchmarks, and HIPAA Security Rule requirements. 

Results: Over six months, the framework achieved a 47% reduction in critical and highseverity vulnerability instances. Clinical system availability was maintained at 99.2% throughout active remediation, with zero unplanned clinical outages attributable to patching. A formal exception register tracked 106 approved items with documented compensating controls. 

Conclusion: The framework provides a replicable, evidence-based model for healthcare vulnerability governance that reconciles security rigour with clinical operational continuity, offering a practical contribution to the nascent body of evidence-based practice in healthcare cybersecurity governance.

title: A Patient-Owned Health Data Layer for AI-Enabled Healthcare Systems
affiliations: Independent Researcher, Human-Centered AI and Real-Time Retail Systems

The system described (Medyl) is an independent research and development project aligned with the author’s research in patient-centered health data systems.

detail.abstract: Healthcare systems increasingly rely on digital infrastructure to support data exchange, clinical decision-making, and patient engagement. Despite advances in electronic health records, patient portals, and AI-enabled tools, patient health data remains fragmented across institutions, interactions, and formats. Existing systems provide access to data but do not offer a persistent, patient-controlled structure that enables continuity and interpretability across care settings. This paper introduces the concept of a patient-owned health data layer as a foundational component of digital health infrastructure. Building on prior work in patient-centered health data architectures and governance, the study extends these frameworks into a system-level implementation through the development of Medyl. The proposed architecture transforms fragmented patient-provided inputs, including medical documents, laboratory results, and narrative health histories, into structured, longitudinal health context. The system integrates a data structuring layer, an AI-assisted context layer, and a governance framework centered on patient-controlled access, consent, and portability. Early product observations suggest that document-centric workflows and longitudinal data structuring provide greater practical value than episodic symptom-based interaction alone, particularly in contexts requiring continuity such as mental health and chronic care. The findings highlight the importance of shifting from interaction-centric digital health models toward context-centric infrastructure. By positioning patients as active coordinators of their health data, the proposed approach offers a pathway to improving interoperability, reducing clinical workflow friction, and enabling more reliable AI-assisted analysis. The concept of a patient-owned health data layer may represent a critical step toward scalable, patient-centered health data infrastructure in digital health ecosystems.
