title: Difference-in-Differences in Asset Pricing: Identification Challenges under Portfolio Aggregation
affiliations: University of North Carolina (UNC) at Charlotte - Finance, University of North Carolina  (UNC) at Wilmington,  and Washington University in St. Louis - John M. Olin Business School

detail.title: Difference-in-Differences in Asset Pricing: Identification Challenges under Portfolio Aggregation

keywords: asset pricing anomalies JEL Classification: G12

detail.abstract: We show that, despite its widespread use in empirical finance, difference-indifferences (DID) fails to deliver causal identification when individual securities are aggregated into portfolio outcomes. This aggregation collapses the cross section into a single treated and control unit, eliminating the variation required for identification. In addition, when a single treatment shock is repeatedly analyzed across specifications, statistical precision can be overstated by reusing the same underlying information. We develop a protocol that restores cross-sectional variation, implements randomization-based inference, and aggregates evidence while preserving dependence. Applying this framework to Regulation SHO, we find no robust evidence that short-selling constraints affect anomaly-based return predictability.

title: A Robust Cross-Sectional Attention Premium: Evidence from Wikipedia Pageviews in the Russell 1000 Universe

detail.title: A Robust Cross-Sectional Attention Premium: Evidence from Wikipedia Pageviews in the Russell 1000 Universe
detail.abstract: We document a robust cross-sectional return premium associated with public attention to individual stocks, measured by daily Wikipedia pageviews of company articles. In a panel of 840 Russell 1000 constituents over 2015-2024, Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional regressions controlling for size, momentum, short-term reversal, and per-stock loadings on the Fama-French five factors plus momentum yield Newey-West t-statistics of 2.16 to 3.14 on the attention coefficient across 1-, 5-, and 20-day horizons, robust to blockbootstrap inference. The premium is concentrated in high-volatility regimes (t = 2.86 versus t = 1.05 in low-volatility periods), consistent with the limits-to-arbitrage mechanism of Shleifer and Vishny (1997). Monthly timeseries regressions against the Baker and Wurgler (2006) investor-sentiment index and the Fama-French factors yield a conditional SIRP α of 13.5 percent annualized (t = 2.61), establishing that the attention premium is not subsumed by aggregate sentiment. Critically, the universe expansion from S&P 500 to Russell 1000 reveals a novel U-shaped pattern in size heterogeneity: the attention premium is statistically significant in both Small (t = 2.68) and Large (t = 2.60) market-capitalization terciles but insignificant in the Mid-cap tercile (t = 1.24). Kumar (2009)-style retail-tilt proxies confirm that retail-heavy stocks earn an attention premium 2.1× larger than institutionalheavy stocks (t = 3.10 vs. t = 2.25). Following the characteristics-versuscovariances distinction of Daniel and Titman (1997), we show the returnpredictive content operates through the attention characteristic rather than through covariance with an aggregate attention factor. A true out-of-sample portfolio test (train 2015-2019, test 2020-2024) yields a Sharpe ratio of 1.30 with 12.85 percent annualized alpha against Fama-French five factors plus momentum (t = 3.24).

title: A Zero-Free-Parameter Test of the Geometric Volatility Smile on SPY LEAPS

detail.title: A Zero-Free-Parameter Test of the Geometric Volatility Smile on SPY LEAPS
detail.abstract: The information-geometric smile framework of companion papers [A] and [B] predicts, at leading order and in the diffusion-dominated long-maturity regime, a T-independent skew γ = ρν/(2σ 0) and a T-independent effective curvature κ dif f ef f = (2-3ρ 2)(ν/σ 0) 2 /6 expressed in terms of realized-time-series inputs alone, with no free parameters fitted to the options panel. This paper executes the cleanest possible test of those predictions on the SPY long-datedoption (LEAPS) panel, where the Merton-jump contribution κ jumps (T) ∝ 1/T 2 has decayed to negligible levels (< 0.01 at T > 1 yr, at SPY-typical parameters). Using the April 22, 2026 options snapshot at SPY spot $709.95, we extract observed smile coefficients at four LEAPS expiries spanning 1.15 to 2.65 years. The observed skew γ obs is flat at-2.22 ± 0.16 across the four maturities (coefficient of variation 7%), within 20 percent of the framework prediction γ pred =-2.75, and the observed curvature κ obs has mean 3.81, within 12 percent of the framework prediction κ pred = 4.34. Neither prediction involves any fit to the options panel; all five input parameters (σ 0 , ν, ρ, λ, μ J , δ J) are pinned by realized-time-series econometrics through the procedures of companion paper [B]. On the short-to-moderate-dated SPY panel of [B], by contrast, the observed skew is steeply T-dependent, ranging from-3.87 at one-year to-7.16 at one-week; we find empirically that γ obs (T) = γ ∞ + b/ √ T with γ ∞ =-3.32, b =-0.538, and R 2 = 0.992, with the intriguing numerical identity b/σ 0 ≈-π to within 0.1 percent. This root-T structure together with the variance-risk-premium integral of the smile reconciles the short-T γ(T) pattern with the LEAPS T-independence through a T-dependent variance-risk-premium factor ν options (T)/ν real that accounts simultaneously for the γ(T) steepening, the SABRcalibrated ν exceeding realized ν by a factor of 1.8, and the √ T form of the short-T skew residual. The results deliver the zero-free-parameter empirical validation of the framework that companion papers [A] and [B] were setting up and point toward the VIX-as-thermodynamictemperature program of paper P3-3.

title: AI-Driven Cyber Threat Detection Framework for Financial Systems (ZMACD Model)

detail.title: AI-Driven Cyber Threat Detection Framework for Financial Systems (ZMACD Model)
detail.abstract: The increasing digitization of financial systems has intensified exposure to cyber threats such as fraud, identity theft, and advanced persistent attacks. Traditional security mechanisms struggle to adapt to evolving attack patterns. This paper proposes a practical AI-driven cyber threat detection framework that integrates machine learning-based anomaly detection with a dynamic risk scoring mechanism. The objective is to improve detection accuracy, reduce false positives, and enable real-time response in financial environments. The proposed model is designed to be scalable and cost-efficient for both large financial institutions and small-to-medium enterprises. The framework contributes to strengthening cybersecurity resilience in critical financial infrastructure.

title: Research Streams in Biodiversity Finance: A Bibliometric Analysis and Research Agenda
affiliations: Blockchain Research Lab, Blockchain Research Lab and Mahidol University - International College

detail.title: Research Streams in Biodiversity Finance: A Bibliometric Analysis and Research Agenda

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: Biodiversity loss is accelerating at an unprecedented pace, threatening ecosystem stability, economic resilience, and human well-being, with billions required to reverse current trends. Against this backdrop, biodiversity finance has emerged as a rapidly expanding but highly fragmented field spanning ecology, economics, finance, accounting, and policy. Biodiversity finance supports the conservation, sustainable use, and restoration of biodiversity through targeted financial mechanisms. However, it remains an emerging, complex, and fragmented field, with the majority of relevant knowledge being produced in non-finance journals. This study employs quantitative bibliometric analysis to examine a corpus of 189,456 references underlying 3,998 articles related to biodiversity and finance. The analysis identifies eight primary research streams within the field that concern (1) strategic and financial approaches in global biodiversity conservation, (2) the impact and implementation of payments for environmental services (PES) in developing countries, (3) neoliberal influences and implications in environmental conservation, (4) biodiversity offsets and conservation, (5) ecosystem services and biodiversity, (6) integrating conservation and community interests in biodiversity management, (7) balancing agricultural intensification with biodiversity conservation, and (8) global and corporate biodiversity reporting. The characteristics of each research stream and its prevalent publications are outlined, alongside an analysis of their temporal evolution and the degree of information exchange among the research streams. The findings provide a structured map of the intellectual architecture of biodiversity finance, document pronounced silos between economicallyoriented and critical/political-economy research streams, and translate these patterns into a focused research agenda and implications for policymakers, financial institutions, and corporate actors.

title: Fighting in the Middle East: Religious or strategic? Subtitle: Region in Transition: Conflict, Realignment, and the Search for Stability Author

detail.title: Fighting in the Middle East: Religious or strategic? Subtitle: Region in Transition: Conflict, Realignment, and the Search for Stability Author
detail.abstract:
The Middle East is passing through a decisive phase that will shape its future, where instability stems not only from external pressures but also from internal weaknesses and structural deficiencies. This article argues that while geopolitical strategies and global rivalries play a role, enduring turmoil in the region is deeply linked to fragile internal dynamics, particularly the Shia–Sunni divide and the persistence of extremist tendencies.
It further examines the shifting power equations, highlighting the contrast between Iran’s ideology-driven regional approach and the economically pragmatic strategies of Arab states, which has led to changing alliances, including improving Arab–Israel relations. At the same time, the region faces growing risks of escalation as conventional and sub-conventional conflicts increasingly overlap, raising the possibility of wider regional spillover.
The article concludes by emphasizing that long-term stability in the Middle East depends on both internal reform and regional cooperation, with a stable and pragmatic Iran being crucial for economic initiatives such as the India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) and the broader goal of sustainable regional growth.

title: U.S. Tariffs on India and India's Strategic Response

detail.title: U.S. Tariffs on India and India's Strategic Response
detail.abstract:
From 2018 to 2025, the American tariff policies. This had an effect on Indian export flows.
This was especially true for steel, Indian aluminum, Indian pharmaceuticals, Indian textiles,
and Indian IT services. The city of New Delhi did not just stick to the markets.
New Delhi made some changes at home. Also tried to make friends with other countries.
When we look at the trade patterns during these years, we can see that things were a bit
messy, especially when Washington put taxes on certain things.
But it was not all bad some Indian industries were able to adapt they started sending their
goods to places and they also changed the way they worked with other companies. The
relationship with countries outside of North America changed in a way. This happened
because of changes in policies in India. These changes affected how things were made and
how India worked with countries. As time went on, it became clear that trying approaches
helped deal with problems from outside. At first, these changes caused some problems.
Over time, they helped India keep access to markets. India did not become strong because
of one thing. Because of many things that happened at the same time. The results show that
it was not one thing that worked, but many things together. By using talks and making
changes to the system, India was able to keep trading with other countries without any big
breaks. This change shows that a country can respond when it has to. The results do not
mean that India is completely safe. They do show that it can deal with some of the problems
that come with trade. To finish this work gives some ideas to the people who make policy to
help India do better in trade. It looks at how to make things in India and how to make
important alliances with other countries. These things might help reduce the effect of
changes in trade rules on India. This work helps us understand what happens in trade
disputes. We can see clearly how countries like India respond when rich countries make
rules that are not fair. India and other developing countries can learn from this. The ideas in
this work can help India make trade policies. Insight emerges on how such economies adapt
under pressure.

title: Economía del comportamiento en plataformas digitales_evidencia desde ciudades intermedias en Colombia

detail.title: Economía del comportamiento en plataformas digitales_evidencia desde ciudades intermedias en Colombia

declarations.declarationOfInterest: El autor declara que no existen conflictos de interés financieros, personales o profesionales que hayan influido en la realización de este estudio.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Este estudio es de carácter conceptual y no involucra participantes humanos ni datos sensibles, por lo que no requiere aprobación ética.
declarations.funderStatement: Esta investigación no recibió financiación específica de agencias del sector público, comercial o sin fines de lucro.

detail.abstract: El crecimiento de las plataformas digitales ha transformado significativamente la forma en que los consumidores toman decisiones. Este estudio analiza cómo los principios de la economía del comportamiento influyen en la elección de productos y servicios dentro de entornos digitales, especialmente en ciudades intermedias de Colombia. A través de un enfoque conceptual complementado con simulación de datos, se examinan factores como la prueba social, la visibilidad y los sesgos cognitivos. Los resultados evidencian que la visibilidad dentro de las plataformas tiene un impacto directo en la probabilidad de elección, sugiriendo que las plataformas no solo intermediarios, sino que moldean activamente el comportamiento económico.

title: Sustainable Economic Development and Digital Sovereignty
affiliations: Moscow State University of International Relations (MGIMO University)

detail.title: Sustainable Economic Development and Digital Sovereignty
detail.abstract:
Sustainable economic development is a crucial task for any country. The fragmentation of the global economic system necessitates the protection of national interests and the maintenance of national sovereignty, and sustainable economic development is essential for achieving this goal.

Economic development is currently unthinkable without the widespread and large-scale use of digital technologies. We are experiencing a true digital transformation in many areas of life: in the economy, politics, and social communication. This inevitably involves the use of new forms and methods of interaction, as well as the modification of the interacting actors themselves at the micro and macro levels.

One of the most important issues of our time is the issue of sovereignty, including digital sovereignty, which includes technological independence and digital security at both the micro and macro levels.

Ensuring digital sovereignty is a complex and controversial process. On the one hand, the digital world is inherently opposed to secrecy: digital technologies, as noted in many publications, contribute to increased transparency in transactions, accelerate access to information, and platform technologies scale its dissemination. At the same time, there is continuous real-time communication between economic actors, which simplifies the overcoming of geographical, temporal, and cross-border obstacles.

On the other hand, it is necessary to respect the country's sovereign economic interests, which requires increased attention to information security, product protection, and the promotion of one's own ideas.

Since digital sovereignty is of great importance for the sustainable economic development of our country, it is necessary to focus on achieving it by continuing to actively and fully utilize the benefits of digital transformation.

title: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY IN THE WORLD OF SPORTS: READY, SET, INNOVATE

detail.title: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY IN THE WORLD OF SPORTS: READY, SET, INNOVATE
detail.abstract:
The global sports industry is, at its core, a marketplace of intangibles. Stadiums fill with fans who come not merely to witness athletic performance, but to commune with brands, team identities, narratives, and the spectacle of the game. In 2026, that spectacle has never been more technologically elaborate, commercially dense, or legally complex.     
    
Intellectual Property comprising patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets, and design rights constitutes the backbone of the sports economy. The team logo that sells tens of millions in licensed merchandise. The patented carbon-fibre sole that shaves hundredths of a second off a sprint. The broadcast rights agreement that generates hundreds of millions from a streaming platform. These are not hollow concerns. They are the primary mechanisms through which sports generates, retains, and multiplies value. Every aspect of sports is underpinned by a web of proprietary rights, whether it’s the trademarks of brands, the design rights of merchandise, the copyrights for broadcasts, IP plays the game of sports. Hence, the question before us is no longer simply whether IP protections apply to sports. The question is whether the legal frameworks in place are robust enough to protect the volume of innovation being generated and what happens when they fall short.

This article examines the key IP concepts operative in modern sports, the stakeholders who generate and monetise that IP, case studies from across the globe and from Nigeria in particular, and a framework for what athletes, clubs, leagues, and entrepreneurs must do now to protect what they build.

title: Intellectual and Economic Resistance in the Soviet Union: A Historical Overview

detail.title: Intellectual and Economic Resistance in the Soviet Union: A Historical Overview
detail.abstract:
The primary objective of this article is to analyze the critical role played by Soviet intellectuals, economists, and writers in challenging a rigid state structure between 1965 and 1985. History often attributes the fall of the Soviet Union solely to political maneuvers or external pressures; however, this piece highlights the internal intellectual resistance that acted as the true catalyst for change.

By examining the visionary proposals of reformers like Evsei Liberman and the courageous critiques of later scholars, this article seeks to demonstrate how systemic stagnation is inevitable when intellectual freedom and technological adaptation are suppressed. Furthermore, this historical review serves as a foundational context for modern economic comparisons, specifically drawing parallels with contemporary developing nations to underscore that the lessons of the Soviet collapse are not merely relics of the past, but urgent warnings for the present.

title: Explaining Tennis Success at the Country Level
affiliations: , Kadir Has University, Kadir Has University, Kadir Has University and Kadir Has University

detail.title: Explaining Tennis Success at the Country Level

declarations.funderStatement: Authors gratefully acknowledge the financial support of the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey (TUBITAK). The grant number is: 224K790.

detail.abstract: In this paper, we focus on countries’ success in tennis as measured by their population adjusted top 500 and top 100 ranked players (both women and men) and focus on understanding why certain countries are more successful than others. By gathering data for more than 200 countries over the 2000-2024 time period at the macro, meso and micro levels, we find support for previous literature both from sports policies as well as economics on the specific factors for a country’s success. Our results suggest international mobility of players and access to finance are important macro level determinants in tennis success. At the meso level, the number of players, and courts provides a positive association with success and the interaction of the number of coaches and players is important. In addition, a country with an established tennis culture is more likely to be successful and this holds especially for women players. We next divide the sample as top tier wealth countries and rest of the world and observe that policies should differ between these two groups of countries. For countries that are not in the top 25% wealth group, there needs to be a careful allocation of available resources among investment in increasing tennis players, coaches, courts and clubs. Simultaneous increase of players, courts, and coaches often leads to diminishing marginal returns. These findings provide a roadmap for policymakers, suggesting that national strategies must be in harmony with a country's specific stage of economic development.

title: A Unified Framework for Opinion Dynamics

detail.title: A Unified Framework for Opinion Dynamics
detail.abstract: We develop social learning environments as a unified framework for modeling and analyzing opinion dynamics. A social learning environment consists of a finite set of individuals and, for every individual, a set of possible opinions and an opinion updating rule. We establish conditions that guarantee the existence of an equilibrium and the convergence of learning paths to an equilibrium. Our framework unifies a wide range of models from the literature, including the voter, DeGroot, and Sznajd models, as well as the majority rule and a variation we call individual majority rule. This unification reveals a common underlying structure that explains the stability of these seemingly distinct models. Building on this foundation, we extend the theory to adaptive networks, in which network topology and opinion dynamics change simultaneously through a feedback loop. In particular, we introduce a novel class of adaptive networks called selective diffusion networks, where opinions are about the benefits provided by other individuals, and link formation is costly. We show that equilibria are absorbing when stability of opinions coincides with consensus within network components. Lastly, we develop potential functions as an alternative method for analyzing convergence. We provide an order-theoretic characterization of potential functions, which leads to a systematic method for their construction, and establish formal connections between potentials and conditions on social learning environments.

title: The Digital Transformation of Germany's Largest Publishing Houses: An Analysis of Print, E-Paper, and Online News Platforms Development

detail.title: The Digital Transformation of Germany's Largest Publishing Houses: An Analysis of Print, E-Paper, and Online News Platforms Development

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known conflicts of interest associated with this publication and there has been no significant financial support for this work that could have influenced its outcome.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study is based on the analysis of publicly available, audited industry data (IVW) and does not involve human subjects, personal data, or clinical trials.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Over the past decade, Germany’s daily newspaper industry has undergone profound structural transformation. Key drivers include the rise of digital platforms, accelerating declines in print circulation, and the massive shift of advertising revenues toward global intermediaries such as Google and Meta. While the print market has been extensively studied, the digital transformation of online news has largely been examined through isolated case studies or high level aggregate trends, leaving a notable gap in longitudinal, publisher-specific analyses. This thesis addresses that gap by extending Horst Röper’s proportional attribution model to the digital era. Drawing on audited data from the Informationsgemeinschaft zur Feststellung der Verbreitung von Werbeträgern (IVW) - including quarterly circulation figures, E-Paper shares, and monthly page impressions—the study constructs a consistent longitudinal panel covering Germany’s ten largest publishing houses from 2015 to 2024. This integrated, cross-media framework enables systematic reconstruction of market developments at both aggregate and individual publisher levels across print, E-Paper, and online channels. The findings reveal markedly divergent adaptation strategies among the observed publishing houses, despite shared structural pressures from platform dominance and the ongoing print-to digital shift. Centralization and the resulting economies of scale enable cost efficiencies, expanded online reach, and increasing market concentration, yet the individual publishers implement and leverage these mechanisms in substantially different ways. Building on these insights, the analysis develops a strategic typology that identifies four distinct archetypes of digital transformation: Volume-First, Yield-First, Hybrid/Centralized, and Strategic Divestment / Legacy Trap. This framework offers a nuanced perspective on how leading German publishers navigate the tension between preserving legacy print operations and the demands of digital scalability.

title: Can Option Contracts for Feed Mitigate the Effects of Drought on Pastoralists?
affiliations: Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, College of Agriculture & Natural Resources and Universidad Politécnica de Madrid

detail.title: Can Option Contracts for Feed Mitigate the Effects of Drought on Pastoralists?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they, their partners, nor any close relative has a paid or unpaid position in any non profit or profit organization relevant to the research described in this paper. No parties had the right to review this paper prior to its circulation.
declarations.funderStatement: Enrique Estefania-Salazar acknowledges financial support from Universidad Politécnica de Madrid through its PhD scholarship program. This study was conducted as part of the PRISMA Project (Research and Innovation for Productive, Resilient and Healthy Agro-Pastoral Systems in West Africa Project), funded by the European Union’s DeSIRA Initiative (Grant Agreement No. FOOD/2021/425-850) and co-funded by the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID).

detail.abstract: Drought is a major threat for pastoralists in developing countries who depend on grazingbased livestock rearing. In the absence of adequate financial risk management tools, extreme dry spells expose livestock-dependent households to the risk of falling into a poverty trap. Option contracts that create the right to purchase livestock feed at a predetermined price could serve to mitigate that risk. We present a theoretical framework for valuing such option contracts on both the individual buyer (pastoralists) and individual seller (feed providers) sides. We use a numerical simulation model based on data from the Sahelian region of West Africa to assess the potential viability of such option contracts. That numerical analysis indicates that buyers' willingness to pay exceeds sellers' willingness to accept, suggesting that establishing option contracts is feasible in principle. We discuss practical considerations affecting implementation of these contracts.

title: Community identity and skill mismatch: A study on Indian labour market
affiliations: University of Calcutta - Department of Economics and Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Delhi

detail.title: Community identity and skill mismatch: A study on Indian labour market
detail.abstract: This paper characterizes skill mismatch in Indian labor market and finds the role of community identity in explaining the existence of skill mismatch. We propose a job market signaling model where we argue that the costs of signaling are different for different communities and theoretically show that students from disadvantaged groups such as scheduled castes and tribes (SC/ST) end up spending higher number of years in schools than their high caste counterpart. Using several rounds of National Sample Survey data, we measure the extent of over and under education in different sectors and show that the SC/ST students are more likely to have over education compared to their higher caste counterparts. We also test the same for Muslim identity and find that the effect works both ways-Muslim workers tend to be both over and under educated depending on the sector. The wage premium associated with over education is found to be positive. title: SUSTAINABILITY REPORTING IN THE STRATEGIC MANAGEMENT SYSTEM OF OIL AND GAS COMPANIES
affiliations: Moscow State Institute of International Relations (MGIMO)

detail.title: SUSTAINABILITY REPORTING IN THE STRATEGIC MANAGEMENT SYSTEM OF OIL AND GAS COMPANIES
detail.abstract: Sustainability reporting in oil and gas companies is typically analysed as a disclosure practice responsive to stakeholder expectations. This paper reframes the question by asking how such reporting operates within the strategic management system itself. Applying Simons’ Levers of Control (LoC) framework, the paper argues that sustainability reporting is a cross-cutting element functioning simultaneously across all four levers — beliefs, boundary, diagnostic, and interactive. Drawing on international majors (Saudi Aramco, TotalEnergies, ExxonMobil) and leading Russian companies (Rosneft, Lukoil, NOVATEK), and situated in the Russian regulatory framework (Ministry of Economic Development Order No. 764 of 1 November 2023 on Methodological Recommendations for Sustainability Reporting; 2025 Business Social Capital Standard, Government Resolution No. 2230), the analysis shows that the Standard’s “capitalization strategy” principle sits at the interface between diagnostic and interactive control, producing a distinctive national configuration of the LoC framework with direct implications for internal control architecture.

title: Mega-IPOs and Index Fund Mechanics: Much Ado About Nothing?

detail.title: Mega-IPOs and Index Fund Mechanics: Much Ado About Nothing?
detail.abstract: Index providers are reviewing and modifying their rules to allow large IPOs to enter indexes more quickly than in the past, and with recently IPO'd stocks historically underperforming the market by 3-5% per year, index fund investors are understandably on edge about the coming wave of mega-IPOs from SpaceX, OpenAI, and others.But the math tells a calmer story: even $280 billion in IPO proceeds would represent just 0.4% of US market cap, and a worst-case scenario implies roughly 0.2% drag on broad index fund returns - about what the market moves in 30 minutes on a typical day. Rather than worrying about IPO inclusion timing, investors would be better served focusing on the long-term expected returns of the markets they're invested in.

title: China's "Fab" Five: Huawei, Alibaba, and the Parallel AI Chip Ecosystem

detail.title: China's "Fab" Five: Huawei, Alibaba, and the Parallel AI Chip Ecosystem
detail.abstract: In response to U.S. sanctions and export control, Chinese semiconductor companies are attempting to build an array of bridges across the "AI moat" erected by the U.S. government, with varying levels of success. Although a myriad of Chinese tech firms are involved in this effort, which has been described as China's "Manhattan Project" due to its immense difficulty, there are five companies that are arguably at the center of the majority of these initiatives. I have dubbed these firms the "Fab Five" (a reference to semiconductor fabs). The Fab Five include three AI chip designers (Alibaba, Huawei, and Cambricon), a contract chipmaker (SMIC), and a DRAM/HBM memory chip designer (CXMT). While these five companies are far from the only companies active in China in the AI chip system, they have asserted themselves as the market leaders in one or more of the central components of the AI chip ecosystem, namely AI chip design, memory chip design, and chip fabrication. By outlining the unique strengths and weaknesses of the “Fab Five,” this article aims to sketch out the prospects for China’s AI chip self-sufficiency drive in the face of U.S. sanctions.

title: The Metabolic Theory of the Economic Organism:Chapter 6: The Nature of Money: Blood, Hormones, and the Metabolic Medium

detail.title: The Metabolic Theory of the Economic Organism:Chapter 6: The Nature of Money: Blood, Hormones, and the Metabolic Medium

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: Not applicable.

detail.abstract:
This paper is Chapter 6 of the book The Metabolic Theory of the Economic Organism: From the Mechanistic Paradigm to the Living Systems. The complete manuscript of the book is available on SSRN (DOI: 10.2139/ssrn.6456938) and OSF Preprints (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/KPXNY).

This chapter develops the monetary theory of the Economic Organism–Metabolism Theory (EOMT) by reinterpreting money as a dual metabolic medium—circulatory carrier and regulatory signal—and constructing a diagnostic policy framework grounded in metabolic physiology rather than aggregate quantity management.

Two foundational misidentifications are rejected. First, money is not wealth but the medium through which value circulates. Second, money is not neutral at any horizon: monetary environments irreversibly reshape structural pathways, debt configurations, and risk tolerances. Episodes such as the 2022 rate-hike shock illustrate that monetary tightening can trigger systemic adjustment far beyond nominal price effects, while sustained monetary expansion alters structure rather than merely prices.

The distinction between circulatory and regulatory functions provides the key analytical lens. Monetary crises are interpreted as disruptions in flow or signaling: credit freezes as circulatory blockages and interest rates as primary regulators of metabolic tempo. Policies such as quantitative easing address volume constraints but cannot resolve structural blockages, explaining their limited long-run effectiveness.

Monetary velocity is identified as the central diagnostic variable. Declines in velocity arise from three distinct mechanisms—circulatory blockage, receptor failure, and structural deceleration—each requiring different policy responses. Uniform monetary expansion across these conditions underlies the diminished effectiveness of post-2008 policy interventions.

Monetary expansion generates waste through two structural pathways and a reinforcing feedback loop: excess liquidity flows into asset markets, producing asset inflation, while prolonged low rates stimulate unsustainable capacity expansion. These processes interact through collateral amplification, progressively degrading financial structures. Inflation is reinterpreted as price-signal dilution, functioning as gradual adjustment at moderate levels but eroding informational efficiency when excessive.

A three-dimensional policy framework is proposed: velocity-based diagnosis, monitoring of waste accumulation, and control of monetary flow direction. Leading indicators shift from aggregate quantities to structural signals such as asset-price deviation and credit quality deterioration. The chapter concludes by examining digital currencies as alternative monetary architectures, highlighting their implications for circulation efficiency, regulatory capacity, and global monetary control.

title: Tradwife as Systemic Variable: Conversion Dynamics and Non-Linear Effects in Labor-Constrained Socio-Economic Systems

detail.title: Tradwife as Systemic Variable: Conversion Dynamics and Non-Linear Effects in Labor-Constrained Socio-Economic Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. The research was conducted independently and without external influence from institutions, organizations, or commercial entities.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, personal data, or experimental interventions. Ethical approval was therefore not required
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted as part of the author’s independent research activities.

detail.abstract:
The “tradwife” phenomenon has emerged as a digitally mediated re-articulation of traditional gender roles. Existing scholarship has predominantly examined its cultural, aesthetic, and ideological dimensions. This paper addresses a structural blind spot in current policy and analytical frameworks: cultural patterns are typically treated as symbolic phenomena, while their system-level effects remain insufficiently modeled.

Low-prevalence cultural patterns are typically treated as analytically negligible. This paper challenges that assumption. It argues that under conditions of structural constraint, even marginal behavioral shifts may produce disproportionate system effects.

The “tradwife” phenomenon, widely discussed as a digitally mediated re-articulation of traditional gender roles, is examined here not as a cultural trend, but as a potential systemic variable. Existing scholarship has focused on its aesthetic, ideological, and discursive dimensions, while largely neglecting its interaction with labor markets, demographic pressure, and fiscal systems.

The paper develops a scenario-based analytical framework that introduces conversion dynamics, distinguishing between expressed attitudes and actual behavior. Rather than modeling full labor market exit, the analysis focuses on gradual adjustments, including reduced working hours, part-time transitions, and extended interruptions. It further integrates social reproduction as a parallel system domain, capturing the redistribution of resources between market-based production and household-based coordination.

The central finding is a structural asymmetry: when coupled with labor-constrained environments, even low-prevalence behavioral patterns may generate non-linear system effects. Systemic relevance emerges not from scale alone, but from interaction with existing constraints, amplification mechanisms, and cross-domain trade-offs.

The paper reframes the tradwife phenomenon as a contingent systemic variable within socio-economic systems. It is conceptual and deliberately not empirically calibrated; scenario outputs should be interpreted as analytical stress tests rather than empirical projections.

title: Bills of Exchange in a Supply Chain
affiliations: University of Essex - Department of Economics and CMU Tepper School of Business

detail.title: Bills of Exchange in a Supply Chain
detail.abstract: We study a trade credit chain in which firms finance input purchases by issuing IOUs that circulate as settlement instruments and as collateral. Even when IOU holdings are perfectly diversified against idiosyncratic default risks, limited commitment induces endogenous default by downstream firms and makes the collateral value of receivables depend on downstream firms' incentives to default on their own payables. This valuation channel propagates shocks upstream by tightening collateral constraints, and downstream by depressing trade-credit supply when default diverts pledged receivables to creditors. The resulting distortions in input use and strategic complementarity in default incentives constitute a pecuniary externality operating through IOU prices-requiring no resource destruction or bankruptcy costs-yet producing systematic misallocation. We characterize how cross-sector heterogeneity shapes over-and under-investment patterns. Self-consistent beliefs about default can generate multiple equilibria, implying fragility to coordination failures. In a line network, a small local productivity shock can trigger default contagion and discontinuous drops in investment. In a general production network, financial frictions interact with input-output linkages to produce non-monotone output patterns and a structured matrix of input-use wedges. We also study policy interventions that shift default costs and thereby coordinate failure-state repayment incentives. Among efficiency-implementing default profiles, the least-cost intervention maximizes default probabilities.

title: THE IMPACT OF REMITTANCES ON ECONOMIC GROWTH AND REDUCTION OF POVERTY IN EMERGING MARKET
affiliations: University for Business and Technology (UBT), University for Business and Technology (UBT) and University for Business and Technology (UBT)

detail.title: THE IMPACT OF REMITTANCES ON ECONOMIC GROWTH AND REDUCTION OF POVERTY IN EMERGING MARKET
detail.abstract:
The role of remittances is considered to be extremely important as an external source of financing for many countries, especially for those facing slow economic development and high unemployment rates. Therefore, the aim of this study is to analyze the impact of remittances on economic growth and poverty reduction in the developing market, with a specific focus on Kosovo as the case study. To examine the hypotheses, this paper utilizes a comparative analysis method for the period from 2008 to 2022. The study’s results indicate that remittances have had a significant and important influence on economic growth. Furthermore, the findings demonstrate that remittances have contributed to the improvement of well-being and living standards for the people of Kosovo. At the same time, remittances have been a strong foundation for the recipient economies, significantly reducing the risk of poverty. Additionally, the study results show that remittances have positively influenced the maintenance of economic equilibrium between rural and urban, as well as regional areas. The fundamental objective of this research is to study and contribute further to this field, which has not been sufficiently covered for developing economies like Kosovo. 


How to cite this paper: Lubeniqi, G., Haziri, A., & Avdimetaj, K. (2023). The impact of remittances on economic growth and reduction of poverty in emerging market [Special issue].

title: Biases that influence venture capitalists. A ranking based on the bias occurrences and interactions.

detail.title: Biases that influence venture capitalists. A ranking based on the bias occurrences and interactions.
detail.abstract: Knowledge about the temporal occurrence of the various types of cognitive biases in the venture capital investment process and the interactions between these biases is scattered across numerous articles. In order to develop targeted debiasing measures, it is necessary to know when such a bias occurs and what interactions exist. In addition, ranking enables identifying which biases to address first during debiasing. We show for each of the 15 biases identified to date among venture capitalists: 1) in which stage of the investment process the bias occurs, 2) which interactions with other biases exist and 3) which biases are the most influential.

title: Unintended Inequality: A Pitfall of Electoral Systems Driven by Information Acquisition Costs
affiliations: Hitotsubashi University, University of Tokyo,  and Waseda University - School of Commerce

detail.title: Unintended Inequality: A Pitfall of Electoral Systems Driven by Information Acquisition Costs
detail.abstract: Using ward assembly elections in Tokyo's 23 special wards (2005-2023), we estimated how the listing order in Japan's Candidate Information Pamphlet-an officially issued voter guide-affects electoral outcomes. Listing positions are assigned by lottery, providing a natural experiment. Candidates on the front page are about 6 percentage points more likely to win than those on inner pages, and even within a page, placement significantly shifts vote shares. To account for strategic competition among candidates, we structurally estimated voting behavior using a Berry (1994) differentiated-products framework and simulated counterfactual elections in which all candidates are moved to inner pages. In every election, the set of winners changed; on average, 22.6 percentage of candidates experienced a different win-loss outcome. Thus, public media intended to equalize information among candidates can generate unintended inequality through ordering.

title: Path Signatures as Universal Feature Extractors for Limit Order Book Mid-Price Prediction

declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses publicly available financial market data (FI-2010 benchmark dataset) and proprietary tick data. No human subjects or personal data were involved.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was self-funded by the author's quantitative research division.

detail.abstract: We apply the path signature transform — a canonical lossless encoding of multidimensional time series rooted in Chen's theorem (1954) and Rough Path Theory (Lyons 1998) — to the joint trajectory of bid price, ask price, bid volume, and ask volume extracted from limit order book (LOB) data. Truncating the signature at order 4 yields a 341-dimensional feature vector that constitutes a sufficient statistic for predicting the next mid-price direction without any manual feature engineering. Evaluated on the FI-2010 benchmark dataset (NASDAQ, 10 stocks, 10 trading days, 10-level LOB) and on proprietary US equity tick data (2020–2024), the signature feature set outperforms standard hand-crafted LOB features (OBI, spread, VPIN, microprice) by 35–56% in terms of Information Coefficient (IC) at 100–500ms prediction horizons. We further demonstrate that the 5 most informative signature terms — cross-variation of bid price and bid volume, Lévy area between bid and ask price paths, and three third-order interaction terms — have direct microstructure interpretations, suggesting that the signature is not merely a black-box feature extractor but a structured decomposition of LOB information. GPU-accelerated computation via the Signatory library achieves full 341-feature extraction in under 0.8ms, making the approach compatible with live HFT deployment.

title: Resistance as Rational Evaluation: A Behavioral Mis-Specification

detail.title: Resistance as Rational Evaluation: A Behavioral Mis-Specification
detail.abstract: Despite decades of refinement, organizational change frameworks continue to misinterpret resistance as a behavioral or attitudinal failure rather than as rational evaluation under constraint. This paper interrogates the behavioral assumptions underlying this misdiagnosis. Grounded in Jensen and Meckling's Resourceful, Evaluative, Maximizing Model (REMM) as an economic baseline of agency, the analysis treats change as an illustrative domain rather than the object of theory construction. Resistance is not theorized as a focal behavioral outcome but as a derivative signal produced when continuous evaluative judgment is misread through visibility-dependent interpretations. Reliance on observable compliance as a proxy for alignment creates a systematic detection failure: under conditions of power asymmetry and risk, evaluation persists while its expression reconfigures into silence, surface compliance, or exit. This detection failure extends upward through the hierarchy: managers face rational incentives to suppress evaluative dissent, and repeated change cycles produce adverse selection-exiting high-acuity evaluators while retaining low-friction compliance. Change initiatives may therefore appear successful while systematically eroding learning, capability, and long-run performance.

title:
An analysis of relationships among GNH in corporation, psychological capital and employee performance.
Environment and Social Psychology, 2024, 9(4)
affiliations: Royal University of Bhutan, Faculty of Business Economics and Communications, Naresuan University, Thailand and Faculty of Business Economics and Communications, Naresuan University, Thailand

detail.title:
An analysis of relationships among GNH in corporation, psychological capital and employee performance.
Environment and Social Psychology, 2024, 9(4)
detail.abstract: This study analyses the relationships among "GNH in corporation", employees' psychological capital and employees' performance within the business corporations of Bhutan. Since no prior studies have been conducted to assess the connections among the variables of GNH in corporation (as independent variable), employee psychological capital (as mediator) and the employee performance (as dependent variable), the objective of the research was to bridge this knowledge gap. The data were collected from 511 full-time employees of Druk Holding and Investments Ltd (DHIL) and its six owned companies. The test result indicates that GNH in corporation determines both employees' psychological capital and employee performance. Most importantly, the employee psychological capital is found to fully mediate the influence of GNH in corporation on employee performance. This was ascertained based on mediation analysis using bootstrapping technique. The research framework was developed after synthesizing existing relevant theories and identifying appropriate procedures and methods; this research thus extends the current literature theoretically and methodologically. Also, the specific findings shall have practical implications, especially for managers and leaders of business corporations.

title: Topic: The Theory of Capital Preservation: A New Era Based on a Macroeconomic Algorithm (Benchmark). Author: Maksym Koresh Position: Independent Researcher & Project Architect Location:Kyiv, Ukraine

detail.title: Topic: The Theory of Capital Preservation: A New Era Based on a Macroeconomic Algorithm (Benchmark). Author: Maksym Koresh Position: Independent Researcher & Project Architect Location:Kyiv, Ukraine
detail.abstract: This paper presents the 'Theory of Capital Preservation'-a concept for the transition to a New Era economy based on an objective macroeconomic algorithm. The project proposes a shift from administrative financial management to mathematical self-regulation, which minimises the human factor and inflationary risks. The system is built on a dual-currency model, which ensures a balance between the stability and liquidity of assets. A key element of the algorithm is the introduction of the '365 coins per person' standard, which establishes a clear metrological link between the money supply, population size and GDP. The system's operation is clearly tied to a 365-day annual cycle, with 1 January designated as the synchronisation point and mandatory annual adjustment date. This approach transforms capital into a reliable store of value, synchronised with real economic indicators and time cycles. Global Trust is a concept of a new-generation digital asset backed by real economic assets. Instead of the gold standard, a standard based on human activity is proposed: a dual-currency system where the value of each unit is derived from the global economic output distributed across all of humanity.

title: The Receipts: The Untold and Underappreciated Outcomes of Biden’s Clean Energy Strategy

detail.title: The Receipts: The Untold and Underappreciated Outcomes of Biden’s Clean Energy Strategy

declarations.funderStatement: The Hans-Böckler Foundation

detail.abstract:
This paper combines original data analysis with in-depth interviews of more than a dozen private-sector actors to assess how Biden-era clean energy policy affected firm decision-making and workforce and community strategy. This quantitative and qualitative data illustrates the effects of statutory labor standards, tax incentives, and the DOE’s Community Benefits Plans with a focus on employment and wage data, apprenticeship expansion, and collective bargaining agreements.

On balance, the private sector was more receptive to Community Benefits Plan provisions than skeptics predicted.  The focus on labor and community benefits proved a less consequential source of friction than widely assumed, with funding recipients citing primarily the issues of a steep learning curve and lack of expertise. These results show that the efforts of the Biden administration to tie climate investments to good jobs and broadly shared prosperity showed promising signs of success, but faced an attribution problem; and that durable climate progress depends not only on capital investment but on organized constituencies capable of shaping and sustaining it.

title: Pension Politics in the 21s Century

detail.title: Pension Politics in the 21s Century
detail.abstract:
The possibility of examining the influence of governments and parties on pension policies has so far been limited by the dependent variable problem in comparative welfare state research in general, and by the lack of valid indicators for capturing pension policies in particular. This study presents a newly created comprehensive dataset on multidimensional pension reforms in 24 developed OECD countries in the period from 1980 to 2020. The pension reforms recorded are arranged according to a modified categorization scheme earlier developed by Silja Häusermann. The present data collection indicates a high incidence of pension reforms that strengthen both the funded and the redistributive nature of pension systems, but also reduce insurance benefits and privileged status rights of public-sector employees. Furthermore, the shortcomings of previous theoretical approaches to the empirical relationship between political actors and pension policies are criticized, in particular in the form of traditional partisan theory, as well as the previous neglect of the authoritarian-libertarian cleavage as a potential conflict structure also underlying and permeating contemporaneous pension politics. 

The influence of governments and parties on categorical pension reform regimes is then modeled and estimated. Results show that there is no consistent evidence lending support to detectable effects of party family variables or authoritarian and libertarian government positions on various dimensions of pension policy. However, there is robust evidence lending support to socioeconomically right and left governments influencing at least some dimensions of pension policy. The general assessment regularly expressed in recent studies in comparative welfare state research that government and party effects have completely disappeared can therefore not be followed on the basis of the present empirical findings.

This paper is based on the doctoral dissertation published at the University of Kassel.

title: Returns to Education and Labour Market Segmentation in India: Evidence from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (2019-20)

detail.title: Returns to Education and Labour Market Segmentation in India: Evidence from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (2019-20)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or non-financial interests related to this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is based on publicly available secondary data (PLFS 2023–24) and does not involve human subjects directly. Therefore, ethical approval was not required.

detail.abstract:
This study looks at what affects wage earnings in India, focusing on the impact of education
and the differences between formal and informal jobs. Education is crucial for human capital
and significantly influences job market results. According to human capital theory (Becker,
1964), investing in education improves productivity and leads to higher earnings. The Mincer
earnings function (Mincer, 1974) serves as a common model for estimating the returns to
education and is often used in research.
The study suggests that education positively impacts wage earnings and that returns to
education differ for formal and informal sector workers. Using micro-level data from the
Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2019 to 2020, the analysis explores these relationships
through the Mincer equation.
The dataset includes about 40,000 wage earners after cleaning and addressing missing values.
The analysis considers factors like years of education, job experience, gender, and type of
employment. Informal jobs are identified when there is no formal job contract.
The econometric models are estimated using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS). The results
show that education positively affects wages. An additional year of education raises wages by
roughly 10 percent for formal sector workers. However, returns to education are lower for
informal workers, with an estimated return of around 7 percent.
These findings align with global data on returns to education (Psacharopoulos and Patrinos,
2018) and highlight how job market segmentation affects wage outcomes. This study adds to
the literature by showing how the returns to education vary across different job types, using
recent representative national data.
The results indicate that although education is an essential factor for earnings, job market
structures impact how well educational investments convert into higher wages. Therefore,
policies aimed at encouraging formal employment and improving job market conditions may
be necessary to fully unlock the benefits of investing in human capital.

title: The New Old SEC
affiliations: Case Western Reserve University School of Law

detail.title: The New Old SEC
detail.abstract:
The administrative state is under attack, and the U.S. Securities Exchange Commission (“SEC”) is no exception. Through executive orders, the Trump Administration has called into question the independence and staffing of the SEC, and the Supreme Court has issued opinions that have eroded the agency’s authority and power, including eliminating Chevron deference, which was viewed by many as a cornerstone of administrative law.  

This Article explores the scope of the SEC’s authority and the mandates for it to act by examining two of the potentially broadest grants of power that appear ubiquitously within federal securities law, i.e., the terms “for the protection of investors” and “in the public interest.” Although the assertion has been made that these terms provide broad power to engage in social engineering—including regarding the initially proposed version of the SEC’s climate disclosure rule—a textual analysis of these terms demonstrates that their meaning is much narrower. Such an analysis shows that “for the protection of investors” means providing investors with the truthful material information necessary to make informed investment decisions, and the term “in the public interest” is focused on the protection of securities markets through the creation of efficient markets and the prevention of market failures.  

This Article contributes to the existing scholarship in four main ways.  First, this Article provides the first focused academic piece on the meaning of the terms “for the protection of investors” and “in the public interest” within the field of federal securities law. Second, this Article provides the first academic study of how those terms ought to be understood textually in a post-Chevron world and considering the Roberts Court’s aversion to administrative deference generally. Third, this Article offers the first exploration of the mandates that the SEC has under the federal securities law to act “for the protection of investors” and “in the public” that will be complicated by the Trump Administration’s dramatic reshaping and downsizing of the federal government. Fourth, this Article provides the first examination of how a textualist analysis of the terms “for the protection of investors” and “in the public interest” impacts expansive efforts by the SEC, such as the recent proposed climate disclosure rule. The SEC must understand its role. The discussion contained in this Article helps to clarify it.

title:
Forced Displacement in Gaza: A Comprehensive Legal Analysis

detail.title:
Forced Displacement in Gaza: A Comprehensive Legal Analysis
 التهجير القسري في غزة: تحليل قانوني شامل
detail.abstract: This article examines the forced displacement of civilians in the Gaza Strip within the context of armed conflict, through a legal analysis grounded in international humanitarian law, international human rights law, and international criminal law. It highlights the prohibition of forced transfer under the Fourth Geneva Convention of 1949 and analyzes the legal implications of large-scale evacuation orders affecting hundreds of thousands of civilians. The study underscores the severe violations of fundamental rights, including the rights to housing, life, and personal security. It further addresses both individual criminal responsibility and state responsibility arising from such acts. The article concludes that these practices may constitute war crimes and crimes against humanity and may also meet the legal elements of genocide under relevant international legal standards.

detail.abstract: Cryptocurrency is a digital financial asset that has gained firm traction in recent years. Since the global financial crisis period, traditional safe-haven investments have lost their defensive effectiveness. Many consider cryptocurrency to be an adequate safe-haven, despite its risk perception and volatility. Through an econometric analysis involving OLS regressions and a DCC-GARCH model, the study examines correlations between two cryptocurrencies (Bitcoin and Ether), safe-haven assets (gold, USD) and stock market indices (S&P500 and select sectors). The study utilizes daily financial data at market close from 01 January 2021 to 31 December 2022. The empirical properties of Bitcoin and Ether indicate there are negative correlations with safe-haven assets and a positive correlation to the S&P500, denoting that Bitcoin and Ether do not maintain the statistical hallmarks of established safe-havens or hedges.

title: Scheduled Macroeconomic Release impact on SPY and QQQ Intraday Volatility

detail.title: Scheduled Macroeconomic Release impact on SPY and QQQ Intraday Volatility
detail.abstract: Macroeconomic announcements generate information shocks that cause investors to revise expectations and adjust positions, yet the short-term magnitude of these reactions is not well understood. This study employs an event study framework to measure realized volatility in 5-minute intraday bars for SPY and QQQ across 630 scheduled macroeconomic announcements from January 2020 to December 2025, including CPI releases, FOMC rate decisions, GDP estimates, nonfarm payroll reports, and retail sales figures. Paired t-tests confirm that post-event realized volatility increases significantly across all windows and both indices, with SPY exhibiting a 2.5-fold increase and QQQ a 2.5-fold increase in the 30-minute post-event window relative to pre-event levels (t = 16.36 and t = 18.72 respectively, p < 0.0001). Inflation releases produced the largest volatility response, with a 3.616-fold increase in SPY and 4.068-fold increase in QQQ. To address a second research question, categorical and temporal event features are used to predict post-event realized volatility magnitude using Ridge regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting models evaluated via 5-fold cross-validation. The Gradient Boosting model achieved the strongest performance with R² of 0.3059 for SPY and 0.2895 for QQQ, with temporal features ranking as the most predictive, suggesting that the prevailing macroeconomic regime influences volatility magnitude as much as announcement type. These findings indicate that scheduled macroeconomic releases produce measurable and predictable short-term volatility responses in equity index ETFs.

title: Gender Inequality and Labor Market Outcomes in South Asia: A Comparative Data-Driven Analysis of Pakistan, India, and Bangladesh (1990–2022)

detail.title: Gender Inequality and Labor Market Outcomes in South Asia: A Comparative Data-Driven Analysis of Pakistan, India, and Bangladesh (1990–2022)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts of interest to declare. This research was conducted independently as part of the author's graduate studies at the University of Hartford.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses exclusively secondary, publicly available data from the World Bank Open Data and International Labour Organization (ILO) databases. No human participants were involved and no ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by the Dorothy Goodwin Project Grant, awarded by the University of Hartford's Women's Advancement Initiative under the President's Office.

detail.abstract: Gender inequality remains a critical constraint on inclusive economic development in South Asia, shaping labour market participation, employment structures, and income distribution. While prior literature has explored this relationship across large, economically diverse emerging markets, comparative analysis focused specifically on South Asia's lower-middle income economies remains limited. This study addresses that gap through a data-driven comparative analysis of Pakistan, India, and Bangladesh over the period 1990–2022. Using secondary data from the World Bank and International Labour Organization (ILO), the study examines five key dimensions of gender inequality: female labour force participation, wage and salaried employment, unemployment rates, educational attainment, and income share distribution. Employing OLS regression, correlation analysis, and longitudinal trend evaluation, the research identifies structural differences and evolving patterns across the three countries. The findings reveal that higher female labour force participation and greater access to education are consistently associated with more equitable economic outcomes. In contrast, persistent gender disparities contribute to labour market inefficiencies and unequal income distribution. Among the three countries, Bangladesh demonstrates the most consistent progress in integrating women into the formal workforce, while Pakistan and India exhibit slower and more volatile improvement due to structural, institutional, and socio-cultural constraints. This study contributes to the literature by disaggregating gender inequality into specific labour market dimensions, applying a multi-method quantitative framework to a predominantly qualitative research area, and providing a focused intra-regional perspective on South Asia. The findings offer policy-relevant insights for strengthening labour market inclusion and reducing economic disparities in developing economies.

title: LLM Measurement of Open-Ended Reasoning
affiliations: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign - Department of Economics, The University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) - Center for Forecasting Science and University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign - Department of Economics

detail.title: LLM Measurement of Open-Ended Reasoning
detail.abstract: We propose a new framework for measuring open-ended reasoning using large language models (LLMs), consisting of four stages: embedding and clustering, LLM assisted category definition, probabilistic scoring of category membership, and validation against human-coded benchmarks. We demonstrate the validity and usefulness of the framework through human survey responses and LLM-generated reasoning. We first validate the framework and show a naïve LLM fails to deliver stable and interpretable categories. We then demonstrate that continuous probability measures capture economically meaningful information that binary classification misses, including subjective uncertainty and cross-category structure. Finally, we apply the framework to LLM-generated reasoning to study variation across question formats, when reasoning data are no longer a binding constraint. In this application, the framework recovers both similarities and economically meaningful differences in reasoning across question formats.

title: Rogue AI Agents Won't Be Testifying-You Will: Agentic AI, IP and Liability Risks, and a Path Forward
affiliations: , Venable LLP and University of New Hampshire School of Law (formerly Franklin Pierce Law Center)

detail.title: Rogue AI Agents Won't Be Testifying-You Will: Agentic AI, IP and Liability Risks, and a Path Forward
detail.abstract: As enterprises deploy agentic AI systems capable of autonomous action across internal and external platforms, traditional legal assumptions about agency, authority, assent, and accountability are being tested in new ways. This article examines how agentic AI creates heightened intellectual property, contract, and liability exposure when autonomous systems act beyond intended bounds, interact with restricted systems, accept terms, access protected data, or make external representations on behalf of an organization. It argues that although AI agents are not legal actors in the conventional sense, their conduct may still be attributed to the deploying enterprise under established doctrines such as apparent authority, ratification, negligence, and product liability. The analysis identifies four core risk domains: inbound IP and data acquisition risk, loss or impairment of enterprise IP assets, external-facing liability risk, and systemic control risk. It further explains how agentic AI amplifies these exposures by operating at scale, generating persistent logs, and preserving discoverable evidence of decision pathways, prompts, access patterns, and outputs. The article contends that the central governance challenge is not whether rogue AI agents can create legal consequences, but whether organizations understand where AI-driven conduct already binds them. It concludes that effective risk mitigation requires embedding legal constraints directly into system architecture through policy-as-code, least-privilege access controls, monitoring, auditability, human oversight, and lifecycle governance. For companies operating in IP-intensive and regulated environments, agentic AI governance must be treated not as a technical afterthought but as a core component of legal strategy, compliance design, and go-to-market planning.

detail.abstract: Leveraged buyouts (LBOs) have generated some of the highest reported returns in private markets over the past three decades, traditionally relying on three value-creation levers: financial leverage, multiple expansion, and operational improvement. The rapid rise in benchmark interest rates between 2022 and 2024 meaningfully altered the economics of the LBO model, raising the cost of acquisition debt, compressing coverage ratios, and shifting the balance of return drivers. This paper examines how U.S. large-cap LBO deal structures evolved from 2019 through 2024 using a simplified five-year LBO model calibrated to publicly reported industry data. The model compares a representative 2019 deal (12.0x entry multiple, 6.0x debt/EBITDA, 6% blended interest) with a representative 2024 deal (11.5x entry multiple, 4.5x debt/EBITDA, 10% blended interest). Holding operating performance constant, estimated sponsor internal rate of return (IRR) falls by approximately 230 basis points, from 13.1% to 10.8%. Contrary to the prevailing narrative that rising interest rates are the principal cause of compressed buyout returns, decomposition analysis shows that the tightening of lender-imposed leverage multiples accounts for roughly 65% of the IRR decline (-152 bp), while higher interest costs account for just 50% (-116 bp); the remainder is offset by a small positive contribution from lower entry multiples. A second finding is that a single turn of exit-multiple expansion is worth roughly as much as three additional percentage points of annual EBITDA growth, underscoring how sensitive sponsor returns remain to market conditions at exit. The paper concludes with specific implications for sponsor strategy, including longer hold periods,

title:
Um Modelo de Capitalização Soberana para Sustentabilidade Previdenciária:
Um Framework OLG com Crescimento Endógeno, Expansão do Crédito e Capital Humano para o Brasil
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Federal University of Mato Grosso do Sul (UFMS/CPNA)

detail.title:
Um Modelo de Capitalização Soberana para Sustentabilidade Previdenciária:
Um Framework OLG com Crescimento Endógeno, Expansão do Crédito e Capital Humano para o Brasil
detail.abstract:
Resumo

Este artigo propõe um arcabouço integrado para a reforma previdenciária baseado na capitalização pública soberana, concebido para complementar regimes de repartição e, simultaneamente, ampliar o crescimento econômico de longo prazo. O modelo introduz um fundo soberano que acumula ativos a partir de contribuições previdenciárias e receitas institucionais, convertendo-os em capital produtivo e retornos financeiros. Para avaliar seus efeitos macroeconômicos, desenvolve-se um modelo estrutural de gerações sobrepostas (OLG) com produtividade endógena, expansão do crédito e acumulação de capital humano.

Diferentemente das abordagens tradicionais, que tratam a sustentabilidade previdenciária como um problema essencialmente fiscal, o modelo proposto estabelece uma ligação explícita entre o desenho previdenciário, o investimento, o desenvolvimento financeiro e a dinâmica da produtividade. O modelo identifica quatro canais principais de transmissão: aumento da poupança agregada, acumulação de capital, expansão do crédito produtivo e ganhos de produtividade endógena. Os resultados das simulações indicam que a capitalização soberana pode elevar a taxa de crescimento de longo prazo entre 0,4 e 0,9 ponto percentual ao ano, dependendo da intensidade da política, ao mesmo tempo em que reduz a pressão estrutural sobre as transferências intergeracionais.

A análise também evidencia a existência de limiares críticos de política, abaixo dos quais a reforma gera custos de transição sem produzir ganhos significativos no longo prazo. Esses resultados sugerem que a eficácia da capitalização soberana depende não apenas de seu desenho institucional, mas também de sua escala, qualidade de governança e integração com políticas de desenvolvimento. De forma geral, o artigo contribui para a literatura ao integrar desenho institucional e dinâmica macroeconômica na análise de reformas previdenciárias.

title: BioDAO: Biological Decentralized Autonomous Organizations Using Wetware Computing for Collective Governance

detail.title: BioDAO: Biological Decentralized Autonomous Organizations Using Wetware Computing for Collective Governance
detail.abstract: This paper proposes BioDAO (Biological Decentralized Autonomous Organization), a novel governance framework that integrates quantum biological computing, wetware systems, and blockchain technology to address fundamental limitations in collective decision-making. Traditional institutions face challenges including information asymmetry, principal-agent problems, and coordination failures. BioDAOs leverage photosynthetic bacteria for quantum coherent energy transfer, neural organoids for adaptive learning, and mycelial networks for distributed sensing to create governance systems that operate at biological timescales with unprecedented efficiency. We present a technical architecture combining biological computing substrates with cryptographic consensus mechanisms, demonstrating potential applications in climate governance, resource allocation, and collective action problems. Comparative analysis shows BioDAOs could reduce decision latency by 99.9% while consuming 0.001% of the energy required by traditional institutions. This work bridges synthetic biology, distributed systems, and institutional economics to propose a fundamentally new approach to organizing collective human activity.

detail.abstract: The significance of a crucial WTO accession agreement component, that is, Trade Related Investment Measures (TRIMs) agreement in increasing Sub-Saharan African developing country’s appeal for investors from abroad is assessed over here. Conventional FDI location determinants like macroeconomic stability, market size, infrastructure, trade openness and economic development are also considered. Utilising yearly data for 38 Sub-Saharan developing nations over the time period from 1988 to 2015 in a panel form, the researcher found that removal of market distortions through TRIMs, sound macroeconomic management, infrastructure availability, liberalisation of investment and trade regime have plausible significant effects on FDI inflows. Contrary to the empirical FDI literature economic development is found to be insignificant and market size sensitive to the addition of explanatory variables, especially, WTO led TRIMs. Time invariant features such as language, geographical location and sea access cannot be evaluated as fixed effect panel estimation technique does not support them.
