detail.abstract: The emergence of financial robo-advisors has completely altered how individuals manage and invest their funds. Given the increasing impact of AI on the financial technology industry, this paper seeks to provide a research approach that might shed light on the adoption of financial roboadvisors. This paper aims to investigate individuals' willingness to adopt financial robo-advisors using UTAUT from potential individuals' perspectives. It analyzes the factors that impact them to adopt robo-advisors which include Financial Literacy, Social Influence, Facilitating Conditions, and Perceived usefulness. Data was collected from an online survey of 220 Mirpur AJK division individuals and analyzed by SMART-PLS statistical software. According to the study, three main factors impact people's willingness to adopt financial robo-advisors: social influence, facilitating conditions, and perceived usefulness. However, financial literacy was found to be insignificant and did not impact the adoption of financial robo-advisors. Key recommendations include leveraging social influence, improving facilitating conditions, and emphasizing perceived usefulness to encourage adoption. Future studies should look at broader geographic areas, greater sample sizes, and more technology acceptance theories. Limitations include a small sample size and a regional focus. This study provides significant insights for developers, marketers, MUST Business School 2 researchers, and policymakers to encourage the adoption of robo-advisors, hence promoting financial inclusion and innovation.

title: Crypto Airdrop Pricing
affiliations: Tongji University - School of Economics and Management

detail.title: Crypto Airdrop Pricing
detail.abstract: This paper develops a valuation framework for option-like claims on cryptocurrency airdrops. Standard option-pricing models are not designed for this setting because the payoff to an airdroplinked claim depends not only on token price risk, but also on qualification uncertainty, walletlevel allocation uncertainty, vesting constraints, and event-driven dilution. I model an airdroplinked claim as a compound contingent claim whose terminal payoff is the maximum of a strikeadjusted product of four primitives: an eligibility indicator, the token allocation, the tradable share of that allocation, and the post-event token price. The paper embeds these institutional features in a reduced-form continuous-time environment under a pricing measure. Token prices follow a jump-diffusion process with stochastic volatility, while the airdrop event may induce a separate dilution shock at the distribution date. Eligibility is modeled as a Bernoulli random variable with a conditional qualification probability, allocation follows either a continuous or tiered distribution, and vesting is summarized by a tradable-share process. The general claim value is therefore the discounted expectation of a nonlinear payoff that jointly integrates market risk and project-design risk. The paper contributes in three ways. First, it provides a tractable theory of airdrop-linked valuation that nests points-based qualification, variable token allocations, and lock-up schedules. Second, it shows that the most relevant comparative statics in airdrop markets concern eligibility, allocation, tradability, and dilution rather than only standard delta or vega. Third, it develops a calibration and robustness exercise built around the Hyperliquid genesis distribution. Using public information on the points program, token supply, launch valuation, and recipient scale, I show how the framework can be operationalized with strike grids, maturity grids, and eventdilution scenarios. The results indicate that airdrop-linked claim values are highly nonlinear in expected allocation and are materially compressed by dilution and vesting frictions. The 1 framework therefore offers both a theoretical benchmark and a practical template for empirical work on token distributions, platform finance, and airdrop markets.

title: Antitrust Enforcement and Product Market Dynamics: Evidence from U.S. Government Procurement
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, HEC Montreal, and Fordham University

detail.title: Antitrust Enforcement and Product Market Dynamics: Evidence from U.S. Government Procurement
detail.abstract: We examine how antitrust enforcement shapes product market dynamics using U.S. government procurement as laboratory. Leveraging large language models to identify DOJ procurement cases, we document a trade-off between broader market participation and procurement performance. Non-defendant contractors, particularly small, women-, and minority-owned businesses, gain market share as antitrust enforcement dismantles the structural barriers erected by anti-competitive conduct. However, enforcement also impairs procurement performance in affected markets, an effect concentrated among new and inexperienced contractors and complex projects, but largely absent in simpler procurements. Our findings provide new insights into how antitrust enforcement influences diverse stakeholder groups in complex product markets.

title: The Impact of Visual and Olfactory Sensory Experiences on Brand Image and

detail.title: The Impact of Visual and Olfactory Sensory Experiences on Brand Image and
detail.abstract: The paper discusses the concept of sensory marketing in the luxury hospitality sector with a particular focus on the role of visual and olfactory eperiecnes in influencing the behavioural intentions of the guests. Based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-OR) framework, the study establishes brand image as the most significant internal state based on which the environmental stimuli and word-of-mouth (WOM) are connected. The study used a quantitative research design, which entailed the gathering of 253 valid survey results of people who had stayed in a five-star luxury hotel in the last twelve months. The analysis of data through Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) has shown that visual aesthetics and ambient scents have a statistically significant positive effect on the perceived brand image of a hotel. It is also worth mentioning that the findings indicate that the predictive ability of brand image of olfactory stimuli is higher compared to that of visual stimuli, which proves the powerful influence of scent as a subconscious and strong variable on the internal image of brand quality by a guest. Moreover, the research proves the pivotal position of brand image as a mediator and shows that the sensory cues do not instigate WOM, but rather operate by creating a strong psychological impression that encourages guests to give recommendations. These findings imply that the luxury hotel managers must consider multisensory design, especially creating special signature scents, as a strategic brand-building outlay, but not aesthetic expenditure to generate organic referrals.

title: Role of Humans in the Protection of the Environment: An Analysis in the Light of the Quran
affiliations: Bahria University Karachi Campus and National University of Modern Languages (NUML)

detail.title: Role of Humans in the Protection of the Environment: An Analysis in the Light of the Quran
detail.abstract: This research explores the Quranic perspective on environmental protection by delving into key Quranic principles. Quran as the primary source of Islam provides fundamental teachings in every walk of life, emphasizing the status of God (Allah) as Creator of essential substance and sustainer of the universe and on the other hand, describes the role of humans as khalifa or guardians of the creation on Earth. the Quran highlights the significance of balance, and prevention of ISAF, by keeping the principle of justice, and accountability in each and every action. The concept of water as a fundamental element for life, linked with the encouragement to reflect on the signs of nature, provides a foundation for responsible environmental behavior. Drawing on verses from the Quran, this research outlines a framework for understanding the ethical and sustainable responsibilities of individuals as custodians of the environment in accordance with Quranic teachings.

title: Patents and Pay: The wage premium and workforce transformation after a firm's first patent
affiliations: and Government of the Commonwealth of Australia - IP Australia

detail.title: Patents and Pay: The wage premium and workforce transformation after a firm's first patent
detail.abstract: Wages help shape the incentives for individuals to engage in the innovation process. Prior research has shown that within businesses, patent grants can cause substantial increases in firm productivity that are passed through into higher wages. Beyond this, there is mixed evidence on how the returns to innovation are shared between employees of different skills and occupations. Some studies find that the largest wage premium to working in innovative firms accrues to inventors and top earning employees (Kline et al., 2020) while others find the largest premium accrues to employees in medium and low skill level occupations (e.g., Aghion et al., 2018). Separately, recent studies have highlighted declining economic dynamism, observed across many advanced economies, including reduced job switching rates and reduced competition for labour among established firms (Hambur, 2023). Labour mobility and positive assortative matching between workers and firms is critical to the innovation performance of organisations. To date, evidence is mixed as to the factors that influence dynamism and matching in inventor markets including the potential role of patents (e.g., Bhaskarabhatla et al., 2020; Melero et al., 2019). This study uses linked employer-employee data covering 14.5 million Australians and their employers from 2010 to 2019 to investigate sources of heterogeneity in the innovation wage response and labour dynamics around patenting firms. The research finds a significant wage premium to working in an innovative business, as indicated by its ownership of patents, which varies systematically across firms of different size and, within firm size categories, across occupational skill levels. We find evidence also of a systematic link between patenting and labour mobility, with significant workforce change in lower-skill-level occupations after the grant, consistent with the firm preparing for commercialisation. The results are consistent with research that emphasises the role of complementary and firm-specific human capital in innovation and wage responses to patenting (e.g., Melero et al., 2019; Bhaskarabhatla et al., 2020).

title: Choke Points, Concentration, and Systemic Fragility: Theory, Evidence, and Policy Implications for Critical Minerals, Semiconductors, and Healthcare in an Age of Hyperglobalization

detail.title: Choke Points, Concentration, and Systemic Fragility: Theory, Evidence, and Policy Implications for Critical Minerals, Semiconductors, and Healthcare in an Age of Hyperglobalization
detail.abstract: Forty years of hyperglobalization have seeded choke points everywhere—from the Strait of Hormuz to Taiwan’s silicon fabs. Paul Krugman identifies the symptom; Nobel Lau reate Michael Spence identifies the cause: decentralized markets systematically under invest in resilience because its benefits, unlike those of efficiency, are non-appropriable network-wide public goods. We formalize both diagnoses. Modeling choke points as two-stage Leontief production networks, we show that processing-stage concentration— measured by the Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (HHI)—amplifies supply shocks into out sized price volatility. Drawing on Samuelson’s (1952) spatial price equilibrium frame work, we introduce the concept of incomparative advantages: developing countries hold comparative advantage in Stage 1 extraction while a single dominant nation (notably China) holds comparative advantage in Stage 2 processing, creating structural con centration that vertical integration could partially dissolve. Panel data for cobalt, lithium, and copper yield an instrumental-variables estimate of ˆβ = 0.612, confirm ing that processing-stage HHI causally raises price volatility. We extend the analysis to semiconductors, healthcare, financial infrastructure (SWIFT), and energy, ranking twelve global choke points by severity and likely disruption duration. Policy must choose among onshoring, international cooperation, and hybrid strategies—with coop eration cheaper but harder. Artificial intelligence amplifies near-term concentration risk while offering long-run resilience dividends through materials substitution and process acceleration.

title: Impact of Digital Tools and Applications on the Research Productivity of Arabic and Islamic Studies Students in Pakistan
affiliations: Bahria University Karachi Campus, , National University of Modern Languages (NUML) and National University of Modern Languages (NUML)

detail.title: Impact of Digital Tools and Applications on the Research Productivity of Arabic and Islamic Studies Students in Pakistan

keywords: Research in Arabic and Islamic Studies

detail.abstract: The growing influence of digital technologies has reshaped the nature of academic research, offering new opportunities for improving efficiency, accessibility, and innovation. However, within the field of Arabic and Islamic Studies in Pakistan, the adoption and effective use of digital tools remain underexplored. The limited integration of technology in religious academia often restricts students to traditional, manual research methods, which can impede productivity and quality. This study aims to evaluate the impact of digital tools and applications on the research productivity of Arabic and Islamic Studies students in Pakistan, focusing on awareness, usage patterns, institutional access, and perceived effectiveness. A descriptive quantitative research design was employed, utilizing a structured questionnaire distributed among 252 students from public and private universities. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics to identify usage frequency, tool preference, and perceived outcomes. Results revealed that over 90% of respondents were aware of digital research tools, with Islam360 (88%) and Maktaba Shamela (82%) being the most widely used applications. A majority of students reported improved research quality (74%) and productivity (56%) due to the use of digital tools. Nevertheless, challenges such as inadequate training, limited institutional support, and unequal digital access persist. The study concludes that digital tools have significantly enhanced the efficiency, accuracy, and scholarly depth of Arabic and Islamic research in Pakistan. Strengthening institutional support and digital literacy programs could further advance research productivity and innovation within the discipline.

title: ChatGPT as a Time Capsule: The Limits of Price Discovery
affiliations: and University of Florida - Department of Finance, Insurance and Real Estate

detail.title: ChatGPT as a Time Capsule: The Limits of Price Discovery
detail.abstract: Frozen large language model (LLM) checkpoints extract information from pre-cutoff public text that is associated with future fundamentals and equity returns beyond standard contemporaneous valuation measures. Because each frozen checkpoint has a fixed knowledge cutoff, it can be interpreted as a compressed representation of publicly available textual information at a given point in time. We treat twelve OpenAI snapshots spanning 2021-2025 as time-stamped summaries of the public textual record and extract a sector-neutral LLM outlook score for roughly 7,000 U.S. equities per cross-section. The outlook score is positively associated with analyst revisions, target-price changes and one-month cross-sectional returns in both Fama-MacBeth regressions and pooled panels with model fixed effects (t = 6.02), after direct controls for market-implied valuation and standard factors. Predictability broadly increases with the return horizon, despite a non-monotonic intermediate dip, and, in the pooled panel, is stronger for firms with high analyst coverage, consistent with the view that the bottleneck is not investor inattention but the cost of aggregating dispersed qualitative information across many documents.

detail.abstract: This research explores the use of human shields in modern warfare and its ramifications under international humanitarian law (IHL). Initially, it identifies explicit prohibitions against human shields, which are widely acknowledged in customary international law. The research then investigates the nuanced issue of how human shields affect the attacker's responsibilities under IHL, distinguishing between forced and voluntary shields. Forced shields maintain their civilian protections, while voluntary shields, as direct participants in hostilities, lose their immunity from attack. This distinction influences the application of proportionality and the requirement to take practicable precautions during attacks. The study posits that in ambiguous situations, shields should be treated as involuntary to maximize civilian protection. It further examines the broader context of this issue, particularly the interplay between human rights law and IHL in counter-terrorism efforts. This intersection often results in jurisdictional conflicts and inconsistencies in the protection of individuals, highlighting the ideological tensions between these legal paradigms. The paper underscores the strategic use of legal definitions and frameworks in political contexts, as seen in the "war on terror." It argues for a more integrated approach to IHL and human rights law to enhance civilian protection and uphold human dignity during conflicts. This requires the continuous adaptation of legal norms to address the evolving nature of warfare while maintaining the moral imperative of protecting human rights. Ultimately, the study calls for cautious and thoughtful application of these laws to avoid undermining their effectiveness and to ensure that legal protections are consistently applied, even in the face of complex and changing battlefield realities. This interplay is critically examined through the lens of cumulative convictions in international criminal law, highlighting tensions between war crimes and crimes against humanity. The research concludes with recommendations for clearer guidelines and cautious application of IHL principles to ensure the protection of civilians and the upholding of justice on the battlefield.

title: Compliance Moral Hazard and the Backfiring Mandate
affiliations: Virginia Tech - Pamplin College of Business, Virginia Tech and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Compliance Moral Hazard and the Backfiring Mandate
detail.abstract: Competing firms that serve shared customer populations face a fundamental information aggregation problem: each firm holds fragmented signals about risky customers, but individual incentives impede efficient collective detection. We develop a mechanism design framework for decentralized risk analytics, grounded in anti-money laundering in banking networks. Three strategic frictions distinguish our setting: compliance moral hazard, adversarial adaptation, and information destruction through intervention. A temporal value assignment (TVA) mechanism, which credits institutions using a strictly proper scoring rule on discounted verified outcomes, implements truthful reporting as a Bayes-Nash equilibrium (uniquely optimal at each edge) in large federations. Embedding TVA in a banking competition model, we show competitive pressure amplifies compliance moral hazard and poorly designed mandates can reduce welfare below autarky, a "backfiring" result with direct policy implications. In simulation using a synthetic AML benchmark, TVA achieves substantially higher welfare than autarky or mandated sharing without incentive design.

title: Who Sets Housing Prices? Evidence from External Demand and the Marginal Buyer

detail.title: Who Sets Housing Prices? Evidence from External Demand and the Marginal Buyer

detail.abstract:
This paper provides empirical evidence on how external demand affects housing price formation in spatially heterogeneous markets. Building on a marginal-buyer framework, it examines whether exposure to non-local demand weakens the relationship between housing prices and local income.

Using municipality-level panel data for the Balearic Islands over the period 2015–2023, the analysis estimates fixed-effects models that allow the price–income elasticity to vary with exposure to external demand. The results show that this relationship is not stable across space. While standard linear specifications fail to detect significant effects, threshold-based models reveal a clear non-linear pattern: the sensitivity of housing prices to local income declines sharply in high-exposure markets.

In particular, statistically significant effects emerge only in the upper tail of the exposure distribution, indicating a regime-dependent shift in the mechanism of price formation. In highly exposed municipalities, housing prices become substantially less responsive to local income, consistent with a marginal price-setting process driven by buyers whose willingness to pay is not locally anchored.

These findings contribute to the literature by providing direct empirical evidence that demand composition affects not only housing price levels but also the underlying mechanism through which prices are determined.

title: Informed Trading in Decentralized Prediction Markets: Microstructure Evidence from Polymarket

detail.title: Informed Trading in Decentralized Prediction Markets: Microstructure Evidence from Polymarket
detail.abstract: This study provides the first structural measurement of informed trading on Polymarket, a leading decentralized prediction market. Applying the Easley et al. (1996) PIN model to 36,596 marketday observations across 1,010 binary contracts, we document a mean Probability of Informed Trading of 0.222 substantially exceeding equity benchmarks. Market size exhibits a robust positive association with PIN (β = 0.0305, p < 0.001), reversing the traditional liquidity-adverse selection nexus. Order imbalance correlates strongly with PIN (ρ = 0.200), and prices drift systematically toward resolution (t = 7.55). These findings demonstrate the portability of structural information asymmetry models to quote-free decentralized venues and offer actionable insights for platform design and regulatory oversight of blockchain-native forecasting markets.

title: YACHAS V'EDUT: THE COVENANT AMERICA FORGOT, THE LINEAGE THE CONSTITUTION NAMED ‫ת‬ ‫דּו‬ ‫ֵע‬ ‫ּו‬ ‫ס‬ ‫ַח‬ ‫ַי‬

detail.title: YACHAS V'EDUT: THE COVENANT AMERICA FORGOT, THE LINEAGE THE CONSTITUTION NAMED ‫ת‬ ‫דּו‬ ‫ֵע‬ ‫ּו‬ ‫ס‬ ‫ַח‬ ‫ַי‬
detail.abstract: This Article argues that the Reconstruction Amendments created a Lineage-Based Constitutional Class (LBCC)-a juridically recognized descent group composed of the formerly enslaved and their identifiable descendants. Through a synthesis of constitutional text, historical practice, administrative law, and comparative covenantal jurisprudence, the Article demonstrates that LBCC constitutes a constitutionally grounded identity category that was later erased through administrative racialization without constitutional amendment. Restoring LBCC clarifies constitutional standing, corrects a century of doctrinal drift, and provides a legally coherent framework for lineage-based remedies.

title: The Ecosystem Model: A New Valuation Framework for Football Clubs

detail.title: The Ecosystem Model: A New Valuation Framework for Football Clubs
detail.abstract: Existing football club valuation methodologies, revenue multiples, the Markham Multivariate Model, sum-of-the-parts, and discounted cash flow, share a common structural limitation: they treat the club as a self-contained operating entity, systematically excluding value dimensions that exist outside its financial statements. This paper proposes the Urban Ecosystem Valuation (UEV) framework, a five-pillar model that decomposes club value into independently valued components: infrastructure and working capital (Value of Assets), urban real estate externalities (Value of District), player liquidation value via hedonic pricing (Value of Squad), institutional brand intangible via royalty relief (Value of Brand), and going-concern premium as an explicit residual (Value of Franchise). The framework produces two outputs from a single formula: an asset floor and an income-implied value, with enterprise value governed by whichever is greater. Applied to Manchester United and Olympique Lyonnais, the framework demonstrates materially different value decompositions: franchise-dominant for United (67% of EV) and assetanchored for Lyon (70% Value of Floor), where the franchise premium is compressed but positive. No existing methodology produces both outputs from a single formulation without structural modification.

title: Bond Market Making with a Hit-Ratio Target
affiliations: HSBC FX eRisk, Global Markets, HSBC Bank Plc., UK and

detail.title: Bond Market Making with a Hit-Ratio Target
detail.abstract: We study OTC bond market making on a size ladder with quadratic inventory penalty and a running target on the dealer's size-weighted hit ratio within a stochastic optimal control approach. We demonstrate that the corresponding reduced Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation remains separable by dualizing the hit ratio target term and provides the exact optimal controls through the inverse of the fill-probability function and the Hamiltonian derivative. We then focus on the quadratic approximation à la Bergault et al., which yields a Riccati equation for the inventory curvature while retaining the exact quote map. In its linearized form, this approximation produces explicit quote decompositions into riskless spread, inventory-risk correction, and hit-ratio correction. The formulation is general and applies to multi-bond, multi-client-tier scenarios, with special cases obtained by restricting the targeted tiers, their bond coverage, and their associated targets.

title: An International Plan for Sustainable Development
affiliations: CNRS, , TERI School of Advanced Studies, Tsinghua univeristy, University of Delhi - School of Economics and University of Oxford - Department of Economics

detail.title: An International Plan for Sustainable Development
detail.abstract: International cooperation on climate and taxation remains inadequate to deliver decarbonization, reduce poverty, and finance sustainable development at the required scale. We propose a Sustainable Union among willing countries, combining carbon pricing, new taxes on wealth, polluting fuels, financial transactions, and corporate income, with international revenue-sharing and conditional cooperation mechanisms. Most revenues would remain with participating governments for domestic spending, while a defined share would be pooled internationally. Specifically, participating countries would contribute 1% of gross national income (GNI) to a common pool redistributed in proportion to population, generating net transfers from richer to poorer countries. Meanwhile, the remainder of the revenue would increase domestic fiscal space by on average 2.2% of GNI. Although politically ambitious, such a framework might be credible, as governments are already advancing related forms of voluntary cooperation, and survey evidence indicates that it would be supported by majorities worldwide.

detail.abstract: Financial markets exhibit structurally distinct regimes characterized by heterogeneous volatility, momentum, and macroeconomic risk. Identifying these latent states is a prerequisite for robust quantitative strategies-particularly intraday momentum approaches where signal quality degrades sharply under crisis conditions. We present a reproducible regime detection pipeline for the S&P 500 ETF (SPY) over 1,270 daily observations, comprising a multi-source data acquisition layer, a curated three-variable feature set (R1, R2, V1 ′) selected for approximate Gaussianity and regime separability, and a multi-start Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (HMM) with penalized BIC order selection. We benchmark the HMM against a Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) hierarchical clustering algorithm on 21-trading-day rolling windows. Across 𝑘 ∈ {2, 3, 4, 5}, the raw BIC decreases monotonically; we select 𝑘 = 3 on economic grounds, mapping to the canonical Bull/Neutral/Bear taxonomy. The three-state HMM identifies a persistent low-volatility bull regime, a transitional neutral regime, and an episodic high-volatility bear regime consistent with known market stress events, with the Bear state exhibiting annualized volatility approximately 2.3× the Bull baseline. While DTW improves upon static K-Means via temporal smoothing, it fails to recover genuine risk topologies. The Markovian persistence of the HMM yields cleaner, more actionable regime boundaries, establishing it as a suitable conditioning layer for adaptive position sizing within our broader intraday momentum strategy.

title: The Performer's Right of Esports Players

detail.title: The Performer's Right of Esports Players
detail.abstract: This paper aims to justify that esports players should be entitled to have their own performer's right from the perspective of international law due to the internationalism of the development of esports. Three important conditions would be highlighted in advance of analyzing the legal definition of performer internationally. Subsequently, such definition would be elaborated in detail in three factors, encompassing the notion of "other persons", "literary or artistic works", and "perform". Finally, the issues of performance and fixation would be tackled and untangled to some extent, as those problems are tending to be used to argue against the rationality of granting performer's right to the players in esports. Thus, they deserve such rights especially concerning their weak position in the environment of esports to date.

title: The Hayek Project and the Limits of the Hayek Machine
affiliations: Kennesaw State University - Michael J. Coles College of Business

detail.title: The Hayek Project and the Limits of the Hayek Machine
detail.abstract: Friedrich Hayek's claim that the price system communicates dispersed knowledge has inspired a productive research program in computer science. Researchers have built Hayek Machines that use price-like signals to solve resource allocation and planning problems in multi-agent systems. This paper argues that such systems, while successful, capture only part of Hayek's project. The Hayek Machine coordinates agents within a given problem space; Hayek's deeper inquiry concerned how problem spaces themselves are constituted. Drawing on Hayek's neglected work in cognitive psychology, particularly The Sensory Order (1952), the paper distinguishes the Hayek Machine (a proven architecture for decentralized coordination) from the Hayek Project (a philosophical inquiry into the recursive co-evolution of minds and institutions). Hayek argued that perception is structured by evolved classificatory systems that differ across individuals, generating the dispersed knowledge that markets coordinate. Institutions shape these classifications even as individual actions reshape institutions. This dual recursion cannot be computationally replicated because it depends on embodied cognition, interpretive judgment, and consequence bearing. The paper concludes that artificial intelligence systems can optimize within inherited categories but cannot meaningfully create new categories, which has significant implications for algorithmic governance and institutional design.

title: Multivariate Economic Tail Risk and Scenario Analysis using the Survey of Professional Forecasters
affiliations: Heidelberg University - Alfred Weber Institute for Economics and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

detail.title: Multivariate Economic Tail Risk and Scenario Analysis using the Survey of Professional Forecasters
detail.abstract: This paper proposes forecasting joint tail risks for key macroeconomic indicators, GDP growth, inflation, and unemployment, using the US Survey of Professional Forecasters (SPF). By incorporating SPF consensus forecasts into the conditional mean of AR-GARCH-type models, the accuracy of univariate and multivariate predictive densities is significantly improved. Modeling a constant correlation matrix captures strong dependencies, particularly between GDP growth and unemployment. Using US data from 1990 to 2024, we show that the joint modeling framework enables scenario-based analysis in which predictive densities, conditioned on adverse developments in other variables, differ substantially from the baseline marginal distributions. The framework allows for a formal out-of-sample evaluation of joint predictive densities and a transparent assessment of conditional tail risks.

title: Respirer un air sain : une inégalité sociale Comment la pollution révèle-t-elle des inégalités de santé ?
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Université de Lomé

detail.title: Respirer un air sain : une inégalité sociale Comment la pollution révèle-t-elle des inégalités de santé ?
detail.abstract: Ce Policy Brief traite des inégalités socio-économiques de santé en lien avec la pollution de l'air, démontrant que l'exposition à celle-ci et les conséquences sanitaires que l'on peut associer sont socialement, économiquement et spatialement différenciées. A travers une analyse à différentes échelles, de l'international au local, il met en évidence des mécanismes économiques tels que la corrélation entre niveau de revenu et mortalité liée à la pollution ou encore le rôle clé de la ségrégation socio-spatiale. Afin d'enrichir ce document, une étude de cas sur la ville de Chongqing illustre les mécanismes et démontre la nécessité de déterminer des politiques publiques efficaces pour réduire la pollution sans négliger la question de la justice sociale.

title: An Automated Approach for Decision-Relevant Scenario Selection under Deep Uncertainty
affiliations: University of Jyväskylä and Iran University of Science and Technology

detail.title: An Automated Approach for Decision-Relevant Scenario Selection under Deep Uncertainty

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nothing.
declarations.funderStatement: This project is partly funded by the Research Council of Finland under grant number 360133. Part of this work was carried out while HR. Seiti was visiting the University of Jyvaskyla in the spring of 2025.

detail.abstract: Efficiently selecting a representative set of future scenarios that balances representativeness, cognitive load, computational efficiency, and tractability is vital, yet it remains challenging in both qualitative and quantitative scenario development methods. This study integrates the narrative clarity of the Intuitive Logics school, the strategic intent of the La Prospective (Prioritization) school, and the quantitative random exploration of Scenario Discovery methods to propose an automated, decision-relevant scenario selection approach for multi-criteria decision-making problems under deep uncertainty. The proposed approach comprises three stages: (1) classifying and prioritizing objectives based on strategic relevance, (2) clustering scenarios jointly in outcome and decision space to identify decision-relevant groupings, and (3) selecting representative scenarios from each cluster based on their contribution to the uncertainty envelope of high-priority objectives. This way, we achieve nearly the same 'vulnerability awareness' as an expert human, but at a fraction of the 'human-in-the-loop' cost, and far outperforms standard automated methods. We also describe the advantages of the proposed approach over previous scenario selection methods using a numerical example. Indeed, we open the "logical next chapter" in the evolution of moving from human-centric "Intuitive Logics" to automated "Decision-Relevant Discovery".

detail.title: Financial Analysis of Reliance Industries Limited: A Python-Driven Multi-Method Quantitative Investigation
detail.abstract: Corporate financial stability requires systematic empirical evaluation using robust quantitative methods. Balance sheet data of Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) spanning 2010 to 2023 was analyzed through seven Python-based analytical techniques. Key financial indicators-total assets, equity capital, reserves, borrowings, and total liabilities-were examined for trend, structure, and interdependence. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation with heat maps, multiple regression, simultaneous equation modeling, ANOVA, factor analysis, and K-Means machine learning were applied sequentially. Bibliometric visualization using VOSviewer complemented statistical findings by mapping research knowledge structures. All analytical procedures were implemented using Python libraries including Pandas, NumPy, Seaborn, Statsmodels, and Scikit-learn. title: Endogenizing Friction: A Structural Mechanism for the Breakdown of Nash

detail.title: Endogenizing Friction: A Structural Mechanism for the Breakdown of Nash
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a dynamic framework in which Nash equilibrium is not treated as a fixed outcome but as a structure that can be systematically destabilized. By introducing the performance function 𝑂 = 𝐿 𝑇 /𝐸, where 𝐿denotes cooperation, 𝑇represents temporal accumulation, and 𝐸captures frictional costs, we extend standard game-theoretic models to incorporate endogenous structural effects. In contrast to classical formulations that assume static payoffs and individual rationality, our model embeds cooperation into a dynamic system where repeated interaction amplifies its value while friction reduces effective payoffs. We formalize this by integrating a structural payoff component into agents' utility functions and modeling the evolution of cooperation and friction as state variables within a Markov framework. We derive sufficient conditions under which the traditional non-cooperative Nash equilibrium becomes unstable. When the marginal structural benefit of cooperation exceeds the short-term incentive to defect, defection ceases to be optimal. The system then transitions toward a cooperative equilibrium as the unique stable outcome. This demonstrates that equilibrium is not merely discovered but can be engineered through institutional design.

title: Exchange rate misalignment and investing firm's gain in terms of asset ownership

detail.title: Exchange rate misalignment and investing firm's gain in terms of asset ownership
detail.abstract: While existing literature has extensively examined the relationship between exchange rate misalignment and FDI flows, relatively little attention has been given to quantifying the firm-level cost advantages in acquiring domestically priced resources arising out of exchange rate differentials. This study contributes to the existing discourse by proposing a simple metric that captures this often-overlooked dimension of international trade. To be precise, here we quantify the cost advantages obtained by the investing firm in terms of ownership of domestically priced assets, stemming from exchange rate misalignment. Building upon the above quantification, here we empirically estimate the regions where US FDI should flow toward in order to reap the maximum benefit of misaligned exchange rates and compare it with the actual US investments abroad. Ceteris paribus, strategy presented here will provide MNCs a new perspective to gauge their overseas investment opportunities in terms of asset ownership. We also compare our new metric with other metrics of overall trade-competitiveness of a country and explain how it differs from the existing ones.

detail.abstract:
Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs) are positioned squarely and more than ever in the financial sector architecture of India. Property ARCs were initially envisioned as special-purpose vehicles to purify banks' balance sheets of non-performing assets (NPAs) by acquiring, managing, and recovering distressed financial assets under the Securitization and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002 [1] (SARFAESI Act). Since the inception of ARC more than 20 years ago, the industry has experienced a disruptive overhaul; it is no longer a reactive debt collector but rather an agent of business salvage.

The paper will be an in-depth legal, regulatory, and empirical study of ARCs as a device for reviving companies in India. It examines the underlying conceptual basis, statutory framework, operational mechanics, and the dynamic interface between ARCs and the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC). The paper examines the contributions of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), and other regulators to the development of the ARC ecosystem. It is a critical analysis of landmark judicial rulings, the new policy, such as the launch of the National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited (NARCL), the RBI Master Directions of 2024[2], and structural issues that still hamper the full potential of ARCs. The paper also concludes with evidence-based suggestions for strengthening ARCs into real corporate revivers rather than debt recovery conduits.


[1] Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002, No. 54, Acts of Parliament, 2002 (India)

[2] Reserve Bank of India, Master Direction – Reserve Bank of India (Asset Reconstruction Companies) Directions, 2024.

title: Roman Empire and Counterintelligence: Managing Uncertainty in Imperial Power - Internal Security, Information, and the Formation of Empire

detail.title: Roman Empire and Counterintelligence: Managing Uncertainty in Imperial Power - Internal Security, Information, and the Formation of Empire

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. The research was conducted independently and without any commercial or financial relationships that could be construed as a potential conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, personal data, or experimental subjects. It is based on historical, legal, and theoretical analysis of publicly available sources. Therefore, no ethics approval was required.

detail.abstract:
This book-length study examines the problem of internal uncertainty in complex political systems through the case of the Roman Empire. It argues that the durability of Roman imperial governance cannot be adequately explained by military power, legal development, or administrative capacity alone. Instead, it must be understood as the result of a continuous effort to detect, interpret, and manage internal threats under conditions of incomplete information and ambiguous intent.

The book approaches counterintelligence not as a modern institutional domain, but as a functional and structural dimension of governance. In the absence of formal intelligence agencies, Roman practices—law, surveillance, denunciation, administrative oversight, and military control—formed a distributed system oriented toward the management of internal instability. These practices operated without formalization, yet fulfilled analogous roles in identifying risk, assessing loyalty, and enabling anticipatory action. 

Methodologically, the study is situated at the intersection of ancient history, political theory, and intelligence studies. It draws on literary, legal, and administrative sources to reconstruct patterns of internal security and to analyze how information was produced, circulated, and interpreted within imperial governance. Particular attention is given to the transformation of Republican practices into imperial legal and institutional structures, including the expansion of treason law and the normalization of preventive control.

The book further introduces the conceptual framework of Institutional Counterintelligence Analysis (ICA), developed independently of the historical material, and applies it as a heuristic device to interpret Roman governance. This approach enables the identification of structural continuities between pre-modern and modern systems without imposing institutional equivalence.

The central argument of the book is that counterintelligence—understood broadly as the continuous management of internal threat under uncertainty—constitutes a fundamental condition of statehood. The Roman case demonstrates how such a system can operate without formal institutionalization, how it becomes embedded across legal, institutional, and cultural domains, and how its effectiveness depends on interpretation, judgment, and the management of informational limits.

title: Battery Strategy in ERCOT's RTC+B: Era Lessons from European Balancing Market Experience

detail.title: Battery Strategy in ERCOT's RTC+B: Era Lessons from European Balancing Market Experience
detail.abstract: ERCOT's Real-Time Co-Optimization (RTC+B), live since December 5, 2025, has fundamentally changed the risk profile for battery storage operators. In the weeks following implementation, some market participants reported reducing or pausing day-ahead ancillary services participation-a signal that existing optimization strategies require rethinking. While European power markets do not feature the same real-time co-optimization mechanism as RTC+B, European operators have extensive experience managing renewable variability and balancing market uncertainty. This paper offers one European practitioner's perspective on operational lessons that may transfer to ERCOT's new environment, with appropriate humility about the limits of cross-market analogies. Our core observation: Under co-optimization, the challenge shifts from forecast accuracy to forecast application speed. Day-ahead forecasts, however sophisticated, cannot anticipate real-time renewable variability. The operators who adapt fastest to changing conditions-not those with the best predictions-tend to outperform. We present strategies focusing on real-time irradiance correction for solar forecasting. Literature shows such techniques can improve short-term PV forecast accuracy by 20-60%. However, we explicitly acknowledge limitations: this paper focuses on solar variability, while ERCOT's generation mix includes substantial wind capacity-a topic that warrants separate analysis.

title: Does Demographic Capital Do Anything? Capital Deepening, the Allocation Puzzle, and the J-Curve of Demographic Investment

detail.title: Does Demographic Capital Do Anything? Capital Deepening, the Allocation Puzzle, and the J-Curve of Demographic Investment
detail.abstract: Capital flows do not reliably promote growth in recipient countries (Prasad, Rajan, and Subramanian 2007), and the allocation puzzle shows capital flowing "uphill" from poor to rich countries (Gourinchas and Jeanne 2013). We show that demographics help explain important heterogeneity in both puzzles. Using gravity-predicted bilateral portfolio flows driven by demographic distance as an instrument for capital inflows into 38 OECD countries over 1990-2024, we document a J-curve in investment: demographic capital inflows have no contemporaneous effect on fixed investment, but produce an increase of approximately 0.7 percentage points in the investment-to-GDP ratio at a two-year horizon in the level specification (p = 0.044), rising to 1.6 pp in the first-differenced specification (p < 0.001). Baseline controls throughout are fiscal balance, lagged NFA position, GDP growth, log GDP per capita, and the Z₁ × log GDP/cap interaction; KAOPEN is no longer in the baseline. This finding survives pre-trend tests, a placebo instrument constructed from non-demographic gravity variables, and a permutation placebo that randomly reassigns demographic distances across bilateral pairs (40 of 1,000 permutations exceed the observed statistic, p = 0.040). The allocation puzzle is concentrated in early-transition countries (β = 0.36, p < 0.001); in late-transition economies, the growth-surplus correlation reverses. Demographics drive investment quantity but not TFP, and FDI rather than portfolio flows produces capital deepening. Institutional quality and financial depth are necessary complements: without them, demographic capital does not translate into productive investment.

detail.title: Reaching for Synthetic Yield
detail.abstract: We examine the emerging phenomenon of "reaching for synthetic yield" through covered call option writing by investment companies, using return and holdings data (including short positions) from a comprehensive sample of all U.S. options-writing funds. Funds become more aggressive in synthesizing income when interest rates, term premiums, and default premiums are low. Investors reward high-yield funds with inflows, conditional on total performance, without distinguishing between asset-generated yield and yield manufactured through option writing. However, yield-manufacturing funds experience greater total return losses, particularly in bull markets. This widespread yield manufacturing activity suppresses option prices and short-term implied volatility.

title: Ambedkar's constitutional morality in modern Indian governance

detail.title: Ambedkar's constitutional morality in modern Indian governance
detail.abstract: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's idea of constitutional morality remains a guiding light for India's government today. It stresses living by the Constitution's core values like fairness, freedom, and brotherhood to keep democracy strong. What is Constitutional Morality? Constitutional morality means more than just following laws on paper. Ambedkar said it is a deep respect for the Constitution's spirit—valuing liberty, equality, and fraternity in everyday actions by leaders and citizens alike.1 He warned during Constituent Assembly debates that India's "soil is essentially undemocratic," so political voting alone won't work without this moral base (Ambedkar, 1949).2 In simple terms, it's like training everyone to play fair, even when no one is watching, to avoid power grabs or hero worship that could turn democracy into dictatorship. Role in Modern Governance Today, this idea checks misuse of power in India. Courts often use it, like in the 2018 Navtej Singh Johar case, where judges struck down laws against private adult choices, saying they violated equality and privacy under the Constitution.3 Similarly, in the Sabarimala temple entry ruling (2018), the Supreme Court leaned on Ambedkar's morality to push women's rights over blind traditions.4 Governments face tests too—think corruption scandals or emergency-like curbs on speech, where leaders sidestep rules for control. Ambedkar's call to "cultivate" this morality urges watchdogs like an independent judiciary and alert voters to hold power accountable (Mehta, 2010).5 Challenges and Path Forward India struggles with caste divides, fake news stirring hate, and weak trust in leaders, echoing Ambedkar's fears. Yet, his vision fits modern needs: ethical rulers, fair elections, and schools teaching constitutional values. By blending ancient Indian ethics with democracy, it builds a just society where everyone thrives (Sharma, 2023).6

title: A CEO-Constrained Endogenous Growth Model of the Firm: Strategic Levers, Market Constraints, and Short Time Horizons: A Unified Treatment Working Paper, April 2026

detail.title: A CEO-Constrained Endogenous Growth Model of the Firm: Strategic Levers, Market Constraints, and Short Time Horizons: A Unified Treatment Working Paper, April 2026

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: This paper develops the formal mathematical structure of a CEO-constrained endogenous growth model of the firm. A chief executive officer with a finite tenure horizon and a compensation contract tied to short-run stock price and reported earnings allocates a budget across six strategic levers: productive capital investment, R&D, stock buybacks, mergers and acquisitions, labor cost management, and offshoring. Dividends are excluded from the CEO's control vector on the grounds that dividend policy is a boardlevel governance commitment rather than a CEO discretionary instrument. The CEO faces three binding constraints: (i) a stock market termination hazard that penalizes shortfalls in earnings per share relative to a time-varying benchmark; (ii) Cournot-Nash competition with N rival firms, each governed by analogous short-horizon CEOs; and (iii) a stochastic demand environment that expands endogenously in response to qualityimproving innovation. The model is formulated as a finite-horizon stochastic differential game. We derive the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation for the CEO's value function, characterize the interior optimality conditions, and establish four analytical results: a myopic lever bias, a financial arms race equilibrium, a tenure extension trap, and a productive investment complementarity. A calibration strategy based on U.S. manufacturing panel data is outlined.

title: The Impact of Innovation on Firm Performance: Empirical Evidence from Vietnamese Enterprises
affiliations: Department of Economics, Macquarie University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Curtin University

detail.title: The Impact of Innovation on Firm Performance: Empirical Evidence from Vietnamese Enterprises
detail.abstract: Innovation is widely recognised as a key driver of firm performance, yet empirical evidence from emerging economies remains limited. This study examines how different forms of innovation affect sales and employment growth among Vietnamese firms using firm-level data from the 2023 World Bank Enterprise Survey. The analysis considers product and process innovation, R&D expenditure, and R&D participation, while controlling for firm characteristics and institutional constraints. Using an instrumental variable (IV) approach with two-stage least squares (2SLS), we find that innovation is significantly associated with improvements in firm performance, with product and process innovations associated with substantial gains in sales growth. In contrast, the impact on employment growth is positive but more moderate, indicating that revenue expansion does not fully translate into job creation. R&D expenditure shows only incremental effects, suggesting limited short-term returns. Export participation is associated with stronger sales growth, whereas legal and regulatory obstacles are associated with lower employment expansion. Overall, the findings highlight that innovation is an important but context-dependent driver of firm growth in Vietnam, with more pronounced effects on revenue than on employment.

Implementation of three farm laws, consequent farmer protest, and repeal of those laws, the demand for legalisation, signifies the importance of MSP in India. In this background, we have studied the causal impact of MSP on price realisation among paddy cultivators in India. Using the spatial fuzzy RDD model, we found that the implementation of MSP significantly increases the price realisation of paddy, leading to a large welfare loss in the treatment state. Any policy to reduce the effectiveness of MSP is highly discouraged.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a blockchain-based framework for cross-border trade settlement that automatically adjusts transaction values to real-time foreign exchange (FX) fluctuations. The proposed Dynamic Forex-Linked Smart Contract (DFLS) integrates oracle-based data feeds, programmable contract logic, and policy compliant settlement layers to mitigate currency exposure in international trade. Monte Carlo simulations over 90 trading days yield mean shortfall of-1.39% and a 95% Value at Risk (VaR) of 1.72%, indicating enhanced stability relative to static contracts. The findings highlight the potential of DFLS systems to improve liquidity predictability, support regulatory compliance, and enhance financial inclusion in global value chains. This research contributes to the discourse on programmable finance and its implications for trade policy and macroeconomic resilience.

title: Instrument-Free Endogeneity Correction: A Unified Framework for Rank-Gaussianized Control Functions

detail.title: Instrument-Free Endogeneity Correction: A Unified Framework for Rank-Gaussianized Control Functions
detail.abstract: In political research, endogeneity correction is critically important. The instrumental variable (IV) method is widely applied for endogeneity correction, but severely constrained by the availability of strictly exogenous shocks. To overcome this pervasive limitation, we introduce a unified framework for instrument-free endogeneity correction based on rank-Gaussianized control functions, in which endogeneity is corrected not through an external shock, but through an internally constructed control term that recovers the latent dependence channel between the endogenous regressor and the structural error. Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) is inconsistent under endogeneity because Cov(Xendo, u) ̸= 0 violates the exogeneity condition — anda any correction must be derived from Xendo itself in a way that is nonlinearly distinct from it, since a linear function of Xendo is already spanned by the model. We show that the Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) transformation isolates the rank information of the endogenous variable, separating it from the scale information that causes bias. Mapping these ranks to a standard normal proxy produces a control term that absorbs the latent dependence channel without redundancy. However, safely deploying this rank-extraction engine requires resolving a critical architectural divergence. Through theoretical synthesis and Monte Carlo simulations, we show that "copula-first" architectures (Park and Gupta (2012) and Yang, Qian, and Xie (2025)) require a Gaussian copula assumption that is rare in general political science data; when this assumption is violated, these estimators are inconsistent and coverage degrades with sample size. In constrast, the "orthogonalize-then-Gaussianize-the-residual" architecture of Breitung, Mayer, and Wied (2024) achieves consistency under a strictly broader class of data-generating processes, making it the preferred default for political science applications. Supported by empirical applications, we provide a comprehensive diagnostic pipeline, equipping political scientists with a rigorously tested, instrument-free approach for unbiased structural estimation.

title: Interpretive Orchestration: An Essay Exploring the Epistemic Intersection of Human Intuition and Machine Intelligence

detail.title: Interpretive Orchestration: An Essay Exploring the Epistemic Intersection of Human Intuition and Machine Intelligence
detail.abstract:
As artificial intelligence capabilities expand beyond pattern recognition to theoretical insight generation, interpretive qualitative research confronts a question of epistemic responsibility:  how can scholars integrate AI capabilities while remaining accountable for their theoretical interpretations? This essay proposes ‘interpretive orchestration’ as a framework that transforms researchers from analysts into skilled orchestrators of human-AI collaboration. The framework addresses two challenges that become opportunities. The translation challenge of articulating tacit knowledge (theoretical orientations, contextual understanding, embodied intuition) into forms AI can process deepens researchers’ awareness of their own expertise. The judgment challenge of evaluating AI-generated patterns for theoretical significance highlights the accountability our scholarly communities require, particularly through “1.5 order data”: patterns invisible to human perception yet requiring human interpretation for recognized theoretical significance. Three strategic models guide this orchestration: Socratic tension surfaces implicit assumptions through deliberate contradiction; Euclidean documentation enables reproducible analysis through systematic context-building; Vitruvian mastery reads across independent analytical passes for synthetic insight. By embracing orchestration, researchers discover that AI can amplify rather than replace human capability. The future of interpretive research lies neither in rejecting AI nor surrendering to automation, but in systematic approaches to human-AI collaboration that preserve the scholarly-accountable judgment our communities require while drawing on AI’s capacity to generate theoretical insights across scales humans cannot process alone.

This is the accepted manuscript version. The Version of Record will be published in Strategic Organization. Author affiliations in the manuscript reflect those at time of publication. At the time of writing, Xule Lin is a Research Associate at Imperial Business School and will join SKEMA Business School as Assistant Professor in August 2026.

title: The Erosion of Moderation: Endogenous Salience Tilting and Political Polarization

detail.title: The Erosion of Moderation: Endogenous Salience Tilting and Political Polarization
detail.abstract: This paper studies the erosion of moderation in the United States. Recent political-science research documents rising partisan polarization, stronger sorting, and a visibly thinner moderate center over the last two decades. The paper develops a projection-rotation account of that shift. Citizens hold latent beliefs across multiple political dimensions, while social-media engagement concentrates attention on dimensions where disagreement is greatest and amplification is strongest. The result is a reweighting of the mapping from latent beliefs to visible politics: issue weights tilt toward more conflictive dimensions, and the visible center thins even without large-scale persuasion. The mechanism is formalized as a mean-field click equilibrium with an active-passive attention structure. The core results characterize how endogenous salience tilts rotate the visible axis and produce center hollowing under transparent sign conditions. A two-block special case then provides the analytical bridge: if high-conflict issues attract more engagement than low-conflict issues, their projection wedges are positive, low-conflict wedges are negative, and center hollowing follows. The paper does not claim empirical validation from aggregate survey evidence. It offers a candidate formal mechanism for a phenomenon documented widely in the polarization literature and is intended as a theory-forward SSRN manuscript rather than a fully identified empirical study.

title: TaxFL: Federated Learning and Federated Graph Intelligence for Cross-Border Tax Compliance – A privacy-enhancing blueprint for collaborative risk analytics without sharing raw taxpayer data

detail.title: TaxFL: Federated Learning and Federated Graph Intelligence for Cross-Border Tax Compliance – A privacy-enhancing blueprint for collaborative risk analytics without sharing raw taxpayer data

declarations.ethicsApproval: his study uses exclusively synthetic data generated for research purposes to replicate operational constraints in tax and AML/CFT environments. No real taxpayer records, personal data, bank transaction data, or human participants were accessed or used at any stage. The experiments were conducted on a fully synthetic oracle graph calibrated to publicly available Brazilian official statistics. Therefore, ethics approval and informed consent procedures were not required or applicable.

detail.abstract: Cross-border tax non-compliance and money laundering exploit fragmented data silos across jurisdictions. This working paper proposes TaxFL, a pragmatic privacy-preserving framework that enables tax authorities and FIUs to collaboratively train risk models without ever sharing raw taxpayer or transaction data. TaxFL combines cross-silo federated learning, federated GraphSAGE for beneficial ownership and transaction graphs, and a layered privacy stack (secure aggregation, Rényi DP, optional TEEs). The framework operates in a hierarchical two-level architecture (Level 1 intra-country + Level 2 cross-border) and includes a novel multi-tier aggregator model with AMLA, GAFILAT/OEA and OECD as natural institutional homes. Synthetic experiments on a calibrated Brazilian oracle graph show: (i) bilateral RFB–Bancos federation detects T1/T5 schemes invisible to either party alone; (ii) GraphSAGE delivers +26 pp AUC and +17 pp recall on T6 (Caixa Dois); (iii) banks correct fraudulent CNAE declarations with 96.7 % accuracy using only behavioral profiles. A conservative “belt-and-suspenders” governance blueprint ensures compliance even under strict Schrems II interpretations. The paper also outlines a Phase 0 domestic pilot (RFB + banks) and a full commercialization-ready roadmap.

title: A Field-Theoretic Construction of Economic Dynamics from an Action Principle

detail.title: A Field-Theoretic Construction of Economic Dynamics from an Action Principle

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no conflicts of interest.

detail.abstract: We construct a field-theoretic framework in which economic dynamics emerge from an action principle defined on a differentiable manifold. The theory does not assume economic primitives such as price, value, or exchange. Instead, these quantities arise from the dynamics of interacting fields describing production, labor, and distribution. The formulation introduces propagation structures that define effective metrics, whose compatibility condition generates price dynamics. Instabilities correspond to mismatches between these propagation structures and lead to endogenous crises. The theory further predicts a phase structure governed by production density, including an asymptotic regime in which labor vanishes and exchange ceases. Stochastic properties of price dynamics, including log-normal distributions, power-law tails, and volatility clustering, are derived from coarse-grained field fluctuations. The framework provides a geometrically grounded and internally consistent description of economic systems that is empirically testable and structurally closed.

detail.abstract: What do climate-growth regressions identify: responses to statistical shocks or to real-time information guiding adaptation? Bilal and Känzig (2026) construct shocks as residuals from fullsample Hamilton (2018) projections. These shocks are ex-post statistical innovations that reflect orthogonality conditions in the data, but need not coincide with the information innovations that agents observe when forming beliefs and making adaptation decisions. Facing climate change, economic agents confront "known unknowns": they understand that the underlying climate process is evolving, but do not know the magnitude or speed of the permanent warming trend. Realized temperature fluctuations therefore serve both as contemporaneous shocks and as signals that update beliefs about the underlying process. This distinction has first-order implications for inference. Full-sample procedures can introduce non-stationary measurement error that distorts early-period variation and reduces statistical power to detect learning-driven adaptation. By contrast, recursive forecast errors constructed using only information available at time t-1 align the econometrician's information set with that of economic agents who choose how much to invest in adaptation to emerging risks. Monte Carlo simulations and a re-examination of the Bilal and Känzig (2026) data demonstrate that empirical conclusions about climate damages and adaptation depend on how shocks are defined. Recursive shocks yield smaller point estimates and less precisely estimated effects, but produce coefficients that are directionally consistent with attenuation of damages over time. These findings highlight a tradeoff between statistical precision and economic interpretation, and underscore the importance of aligning empirical shock measures with the information that agents actually observe in environments characterized by persistent uncertainty.

title: Assembly, Dissipation, and the Kinetic Foundations of Collapse in Complex Adaptive Systems

detail.title: Assembly, Dissipation, and the Kinetic Foundations of Collapse in Complex Adaptive Systems
detail.abstract: The Capacity-Load Mismatch (CLM) framework, developed across the preceding four papers in this series (Rosen, 2026a, 2026b, 2026c, 2026d), has established that complex adaptive systems fail through tempo-weighted excess rather than through scarcity. Across substrates as different as algal photosystems, neural networks, interpersonal bandwidth, and planetary carbon cycles, the same pattern has recurred: identical loads produce survival or collapse depending on the rate at which they arrive. What the framework has not yet explained is why this pattern is so universal. This paper proposes that the answer lies in a deeper structural principle, the kinetic mismatch between two fundamental imperatives of matter. The abiotic domain, governed by the Second Law, pulls matter toward low-Assembly-Index configurations and thermodynamic equilibrium. The biotic domain, sustained through continuous energy dissipation, constructs and reproduces high-Assembly-Index configurations against that pull. Drawing on Assembly Theory (Sharma et al., 2023) and the thermodynamics of self-replication (England, 2013), I argue that every regulated system occupies a metastable position between these two imperatives, and that its 1 viability depends on a variable introduced here as the Assembly-Dissipation Ratio (ADR): the rate at which high-AI configurations are constructed relative to the rate at which the environment can dissipate the entropic byproducts of that construction. The CLM tempo variable, T, is reinterpreted as an empirical proxy for ADR. Collapse Through Excess, formalized in earlier papers as a tempo-driven bifurcation, is reframed here as Kinetic Overload: a forced return toward lower Assembly Index when the dissipation capacity of the abiotic anchor has been exceeded. This extension grounds the CLM framework in fundamental physics, provides a substrate-independent metric for cross-domain comparison, and generates testable predictions that the earlier formulation could not produce. Cross-domain applications are developed in the algal, neural, relational, and planetary domains.

title: Watt's fair? Distribution and energy savings in electricity compensation schemes
affiliations: CICERO Center for International Climate Research, , Institute of Transport Economics and Statistics Norway

detail.title: Watt's fair? Distribution and energy savings in electricity compensation schemes

declarations.funderStatement: This study was funded by The Research Council of Norway, grant no. 344361

detail.abstract: Energy price volatility poses a central policy dilemma: how can governments shield households from high energy prices while preserving incentives for the energy transition? Exploiting spatial variation in electricity price increases across Norway's bidding zones during the energy price crisis, we estimate price elasticities of residential electricity demand using household-level panel data from smart meters covering more than 1.5 million households. Electricity consumption varies substantially within income groups. We find that electricity demand is relatively inelastic, with an average price elasticity of -0.10. Within each income quintile, low-consumption households are less price-responsive than high-consumption households. We use these estimates to simulate welfare and electricity consumption outcomes under the full price increase, the implemented price subsidy, fiscally equivalent uniform cash transfers per person and per square meter, and a recently introduced fixed price scheme. We find substantial heterogeneity in the welfare impacts of these schemes, both across and within income groups. Uniform transfers that maintain price signals are less effective at preventing large welfare losses among low-income, high-consumption households, but transfers based on dwelling size perform better than those based on household size. Overall, the uniform transfer schemes perform better than the price-distorting schemes when comparing policy costs, total prevented welfare losses, and efficiency costs, revealing a trade-off between targeting and efficiency.
