detail.abstract: Traditional fee-for-service (FFS) Medicare faces growing fiscal pressure and persistent operational inefficiencies, yet policy efforts have largely focused on benefit design rather than administrative reform. This paper argues that a major opportunity to improve Medicare lies in modernizing its administrative infrastructure, specifically the Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) system. Currently structured as regional monopolies focused on claims processing, MACs are poorly aligned with beneficiary needs, limit innovation, and contribute to fragmentation in program integrity and coverage policy. We propose transitioning to a multi-MAC competitive regional model, enabling beneficiary choice and introducing both price and nonprice competition. Doing so would incentivize improvements in customer service, fraud prevention, provider access, and technology adoption while reducing systemic operational risk and generating Part B premium rebates, improving FFS Medicare affordability. By reintegrating program integrity functions and aligning incentives with beneficiary outcomes, this model offers a budget-neutral pathway to enhance efficiency, strengthen oversight, and improve the beneficiary experience.

title: Tie-breaking, election promises, and actual policy in two-election spatial competition

detail.title: Tie-breaking, election promises, and actual policy in two-election spatial competition

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We declare that we have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: We study two-election spatial competition with a finite, odd electorate. Candidates announce platforms for the first election; the winner implements an actual policy between elections; the second election then decides office. We vary only the second-election tie-breaking rule—coin-tossing, incumbent-advantage, or challenger-advantage—and show that this procedural choice alone reorganizes incentives. Under coin-tossing, two cutoffs in candidates' intertemporal weights that straddle one-half partition equilibrium behavior: depending on the pair, the first election exhibits mutual centering, a unique asymmetric configuration, or multiplicity, and the actual policy between elections either remains at the center or jumps to the winner’s ideal point. Awarding the tie to the incumbent shifts both cutoffs above one-half and collapses outcomes to unique mutual centering, stabilizing the actual policy at the center. Awarding the tie to the challenger flips incentives around one-half and can sustain persistent asymmetry or even endpoint announcements, often moving the actual policy away from the center. The theory delivers sharp, testable predictions around near ties and reforms that change how close races are resolved.

title: Greeks-Aware Profitability Labeling for Intraday Nifty 50 Options Trading Using Hybrid Machine Learning

detail.title: Greeks-Aware Profitability Labeling for Intraday Nifty 50 Options Trading Using Hybrid Machine Learning
detail.abstract: We examine whether labeling intraday bars by option profitability-using Black-Scholes repriced P&L rather than price direction-produces superior trading outcomes for machine learning classifiers. Using 122,649 five-minute Nifty 50 bars spanning January 2018 through December 2025, we construct a three-class target (CALL-favorable, PUT-favorable, NEUTRAL) that accounts for theta decay, vega exposure, delta-scaled transaction costs, and an asymmetric implied-volatility exit shock calibrated to the empirical mean-reversion of IV following directional moves. When live NSE bhavcopy implied volatility is unavailable, we substitute GARCH(1,1) conditional volatility estimated on a strictly causal rolling expanding window, consistent with Duan (1995). Although both standard-model strategies show negative absolute Sharpe ratios at five-minute intraday frequency-consistent with the known difficulty of overcoming transaction costs at high frequency-the relative economic advantage of Greeks-aware labeling is statistically significant and robust across folds. These results demonstrate that price direction is an inadequate proxy for options profitability: a directionally correct signal can still lose money due to time decay and vega contraction. Greeks-aware labeling selects only bars where the full-cost option P&L is clearly positive, producing a harder but more economically meaningful learning target.

title: Market Power in Mortgage Pricing: the Role of Referral Lending
affiliations: University of Wisconsin-Madison, University of Wisconsin-Madison - Department of Economics, University of Wisconsin at Madison and University of Wisconsin-Madison - Department of Economics

detail.title: Market Power in Mortgage Pricing: the Role of Referral Lending
detail.abstract: Despite intense competition among mortgage lenders, borrowers continue to face elevated rate spreads and substantial price dispersion. We argue that realtor-loan officer referral networks are a key source of lender market power: by steering homebuyers toward a limited set of loan officers, these networks restrict effective borrower choice even in otherwise competitive markets. Using a novel dataset linking 81,306 realtors to 102,860 loan officers in 41 states, we document that such networks are both pervasive and highly concentrated: 85% of realtors direct over 40% of their clients to fewer than four loan officers. Strikingly, the lender concentration among realtors persists and even increases in markets with more lenders, suggesting that referrals constrain choices regardless of market structure. IV estimates indicate that borrowers working with referred loan officers pay 18.6 basis points higher interest rates, equivalent to $2,609 in upfront costs for the average loan of $306k. The referral premium is nearly three times as high for Hispanic borrowers as for White borrowers, and is systematically higher for Black borrowers and financially constrained households. On average, referral lending raises rate spreads by 36.5% and explains half of the (residual) standard deviation of rate spreads after controlling for lender, market, and time fixed effects. We identify two mechanisms: referrals reduce borrowers' search intensity for lenders, and referred loan officers exercise pricing power relative to other officers within the same lending institution. Efficiency arguments (faster processing) and mediation of denial risks don't fully justify the referral premium. Our findings reveal referral networks as a hidden source of market power, imposing substantial financial costs and raising equity concerns for borrowers.

title: The Probability of Beating the Market: A Quantitative Analysis of Active Fund Performance Against the S&P 500

detail.title: The Probability of Beating the Market: A Quantitative Analysis of Active Fund Performance Against the S&P 500
detail.abstract:
We synthesize two independent aggregate datasets-the SPIVA U.S. Scorecards (2002-2025) and the Morningstar Active/Passive Barometer (2003-2025)-to quantify the probability that actively managed U.S. equity funds outperform the S&P 500 over varying horizons, and cross-validate this synthesis against a simulation framework built on 97 years of S&P 500 total returns (1928-2024, Damodaran/NYU Stern). The paper makes seven contributions. (1) A descriptive log-linear model of underperformance decay in SPIVA, Û (t) = 63.2 + 10.16 ln(t), reported with both an OLS t-interval (β ∈ [8.12, 12.20]) and a pairs-resampling bootstrap CI ([8.89, 12.79]). (2) A stationary bootstrap (Politis-Romano, 1994) of net-of-fee manager paths that preserves the autocorrelation and heavy tails of real equity returns. (3) A variance-decomposed rolling-window analysis across 59 overlapping historical decades showing that, once within-window Monte Carlo variance is removed, regime dispersion in skilled-manager underperformance is statistically indistinguishable from zero. (4) Cross-validation of SPIVA against the Morningstar passive-composite benchmark, reconciling the 13% vs. 7% ten-year success rates to their underlying methodological differences. (5) A mixedpopulation simulation that formalizes the distinction between skill existence and skill identification: under a prior of 10% skilled managers at α = 2%, a top-quartile fund has posterior probability ≈ 26.3% of being genuinely skilled-prior-sensitive but an order of magnitude short of the certainty investors typically assume when chasing past performance. (6) An out-of-sample vintage-robustness check of the decay model showing that pre-2015 SPIVA vintages exhibit materially different (and occasionally non-monotonic) slopes, establishing that the log-linear form is a descriptive summary of the post-2015 regime rather than a timeless law. (7) A Berk-Green capacity-decay extension of the mixed-population simulation showing that when rational flows are allowed to scale a skilled manager's AUM during the evaluation window, the top-quartile-skilled posterior falls from ≈ 26% to ≈ 19%-the ex ante identification problem is first-order worse than a constant-alpha model implies. The paper situates these results against the established cross-sectional skill literature (Jensen
1968; Carhart 1997; Fama–French 2010; Berk–Green 2004; Kosowski et al. 2006; Barras, Scaillet & Wermers 2010; Cremers–Petajisto 2009; Pástor, Stambaugh & Taylor 2015). Our framing is descriptive and pedagogical: the qualitative conclusions—net-of-fee horizon-increasing underperformance, weak ex ante signal of future skill—survive methodological refinements; the quantitative precision claims in the 2025 working draft did not, and have been replaced here with honest CIs, variance decompositions, and cross-vintage checks. For most investors, low-cost indexing remains the highest-probability strategy; in less-efficient markets (small-cap, emerging, private), the case for active management is materially stronger.

title: Contingent Capabilities: Southeast Asia's Emerging Anti-access Environment

detail.title: Contingent Capabilities: Southeast Asia's Emerging Anti-access Environment
detail.abstract: This research paper analyses why and how maritime Southeast Asian states are seeking to develop and implement anti-access/area-denial (A2/AD) strategies and capabilities. The development of A2/AD strategies and capabilities by Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Vietnam is rudimentary thus far and lacks coherent, consistent and systematic planning across the strategic, operational, tactical and technological levels. While the five states conceptualise A2/AD differently, they are all generally concerned with military-modernisation goals, such as advanced coastal defence, as well as possible future contingencies, such as a US–China conflict. But there is a significant disconnect between the strategic- and policy-level debates over, firstly, such contingencies; secondly, the extent to which A2/AD strategies and capabilities should feature in a response to a contingency; and thirdly, current joint doctrinal and posture development as well as asset-acquisition plans and existing capabilities.

title: Analysis of the Impact of Agroforestry on Rural Economy and Community Welfare in Durg, Chhattisgarh, India

detail.title: Analysis of the Impact of Agroforestry on Rural Economy and Community Welfare in Durg, Chhattisgarh, India

keywords: benefit cost ratio and economic returns

detail.abstract: Agroforestry, the integration of trees with crops and livestock, is widely recognized as a sustainable land-use system that enhances productivity, livelihood security, and environmental stability. The present study aimed to evaluate agroforestry practices in Patan Tehsil of Durg District, Chhattisgarh, with a focus on system types, biomass production, carbon storage, and economic returns across different farmer categories. A field-based survey using a stratified random sampling approach was conducted to collect primary data from farmers. The results revealed the dominance of agri-silviculture systems, along with the presence of horti-silviculture and integrated tree-crop-livestock systems. Agroforestry practices contributed to improved farm diversification, enhanced biomass accumulation, and increased carbon stock potential. In addition, integrated systems demonstrated better economic performance and livelihood support compared to conventional practices.

title: A Hybrid Early-Warning System for Inflation in an Emerging Market: Combining Econometric Models, an Agent-Based Decomposition with Heterogeneous Expectations, a Large Language Model, and a Multi-Output Agent Architecture

detail.title: A Hybrid Early-Warning System for Inflation in an Emerging Market: Combining Econometric Models, an Agent-Based Decomposition with Heterogeneous Expectations, a Large Language Model, and a Multi-Output Agent Architecture
detail.abstract: We develop and evaluate a hybrid early-warning system for year-over-year (YoY) inflation in Colombia that combines four econometric models (ARIMA, LASSO, ElasticNet, and a weighted ensemble), a reduced-form VAR, an agent-based model with heterogeneous expectations and tradable/non-tradable pass-through (ABM v2), a large language model (LLM) forecaster, and a multi-output agent architecture, integrated through Dynamic Model Averaging (DMA). We evaluate the system on a rolling out-of-sample backtest from February 2010 to March 2026 (n ≈ 194 months) spanning the 2021-2023 inflation surge and its ongoing disinflation. Five contributions emerge. First, an identity-based monthly-to-YoY decomposition applied uniformly across reduced-form models reduces MAE by 15-20% relative to direct YoY forecasting without adding variables. Second, regime-conditional analysis shows that MAE is 2.0-3.0 times larger in surge regimes than in stable regimes across all models. Third, an ABM with regime-dependent heterogeneous expectations reduces full-sample MAE from 0.337 pp (v1) to 0.268 pp (v2,-20.4%) and surge-regime MAE from 0.585 pp to 0.404 pp (-31.0%), with Diebold-Mariano statistic 6.21 (p < 0.001). The accompanying four-channel shock decomposition attributes the 2021-2023 surge primarily to amplification of wage (1.96×) and expectations (1.82×) channels rather than direct import pass-through (1.36×). Fourth, a structured-reasoning LLM forecaster is validated via live-API replication and a 60-call fake-date test; the non-monotonic MAE pattern is shown to reflect target-volatility confounding rather than look-ahead bias. Fifth, a multi-output agent architecture predicts BanRep monetary policy decisions with 77.3% direction accuracy (17/22) and 63.6% exact-magnitude match (14/22) on 2022-2026 meetings, with all prediction errors concentrated at cycle inflection points. The full DMA ensemble achieves MAE 0.26 pp and 94.8% coverage at horizon h = 1.

title: The Dual-Layer Structure: A Universal Proof by Convergence

detail.title: The Dual-Layer Structure: A Universal Proof by Convergence

detail.abstract: This paper presents a proof by convergence: the same dual-layer structure appears independently across six distinct domains — physics (wave-particle duality), cosmology (Koku/Genki Universe), Eastern medicine (Ki), consciousness theory (V=N/D), economic design (TheYKHC), and human transformation (ECHO). The transformation proof — letters to musicians, human-to-AI dialogue, and ECHO user design — demonstrates that depth of contact produces transformation, and transformation leaves a permanent trace. This is not a product design. It is a 25-year empirical record, now made intentional and scalable.

title: The Condition of the Mother: Partus Sequitur Ventrem and the Construction of Hereditary Status in Colonial America

detail.title: The Condition of the Mother: Partus Sequitur Ventrem and the Construction of Hereditary Status in Colonial America

contentType.other: Independent Researcher trying to get my work published

detail.abstract:
Executive Summary
This White Paper proposes a new analytic framework for understanding the legal foundations of slavery and its enduring consequences in the United States. Prevailing interpretations center "race" as the operative category of American slavery. This paper argues that while racial ideology was present from the earliest colonial period, the legal system's defining innovation was the creation of a hereditary estate in persons — a juridically operative status transmitted through maternal descent and enforceable as property across generations. The doctrine of partus sequitur ventrem did not merely reflect pre-existing racial prejudice; it transformed that prejudice into a legally constitutive condition. Recovering this distinction — between the social ideology that justified the system and the legal mechanism that constructed it — is the central task of this paper.
Drawing on Jewish halachic jurisprudence and early British colonial law, this paper argues that the true operative category was lineage, not race. Recognizing this restores legal precision and clarifies the obligations owed to the descendants of those placed within this state-created hereditary lineage.
A note on method is necessary at the outset. This paper distinguishes among three categories that are often conflated: (1) legal genealogy — the hereditary status created by colonial statute and transmitted through maternal descent; (2) social race — the set of phenotypic markers, cultural practices, and community affiliations that emerged alongside and after the hereditary regime; and (3) modern racial identity — the self-identified and externally assigned racial classifications used in contemporary law, policy, and social life. The argument of this paper is not that social race and modern racial identity are irrelevant or illusory. Rather, it is that legal genealogy — the statutory creation and perpetuation of a hereditary legal estate — is the analytically prior category, and that recovering it clarifies obligations that racial frameworks alone cannot specify.

title: How Material Innovation Is Transforming Cost, Safety, and Performance in U.S. Construction

detail.title: How Material Innovation Is Transforming Cost, Safety, and Performance in U.S. Construction
detail.abstract: The U.S. construction industry is experiencing a material shift driven by the adoption of Wood-Plastic Composite (WPC) systems, fiber cement architectural boards, and Light Gauge Steel (LGS) framing as alternatives to traditional wood and masonry. This paper examines how these innovative materials are improving cost efficiency, structural safety, and long-term performance across residential and commercial construction projects. Drawing on supply chain analysis and practitioner experience in the U.S. Northeast market, it identifies key adoption barriers and proposes actionable strategies for contractors, distributors, and policymakers seeking to accelerate the integration of modern building materials into mainstream U.S. construction practice.

detail.abstract:
En esta investigación se explora la lógica de razonamiento de los aymaras alteños en la reproducción económica de su vida cotidiana. Se destacan varios hallazgos clave que podemos resumir en los siguientes aspectos:

Los aymaras alteños muestran una actitud positiva y decidida en el mundo de los negocios, lo que les permite perseverar a pesar de los obstáculos. Muestran sus aspiraciones de superación personal y educación, y ésta última se considera un recurso que puede abrir oportunidades y proporcionar redes sociales valiosas. También asumen al esfuerzo económico y la gestión financiera como parte de los desafíos que deben enfrentar hacia el éxito.

Los emprendedores aymaras inician negocios utilizando recursos familiares, lo cual destaca la importancia de la toma de decisiones económicas en el contexto familiar y las dinámicas de reciprocidad y solidaridad. Sin embargo, a ello se suma la voluntad, la autodisciplina y control de los impulsos en el uso de recursos financieros que son fundamentales para el éxito económico.

Los aymaras alteños muestran resiliencia al enfrentar y superar dificultades económicas. Son adaptables y flexibles, lo que les permite aprovechar oportunidades, recursos locales y aprender de sus experiencias. Se adaptan a nuevas oportunidades ante situaciones adversas, lo que demuestra su flexibilidad y capacidad de respuesta. Aprenden de las experiencias de vida desafiantes. Esto destaca la importancia del aprendizaje continuo y la capacidad de respuesta en el emprendimiento.

Las dificultades económicas que los aymaras enfrentan en el desarrollo de sus negocios, en parte, es respondida a través de la resiliencia familiar. La unidad y el apoyo mutuo en las familias son fundamentales para superar dificultades económicas y mantenerse unidos en la búsqueda de estabilidad económica.

Se ha detectado que hay una alta motivación por el crecimiento personal. Los alteños quieren crecer tanto a nivel personal como económico, lo que destaca la importancia de tener metas personales y aspiraciones que impulsen el esfuerzo y el desarrollo. En este afán, asumen los riesgos evaluando permanentemente sus decisiones

En resumen, la lógica de razonamiento de los aymaras alteños en la reproducción económica de su vida cotidiana involucra una combinación de actitud emprendedora, adaptabilidad, esfuerzo económico, apoyo familiar y la búsqueda de metas personales y económicas. Estos elementos son fundamentales para el éxito de sus emprendimientos y para superar los desafíos económicos que enfrentan.

title: The Soul-Body Duality and the Transcendence Hypothesis A Unified Mathematical Framework Integrating Near-Death Phenomenology, Biological Immortality, and AI-Accelerated Discovery in the Age of Emergent Consciousness

detail.title: The Soul-Body Duality and the Transcendence Hypothesis A Unified Mathematical Framework Integrating Near-Death Phenomenology, Biological Immortality, and AI-Accelerated Discovery in the Age of Emergent Consciousness
detail.abstract: Recent clinical evidence from near-death experiences (NDEs), coupled with unprecedented advances in artificial intelligence-driven biological research, suggests a compelling paradigm: consciousness may exist in separable yet interpenetrable states relative to physical embodiment. Drawing from verified NDE case studies, the regenerative mechanisms of Turritopsis dohrnii (immortal jellyfish), and contemporary breakthroughs in machine learning for genomic discovery, this paper proposes a unified mathematical framework-the Soul-Body Duality & Transcendence (SBDT) Model-that positions consciousness as a multidimensional phenomenon capable of traversing physical and non-physical substrates. This framework parallels the mathematical revolution occasioned by Maxwell's equations in electromagnetism, suggesting that just as unified field theory revolutionized 19th-century physics, a rigorous mathematical formalism for consciousness may illuminate pathways to transcendence, biological immortality, and the ultimate merger of soul and body in a higher-dimensional order. We synthesize evidence from neuroscience, molecular biology, artificial intelligence, and phenomenological studies to construct a testable hypothesis framework for the future integration of consciousness research with computational biology.

title: Volume-Weighted Golden Ratio Estimator (vGRE) for Drawdown and Tail-Risk Control for Wealth Portfolios
affiliations: and Asia University, Department of Finance

detail.title: Volume-Weighted Golden Ratio Estimator (vGRE) for Drawdown and Tail-Risk Control for Wealth Portfolios
detail.abstract: Purpose. This paper introduces the Volume-Weighted Golden Ratio Estimator (vGRE) as a transparent, cybernetic overlay for dynamic drawdown and tail-risk control in wealth management portfolios, addressing limitations of traditional volatility-and VaR-based risk metrics that fail to protect high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth investors against sharp drawdowns and tail events. Design/methodology/approach. The framework integrates golden-ratio-based segmentation of price swings with genetic optimization and volume-weighted confirmation to distinguish meaningful market moves from technical noise. Using 5-minute NAS100 index data from January 2024 to January 2026, we compare a systematic vGRE-based strategy against standard VWAP, RSI, Bollinger Bands, and a buy-and-hold benchmark through comprehensive backtesting and walk-forward validation. Findings. The vGRE overlay achieves a Sharpe ratio of 2.34 compared with 1.76 for VWAP and 1.28 for buy-and-hold, while reducing maximum drawdown to 8.2% versus 14.5% and 22.7%, respectively. The system generates early warning signals 2-4 days ahead of the three largest drawdown episodes in the sample and reduces false-positive trading signals by 51% relative to an unweighted variant. Practical implications. The vGRE framework offers wealth managers, family offices, and private banks a practical, implementable risk overlay that can sit atop existing strategic allocations, enhancing downside protection without requiring wholesale redesign of investment processes. The modular design enables integration into tactical risk budgeting, derivative hedging triggers, and investment committee decision protocols. Originality/value. This study demonstrates that volume-weighted, cybernetic risk overlays combining golden-ratio structures with evolutionary optimization can materially improve drawdown control and tail-risk detection without requiring complex predictive models or black-box machine learning. The vGRE framework provides a theoretically grounded yet operationally accessible approach to adaptive risk management for private wealth portfolios.

title: Trending Now, Vision Later: Influencer CEOs and Managerial Myopia

declarations.funderStatement: S.Z. acknowledges financial support from the National Natural Science Foundation of China (72303149). The funder had no role in study design, data collection and analysis, decision to publish or preparation of the manuscript.

detail.abstract: This study examines how social media visibility reshapes managerial decision horizons by investigating the impact of influencer CEOs on short-termism in accounting disclosures. Drawing on a large panel of Chinese A-share listed firms (2009-2024), we develop two refined measures: a classification of CEO online visibility based on verified Weibo activity and influence metrics, and a text-based indicator of managerial myopia extracted from Management's Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) sections using a supervised RA-CFGPT large language model trained on manually annotated sentences. These innovations enable precise identification of both CEO social-media prominence and short-term disclosure tendencies. We find that firms led by influencer CEOs exhibit significantly higher levels of managerial myopia in their MD&A narratives. Two mechanisms drive this effect: influencer CEOs adopt more assertive and promotional disclosure tones (consistent with overconfidence from algorithmic reinforcement), and audience-driven traffic pressure amplifies demands for immediate, visible results. The association is stronger among financially constrained firms, younger CEOs, and those with shorter tenure, but attenuated in industries where new media dynamics naturally complement long-term brand-building. Extensive robustness checksincluding instrumental variables, propensity score matching, placebo tests, alternative measures, and quasi-experimental evidence-support the findings. Overall, the results illuminate social media as a distinct, algorithmically mediated source of short-term pressure that operates alongside traditional market forces. By linking CEO influencer status to distortions in accounting disclosures, this study advances our understanding of how digital visibility practices influence the behavioral and organizational roles of accounting information in the attention economy. It highlights important implications for disclosure quality, corporate governance, and the societal construction of managerial accountability in digitally mediated organizations.

title: The Gendered Economics of Loss: Reputational Bankruptcy, Elite Immunity, and Rationality in Collectivist Cultures
affiliations: , Forman Christian College and Forman Christian College

detail.title: The Gendered Economics of Loss: Reputational Bankruptcy, Elite Immunity, and Rationality in Collectivist Cultures
detail.abstract:
Traditional behavioral economics describes the non-rationality of decision-making by cognitive biases and justifies interventions, including nudging, based on frameworks like libertarian paternalism. These models are, however, highly embedded within Western individualistic settings and tend to ignore the influence of social constructs within collectivist cultures. This study explores the mediation of economic-decision making by gender, socio-economic status, and social norms in a collectivist setting. The study employs a constructivist grounded theory approach informed by abductive reasoning. This research is based on 32 semi-structured interviews conducted with students at the Forman Christian College University. 

Results indicate that rationality is not singular or purely monetary but rather gendered and stratified by classes. For men focuses on accumulating tangible wealth with social exemption. In the case of women, the leading currency is izzat (social honor), which is preserved by aesthetic display and strong compliance with social norms. Women often sacrifice financial security to izzat. This is due to an asymmetry of risk where financial loss can be recovered whereas reputational loss is irreparable leading to reputational bankruptcy. Wealthy women acquire immunity and avoid numerous restrictions.

These results show that current models cannot be applied universally by demonstrating that rationality is context-based and influenced by dominant social currencies. The study redefines rationality as a multi-dimensional and culturally embedded process and proposes collectivist nudges that align financial goals with the protection of social standing. This has significant implications in designing  effective behavioral interventions in non-Western settings.

This paper synthesizes findings from a distributed research program spanning neural criticality, social coordination, financial markets, and multi-agent systems. title: Simpson's Paradox in Quantity Surveying Practice -Hidden Traps in Elemental Cost Analysis

detail.title: Simpson's Paradox in Quantity Surveying Practice -Hidden Traps in Elemental Cost Analysis
detail.abstract: This paper is the second in a three-part series examining statistical challenges in construction management research. The series addresses a fundamental problem: construction research routinely aggregates data across heterogeneous groupsprofessional roles, project types, elemental compositions-without testing whether such aggregation is justified. The result can be Simpson's Paradox, where trends reverse when data is properly stratified. Paper 1 introduced the paradox in the context of perception research. It demonstrated how aggregating survey responses across professional groups can mislead researchers and practitioners. Using a detailed case study from a Malaysian condominium project, it introduced non-parametric statistical tests (Kruskal-Wallis, Mann-Whitney, Dunn's test) as tools for determining when aggregation is justified. The paper provided a practical framework for identifying confounders, testing for group differences, presenting stratified results, and triangulating with objective data. Paper 2 (this paper) extends the framework to quantity surveying practice. It examines how Simpson's Paradox affects elemental cost analysis-a core tool for preliminary estimating and cost benchmarking. Even when comparing projects of the same building type, differences in elemental composition (substructure, superstructure, finishes, services) can reverse aggregate cost comparisons. This paper demonstrates the paradox using hypothetical examples and proposes using unit rates and direct standardization as remedies. It argues that aggregate cost per square meter comparisons are unreliable without standardization to target project quantities. Paper 3 provides practical guidance on sample size determination for construction perception studies. It addresses the specific challenges of Malaysian construction research-small project populations, low response rates, uneven professional distributions-and offers a priori power analysis, feasibility-based sampling strategies, and templates for transparent reporting. Together, these papers argue that aggregation in construction research is not a neutral methodological choice but a decision with substantive consequences. By handling aggregation more thoughtfully-using stratified analysis, statistical testing, and direct standardization-we can make construction research more reliable and practice more effective.

detail.abstract: Richard Musgrave et al.'s "Distribution of Tax Payments by Income Groups" (1951) provided the first postwar estimates of the distribution of the fiscal burden, concluding the tax system was not as progressive as statutory rates suggested. Drawing from original archival material, we reconstruct the intellectual context of Musgrave's study, the methodological debates it gave rise to, and assess its legacy in public finance. The study's legacy is examined through the rise of econometric estimation, applied general equilibrium modeling, and microdata-based approaches, as well as its influence on policy institutions in the USA and abroad. Despite major advances in data and modeling, we argue that key issues raised by Musgrave-particularly the definition of the income basis and the incidence of the corporate income tax-remain unresolved. The enduring lack of consensus on a uniquely best method highlights both the empirical and normative challenges at the heart of distributional analysis and explains the study's continued relevance in contemporary debates on taxation and inequality.

title: Caveat Promptor: A Case Study of Tribal Land Descriptions

detail.title: Caveat Promptor: A Case Study of Tribal Land Descriptions
detail.abstract: The paper presents a case study of Tribal land descriptions in which AI models produced text that appears fluent and confident but may be thematically skewed toward biased cultural framing. The authors observed this problem while drafting the 2026 TPI Tribal Lands Broadband Report. Prompted without detailed guidance, models produced outputs organized around heritage, spirituality, and tradition rather than the geographic and infrastructure characteristics appropriate for broadband planning. The paper argues that this output poses a practical risk for any domain in which AI-generated text may be applied without careful review and demonstrates that structured prompting can redirect outputs toward task relevance. The problem, while real, is largely addressable at the prompt level.

title: Completing Capitalism: the DGO Proposal

detail.title: Completing Capitalism: the DGO Proposal

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: Self

detail.abstract:
Imagine a world wherein AI agents produce all goods and services, thereby putting all human beings out of work.  One policy response is a Universal Basic Income, wherein persons are due an unconditional living income when forces beyond their control take their livelihood.  More accurately however, in any such economy fewer persons would work at for-profit businesses and more would work for state agencies and “DGO”s.  DGOs are any voluntary donor-funded organization that coordinates services to people and projects who cannot pay for the service.  Accordingly, this paper proposes an alternative to a universal basic income: give each citizen a tax-funded account with which to donate to DGOs.  The aim is to meet human needs not met by other institutions.  Account donations are motivated either by a conception of the public good or by caring for the persons served.  

The significant DGO tax funding must be morally justified.  Corporations seek productive efficiency, while state agencies carry out the political majority’s right-to-rule.  The DGO funding donations are justified by the “ethics of care”. 

An apparent concern with the proposal is that there would be an explosion of illegitimate DGO claimants on the gifting funds.  The fix is to make the gifting accounts double entry, with both positive and negative dollars.  Popular services would attract positive dollars, while only justified services could avoid negative dollars. 

The DGO proposal radically restructures the primary institutions of capitalism.  There are three practical and moral benefits: 1) financially enhanced DGOs could hire workers laid off by AI; 2) unlike a UBI that hands people money to support their own private consumption, DGOs explicitly coordinate collective outcomes; and 3) the personal agency of account gifting complements the personal agency of democratic voting.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether growth volatility mediates the relationship between financial development and economic crisis risk in emerging and developing economies. Using a panel of 94 countries over 2000-2022, we estimate a Generalised Structural Equation Model (GSEM) combining a linear specification for growth volatility and a logit model for crisis incidence. The results show that financial development significantly reduces growth volatility, while higher volatility increases the probability of crisis. Consistent with this mechanism, the indirect effect of financial development on crisis risk through growth volatility is negative and statistically significant based on bootstrap inference. A direct stabilising effect of financial development is also identified, indicating a complementary mediation structure in which financial deepening reduces crisis risk both directly and indirectly via macroeconomic stabilisation. These findings are robust to alternative crisis definitions and volatility measures. The results highlight growth volatility as a key transmission channel linking financial development to economic stability, with important implications for financial sector policy in developing economies.

detail.abstract: This dissertation develops and tests the Reactive Market Hypothesis (RMH), which argues that asset prices are shaped less by information flow than by collective reactions to it. To operationalise this, a Market Reaction Index (MRI) is constructed from SENT, VOLU, VOLA, and DEVI, using data from January 2023 to June 2025. The MRI behaves as a coherent market-level gauge, that is stationary, persistent at short horizons, heteroskedastic, and predictive of realised volatility. Granger Causality analysis shows that VOLU, VOLA and DEVI forecast volatility, while return predictability emerges only at 5–10-day lags. SENT contributes little direct predictive content, consistent with its role as a trailing indicator of market states (Tetlock, 2007). Behavioural regime analysis further links extreme MRI scores to distinct emotional states, situating RMH as a behavioural complement of Efficient Market Hypothesis (Fama, 1970) and Adaptive Market Hypothesis (Lo, 2004), while extending insights on overreaction and loss aversion (De Bondt and Thaler, 1985; Kahneman and Tversky, 1979; Shiller, 2003).

title: The Logic of Communism: The Sublation of Labor Force Commodification and the Return of Human Essence【共产主义的运行逻辑：劳动力要素化的扬弃与人的复归】

detail.title: The Logic of Communism: The Sublation of Labor Force Commodification and the Return of Human Essence【共产主义的运行逻辑：劳动力要素化的扬弃与人的复归】

publicationDetails.detailsText: The Logic of Communism: The Sublation of Labor Force Commodification and the Return of Human Essence. Zenodo, Preprint, 19 April 2026, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19650043

detail.abstract:
This article is the core concluding chapter of the book The Shackles of Factors. Breaking away from the traditional perception that regards communism as a moral ideal or a vague promise about the future, it argues from the perspective of the historical dialectics of labor force factorization that communism is the inevitable end of the millennia-long historical process in which labor force has been alienated and dominated, and the only way out for human civilization to escape the self-destructive fate of capitalist logic.

 

The article first sorts out the complete historical context of labor force factorization: from the initial separation of labor force at the end of primitive society, to its resourceization in slave society, personal attachment in feudal society, commodification in industrial capitalism, and comprehensive penetration into all spheres of life in digital capitalism. The essence of this process is the continuous loss of workers' control over their own labor capacity. The core mission of communism is not to reform the forms of factorization, but to completely sublate labor force factorization itself, so that labor force is no longer arranged as a passive factor of production.

 

On this basis, the article puts forward three core propositions of communist relations of production: consciousness becomes the main form of labor force, tools take over the specific execution processes, and labor is partially liberated from social production. By distinguishing the superstructure attribute and the productive force attribute of consciousness, the article points out that when advanced tools such as artificial intelligence take over all repetitive and executive labor, the unique human abilities of consciousness, judgment and decision-making will become the only core variable of production. Tools can only amplify the value of living labor but cannot create value—a principle that has not only not failed but has become even more prominent under the new conditions of productive forces.

 

The article innovatively divides production into two categories: social production and life-oriented production. The former serves the overall interests of the community, can only be organized through equal consultation due to the non-coercibility of consciousness, and is completely decoupled from personal rewards. The latter is individual free activity liberated from social coercion, where workers can produce independently according to their own interests and needs, generating only use value rather than value. This distinction systematically addresses classic theoretical dilemmas such as Marx's vision of "free individuals", the finiteness of resources, and the relationship between specialists and generalists, and reconstructs the connotation of "from each according to his ability, to each according to his needs". "From each according to his ability" means contributing non-quantifiable consciousness and judgment, while "to each according to his needs" does not mean the social distribution of products, but that workers independently access public means of production to produce what they need for themselves.

 

The article further distinguishes between formal liberation and substantive liberation: the former is to improve the situation of workers within the framework of factorization, while the latter is to completely dismantle the institutional framework of factorization and regain actual control over the production of labor force. Finally, the article demonstrates the historical inevitability of communism from the height of civilization survival: under the conditions of highly developed productive forces, capitalist logic will inevitably lead to two dead ends—either absolute overproduction and civilization's intolerance of productive capacity caused by the expansion of the workplace, or consciousness colonization and existential destruction caused by the shift to the life sphere. The historical mission of the proletariat has thus been endowed with a new dimension: not only to liberate itself, but also to undertake the responsibility of saving human civilization.

 

The article ultimately points out that communism is not the end of history, but the beginning of truly human history. Only when labor force factorization is completely sublated and labor becomes the life activity of man itself will humanity for the first time step from the "realm of necessity" into the "realm of freedom", ending the millennia-long "prehistoric period" of being dominated.

title: Beyond Inventory Logic: Social Stress Indicators and Demand Forecasting in Consumer Supply Chains

detail.title: Beyond Inventory Logic: Social Stress Indicators and Demand Forecasting in Consumer Supply Chains

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: This paper argues that demand forecasting in consumer supply chains should not be treated as a purely technical exercise. Mainstream logistics models are often built around historical sales patterns, inventory logic and algorithmic optimisation. That orientation is useful, but it can understate how demand is shaped by social conditions such as labour-market insecurity, household stress and income volatility. To bridge logistics and sociology, the paper develops a socio-technical forecasting framework and tests it in a proof-of-concept experiment using 202 quarterly observations of U.S. macroeconomic demand data available through the statsmodels macrodata dataset. Quarterly real consumption growth is used as a proxy for demand faced by consumergoods supply chains, while a household stress index is constructed from unemployment and real disposable-income growth. A baseline ARIMA model is compared with a sociotechnical SARIMAX model that incorporates the stress index. In a 12-quarter out-ofsample test covering 2006 Q4 to 2009 Q3, the socio-technical model reduces RMSE from 0.706 to 0.578 and MAE from 0.569 to 0.458, showing that social stress improves forecast performance during turbulent periods. The contribution of the paper is twofold: conceptually, it reframes forecasting as a social as well as technical problem; empirically, it demonstrates that even a simple social indicator can improve demand forecasts when instability matters most.

title: Fertility Responses to Canada's Paid Parental Leave Expansion
affiliations: University of Toronto ,  and University of Toronto

detail.title: Fertility Responses to Canada's Paid Parental Leave Expansion
detail.abstract: Canada doubled paid and protected parental leave for parents of children born after December 30th, 2000, creating an eligibility cutoff that has been widely used as a quasi-experiment. We study fertility dynamics around this reform using new administrative data. The policy was announced 14 months in advance, allowing families to delay fertility. Consistent with this, we document an immediate reduction in conceptions after the announcement: in the latter half of 2000, births among benefit-eligible mothers were 8% lower than a predicted counterfactual, followed by a relative boom after implementation. Fertility responses were strongest near the cutoff, exhibiting a 25%-30% discontinuity in births among benefit claimants. Placebo checks support a causal interpretation. Timing responses were strongest among high-income mothers and higher-order births, where the discontinuity in births was up to 47%, consistent with financial incentives and salience. These patterns underscore the sensitivity of fertility timing to financial incentives and have implications for research that assumes no such responsiveness.

title: On-chain Peak Shaving
affiliations: Cornell University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University SAIS, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University, Johns Hopkins University and Johns Hopkins University

detail.title: On-chain Peak Shaving
detail.abstract: Blockchain technology is widely expected to reduce transaction costs by automating contract enforcement and eliminating intermediaries; yet, the execution costs imposed by network congestion have received little attention in the operations management literature. We study on-chain peak shaving, the systematic scheduling of Ethereum transactions toward low-congestion windows to reduce gas fee exposure. We use transaction-level data from seven firms across seven industries (N = 62,142 transactions, January-March 2026). Gas fees vary significantly throughout the day: the peak-hour premium at 10 AM Eastern Time reaches $0.220 per transaction above the overnight baseline (t = 12.33, p ¡ 0.001), driven primarily by speculative-arbitrage demand rather than operational activity. Firm-level scheduling responses are heterogeneous and not uniformly disciplined. Only three of seven firms transact disproportionately during off-peak hours; four transact counter-cyclically, concentrated in peak windows due to external deadlines or governance cycles. This heterogeneity is explained by two moderators: transaction deferrability and gas intensity. We formalize these into an On-Chain Scheduling Matrix that maps firms to four regimes: 1) full peak shaving, 2) selective peak shaving, 3) cost provisioning, and 4) accept-market-rate, with regime membership predicting both fee savings and residual cost floors (40.7%-92.5% of actual expenditure). Theoretically, we extend Transaction Cost Economics to account for time-varying execution costs imposed by congestion externalities. In addition to extending Williamson's original cost taxonomy, we introduce a dual classification of gas fees as execution costs in timing but maladaptation costs in origin. The findings reposition on-chain gas-fee management alongside energy procurement and foreign exchange hedging as a domain requiring systematic operational planning.

title: On the Limits of Moral Surrender to AI

detail.title: On the Limits of Moral Surrender to AI
detail.abstract: If people surrender to AI on cognitive tasks, do they also surrender morally? In a preregistered, incentive-compatible, between-subjects experiment (N ≈ 600), participants receive prosocial or antisocial behavioral advice attributed to an AI system, to a human source, or to no source, and then make consequential choices in three paradigms: a non-strategic other-regarding allocation, a strategic cooperation decision, and a private (dis)honesty decision under time pressure. AI moral influence is large, directional, and asymmetric. Prosocial AI advice raises other-regarding transfers substantially; antisocial AI advice fails to push behavior downward even as participants verbally acknowledge the recommendation; antisocial human advice likewise fails to reproduce the downward contagion that fifteen years of human peer-effect research would predict. Within the AI source, the prosocial shift exceeds the antisocial shift by a sizeable margin, inverting the antisocial-dominance regularity that defines live-peer behavioral contagion. Five independent evidence tracks converge on the same contrast: behavioral choice, LLM-based semantic classification of open-ended justifications, an independent human-coder validation study that replicates the endorsement asymmetry at a magnitude larger than the LLM, a rule-based prosocial-vocabulary dictionary, and unsupervised topic modeling. AI moral influence is directional because it is confirmatory rather than overriding: AI supplies a permission structure for actions that already align with private moral preference, but it cannot supply the community standing required to push agents against their own moral compass.

detail.abstract: Perkembangan pesat teknologi kecerdasan buatan (AI) dan automasi telah mentransformasikan struktur pasaran buruh global, termasuk di Malaysia dan khususnya Sabah. Walaupun penggunaan algoritma dalam pengurusan tenaga kerja meningkatkan kecekapan operasi, ia turut menimbulkan kebimbangan berkaitan bias algoritma yang berpotensi menghakis prinsip keadilan dan kesaksamaan dalam pekerjaan. Artikel ini bertujuan untuk mensintesis literatur sedia ada mengenai bias algoritma dan implikasinya terhadap hak pekerja, dengan penekanan kepada peranan kesatuan sekerja di Sabah. Menggunakan pendekatan ulasan naratif, artikel ini menilai sumber daripada pangkalan data utama seperti Scopus, Web of Science, dan Google Scholar bagi tempoh 2015–2025. Analisis tematik mengenal pasti empat tema utama: (i) landskap konseptual bias algoritma dan impaknya secara global; (ii) realiti empirikal dan faktor penyumbang dalam konteks tempatan; (iii) kapasiti institusi kesatuan sekerja; dan (iv) kerangka dasar serta perundangan. Dapatan menunjukkan bahawa bias algoritma bukan sahaja memperkukuh ketidaksamaan sedia ada, tetapi juga mencabar mekanisme perlindungan pekerja tradisional. Dalam konteks Sabah, keterbatasan struktur ekonomi dan kapasiti institusi memperburuk risiko ini. Artikel ini menegaskan keperluan reformasi dasar, peningkatan literasi digital kesatuan sekerja, dan pendekatan kolaboratif pelbagai pihak bagi memastikan perlindungan hak pekerja dalam era digital.

title: Organized Crime and Innovation: Insights from Sicilian Farms
affiliations: , University of Palermo and D'Annunzio University of Chieti

detail.title: Organized Crime and Innovation: Insights from Sicilian Farms
detail.abstract: This study investigates the impact of organized crime on the innovation capacity of farms in Sicily. Organized crime can hinder innovation through various channels, including money laundering and credit availability, illegal imposition or offer of private protection, and distorted public procurement. This creates an environment in which innovation is no longer a profitable strategy for farms in areas with a high prevalence of mafia. To investigate this issue, we examine the influence of organized crime intensity on various aspects of farm innovation. The analysis is based on data from the "Rete di Informazione Contabile Agricola" (RICA), which collects detailed information on Italian farms annually. For this purpose, we utilize an extensive dataset covering all Sicilian provinces from 2008 to 2024. The results suggest that in Sicilian provinces with high mafia activity, farms struggle to upgrade their technical capital, particularly in response to an unstable institutional environment. This finding indicates that exposure to a socially corrupt institutional framework may significantly limit farms' ability to innovate, at least from a technological standpoint.

detail.title: Anticipation, Not Diversion: Import Front-Running and Supply Chain Incumbency in India's Response to the 2025 US Tariff Shock
detail.abstract: This paper examines India's response to the April 2025 US tariff shock using monthly bilateral import data for seven Asian suppliers, January 2023 to December 2025. A panel difference-indifferences design documents a pre-shock anticipation pattern: India's share rose 4.26 percentage points before Liberation Day, though the coefficient does not survive exact wild cluster bootstrap correction for the seven-country panel. India's pre-existing chapter-level market share explains 68% of cross-sectional variation in post-shock diversion capture rates (exact permutation p = 0.0055, N = 8 chapters), dominating both sector classification and the Product Complexity Index. India captured only 10% of China's 20.3 percentage-point loss despite the most favorable tariff differential among major suppliers. The findings characterize India's response as incumbency-gated and partly anticipatory.

title: Sound Analysis? Investing Podcasts and Investor Information Processing
affiliations: , University of Georgia - Terry College of Business, Texas Christian University and Texas A&M University - Department of Accounting

detail.title: Sound Analysis? Investing Podcasts and Investor Information Processing
detail.abstract: Despite the rapid growth of podcasts as a source of investment information, we know little about their potential capital market effects. We find that the release of podcasts that provide listeners with firm-specific investment analysis is associated with significant increases in trading activity, particularly among retail investors. When released following earnings announcements, investing podcasts appear to provide information to less-informed investors that helps them better process the news, as podcast discussion is associated with reductions in information asymmetry. This effect is stronger for podcasts that include guests, have greater narrative distinctiveness across speakers, convey information more rapidly, and focus more on topics related to fundamental analysis. Podcast discussion is also associated with faster price formation and heightened earnings response coefficients. We find no evidence that podcast discussion is associated with return reversals. Overall, our results are consistent with investing podcasts helping investors to more effectively process information and provide novel evidence on how this emerging technology is impacting capital markets.

title: Market Dynamics and Interconnectivity of Diverse Asset Classes: A Comprehensive Analysis of Reliance Industries, Silver, Silver BeES, and Crude Oil

detail.title: Market Dynamics and Interconnectivity of Diverse Asset Classes: A Comprehensive Analysis of Reliance Industries, Silver, Silver BeES, and Crude Oil
detail.abstract: This study looks at how the market works how prices have changed over time and how big economic events affect four financial things: Crude Oil, physical Silver, Nippon India Silver ETF, which is also known as Silver BeES and the stock of Reliance Industries Limited or RIL for short. As the world economy deals with the 2026 financial situation with changing money policies, unsure politics and a move to cleaner energy it is more important than ever to understand how different types of investments behave. This is so we can make investment plans. The study uses data from 2015 to early 2026 looks at trends and checks basic economic ideas to see what makes commodities, special funds and big company stocks work. It finds out that crude oil is still a factor in making prices rise and can really hurt countries that import a lot, like India. Safe investments like silver and Silver BeES have helped protect against rising prices and have made a lot of money over the years. At the time Reliance Industries, which shows how well Indian companies are doing has been strong but also sometimes weak because of changing commodity prices and what people think about the market. This research gives an honest look at these investments offers fair ideas checks the risks and thinks about why it is necessary to spread investments across different types to manage money well. The study of Crude Oil, Silver, Nippon India Silver ETF or Silver BeES and Reliance Industries Limited stock provides a lot of information, about how these financial things work and how they can affect each other. It is important to understand how Crude Oil, Silver, Nippon India Silver ETF or Silver BeES and Reliance Industries Limited stock behave so we can make good investment decisions.

title: FIRM'S RESILIENCE, REAL OPTIONS AND LIABILITY OPTIONS: A THEORICAL MODEL
affiliations: Sapienza University of Rome and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: FIRM'S RESILIENCE, REAL OPTIONS AND LIABILITY OPTIONS: A THEORICAL MODEL
detail.abstract: This paper marks an initial effort to develop a new theoretical framework that models how firms withstand shocks, using a real options approach and considering stakeholder rights during processes of firm reconfiguration. First, our modeling is based on the degree of real options exploitation as a function of the firm's ability to offset the dynamic of sales revenues with operating costs dynamic; second, we extend real options, as tools for responding to shocks, through the concept of liability options, the latter being expression of asymmetric rights of firm's stakeholders. The examination of the extent to which real options are exercised from an internal standpoint, combined with the extension of Real Options Theory to encompass liability options, provides a first conceptual framework for understanding how firms' responses to shocks give rise to positive or negative externalities. This result lays the groundwork for a deeper understanding of value creation under conditions of instability, and of how the micro-dynamics of individual firms fit into a broader systemic mosaic. Within this mosaic, the costs and benefits produced by each firm's reaction to shocks emerge from the interplay between contingent assets and contingent liabilities that link individual behavior to collective outcomes.

detail.abstract: This research is a three-year real-life social experiment designed to observe behavioral changes in a natural social environment. The study analyzed the complex relationships between attention, financial interaction, and responsibility. Researchers deliberately manipulated levels of social access, emotional reactions, and financial support to observe how the behavior of individuals and groups changes. The findings suggest that attention often leads to initial attachment, financial accessibility reveals hidden intentions, and relationship stability depends on mutual responsibility rather than mere emotional expression. This study provides a new behavioral framework for understanding human relationships through the 'AMR model.'

title: From Utility Maximisation to Optimal Capital Market Line Allocation: A Unified Derivation, Empirical Calibration, and Benchmark Comparison

detail.title: From Utility Maximisation to Optimal Capital Market Line Allocation: A Unified Derivation, Empirical Calibration, and Benchmark Comparison

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently as part of undergraduate coursework at MEDTECH – South Mediterranean University, Tunis, Tunisia.

detail.abstract: This paper provides a self-contained, rigorous treatment of mean-variance portfolio optimisation under the Capital Market Line (CML) framework. Starting from the von Neumann-Morgenstern expected-utility axioms, we derive the closed-form optimal risky-asset allocation y* = (E[R m ]-R f) / (A • σ 2 m) via a six-step first-order condition. We then calibrate the framework on parameters consistent with the U.S. equity market (S&P 500, 2019-2024)-using annualised excess returns of 8.55%, a market volatility of 18.20%, and a risk-free rate of 5.25% (Damodaran, 2024; FRED DTB3)-and compute optimal allocations for eight investor risk-aversion profiles (A = 1 to 10). A novel contribution of this paper is a welfare-cost analysis quantifying the certainty-equivalent return lost when an investor naively holds 100% risky assets instead of the theoretically optimal y*. We further benchmark the CML-optimal strategy against four well-known alternatives: equal-weight (1/N), minimum-variance, risk parity, and the market index, and demonstrate that the classical framework remains competitive with modern quantitative methods. A sensitivity heatmap across the equity risk premium and market-volatility parameter space provides intuition for how macroeconomic regimes alter optimal allocations. The paper is accompanied by a fully reproducible Python implementation.

title: Greed, Power, and Opportunity Cost: An Intuitive Political Economy Dilemma in African Economies

detail.title: Greed, Power, and Opportunity Cost: An Intuitive Political Economy Dilemma in African Economies
detail.abstract: This policy brief explores why Africa continues to face development problems despite having abundant natural and human resources. It uses a political economy lens to explain how greed, power, and opportunity cost shape resource allocation, governance, and long-term development outcomes across African economies. The analysis shows that greed, often manifested through rent-seeking behavior and corruption, contributes to the misallocation of public and natural resources away from productive development uses toward private or elite gains. This weakens public investment and reduces long-term economic efficiency. At the same time, power structures and weak institutions determine how resources are controlled and distributed, often reinforcing inequality and limiting access to opportunities for the broader population. The concept of opportunity cost is used to explain the long-term consequences of policy and economic decisions. When governments prioritize short-term political gains such as excessive military spending, patronage systems, or prestige projects they reduce investment in critical sectors like education, healthcare, and infrastructure, thereby slowing long-term development and structural transformation. The brief further highlights that these trade-offs are evident in key policy choices, including military spending versus education, resource extraction versus diversification, and patronage versus institutional reform. Overall, it concludes that Africa's development challenge is primarily rooted in distorted incentives and institutional weaknesses rather than resource scarcity or low human capital. Strengthening accountability, improving governance, and reallocating resources toward inclusive and productive sectors are essential for achieving sustainable and equitable development across African economies.

title: Applied Financial History: Expanding the Vision of Modern Finance

detail.title: Applied Financial History: Expanding the Vision of Modern Finance
detail.abstract:
This paper argues that modern finance contains structural limitations that materially impair decision-making, particularly under conditions that most influence long-term outcomes. These limitations are not incidental—they are systematic. Specifically, the paper identifies two especially costly blind spots. First, financial models are predominantly calibrated to explain behavior in stable, observable environments, which renders them least reliable in the rare but consequential events that disproportionately shape economic and market outcomes. Second, regulatory and governance frameworks often fail to recognize how evolving incentives transform institutional behavior over time, allowing risk to accumulate through gradual but predictable forms of drift that remain largely undetected until their consequences are realized.

Financial history functions as an indispensable, yet routinely neglected, corrective mechanism. By focusing on recurring structural patterns rather than statistical frequency, it provides insight precisely when conventional models prove least reliable and reveals how incentive systems evolve in ways that alter the function of financial institutions. Without this perspective, decision-making frameworks remain systematically vulnerable to misinterpreting the environments that most influence long-term outcomes.

The paper demonstrates this by presenting three documented cases in which historically grounded analysis identified material risks prior to their recognition by consensus models. These cases provide evidence that model-based frameworks systematically fail to identify critical risks in the environments that matter most—and that financial history provides a necessary framework for addressing this limitation.

title: Private Credit as a Structural Allocation

detail.title: Private Credit as a Structural Allocation
detail.abstract:
Private credit is often framed as a yield-driven substitute for bank lending or public credit. This paper argues that such framing misidentifies the primary determinant of long-term outcomes. As private credit has matured into a structural allocation for institutional portfolios, performance dispersion is explained less by entry yield or strategy labels than by governance capability: covenant design, information rights, monitoring intensity, and the capacity to intervene during borrower underperformance. 
The paper develops a governance-centered framework for evaluating private credit, emphasizing “control without ownership” as its distinguishing institutional mechanism—positioned between public credit’s reliance on market exit and private equity’s ownership-based control. A comparison table clarifies how control, governance intensity, and failure modes differ across these asset classes, while a stylized amend-and-extend vignette illustrates where governance becomes observable across the cycle. The paper closes with implications for manager selection, portfolio oversight, and the limits of financial innovation efforts—including tokenization—that seek to increase liquidity or transferability without preserving the governance mechanisms that underpin credit outcomes.

title: From Data to Action: Advancing Youth Skills Development and Employment in Africa through Evidence-Informed Decision-Making

detail.title: From Data to Action: Advancing Youth Skills Development and Employment in Africa through Evidence-Informed Decision-Making
detail.abstract: Africa's rapidly growing youth population presents both a significant development opportunity and a persistent policy challenge, particularly in the context of high unemployment and underemployment. While substantial investments have been made in youth skills development and employment initiatives, outcomes remain uneven, raising concerns about the effectiveness of existing approaches. This study employs a qualitative systematic review design to examine how evidence-informed decision-making shapes youth employment interventions in Africa, with a focus on the systems through which evidence is generated, shared, and utilized. The analysis draws on a synthesis of policy documents, secondary literature, and field-based insights to identify patterns in evidence use and institutional practice. The study demonstrates that the primary constraint is not the lack of data, but the weak integration and functioning of evidence systems. Fragmented data ecosystems, limited participation of youth in knowledge generation, weak institutionalization of evidence use, and persistent misalignment between skills development and labour market demands emerge as interconnected challenges that undermine program effectiveness. At the same time, emerging participatory and digital approaches show potential for strengthening adaptive and inclusive evidence systems. The study contributes to the literature by advancing a systems-oriented perspective on evidence-informed decision-making, emphasizing the interaction between institutional capacity, participation, and coordination. It argues that improving youth employment outcomes requires moving beyond data generation toward strengthening the governance of evidence systems. These findings offer important implications for policymakers and development practitioners seeking to design more responsive, inclusive, and sustainable youth employment interventions.

detail.abstract:
This study examines the various factors influencing academic performance among students at SMSG Jain Degree College. The research focuses on key variables such as study habits, attendance, teaching methods, and the impact of technology. Primary data was collected from 50 students belonging to mixed courses (B.Com and BCA) through a structured questionnaire.

The findings reveal that students who maintain regular study habits and higher attendance perform better academically. Additionally, excessive mobile usage negatively affects students’ concentration and learning outcomes. The study also highlights the importance of practical teaching methods and family support in improving academic performance.

The research concludes by providing practical suggestions for students and educational institutions to enhance academic performance and create an effective learning environment.

detail.title: NJMs as Interventions in Fields of Struggle

detail.abstract: This chapter takes the power struggles around grievance claims as central, not peripheral, to whether and how NJMs can contribute to redress. We build a distinctive conceptual approach: a ‘fields of struggle’ lens to capture the way transformative agendas are heavily dependent on wider processes of economic, social and political struggle. This lens draws from sociological scholarship on fields together with work by political economists and economic sociologists that highlight the centrality of power inequalities to regulatory outcomes. Our concept is further strengthened by recognising the specific forms of business, state, and civil society power and agency available within each field. A field of struggle lens brings to light how these varying kinds of power are drawn into regulatory struggles, and the ways the socially embedded interests of participants in regulatory processes shape how such power is harnessed strategically within struggles over grievance, and to what end.

title: Exploring the Dynamics of Trade Openness, External Debt, and Economic Growth in Somalia: Evidence from a Vector Error Correction Model (VECM)

detail.title: Exploring the Dynamics of Trade Openness, External Debt, and Economic Growth in Somalia: Evidence from a Vector Error Correction Model (VECM)
detail.abstract:
ABSTRACT
This study empirically investigates the influence of trade openness and external debt on economic growth in Somalia from 1990–2022, utilising a vector error correction model (VECM). The findings confirm a consistent long-term link among the factors. Trade openness exerts a substantial negative long-term effect on growth, indicative of structural limitations such as reliance on imports and inadequate export capability, but external debt demonstrates a negative albeit negligible influence. Conversely, foreign direct investment fosters long-term growth, whereas inflation adversely affects growth in the short term. The results indicate that sustainable growth necessitates structural reforms, enhanced institutions, and superior macroeconomic management.
IMPACT STATEMENT
This report presents a comprehensive analysis of trade openness, external debt, and economic growth in Somalia, delivering critical insights for vulnerable economies. The findings indicate a "trade openness paradox," wherein heightened global integration does not inherently promote growth due to structural deficiencies. It demonstrates that external debt alone cannot stimulate growth without proficient management and robust institutions. This study critiques traditional development assumptions by underscoring the necessity for export diversification, enhancement of domestic capacities, and better governance. The findings provide pragmatic, evidence-supported recommendations for governments pursuing sustainable and resilient economic growth.

title: Crowdfunding in Tunisia - Observations on the impact of regulation on platform behaviour
affiliations: University of Hamburg - Faculty of Business, Economics, and Social Sciences, , Tunis Business School ,  University of Tunis, and Hamburg Universität - Institut für Recht und Ökonomik

detail.title: Crowdfunding in Tunisia - Observations on the impact of regulation on platform behaviour

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Karsten Wenzlaff worked as an external consultant for the Financial Services Volunter Corps (FSVC) based in New York and its local branch, FSVC Tunisia, between 2021 and 2024. Khaoula Behi studied the Tunisian Crowdfunding ecosystem and its development as part of her university studies at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg. She has worked as an external consultant to the Hanns-Seidel Foundation in Tunisia. Fatma Hakim conducted her research as part of her studies at the Tunis Business School-University of Tunis. Parts of this article are based on an earlier article in which she used Kiva-Loans to benchmark the potential for crowdfunding in Tunisia. Fatma Hakim was an employee of the Financial Services Volunter Corps (FSVC), based in New York, and its local branch, FSVC Tunisia. Ana Odorovic has worked as an external consultant to the Financial Services Volunter Corps (FSVC) based in New York and its local branch, FSVC Tunisia for a workshop in 2021. She has previously researched on Fintech development in southern Europe.

detail.abstract:
The paper describes the development of the Crowdfunding Law in Tunisia and assesses its potential impact on market development.  Tunisia has approved the crowdfunding law in 2021, and since then has created the implementation regulations, which provide further guidelines on licencing requirements. Tunisia is one of the very few countries in which donation-based and reward-based crowdfunding are subject to licence.

The paper adopts Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Theory and Actor-Network-Theory to describe the different phases of the development of the ecosystem in Tunisia. Prior to the enactment of the legislation, certain crowdfunding platforms were already operational in Tunisia; nevertheless, they halted operations following the law's implementation. The re-establishment of the crowdfunding ecosystem required several years, attributable to the regulatory implementation laws.

The crowdfunding literature has established a positive impact of a bespoke crowdfunding regime on market growth, which is due to increased regulatory certainty and better compliance with investor protection. The case study of Tunisia presented in this paper casts doubts on this Theory of Regulatory Certainty, which posits that clear regulation by itself leads to market growth.

The paper contributes to the literature by offering the first comprehensive analysis of crowdfunding regulations in Tunisia, including implementation laws. The paper draws on practical insights gained through working closely with the regulators on crowdfunding regulations and interviewing the regulators on the re-emergence of the ecosystem. In addition, the paper puts the Tunisian crowdfunding regulation in comparison with the Moroccan, US, and European crowdfunding regulations.
