title: Gamifying Legal Education: Integrating Kahoot and AI-Supported Pedagogy to Enhance Engagement and Learning Outcomes in Corporate Law

detail.title: Gamifying Legal Education: Integrating Kahoot and AI-Supported Pedagogy to Enhance Engagement and Learning Outcomes in Corporate Law
detail.abstract: Legal education has long been characterised by doctrinal rigidity and passive learning approaches that often fail to engage contemporary students. This paper examines a pedagogical intervention implemented in the LAWS200 Business Organisations unit at an Australian law school, which integrated gamification through Kahoot and artificial intelligence (AI)-supported content development using GROK AI. Drawing on constructivist learning theory and empirical student feedback, the study evaluates the effectiveness of these tools in enhancing engagement, participation, and conceptual understanding. The findings demonstrate that gamified learning environments, when combined with AI-assisted scenario design, significantly improve student experience and accessibility. The paper argues that digital pedagogy, when thoughtfully implemented, offers a transformative pathway for modern legal education.

title: Integrated Contextual Practice Theory (ICPT): A Mid-Range Socio-Mathematical Model of Adaptive Behavior

detail.title: Integrated Contextual Practice Theory (ICPT): A Mid-Range Socio-Mathematical Model of Adaptive Behavior
detail.abstract:
The “value–action gap”—where individuals fail to act in accordance with their own beliefs—remains a persistent challenge across the social sciences. Existing theoretical frameworks often interpret such behavior as inconsistency or hypocrisy, yet struggle to explain rapid behavioral shifts under conditions of acute real-world stress.

This paper introduces the Integrated Contextual Practice Theory (ICPT), a socio-mathematical model that reconceptualizes individuals as “Adaptive Agents.” The model formalizes behavior as a dynamic function of internal drivers—Habitus, Values, and Identity—and external constraints, termed Contextual Stress, operating within a broader Cultural Governor that defines societal permissibility.

A key contribution of the framework is the inclusion of a stability parameter (ε), which ensures mathematical consistency across both high- and zero-stress conditions. By integrating established sociological theory with a formal analytical structure, ICPT provides a parsimonious and generalizable tool for modeling and predicting adaptive human behavior across varying contexts.

title: The Cube Method Beyond Economics

detail.title: The Cube Method Beyond Economics
detail.abstract: The Cube method, introduced by Deville and Tillé (2004) and initially implemented for institutional survey purposes at INSEE (French national statistical institute) in 1999 by Bousabaa, Lieber and Sirolli, has been applied almost exclusively to economic and demographic surveys since its inception. This article proposes a novel application of this balanced random sampling algorithm to the field of computational historical linguistics, approximately thirty years after its original implementation. The research question is the following: "what is the true proportion of French common nouns and adjectives that originate, through the complete etymological chain, from Arabic?" Standard French dictionaries systematically report only the proximate etymological source-often an Italian or Spanish intermediary-thereby concealing the Arabic ultimate origin. We term this phenomenon etymological masking. Using a stratified balanced sample of 500 lemmas drawn from a population of French nouns and adjectives, balanced simultaneously on five auxiliary variables (frequency rank, part of speech, semantic domain, word length and Arabic prefix indicator), the Horvitz-Thompson estimator yields an Arabic-origin rate of 15.4%. This result substantially exceeds the 1-3% figure commonly reported in standard etymological references, and suggests that Arabic is in fact the third most important source language of French vocabulary, after Latin and Proto-Indo-European. The article discusses both the methodological contribution-a rare application of the Cube method outside its original economic domain-and the linguistic implications of the findings.

title: A COMPARATIVE INSTITUTIONAL AND TECHNOLOGICAL ANALYSIS OF INDIA'S UNIFIED PAYMENTS INTERFACE (UPI) AND JAPAN'S PAYMENT ECOSYSTEM: Adoption Dynamics, Structural Constraints, and Cross-Border Future Potential

detail.title: A COMPARATIVE INSTITUTIONAL AND TECHNOLOGICAL ANALYSIS OF INDIA'S UNIFIED PAYMENTS INTERFACE (UPI) AND JAPAN'S PAYMENT ECOSYSTEM: Adoption Dynamics, Structural Constraints, and Cross-Border Future Potential

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: The global transition toward cashless economies presents a clear paradox: India, an emerging economy with persistent infrastructure deficits, achieved nearly universal digital payment penetration within a decade of launching its Unified Payments Interface (UPI), while Japanamong the world's most technologically advanced societies-continues to conduct over 60% of consumer transactions in cash. This paper offers a comparative institutional and technological analysis of UPI and Japan's multi-layered payment ecosystem, examining adoption patterns, systemic barriers, and potential for cross-border cooperation. Drawing upon a synthesis of peer-reviewed literature, official government policy documents from India's NPCI and Japan's METI, BIS payment statistics, and critical platform theory-including Steinberg's (2025) analysis of PayPay's "cashless payment wars"-this study argues that UPI's success cannot be explained by technological superiority alone. Rather, it reflects the combination of three key factors: the institutional shock of demonetization in 2016, an open-architecture API framework that eliminated entry barriers for fintech innovation, and deliberate policy design that prioritized financial inclusion over protecting existing revenue models. Japan's continued reliance on cash, by contrast, reflects a structural condition in which deeply embedded payment habits, demographic aging, platform fragmentation, and what Steinberg terms the "existing convenience of cash" collectively resist voluntary cashless transition. Applying the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) as a behavioral analysis framework, this paper introduces the concept of Institutional Disruption Pressure (IDP)-an extended construct capturing whether the adoption environment includes external pressure that pushes adoption and remove behavioral fallbacks. The paper concludes with policy recommendations for India-Japan FinTech collaboration, including a proposed UPI-Zengin realtime interoperability corridor, and offers insights for Japan's Society 5.0 digital inclusion agenda.

title: Markup, Money, and the Price Level: Toward a Post-Keynesian-Marxist Theory of Inflation

detail.title: Markup, Money, and the Price Level: Toward a Post-Keynesian-Marxist Theory of Inflation
detail.abstract: This paper develops a unified Post-Keynesian-Marxist theory of the aggregate price level by integrating Kalecki's markup pricing with Marx's theory of value and the New Interpretation of the monetary expression of labour time (MELT). The central argument is that the aggregate price level is not a veil over relative prices but a distributional variable shaped by class conflict, credit conditions, and the monetary circuit. Markup pricing is reinterpreted as the mechanism through which surplus value is realised in money form: the degree of monopoly is not a behavioural parameter but an index of the balance of class power encoded in production and circulation. The paper formalises the connection between the wage-markup relationship and the MELT, showing that inflation is partly a struggle over the real wage conducted through the price system. The model is extended to incorporate endogenous credit-money, demonstrating that the credit system amplifies distributional conflicts and can generate inflationary or deflationary dynamics depending on the regime of accumulation. Drawing on Minsky's financial instability hypothesis, the analysis identifies distinct monetary regimes and their implications for price level dynamics. The framework offers a more coherent account of stagflation, cost-push inflation, and the limits of inflation targeting than either Post-Keynesian or Marxist theory provides independently.

title: Technological Innovation and the Cross Section of Returns
affiliations: and Technische Universität München (TUM) - TUM School of Management

detail.title: Technological Innovation and the Cross Section of Returns
detail.abstract: We introduce Technological Innovation Novelty (TIN), a text-based measure quantifying each patent's semantic distance from the existing technological frontier. Aggregating to the firm level (FTIN), we find that firms producing market-wide novel innovation earn significantly higher risk-adjusted returns. A value-weighted long-short portfolio generates risk-adjusted returns of up to 53 basis points per month, robust across alternative factor models, the exclusion of microcaps and other innovation based factors. Comparing FTIN to firm-based innovation strategy measures, market-wide novelty and firm-based exploration carry opposing return predictions, confirming they capture distinct pricing dimensions. While prior innovation-based anomalies have been attributed to limited investor attention, the FTIN premium is strongest among well-covered firms with high investor disagreement, consistent with models about heterogeneous beliefs among investors.

title: LARGO: A TRAVEL ASSISTANCE APPLICATION DESIGNED TO EMPOWER FIRST-TIME TRAVELERS BY PROVIDING A STEP-BY-STEP GUIDE TO THEIR DESTINATION An Undergraduate Capstone Project Presented to the Information Technology Education Program Davao Central College Toril, Davao City In Partial Fulfilment of the Requirements in Capstone Project

detail.title: LARGO: A TRAVEL ASSISTANCE APPLICATION DESIGNED TO EMPOWER FIRST-TIME TRAVELERS BY PROVIDING A STEP-BY-STEP GUIDE TO THEIR DESTINATION An Undergraduate Capstone Project Presented to the Information Technology Education Program Davao Central College Toril, Davao City In Partial Fulfilment of the Requirements in Capstone Project
detail.abstract: First-time travelers often experience anxiety and confusion due to unfamiliar routes, transportation systems, pricing uncertainty, and communication barriers. Many rely on fragmented information sources such as social media posts, verbal instructions, or printed guides, which are often inconsistent and difficult to follow during actual travel. This study presents LARGO, a digital travel assistance system designed to support first-time travelers by providing step-by-step travel guidance, transportation options, estimated fare information, visual transfer points, and basic auto-translation features in a single platform. Using a descriptive system development approach, LARGO was designed and implemented to address common travel challenges and improve user confidence. Results from system use and user feedback indicate that LARGO helps simplify navigation, improve access to reliable travel information, and reduce uncertainty during travel.

detail.abstract: Tax administrations increasingly seek cooperation with Small-and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) and their stakeholders for taxpayer supervision to address challenges such as scarce capacity, limited financial resources, and an expanding SME segment. The Netherlands Tax Administration (NTA) introduced a Cooperative Compliance Programme (CCP) to support the voluntary tax compliance behaviour of SMEs. This CCP features a tripartite cooperative relationship between the NTA, the tax intermediary and the SME. Research on CCPs for SMEs remains limited, partly due to the absence of a clear theory, which may hinder further development. Therefore, this exploratory research identifies the underlying principles of SMEs' CCP, forming a basis for further (empirical) research. The NTA assumes SMEs' compliance behaviour is influenced by five principles: a cooperative relationship, the NTAs' service-level, the tax intermediaries' role and quality system, tax audits, and the determinants of (SMEs) compliance. We formalised these principles into a working theory and our analysis shows, some principles contradict academic literature and hence NTA's intended purpose. For example, the indirect relationship between the NTA and the SME raises questions about how the NTA can influence SME behaviour. The dual role of tax intermediaries is another example, as they may face conflicts when serving both the NTA and their SME clients. Furthermore, tax audits usually deter taxpayers from non-compliance but are currently used to assess tax intermediaries' quality systems. Future empirical research on these principles in the context of SMEs' CCP is recommended.

title: Disaggregating the Gender Funding Gap in UK Entrepreneurship: Pipeline Attrition, Sectoral Concentration, and the Limits of Aggregate Measurement

detail.title: Disaggregating the Gender Funding Gap in UK Entrepreneurship: Pipeline Attrition, Sectoral Concentration, and the Limits of Aggregate Measurement
detail.abstract: The persistent assertion that female-founded businesses in the United Kingdom receive approximately 2p for every £1 of venture capital investment has become a widely cited benchmark in policy discourse, media coverage, and academic literature on entrepreneurial finance. This paper critically examines the analytical validity of this aggregate statistic as a measure of gender-based capital access discrimination. Drawing on secondary data analysis of six primary UK datasets — including British Business Bank pipeline data, the Investing in Women Code Annual Reports (2020–2025), Beauhurst high-growth enterprise data, the Rose Review (HM Treasury, 2019), ONS Business Population Estimates, and the Women-Led High-Growth Enterprise Taskforce Report (2024) — this study identifies three analytically separable mechanisms that jointly produce the observed aggregate disparity: (1) a participation gap, whereby female-founded firms enter equity-seeking pathways at substantially lower rates than male-founded counterparts, partly mediated by network access deficits and motivational framing asymmetries; (2) a sector structural gap, whereby female entrepreneurial activity is concentrated in industries that are structurally excluded from the venture capital asset class; and (3) a capital access gap, reflecting genuine differential treatment within investment processes, evidenced by pipeline attrition rates and investor questioning asymmetries documented by Kanze et al. (2018). The paper argues that conflating these three mechanisms within a single aggregate statistic impedes both scholarly understanding and effective policy design. We propose a theoretically grounded analytical decomposition framework and identify five critical data requirements necessary for robust measurement of gender-differentiated capital access in the UK. Implications for policy, investor practice, and future research are discussed.

title: 吞噬 - 存续双因子模型（ES 模型）：系统性经济危机的内生预警与临界相变研究 The Extraction-Survival Dual-Factor Model (ES Model): An Endogenous Early-Warning Framework and Critical Phase-Transition Research for Systemic Economic Crises

detail.title: 吞噬 - 存续双因子模型（ES 模型）：系统性经济危机的内生预警与临界相变研究 The Extraction-Survival Dual-Factor Model (ES Model): An Endogenous Early-Warning Framework and Critical Phase-Transition Research for Systemic Economic Crises

detail.abstract:
主流宏观经济学长期难以有效预警系统性经济危机，传统模型无法刻画危机非线性特征，现有预警框架漏判率高、假阳性频发且跨国不可复现。本文基于存续优先公理与非吞噬原则，构建吞噬 - 存续双因子（ES）极简危机预警模型。
文章构建吞噬指数 Φ、存续指数 D 两大指标，基于 15 个核心经济体 2000-2025 年面板数据，经 ROC 校准得到危机阈值 Φ₀=0.6、Dₘᵢₙ=0.2，建立内生与外生危机判定体系。

模型对 1990-2025 年 11 次核心事件实现零漏判、零假阳性，预警窗口 3-24 个月，稳健性检验结论可靠。依据 2026 年 4 月 IMF 数据预测：2026-2030 年全球经济高脆弱易触发外生危机，中国 2030 年前无系统性经济危机。

title: Automated Public Capitalism: A market-based pathway to public provision in the post-labor economy

detail.title: Automated Public Capitalism: A market-based pathway to public provision in the post-labor economy
detail.abstract: The AI-and robotics-driven automation of production systems is currently led primarily by private firms operating within existing capitalist institutions, raising growing concerns about wealth concentration among the narrow class of capitalists who successfully automate, rising unemployment, and widening disparities in access to essential goods and services. This paper develops a mathematical framework to clarify a central institutional bottleneck of deep automation-how productivity gains translate (or fail to translate) into broadly shared welfare through distribution, demand stabilization, and reliable provision of essential goods. Building on these results, we propose Automated Public Capitalism (APC): a policy regime in which the state acquires verified automation systems from private firms and operates them as auditable public infrastructure, delivering essential services (for example, water, electricity, and staple foods) at lower cost and with more stable access. APC is framed not as a purely redistributive policy, but as an institutional redesign that simultaneously reorients private-sector incentives toward R&D and deployment of automation for public service provision, while enabling the public sector to internalize long-run access, reliability, and accountability. We characterize the conditions under which APC can generate mutually beneficial outcomes for firms, the state, and citizens, and outline the governance and audit requirements that render the framework empirically testable and implementable.

title: Political Uncertainty and Corporate Investment: Evidence from the 2017 Catalonia Referendum
affiliations: University College Dublin and University of Valladolid - Department of Finance and Accounting

detail.title: Political Uncertainty and Corporate Investment: Evidence from the 2017 Catalonia Referendum

declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by project PID2023-150140NA-I00, funded by the Spanish Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities (MCIU), the Spanish Agency for Research (AEI), and the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF).

detail.abstract: We estimate the effect of political uncertainty on corporate investment using the 2017 Catalan independence referendum as a quasi-natural experiment. Applying a doubly robust difference-indifferences design to a large panel of predominantly private Spanish firms for the period 2014-2019, we find that the referendum reduced capital investment by 3.6%, with the effect peaking at 5.3% in the referendum year, but did not affect intangible investment. The decline in capital investment concentrates among firms with more irreversible capital and weaker growth opportunities, consistent with real-options theory. Results are robust to industry composition, geographic spillovers, and a parallel-trends sensitivity analysis.

title: ECOLOGICAL DEGRADATION AND POPULATION DYNAMICS OF MIGRATORY BIRDS AT SURHA TAAL BIRD SANCTUARY

detail.title: ECOLOGICAL DEGRADATION AND POPULATION DYNAMICS OF MIGRATORY BIRDS AT SURHA TAAL BIRD SANCTUARY
detail.abstract: This study examines the critical intersection between habitat quality and avian biodiversity at the Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary (Surha Taal). It identifies environmental degradation—specifically through invasive species proliferation and anthropogenic waste—as a primary driver of shifting population dynamics among migratory species. The research argues for a management paradigm shift that prioritizes ecological timelines over seasonal tourism.

title: GENDER DETERMINANTS OF ECONOMIC INFORMALITY IN IRAQI CITIES: A COMPARATIVE MICROECONOMIC ANALYSIS

detail.title: GENDER DETERMINANTS OF ECONOMIC INFORMALITY IN IRAQI CITIES: A COMPARATIVE MICROECONOMIC ANALYSIS
detail.abstract: This research aims to identify the gender-specific determinants of informality in four Iraqi cities using a comparative microeconomic approach. Using data from the Informal Sector Business Survey in Cities in Iraq, 2021, we construct a multidimensional index of economic informality and analyse its determinants using regressions and Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition. Our results show the existence of two parallel entrepreneurial ecosystems with different informality dynamics. Women have a slightly higher informality index, a turnover 3.6 times lower, and lag significantly in educational attainment. The econometric analysis indicates a differential effectiveness in the determinants of formalisation. Among men, the level of education, business size, and access to banking significantly reduce informality, whereas only access to banking remains significant among women. Microfinance presents a counter-intuitive result with a paradoxical effect: it reduces informality among men but increases it among women. This research contributes to the literature on gendered entrepreneurship in post-conflict economies by demonstrating that the determinants of informality differ by gender.

title: How to boost income mobility in the UK IEA Discussion Paper No.122

detail.title: How to boost income mobility in the UK IEA Discussion Paper No.122
detail.abstract: Many people in Britain argue that income mobility is declining. This applies to all forms of income mobility, as a medicine for this many propose that welfare programmes must expand. We propose that economic freedom is a more effective means of improving income mobility than redistributive policies. This includes strengthening property rights, open trade, lower taxes, and less market regulation. The direct effects of economic freedom are that it reduces barriers to work and indirectly affects growth in a way that is biased towards the penurious. There is new international evidence suggesting that economic freedom promotes intragenerational absolute and relative income mobility. There is rich subnational data from Canada suggesting that economic freedom promotes intragenerational income mobility. There is indirect evidence from economic history, economic geography, and the economics of occupational licensing that confirms the above results. The UK is a middling country in terms of both income mobility and occupational licensing. We highlight two main areas of reform to promote economic freedom to increase the UK's performance in mobility: deregulation in occupational licensing laws and housing restrictions.

detail.abstract: Strategic competition between China and Western countries is increasingly shaping sovereign debt restructuring outcomes, with developing countries bearing the greatest economic and social costs. Sri Lanka’s recent restructuring illustrates how geopolitical fragmentation can stall necessary financing and delay crisis resolution. While Western governments, alongside India and Japan, moved to finalize financing assurances, China withheld support pending its demand that multilateral claims be included in the restructuring framework. The resulting deadlock delayed approval of Sri Lanka’s International Monetary Fund (IMF) program by several months, prolonging macroeconomic instability and slowing recovery. With approximately 27% of countries globally facing debt stress, these obstructions underscore how such power dynamics can exert substantial consequences for developing nations.

title: 2025 Annual Antitrust Report: Class Actions in Federal Court

detail.title: 2025 Annual Antitrust Report: Class Actions in Federal Court
detail.abstract: The 2025 Private Antitrust Enforcement Report provides various empirical analyses of antitrust class actions litigated in federal court from 2009 through 2025. It addresses the number of antitrust class action complaints filed each year, the amount of time on average to reach a settlement, the mean and median recoveries, the attorneys' fees and costs awarded, the total settlement amounts in each year and overall, the law firms that represented plaintiffs and defendants in antitrust class action settlements, the cumulative totals for claims administrators involved in the settlement process, and related information. The Report also distinguishes private antitrust enforcement by industry, by type of claim—conspiracy claims (under Section 1 of the Sherman Act) as opposed to claims based on unilateral conduct (Section 2 of the Sherman Act)—and by type of plaintiff—whether claims were brought on behalf of direct or indirect purchasers. This annual report offers a firmer empirical basis than would otherwise be possible of federal antitrust class actions, including private enforcement of the antitrust laws.

title: The Metabolic Theory of the Economic Organism:Chapter 2: What Is Value? Negentropy, Order, and the Driving Force of Economic Life

detail.title: The Metabolic Theory of the Economic Organism:Chapter 2: What Is Value? Negentropy, Order, and the Driving Force of Economic Life

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: Not applicable.

keywords: law of value JEL Classification: B41

detail.abstract:
This paper is Chapter 2 of the book The Metabolic Theory of the Economic Organism: From the Mechanistic Paradigm to the Living Systems. The complete manuscript of the book is available on SSRN (DOI: 10.2139/ssrn.6456938) and OSF Preprints (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/KPXNY).

This chapter establishes the value-theoretical foundation of the Economic Organism–Metabolism Theory (EOMT) by redefining economic value as negentropy—the capacity of the economic system to generate and maintain ordered structure against entropic decay.

It begins by identifying a shared limitation of existing value theories: while labor, utility, equilibrium, and innovation theories each capture partial mechanisms of value generation, they remain confined to social or behavioral levels and do not address the underlying physical process of value formation.

The chapter then advances the central ontological claim that value is negentropy, understood as a functional isomorphism rather than a metaphor. It clarifies this claim by distinguishing value existence from value realization, rejecting locally entropy-reducing but systemically destructive “pseudo-values,” and emphasizing the multi-layered nature of negentropy across material, informational, and cultural-cognitive dimensions.

A general value expression, Vt = f(Et, It, Ct), is proposed, where material-energy inputs, informational inputs, and circulatory efficiency jointly determine value creation. The framework leaves the functional form open, reinterprets the Solow residual as informational contribution, and identifies circulatory efficiency as a critical but underexplored dimension. Empirical patterns such as the post-2008 liquidity trap, the Soviet efficiency paradox, and stagflation are reinterpreted as cases of circulatory constraint.

Building on this foundation, the chapter develops a five-category typology of value—material, informational, meaning, institutional, and ecological—corresponding to different levels at which negentropy is established. It concludes by reformulating the law of value: prices function as dynamic metabolic signals rather than equilibrium anchors, and economic stability is better understood as homeostasis. This framework provides the conceptual bridge to subsequent analysis of crisis as metabolic imbalance and systemic adjustment.

title: E Pluribus Euro: Minimum Fiscal Capacity for Collective Trade Policy in a Currency Union

detail.title: E Pluribus Euro: Minimum Fiscal Capacity for Collective Trade Policy in a Currency Union
detail.abstract: As major powers deploy trade policy as coercion, what fiscal capacity does a currency union need to sustain a credible collective response? I embed the multi-sector trade model of Caliendo and Parro (2015) into a monetary union with heterogeneous members, calibrated to the world input-output database (WIOD) for 20 individual Eurozone members. A US tariff escalation of 20% plus EU retaliation requires 0.69% of Eurozone GDP (€97 billion); a Chinese critical minerals restriction requires 0.44% (€62 billion); both simultaneously require 1.12% (€157 billion). A substantial share of the fiscal need arises from the asymmetric costs of collective action itself: the costs that EU countertariffs impose on members with concentrated trade exposures. This reframes the fiscal requirement as the price of strategic credibility. Single market deepening generates welfare gains, but barely reduces the fiscal requirement, showing that integration and fiscal capacity are complements. Joint borrowing is needed, as budget-balanced redistribution cannot sustain collective action. However, the headline fiscal requirement is an upper bound. Embedding the model in existing EU institutions (cross-conditionality of EU fiscal flows and qualified majority voting rules) reduces the practical requirement to 0.33% of Eurozone GDP (e46 billion) in the combined scenario, since the EU need only compensate a handful of pivotal large members to prevent a blocking minority.

title: Dynamics of Incomplete Contracts and Sanctions in a Multilateral Game: A Theoretical Consideration of U.S.-Cuba Relations

detail.title: Dynamics of Incomplete Contracts and Sanctions in a Multilateral Game: A Theoretical Consideration of U.S.-Cuba Relations
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the "Maximum Pressure" policy in U.S.-Cuba relations using key mathematical models from corporate finance theory. Specifically, we formalize the presence of external powers (Russia and China) as a problem of asset mobility and borrowing capacity, the transition of administrations as a dynamic of reputational capital, and the intensification of sanctions as an exercise of control rights under incomplete contracts. Our analysis demonstrates how endogenous tariffs (τ) on oil-supplying countries fluctuate the pledgeable income in a multilateral equilibrium, inevitably triggering inefficient sanctions (liquidation).

title: Do Art Market Rankings Cause Future Auction Performance?

detail.title: Do Art Market Rankings Cause Future Auction Performance?
detail.abstract: Rankings are pervasive in asset markets, but whether ordinal labels causally affect future performance remains debated. Using annual regression discontinuity designs at the official Top-100 cutoff of Artprice's Top 500the leading annual ranking of contemporary artists by auction turnover-across 19 editions (2006-2025), we find no discontinuity in next-period auction turnover, prices, or quantities. In the preferred specification with edition fixed effects and artist-clustered standard errors, the 95% confidence interval for log turnover at the cutoff is [-0.161, +0.167], ruling out effects larger than approximately-15% to +18%. Results are confirmed under a continuous turnover-based running variable (CI:-13% to +14%), rank-cell aggregation, and Fisherian local randomization inference. The evidence suggests that, in this illiquid and information-fragmented alternative asset market, rankings primarily reflect underlying fundamentals rather than independently shaping auction outcomes.

title: Tariff Policy with an Exorbitant Privilege

detail.title: Tariff Policy with an Exorbitant Privilege
detail.abstract: We study tariffs in a reserve-currency economy where foreign demand for the dominant transaction asset finances a persistent trade de cit for the issuer and shrinks its tradables sector over time. In this environment, a unilateral import tariff cannot reduce the net real transfer that reserve-currency status finances: the long-run quantity of home imports driven by foreign asset demand is invariant to the tariff. In the benchmark, this also leaves tradables employment and output unchanged; with imperfect substitutability between home and foreign goods, tariffs further reduce home tradables employment. The tariff's main effects are on relative prices, fiscal revenue, and the measured trade-de cit-to-GDP ratio, which falls through a valuation effect rather than real trade rebalancing. This neutrality extends to a multi-country setting with a competing settlement currency and endogenous portfolio choice.

title: The Metabolic Theory of the Economic Organism:Chapter 3: The Anatomy of the Economic Organism: Structures, Organizations, and Nested Hierarchies

detail.title: The Metabolic Theory of the Economic Organism:Chapter 3: The Anatomy of the Economic Organism: Structures, Organizations, and Nested Hierarchies

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: Not applicable.

detail.abstract:
This paper is Chapter 3 of the book The Metabolic Theory of the Economic Organism: From the Mechanistic Paradigm to the Living Systems. The complete manuscript of the book is available on SSRN (DOI: 10.2139/ssrn.6456938) and OSF Preprints (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/KPXNY).
This chapter develops the anatomical foundation of the Economic Organism–Metabolism Theory (EOMT) through a systematic structural map across nested levels. All functional correspondences are established under two criteria—functional irreplaceability and correspondence of failure modes—ensuring diagnostic rather than merely illustrative value.
At the cellular level, individuals act as behavioral carriers embedded within organizations. Households function as reproductive and consumption units, while firms serve as primary productive cells whose boundaries reflect the trade-off between internal coordination and market exchange. Large-scale firm failure generates cascading dysfunction analogous to tissue-level breakdown.
At the tissue level, industries are conceptualized as collections of firms rather than one-to-one organ analogues, correcting a common analytical error. This perspective captures firm aggregation, cross-industry mobility, and shifting functional dominance across development stages. Three laws of industrial metabolism are identified: differentiation, waste accumulation, and renewal. Crisis emerges when waste exceeds excretory capacity or when firm exit is obstructed, as in the case of zombie firms. Markets function as inter-tissue coordination interfaces, whose failures—monopoly, information asymmetry, and price distortion—correspond to breakdowns in coordination.
At the regulatory level, a distinction is drawn between money as circulatory medium and policy as regulatory signaling. Financial crises are interpreted as disruptions in circulation or signal transmission, including credit freezes as circulatory arrest and liquidity traps as receptor failure. Under such conditions, fiscal intervention becomes necessary. The price mechanism operates as a distributed coordination system, while government serves as a central regulatory authority when decentralized coordination fails. A further epigenetic layer—culture and historically embedded norms—imposes path-dependent constraints beyond the reach of short-run policy.
At the systemic level, the chapter develops a holonic nested structure in which each unit is both whole and part of a larger system. It traces the historical emergence of the global economic super-organism from loosely connected regional systems to deeply integrated structures, highlighting its contingent and reversible nature. Recent deglobalization trends are interpreted as adaptive responses to declining system-level stability.
The chapter concludes with a unified anatomical framework and a diagnostic principle: structural problems require interventions at corresponding levels, and mismatched responses risk masking deeper systemic imbalances.

title: naics to ff: Converting NAICS codes to Fama-French industry classifications
affiliations: Nanyang Business School, Nanyang Technological University

detail.title: naics to ff: Converting NAICS codes to Fama-French industry classifications
detail.abstract: The industry classification schemes of Fama and French (1997), hereafter FF schemes, are standard in empirical finance research, but Kenneth French provides mappings only from Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) codes. As modern databases increasingly report codes from the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS), researchers need a transparent method to assign Fama-French industries to NAICS-coded data. This article introduces the Stata command naics to ff, which bridges NAICS to Fama-French by combining Dorn's crosswalk from NAICS to SIC (Autor et al. 2013 and Dorn 2024) with Census concordances (U.S. Census Bureau 2025) and the companion command sic to ff (Law 2025). The command resolves many-to-many concordances with employment weights and links modern NAICS vintages to historical crosswalks by concordance chaining. The shipped lookup achieves 99.8% coverage of NAICS 2022 codes. Validation against 159,454 Compustat firm-years shows 93.3% agreement between SIC-based and NAICS-based FF48 classifications. The package also includes isic to ff for mapping ISIC Revision 4 codes and nace to ff for mapping NACE Revision 2 class codes to Fama-French industries. All three commands support all eight Fama-French schemes (5, 10, 12, 17, 30, 38, 48, and 49 industries) and return diagnostic statistics through r().

title: Can the U.S.-Iran War Trigger a Global Goods and Services Shortage?

detail.title: Can the U.S.-Iran War Trigger a Global Goods and Services Shortage?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.ethicsApproval: none
declarations.funderStatement: none

detail.abstract: This paper evaluates how a prolonged war between the United States and Iran could generate a severe energy crisis, as well as significant food and services scarcity in the Middle East and neighbouring countries in the short run, and globally in the long run. We introduce a new economic simulator designed to analyse the combined effects of war and oil crises, entitled the War Oil Crisis Impact Simulator (WOCI-Simulator). The primary objective of the WOCI-Simulator is to examine wars at different stages and assess their overall socioeconomic impact in both the short and long term, particularly focusing on oil price fluctuations and their negative effects on food and services scarcity. In addition, this framework moves beyond traditional cost-benefit analysis by offering a more complex and dynamic representation of war scenarios. The WOCI-Simulator evaluates the economic impact on countries under both partial and full war scenarios. It incorporates several key indicators, including economic desgrowth from war (-δwar), war intensity (Iwar), war losses (-Lwar), oil trade deterioration from war (Πwar), level of military tension (Twar), and oil trade leakage from war (Ωwar). Finally, this study applies the WOCI-Simulator to evaluate the potential consequences of a prolonged and highly destructive full-scale war between the United States and Iran over the long term.

title: WHITE PAPER: The Sentinel Threshold Rule by Sreejith A Dynamic Multi-Factor Framework for Absolute Precision in Predicting Market Crashes and Macroeconomic Recessions

detail.title: WHITE PAPER: The Sentinel Threshold Rule by Sreejith A Dynamic Multi-Factor Framework for Absolute Precision in Predicting Market Crashes and Macroeconomic Recessions
detail.abstract: Historically, the central flaw in financial forecasting has been the assumption that the stock market and the real economy operate on the exact same chronological timeline. Traditional models fail because they either use lagging economic data to predict a forward-looking stock market, or they use volatile stock market breadth to predict slow-moving economic shifts. The Sentinel Threshold Rule (Ultimate Edition) solves this "timing disconnect" by splitting the algorithm into a multi-engine framework. It pairs an infallible macroeconomic engine-designed strictly to predict the onset of a structural recession-with market breadth filters and a complex-systems physics engine designed strictly to calculate the exact date of a stock market crash. By synthesizing these models, investors can definitively know when the stock market will break and whether that break is a temporary correction or a catastrophic recessionary bear market.

title: The National Production Platform Base (NPPB)

detail.title: The National Production Platform Base (NPPB)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.ethicsApproval: none
declarations.funderStatement: none

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the National Production Platform Base (NPPB) as a novel multidimensional economic indicator designed to evaluate the potential and effective development of a country's national production base establishment and integral development. Unlike traditional measures such as Gross Domestic Product, which focus primarily on aggregate output, the NPPB emphasizes the structural capacity and foundational performance of an economy. The model is built upon nine fundamental platform bases: Natural and fauna resources platform base; Information, communication, and technology access platform base; Human training and education capability platform base; Infrastructure and Transportation platform base; Energy resources platform base; Industrial, agriculture, and services production capacity platform base; Money, credit, and banking systems platform base; Government efficiency platform base; and the Domestic and international trade interconnectivity platform base. By integrating these interconnected dimensions, the NPPB provides a comprehensive framework to assess economic resilience, sustainability, and long-term productive potential. The proposed model allows for a more accurate identification of structural strengths and weaknesses across economies, offering policymakers and researchers a powerful tool for strategic planning, economic analysis, and comparative evaluation. Ultimately, the NPPB contributes to the advancement of economic measurement by shifting the focus from outputbased indicators to a multidimensional assessment of national production capabilities.

title: Personalized vs. Uniform Algorithm Design: The Unintended Consequence of Restrictions in Data Access
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, School of Management, Fudan University and Fudan University - School of Management

detail.title: Personalized vs. Uniform Algorithm Design: The Unintended Consequence of Restrictions in Data Access
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the unintended consequences of restricting third-party pricing algorithm providers' access to firms' private cost data. We model a monopoly provider serving competing firms characterized by heterogeneous costs and demand volatility, comparing two design regimes: Personalized Design (PD), which tailors algorithms using private data, and Uniform Design (UD), where data restrictions necessitate a standardized algorithm. While PD maximizes information value through precise demand forecasting, UD serves as a commitment device that softens competition by aligning adopters' prices. Although UD can be more profitable for both provider and adopters, it is more harmful to consumers and social welfare than PD because it softens competition, eliminates price dispersion, and distorts production. Our findings suggest that regulatory restrictions on data access-intended to prevent collusion-may unintentionally incentivize uniform designs that facilitate coordination-like outcomes and reduce overall welfare.

title: Political Barriers to Green Investment in Brazil and Their Effects on Latin America’s Green Economy

detail.title: Political Barriers to Green Investment in Brazil and Their Effects on Latin America’s Green Economy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author conducted this research through the Lumiere Research Program under the Lumiere Inclusion Foundation Full Scholarship, with academic mentorship provided by a PhD researcher affiliated with the University of Leeds. The author declares no personal or financial relationships with any individuals or organizations that could have influenced the study’s design, analysis, or conclusions.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study involved human participants in the form of semi-structured interviews. All participants were informed of the purpose of the research and provided written informed consent prior to participation. Participation was voluntary, and respondents were assured of anonymity and confidentiality. No personally identifiable information was collected or disclosed. In accordance with institutional and international research ethics standards for non-clinical social science research, formal ethics committee approval was not required.

detail.abstract:
Green investment, defined as the allocation of capital toward ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) initiatives, companies, and renewable energy projects, plays a central role in advancing sustainable development and accelerating the transition to low-carbon economies. Despite Brazil’s position as a regional leader in environmental policy and renewable energy capacity, political and institutional constraints continue to limit the scale and effectiveness of such investments. This study investigates the political barriers to green investment in Brazil and examines their broader implications for Latin America’s green economy.
Using a mixed-methods approach that combines semi-structured interviews with investors, environmental activists, and ESG professionals alongside quantitative and secondary data analysis, the research identifies key structural and political obstacles. These include regulatory instability, inconsistent policy implementation, limited financial incentives, bureaucratic complexity, and political influence over environmental governance. The findings also highlight the role of entrenched economic interests, particularly in agribusiness and extractive sectors, in shaping policy priorities that disadvantage sustainable investment.
The study further reveals a divergence between domestic and foreign investor perceptions, particularly regarding political risk and institutional reliability. While domestic actors emphasize regulatory inefficiencies and limited support mechanisms, foreign investors are more sensitive to political volatility and governance concerns. These dynamics reduce investor confidence and constrain capital flows into green sectors.
By situating Brazil within the broader Latin American context, this research demonstrates how national political barriers can generate regional spillover effects, slowing the development of sustainable finance markets. The study concludes that strengthening regulatory consistency, enhancing transparency, and aligning economic incentives with environmental goals are critical steps toward unlocking Brazil’s potential as a driver of green growth in Latin America.

title: Who Bears the Risk of Subsidized Sports Venues?

detail.title: Who Bears the Risk of Subsidized Sports Venues?
detail.abstract: Public subsidies for sports venues impose fiscal costs on taxpayers. We show that these subsidies also transfer risk from team owners to taxpayers and estimate the resulting exposure. The upper bound on uncompensated tail risk often exceeds construction costs, even under implausibly optimistic assumptions. This downside is driven by just two sources of uncertainty: tax revenue growth and interest rate volatility. To manage the risk, we suggest setting aside approximately 2–10% of total project costs, an amount expected to cover the initial outlay when compounded at market rates over the venue's lifespan.

title: Trading Toward System Stability: An Empirical Assessment of JEPX Intraday Market Operations and Imbalance Reduction

detail.title: Trading Toward System Stability: An Empirical Assessment of JEPX Intraday Market Operations and Imbalance Reduction
detail.abstract: Following the amendment of the imbalance pricing mechanism and introduction of the feed-in premium scheme in April 2022, the need for intraday trading to address renewable forecasting errors has increased, stimulating activity in the Japan Electric Power Exchange (JEPX) intraday market. By adopting dynamic panel data estimation with both first-difference generalized method of moments (GMM) and system GMM model, we empirically examine how intraday trading affects the balancing needs of power generators and retailers. Our results confirm that intraday trading significantly reduces electricity imbalances, not only overall system imbalances and those from demand forecast errors, but also predictable imbalances from renewable generation. Although most renewable generators are not exposed to imbalance risks, intraday trading remains essential for integrating renewable energy. We also find that intraday trading is less effective in areas with higher solar curtailment, suggesting that inefficient dispatch-priority rules and limited automated dispatching infrastructure hinder effective use of the JEPX intraday market.

title: Tolerance Norms Across Countries
affiliations: Department of Political Science, Yale University, Yale University and King's College London

detail.title: Tolerance Norms Across Countries

declarations.ethicsApproval: The research protocol for this study was submitted to the Yale University IRB and was exempted from full review.

detail.abstract: Democratic theorists consider respect for pluralism, equality, and inclusion as cornerstones of good democratic citizenship. But what do ordinary citizens believe? Is their commitment to equality, tolerance, and pluralism as strong as their commitment to obeying rules? We answer this question by eliciting and analyzing normative expectations and individual normative beliefs regarding the meaning of good citizenship in 19 democracies. We find a global consensus on the importance of following rules, obeying the law, and contributing to the common good. The same is not true for tolerance and pluralism-the norms that uniquely define democratic civic identity. The idea that the good democratic citizen should support equality, tolerance, and inclusion is contested and polarizing in many countries. Our results shed light on sources of democratic backsliding by uncovering societal foundations of liberal democratic fragility.

detail.abstract: This paper argues that the phrase "attention economy" is analytically misleading if it implies that attention itself has only recently become scarce. Attention scarcity is an old human condition. What is historically new is the declining threshold of extractability under platform capitalism. Digital infrastructures now make it possible to capture, measure, and monetize sub-threshold attention fragments-brief, low-intensity units of cognitive participation such as glances, pauses, scroll hesitation, interruption windows, and minor affective spikes-that earlier media systems could not profitably organize. The paper situates this claim in relation to audience commodity theory, surveillance capitalism, data colonialism, and the political economy of media. It argues that the contemporary regime is defined not simply by the commodification of audience time or the harvesting of behavioral data, but by the industrial seizure of previously negligible cognitive residues. It further proposes a minimal threshold model in which an attentional unit becomes extractable when its expected monetizable return exceeds the marginal cost of capturing and acting upon it. On this basis, the paper interprets the platform era as a widening of the extractable range of attention. Finally, it advances a class-structured account of attention organized around sellers, buyers, and protectors, arguing that one of the key inequalities of contemporary capitalism lies in unequal power over the conditions under which cognition can be fragmented, monetized, or defended.

title: Do Medicaid Work Requirements Work?

detail.title: Do Medicaid Work Requirements Work?
detail.abstract: In June 2018, Arkansas became the first state in U.S. history to implement work requirements for Medicaid. This study adopts a difference-indifferences framework to evaluate the effects of work requirements on Medicaid participation and labor supply using monthly national administrative enrollment and survey data. Work requirements led to substantial declines in total Medicaid participation exceeding the 18,164 directly terminated for noncompliance, suggesting a potential chilling effect that deterred new or returning adults from enrolling in Medicaid. Coverage losses persisted until the mandate was halted by a federal court in March 2019. No discernible changes in labor supply at the intensive or extensive margins are detected.

title: The Xi Jinping's Community with a Shared Future for Mankind: Understanding in China-Africa Cooperation

detail.title: The Xi Jinping's Community with a Shared Future for Mankind: Understanding in China-Africa Cooperation
detail.abstract: The concept of a community with a shared future for mankind is the basic variable of President Xi Jinping's foreign policy construction. It is misunderstood or regarded as wishful thinking but this concept has an ideal view of what the world should be. It embodies quite rational pragmatism in the implementation of our times. This concept is the intersection of Chinese and Western ancient and modern philosophical thoughts. It is deeply rooted in the Sinicized Marxist socialist philosophy. This paper attempts to simplify its understanding and enhance its pragmatism consciousness under the background of China-Africa cooperation.

title: Identifying the effect of the US embargo on the Cuban economy: A comment on Bastos, Geloso, and Bologna Pavlik (2026)

detail.title: Identifying the effect of the US embargo on the Cuban economy: A comment on Bastos, Geloso, and Bologna Pavlik (2026)
detail.abstract: Bastos, Geloso, and Bologna Pavlik (2026) argue that the US embargo explains less than one-tenth of the difference in per capita income between Cuba and a counterfactual scenario in which the country did not follow socialist economic policies. We show that their results are driven by the use of an elasticity of income to trade openness that is neither representative nor a reasonable upper bound of the values found in the literature and by their choice to attribute the effect of the interaction between the embargo and other determinants of growth solely to those other determinants. We show that, once these problems are corrected, the embargo can account for a substantial fraction, and in some cases all, of Cuba's post-1959 economic underperformance.

detail.abstract: Emerging markets have experienced a significant shift in consumer behaviour due to increasing incomes, demographic shifts, rapid digitalization, and post-pandemic lifestyle modifications. In the Indian contextas one of the world's fastest-growing consumer economiesprovides a unique opportunity to review these changes. This paper explores the main determinants of consumer behaviour based on primary and secondary data. Primary data were collected via a structured questionnaire from 230 respondents ranging in age, income level, educational background and geographic location. The study hypotheses were tested by statistical procedures such as descriptive statistics,  2 tests, correlation analysis, regression models, and factor analysis. And based on the insights, as described above, product value, price perception, convenience, brand trust and social influence are leading aspects of purchasing decisions. Digital adoption and trust in digital payment systems significantly predict online purchase intention. Trends in the post-pandemic world, like increased health consciousness and digital reliance, are also factors that play a role in consumers' decisions as to which products should be bought. The study provides business, marketing and policy advice on the changing consumer market landscape of India in light of business practices.

detail.abstract:
This study examines the relationship between Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance and stock return volatility among firms constituting the NIFTY 50 index in the Indian equity market. Using daily stock price data spanning January 2021 to December 2025, firm-level volatility is estimated through GARCH(1,1) models, yielding measures of average conditional variance, logarithmic volatility, and volatility persistence (α + β). ESG scores sourced from National Stock Exchange of India disclosures serve as the primary explanatory variable in cross-sectional regression analysis.

Descriptive statistics reveal that ESG scores among NIFTY 50 firms cluster within a narrow band (58–80), reflecting convergent sustainability disclosure practices among large-cap Indian companies. GARCH estimation confirms canonical features of financial return series, including volatility clustering and near-unit-root persistence. Correlation analysis indicates a weak negative association between ESG scores and logarithmic volatility; however, regression models across multiple volatility specifications yield statistically insignificant ESG coefficients, suggesting that ESG performance does not significantly explain cross-sectional variation in short-term stock return volatility within this sample.

These findings imply that while ESG disclosure has become increasingly institutionalized in India—propelled by regulatory frameworks such as the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) mandate—its influence on short-term market risk remains limited. The results contribute to the nascent empirical literature on ESG and financial risk in emerging markets and suggest that sustainability practices may affect corporate outcomes primarily through long-term channels, including governance quality, stakeholder trust, and reputational capital, rather than through immediate changes in return volatility. Future research incorporating longer time horizons, granular ESG pillar-level scores, and broader samples may yield richer insights into the dynamics between sustainability performance and financial market risk.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the news-driven factors that predict the adoption of RWA markets. Using a large language model (LLM) to analyze more than 14,000 RWA news articles, we identify key themes and construct a set of RWA indices from text. Our indices show a steadily maturing market, with sentiment becoming more positive, uncertainty declining, topic coverage remaining broad, and news becoming increasingly timely as the ecosystem evolves. We also find that news dynamics and RWA indices (sentiment and uncertainty) significantly predict subsequent RWA market adoption. Among RWA themes, Legal and Regulatory Frameworks, Jurisdictions, and Institutional Adoption dominate the RWA news. Among asset classes, news about stablecoins is more dominant and aligns with their early adoption, followed by U.S. Treasuries. Overall, our research provides a comprehensive overview of the RWA market and serves as a "compass" for understanding how and where the market is likely to grow. In addition, we develop a set of key indices to support the industry and guide future in-depth research.

detail.title: Cross-sectional currency momentum and order flow *

detail.abstract: This study investigates whether high buying pressure is associated with higher crosssectional currency momentum returns. We employ order flows from the spot, forward, and swap markets, as well as the maturities of swap and forward contracts, to construct portfolios based on momentum and buying pressure. We find heterogeneous effects of order flows across instruments and maturities on cross-sectional currency momentum portfolios. High buying pressure in the short-term swap market leads to stronger momentum returns. This pattern is particularly significant when using order flows from banks, suggesting that banks extract information through trading with other informed traders. Our double-sorted portfolios based on momentum and order flows generate higher returns when the demand for USD hedging is strong.

title: Intangible Capital and the Technology of Scale : Disentangling Scalability from Market Power

detail.title: Intangible Capital and the Technology of Scale : Disentangling Scalability from Market Power
detail.abstract: This paper shows that intangible capital fundamentally reshapes firm-level scale economies and the measurement of market power. I develop a structural nonparametric production framework that incorporates intangible capital as a factor input and external R&D as a source of productivity spillovers, and estimate it using U.S. public firm data from 1975 to 2024. I find that returns to scale increase sharply with firm size only when intangible capital is included; absent intangibles, returns to scale are approximately constant across firms. Markups rise with intangible intensity but follow an inverted-U shape in firm size, indicating that pricing power reflects asset composition rather than scale. Incorporating intangible capital lowers aggregate markup estimates by up to 20 percent, implying that traditional models overstate market power by attributing technological scale effects to price-cost margins. Large firms exhibit lower relative productivity within industries, suggesting they grow through scalability rather than efficiency. Consistent with this, exposure to external R&D spillovers declines with firm size as large firms internalize innovation through intangible accumulation. These findings suggest that intangible capital is a central source of modern scale economies and that failing to account for it leads to a systematic conflation of technological scalability with market power.

detail.abstract: This study develops a Bayesian Poisson GLM (Generalized Linear Model) to estimate external corrosion-driven failure rates per mile-year for Highly Volatile Liquid (HVL) pipeline infrastructure in the United States. The analysis fuses two federal datasets from PHMSA: the Hazardous Liquid Accident Database (2010-2026) and the Annual Report Part I-Miles of Pipelines by Decade Installed. The study transforms over 16 years of reactive federal accident data into a predictive risk framework to provide pipeline operators with a probabilistic, defensible basis for deciding which vintage cohorts warrant priority integrity interventions. The analysis finds that asset age is the dominant driver of external corrosion failure risk, representing nearly a tripling of per-mile risk per standard deviation of age. Operating pressure is statistically non-significant, confirmed by both Bayesian and frequentist MLE. A prior sensitivity analysis across Normal (0, 0.5), Normal (0, 1),Normal (0, 2) priors confirms all conclusions are data-driven rather than prior-driven. The Bayesian framework is motivated by the small aggregate sample size of N=12 decade-level observations, where frequentist MLE relies on large sample approximations. The Bayesian 95% HDIs are consistently narrower by around 10% to 11% than the MLE confidence intervals while yielding nearly identical point estimates.

detail.abstract:
As a tenured global ESG consultant and honorary PHD in Sustainable AI , IGBC AP , EHS and BIOCHAR certified ESG expert , with over two decades advising Fortune 500 corporations and multilateral institutions on high-integrity carbon markets, I introduce CAQSG™ (Correlated AI/Quantum Spectral Graphing) — a practical hybrid MRV framework that combines hyperspectral drone and satellite imagery with graph-Laplacian spectral analysis solved via quantum-accelerated eigensolvers (hybrid VQE/QAOA).

CAQSG™ significantly increases carbon credit potential by identifying sequestration hotspots at sub-hectare resolution and reducing MRV uncertainty buffers by 30–40%. The method is applied to five land-use systems plus a new urban golf course case, and an integrated Pisciculture + Aquaveritas model that valorises fisheries effluents, dairy slag-water, and locally sourced steel slag within a 200 km radius. It layers Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) onto agroforestry, aquaculture, and managed turf systems, fully aligned with Verra VM0047 v1.1 and Puro.earth ERW Edition 2025.

Corporates can co-join their CSR initiatives and IGBC/LEED green land restoration projects with CAQSG™ to generate high-integrity carbon credits while strengthening BRSR reporting for their own operations and Scope 3 value-chain partners. Drawing on India’s 19 million tonnes annual steel slag waste stream and the 2026 urea crisis triggered by Strait of Hormuz disruptions, the approach delivers 2.5–3× higher ROI compared to traditional downgraded Indian CCB projects, while creating skilled local livelihoods.

The framework models the landscape as a weighted graph G = (V, E), where nodes are spatial units and edges carry Gaussian-kernel similarities based on hyperspectral features. Principal eigenvectors of the normalized Laplacian identify sequestration hotspots and quantify per-cell carbon-flux uncertainty. Projected outcomes include 30–40% lower uncertainty buffers and 12–24 months faster verification cycles. A worked example on a simulated 70-acre pilot plot, complete CAQSG™ pipeline specification, and reproducible Python code are provided in the appendices.

A provisional patent on the CAQSG™ Pipeline (hyperspectral → graph → deployment-dependent solver selection → uncertainty propagation) is being filed prior to publication. Strategic collaborations with sequestration developers and corporate buyers are invited.

title: Why Party Conflicts Emerge in Mexico: Electoral Incongruence and Institutional Strength in PAN, PRI, PRD, and Morena

detail.title: Why Party Conflicts Emerge in Mexico: Electoral Incongruence and Institutional Strength in PAN, PRI, PRD, and Morena
detail.abstract: This article examines why internal conflicts emerge during the selection of state party leaders in Mexico. It analyzes 438 leadership selection processes in PAN, PRI, PRD, and Morena between 2010 and 2022. The study focuses on two main factors: differences between national and state electoral results, and the strength of party organization at the subnational level. Using mixed-effects logistic regression, the findings show that electoral incongruence increases the probability of internal conflict. However, this effect weakens when parties have strong and stable local organizations. In these cases, internal rules and structures help manage competition and reduce disputes. The results suggest that party organization plays a key role in shaping internal stability, even under conditions of electoral tension. The study contributes to the understanding of party behavior in multilevel political systems and highlights the importance of subnational institutional strength in preventing internal conflict.

title: Ontological Limits of Historical Validation for Wavefunction-Calibrated Financial Systems

detail.title: Ontological Limits of Historical Validation for Wavefunction-Calibrated Financial Systems
detail.abstract: We establish that classical backtesting is structurally incompatible with wavefunction-calibrated financial systems through three independent arguments. The dimensional collapse problem shows that the options-implied wavefunction ψ(S,t)-a field over the entire price domain-cannot be reconstructed from the realized price trajectory or from aggregate proxies such as VIX. Ergodicity breaking shows that time-averaged evaluation is circular for a system designed for non-ergodic multiplicative dynamics. The non-perturbative nature of instanton tunneling signals shows that exponentially sensitive quantities cannot be recovered from perturbative historical statistics. We propose a forward-looking validation paradigm consisting of prospective experiment tracking with pre-registered signal thresholds (Harvey et al., 2016), external blind validation on obfuscated data (Numerai), and real-time wavefunction-divergence monitoring. This paradigm is strictly stronger than backtesting: it requires prediction on data that could not have been used in system design, using inputs available only in real time.

title: The Fiscal Reciprocity Paradox: Extraction, Social Goods, and Political Indifference in Public Finance

detail.abstract: Fiscal systems are commonly interpreted as reciprocal exchanges in which citizens provide taxation and compliance in return for public goods and social protection. Conventional fiscal contract theory therefore assumes that weak reciprocity between state extraction and social provision should generate political resistance. Cross-national evidence, however, reveals a more complex pattern. While relatively modest welfare reforms in advanced economies often provoke strong political mobilization, many countries characterized by limited social provision sustain fiscal extraction with comparatively little collective resistance. This paper argues that fiscal stability under conditions of weak reciprocity should not be interpreted as evidence of legitimacy, but as the outcome of historically conditioned expectations that normalize asymmetrical fiscal relations. To account for this pattern, the study introduces the concept of the Fiscal Reciprocity Paradox, defined as a structural condition in which states maintain fiscal extraction while allocating comparatively limited resources to social goods, yet widespread political resistance does not emerge. To analyze this phenomenon, the paper further develops the Social Contract Ratio (SCR), a measure of the relative allocation of public spending between human development and institutional functions. By focusing on the composition of public budgets, the SCR provides a framework for evaluating how fiscal systems distribute resources between citizens and the state. The analysis also extends Indifference Theory to the domain of public finance, conceptualizing political inaction as a region of structural inertia shaped by historically embedded expectations. Together, these contributions provide a framework for understanding how fiscal structures and adaptive expectations interact to produce divergent political responses across societies.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a finance-oriented conceptual framework linking Indigenous business principles to the funding and governance of circular economy firms. The core argument is that Indigenous governance logics-intergenerational stewardship, reciprocity, collective accountability, and relational value creation-alter how firms evaluate projects, allocate control rights, disclose non-financial risks, and build legitimacy with capital providers. In finance terms, these mechanisms can lengthen decision horizons, reduce social-license and regulatory risk, improve stakeholder monitoring, and widen access to patient capital for regenerative investments whose benefits are realized over long horizons. Building on Indigenous entrepreneurship and commons-governance scholarship, the paper derives four propositions connecting Indigenous governance to capital budgeting, financing frictions, cost of capital, and downside-risk management. The contribution is to reposition Indigenous business practice from a cultural addon to a governance architecture with direct implications for sustainable finance, entrepreneurial finance, and corporate governance. The framework also clarifies boundaries: the argument is not for symbolic appropriation, but for Indigenous-led, context-specific governance design in which financing structures respect community rights and long-term ecological obligations.

title: Two Primitives, One Synthetic: A Unified Framework for Understanding Structured Products and Range-Based Strategies

detail.title: Two Primitives, One Synthetic: A Unified Framework for Understanding Structured Products and Range-Based Strategies
detail.abstract: This paper proposes that only two fundamental trading strategies exist in a single, reasonably efficient spot market-Momentum and Mean Reversion-and that both require directional price movement. Yet markets spend significant time in sideways ranges where neither strategy naturally profits. Structured products fill this gap. We illustrate their economic rationale through a merchant parable, examine implementation via derivatives and ETFs, and present a case study demonstrating how combining mean reversion with a momentum overlay can replicate range strategy payoffs without options. The "Two Primitives, One Synthetic" framework explains why structured products exist; the case study illustrates how similar effects can be achieved using the fundamental primitives themselves.

title: Can Renewable Energy Boost the Business Outcomes of Power Suppliers? An Empirical Study on Japan's Power Producers and Suppliers

detail.title: Can Renewable Energy Boost the Business Outcomes of Power Suppliers? An Empirical Study on Japan's Power Producers and Suppliers

keywords: Business Outcomes JEL Classification Codes: Q42

detail.abstract: This study provides firm-level evidence on how renewable electricity generation affects the business performance of Japan's power producers and suppliers (PPSs), using a double machine learning framework that accounts for policy and regional heterogeneity. By focusing on two key performance indicators, annual revenue and net profit after tax, our study reveals three main findings. First, renewable electricity generation significantly enhances PPSs' profitability by improving after-tax earnings and promoting more active participation in electricity markets. Second, we examine the distinct impacts of two key policies. The gradual reduction of feed-in tariff purchase prices has undermined the financial stability of small solar power producers. Conversely, the feed-in premium scheme has enhanced the profitability of large wind power producers by providing more favorable energy market opportunities. Third, it underscores the importance of regional disparities: Solar curtailment, particularly in Kyushu, negatively affects PPSs' revenues due to grid and demand constraints. Overall, this study advances the understanding of how renewable energy expansion and market reform interact to shape firm competitiveness and offers policy implications for enhancing market participation and resilience in Japan's electricity sector.

title: الإدارة التنظيمية في مرحلة التمكين:قراءة تحليلية في نموذج موسى (عليه السلام) من خلال سورة يونس (الآية 87)

detail.abstract: يتناول هذا البحث بالدراسة والتحليل الآية 87 من سورة يونس، والتي تضمنت توجيهاً إلهياً لموسى وهارون (عليهما السلام) بتبوء البيوت لبني إسرائيل في مصر، وجعل هذه البيوت قبلة، وإقامة الصلاة، والتبشير للمؤمنين. ينطلق البحث من فرضية أن هذه الآية تحمل أبعاداً إدارية وتنظيمية عميقة تمثل استراتيجية متكاملة لقيادة المجتمعات المستضعفة تحت الأنظمة القمعية خلال فترة "الحرب الباردة" التي سبقت الخروج من مصر. يقع البحث في مبحثين: الأول يرصد واقع بني إسرائيل تحت العبودية، محللاً حالة الانهيار البنيوي التي أصابتهم على المستويات النفسية والاجتماعية والسياسية، مستعيناً بمصادر تاريخية وتحليلية متنوعة. أما المبحث الثاني فيحلل الاستراتيجية الموسوية عبر أربعة محاور: التأسيس للقيادة التشاركية (موسى وهارون)، الإدارة اللوجستية وبناء القواعد الخلفية (تبوء البيوت)، البعد التنظيمي والأمني (جعل البيوت قبلة)، والبناء المعنوي وإدارة التوقعات (إقامة الصلاة والتبشير). يوظف البحث مفاهيم إدارية حديثة كالقيادة الموزعة، والأمن النفسي، والثقافة التنظيمية، والذاكرة الثقافية، ليقدم نموذجاً متكاملاً للإدارة في ظروف استثنائية. يخلص البحث إلى أن الآية تقدم رؤية إدارية فريدة تقوم على تحويل الوحدة الاجتماعية الأساسية (البيت) إلى خلية تنظيمية فعالة، تجمع بين الوظائف اللوجستية والأمنية والمعنوية، مما مكن بني إسرائيل من الصمود وصولاً إلى ساعة التحرير.
