detail.abstract: While a growing body of literature explores heterogeneity in peer effects on photovoltaic (PV) system adoption, most studies rely on strong a priori assumptions and struggle to flexibly capture complex interactions between household characteristics. In this paper, we use a novel Causal Forest approach to estimate heterogeneous peer effects, leveraging exogenous variation from public housing PV installations as a natural experiment. By combining machine learning with a residualization strategy to address spatial confounding, we flexibly estimate how responsiveness to peer influence is mediated by household characteristics. We find that peer influence is strongest among households typically considered less likely to adopt PV, such as older residents or those with lower energy use, suggesting that social exposure can help overcome informational or behavioral barriers. In contrast, households with high adoption potential appear less responsive to peer influence, challenging the notion that peer effects simply reinforce existing adoption patterns. However, while peer influence can nudge hesitant adopters, it is unlikely to generate the scale or speed needed to meet energy transition targets. Influence-based interventions may support local diffusion but must be paired with direct measures that address structural adoption barriers.

title: Does Fiscal Consolidation Reduce Public Debt? Evidence from the European Union Using Local Projections
affiliations: University of Malaga - Department of Economics, European University of the Atlantic and University of Malaga

detail.title: Does Fiscal Consolidation Reduce Public Debt? Evidence from the European Union Using Local Projections
detail.abstract: We examine whether fiscal consolidation reduces public debt, using local projections difference-in-differences on 126 consolidation episodes in the EU-27 between 1996 and 2024. Entering consolidation raises the debt-to-GDP ratio in the short run rather than lowering it. A decomposition of debt dynamics traces the pattern to a widening interest–growth differential and to stock-flow adjustments that together more than offset the improvement in the primary balance. Two transmission channels sustain the outcome. Output contracts and sovereign spreads rise rather than fall, so no credibility dividend absorbs the adjustment. The effect is not uniform across episodes. Consolidations that protect public investment are associated with better debt outcomes, and the adverse response concentrates in episodes with an unfavourable interest–growth differential. These results qualify the debt-reduction logic behind fiscal consolidation and connect with key elements of the EU's 2024 reformed fiscal framework, notably investment protection and country-specific adjustment paths.

title: Sacred Dissent: Provocative and Heterodox Interpretations in Jewish Biblical Commentary
affiliations: City University of New York (CUNY) - Koppelman School of Business

detail.title: Sacred Dissent: Provocative and Heterodox Interpretations in Jewish Biblical Commentary
detail.abstract: Jewish biblical commentary spans more than two millennia and includes an extraordinary variety of interpretive methods. These approaches range from a strict commitment to tradition to daring deviations from the rabbinic consensus. This paper examines the work of several influential exegetes, such as Saadiah Gaon, Rashbam, Ibn Ezra, Bechor Shor, Ralbag, and Abarbanel, to highlight the creativity and intellectual bravery inherent in their writings. Many of their interpretations were considered provocative in their own eras and remain so today because they challenged Talmudic aggadah, questioned the nature of miraculous events, and at times contradicted established halacha. Despite their historical significance, some modern publishers and educational institutions are currently censoring these texts. The rich diversity and frequent disagreements among these scholars offer a vital lesson regarding the lasting importance of tolerance and intellectual humility.

title: Phoenix Activity, Systemic Economic Risk, and the Infinite Societal Loop: The Structural Nature of the Octahedron — An Inquiry into Medical Economics.

detail.title: Phoenix Activity, Systemic Economic Risk, and the Infinite Societal Loop: The Structural Nature of the Octahedron — An Inquiry into Medical Economics.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
This study presents a multidisciplinary systems-level analysis of the structural vulnerabilities embedded within modern capitalist economies, with particular emphasis on the United States. Drawing on over thirty academic disciplines — including cybernetics, thermodynamics, macroeconomics, corporate law, neuropsychiatry, and computer science — the author constructs a three-dimensional semantic network modeled on the geometric properties of the Platonic solid known as the Octahedron, proposing it as a novel framework for mapping and analyzing the global societal structure.


At the center of the inquiry is a previously underexamined financial mechanism known as Phoenix Activity — a form of corporate fraud in which a business entity deliberately exploits insolvency law to extinguish its liabilities while continuing operations through a successor entity. Drawing on peer-reviewed literature from Australian and United Kingdom corporate law scholarship, the author argues that Phoenix Activity represents a systemic economic backdoor embedded within the legislative architecture of capitalist financial systems, and that its large-scale practice constitutes a measurable contributor to systemic financial risk. The author further asserts that nations formerly colonized by the British Empire — including the United States and Australia — face a disproportionately elevated exposure to Phoenix Activity due to the structural and regulatory similarities inherited from their shared colonial financial architecture, similarities that existing regulatory frameworks have failed to adequately identify or address. This international dimension extends the risk profile of Phoenix Activity well beyond any single jurisdiction, suggesting a coordinated multinational policy response may ultimately be required.


The study further introduces the concept of the Infinite Societal Loop — a structural analogy drawn from computer science — to describe the self-perpetuating economic cycle powered by the Military Industrial Complex, which the author argues traps modern society in a pattern of historical repetition that inhibits systemic progress across medicine, education, criminology, and macroeconomics.


Building on these structural findings, the author introduces Phoenix Syndrome — a hypothesized neuropsychiatric disorder proposed to have emerged as an unintended consequence of the widespread practice of Phoenix Activity and the corresponding deployment of cognitive programming within consumer societies. The syndrome is theorized to manifest at the intersection of multiple established neurological and psychiatric disorder categories, and its proposed existence is offered as a framework for understanding the persistence of certain incurable neuropsychiatric conditions in modern populations.

The work concludes with a comprehensive cybernetic mapping of the global economic system across major market sectors, control group structures, and geopolitical subsystems, and proposes a systemic rebalancing framework as a prospective solution to the entropic risk of total market failure. The findings carry implications for financial risk assessment, forensic accounting, corporate law reform, public health policy, and the emerging field of Medical Economics.

title: A JANIB Framework for Economic Systems Need, Resource Mobility, and Economic Health

detail.title: A JANIB Framework for Economic Systems Need, Resource Mobility, and Economic Health
detail.abstract: This paper proposes JANIB System Economics as a system-centric framework for reading economic health beyond output alone. It begins from a simple dissatisfaction: GDP, inflation, debt, and employment remain indispensable, but they do not fully reveal whether resources are reaching what life requires, whether visible growth becomes usable room in households and communities, and whether present expansion is being financed through hidden burdens shifted into labour, ecology, institutions, or future time. Major institutional work already supports the need for a broader reading. The OECD's well-being framework states that GDP is a well-established measure of economic output but does not tell us whether life as a whole is getting better, and for whom. The World Bank's The Changing Wealth of Nations 2024 similarly argues that broader wealth, including produced, human, and natural capital, better captures the asset base underpinning sustainable progress and intergenerational equity. Building on that widening move, this paper reorganizes economic reading through a distinct architecture centred on need, resource, and the Resource Mobility Field. Need is treated as prior to demand; demand is treated as the visible market expression of interpreted need under actual conditions of affordability, access, influence, and available means. The framework introduces a set of core constructs-Need Interpretation and Reading (NAIR), Economic Need Behaviour Tone (ENBT), Baseline Regulatory and Economic Capacity (BREC), Economic Need Trajectory Formation (ENTF), and Resource Mobility Effectiveness and Performance (RMEP)-to explain how need becomes economically visible, how capacities shape movement, and how resources do or do not become relief. The paper further distinguishes reported growth from real relief, places hidden cost and future burden inside the core economic reading itself, and treats governance as organized pressure management under risk of institutional drift. The final claim is that a stronger economics should judge visible activity through the deeper architecture of need, mobility, relief, hidden cost, trust, and future continuity rather than through output alone.

title: Energy Transition, or Anthropic Transfer?

detail.title: Energy Transition, or Anthropic Transfer?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This working paper is self-funded and produced as part of independent research, with no institutional or commercial affiliation.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. Self-funded independent research.

detail.abstract: Existing critiques of the energy transition-extractivism, rebound effects, technological debt-are typically treated as separate problems, leaving unanswered how they connect as components of a single mechanism of disorder displacement. This paper applies the concept of anthropy-the hypothesis that social systems displace disorder rather than resolve it-to the dominant model of energy transition. Drawing on IEA critical minerals data (IEA, 2023), IPCC consumption-based accounting frameworks (IPCC, 2022), and recent rebound-effect syntheses (Brockway et al., 2021), it shows that the transition shifts disorder spatially (from fossil fuels to mining in the Global South) and temporally (from carbon emissions to technological debt), while carbon accounting metrics function as the key invisibilisation device. The paper proposes three criteria for evaluating a less displacive transition: reduced spatial distance between consumption and extraction, shortened temporal deferral, and political visibility of residual transfers.

title: From Volume to Identity: A Structural Framework to Eliminate Illegal Timber Laundering Through Tree-Level Traceability

detail.title: From Volume to Identity: A Structural Framework to Eliminate Illegal Timber Laundering Through Tree-Level Traceability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest related to this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants or animals and therefore does not require ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

keywords: Timber traceability Illegal logging Tree-level identification RFID Forest governance Supply chain integrity Amazon rainforest Chain of custody Environmental compliance Timber laundering

detail.abstract: This study examines the structural limitations of volume-based forest governance systems in regulating timber production and commercialization. While these systems rely on comprehensive forest inventories and regulatory oversight, they inherently generate discrepancies between authorized and physically extracted volumes, enabling the creation of surplus credits that can legitimize illegally sourced timber. Drawing on field-based experience in the Brazilian Amazon, this paper identifies a fundamental systemic flaw: the decoupling of legal documentation from physical origin. To address this gap, the study proposes a structural shift toward tree-level traceability, in which individual trees are uniquely identified, georeferenced, and monitored throughout their lifecycle. By replacing aggregated volume control with individual-based verification, this approach significantly increases the operational and economic barriers to timber laundering, offering a scalable framework for improving supply chain integrity.

title: 3.3 million years distilled into one principle anthropy in the longue durée

detail.title: 3.3 million years distilled into one principle anthropy in the longue durée

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This working paper is self-funded and produced as part of independent research, with no institutional or commercial affiliation.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. Self-funded independent research.

detail.abstract: Existing frameworks for analysing social disorder-from world-systems theory to ecological economics-tend to treat spatial, temporal, and social externalities as separate phenomena. Anthropy proposes a unified mechanism: social systems displace disorder rather than resolve it. This paper offers a long-duration stylisation-from stone tools to data centres-to show that anthropy is a structural constant of human social organisation, observable over 3.3 million years. Applying a uniform analytical protocol (order created / disorder displaced / dominant transfer type) to seven historical configurations reveals that the modalities of anthropic transfer migrate as displacement spaces become saturated: from spatial to social, then from social to temporal and cognitive.

title: Thinking Beyond the Walls

detail.title: Thinking Beyond the Walls

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This working paper is self-funded and produced as part of independent research, with no institutional or commercial affiliation.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. Self-funded independent research.

detail.abstract: Epistemic order denotes the configuration by which a disciplinary field stabilises its criteria of validity, its publication formats, and its hierarchies of legitimacy. This article argues that the academic field in the social sciences maintains that order by relegating certain anomalies-questions, formats, postures-to its margins, through a mechanism analogous to anthropic transfer. Drawing on the AFEP/CNU controversy in French economics, on Merton's analysis of cumulative advantage, and on open infrastructures (HAL, ORCID, and overlay journals), the paper shows that these infrastructures alter the visibility of relegation without suppressing its underlying logic-and may generate new forms of epistemic disorder through information overload and filtering collapse. It concludes with a reflexive falsifiability clause: the anthropic framework cannot serve as its own justification for the marginality of its author.

title: Macroeconomic Stability as a Precondition for Long-Term Growth in Uzbekistan

detail.title: Macroeconomic Stability as a Precondition for Long-Term Growth in Uzbekistan
detail.abstract: This paper examines the determinants of GDP growth in Uzbekistan through an econometric analysis of four macroeconomic variables: investments in fixed capital, economically active population, foreign trade turnover, and inflation. Using a dataset of 15 annual observations, the regression model demonstrates exceptionally strong explanatory power, with an R² of 0.9954 and an adjusted R² of 0.9936. The findings reveal that investments in fixed capital and the economically active population exert statistically significant positive effects on GDP, confirming their role as robust drivers of economic expansion. By contrast, foreign trade turnover and inflation exhibit weaker and statistically unreliable effects at the 95% confidence level, suggesting that their influence is more supportive than central in sustaining growth. Diagnostic tests reinforce the reliability of the model's variance and independence assumptions, with results confirming homoskedasticity and absence of autocorrelation. However, severe multicollinearity among predictors and nonnormal residuals limits the precision of coefficient interpretation, underscoring the complexity of disentangling overlapping economic effects. The analysis highlights the interconnected nature of capital and labor: investments in infrastructure and industrial modernization not only enhance productivity but also generate employment opportunities, while a larger workforce supports higher levels of production. Policy implications emphasize the need for integrated strategies that combine investment incentives with labor market development, rather than relying on isolated interventions. Trade and inflation management should be treated as complementary measures, while priority should be given to strengthening productive investment and workforce participation. Overall, the study contributes to the literature by providing empirical evidence on Uzbekistan's growth dynamics and offering actionable insights for policymakers seeking to enhance productivity, stability, and long-term development.

title: Public Debt and Anthropy Who Really Pays for Disorder?

detail.title: Public Debt and Anthropy Who Really Pays for Disorder?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This working paper is self-funded and produced as part of independent research, with no institutional or commercial affiliation.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. Self-funded independent research.

detail.abstract: Mainstream analyses of public debt focus on volume, sustainability ratios, and fiscal trajectories, leaving unanswered a prior question: who actually absorbs the disorder that debt displaces, and through what mechanisms does that displacement remain invisible? This paper applies the framework of anthropythe hypothesis that social systems reroute disorder rather than resolve it-to French public debt. It identifies four simultaneous transfer circuits (temporal, social, political, and monetary) whose cascading sequence constitutes a single mechanism of disorder displacement. Three criteria distinguish anthropic transfer from standard intertemporal smoothing: a cascade of circuits activated by the same fiscal episode; a systematic asymmetry between mobile actors, shielded from the shock, and captive actors, who absorb it; and an active process of invisibilisation whereby technocratic discourse reframes political choices as accounting constraints. Drawing on institutional data (INSEE, Cour des comptes, DREES, ECB) and three comparative configurations-Japan, Norway, Greece-the analysis recasts public debt not as a stock to be reduced, but as a configuration for allocating disorder.

title:
AI and the Future of Work in India:
Policy Challenges and Pathways for Inclusive Labour Transition

detail.title:
AI and the Future of Work in India:
Policy Challenges and Pathways for Inclusive Labour Transition
detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping labour markets across the world but its impact is particularly complex in developing economies such as India. Unlike advanced economies, where technological transitions occur within relatively structured labour systems, India presents a unique case marked by deep structural challenges such as widespread informality, persistent skill mismatches and uneven sectoral distribution of employment. This research paper is an original work and all sources of data and references have been duly acknowledged. In light of these findings, the paper emphasises the importance of policy intervention. The impact of AI is not predetermined; rather, it depends on institutional capacity, governance frameworks and the ability of the workforce to adapt to changing demands. Inclusive policy measures focusing on reskilling, labour protection, and equitable access to digital infrastructure are essential to ensure that technological progress translates into broad-based development. The study concludes that while AI holds significant promise as a driver of economic transformation, its contribution to inclusive growth in India will ultimately depend on how effectively this transition is managed.

title: Islamist Resistance in the July Revolution: Recognition of Madrasah Students in Rebuilding of Bangladesh

detail.title: Islamist Resistance in the July Revolution: Recognition of Madrasah Students in Rebuilding of Bangladesh
detail.abstract: The July Revolution marked a pivotal moment in Bangladesh's history by ousting Sheikh Hasina from the throne of power after 15 years of her fascist reign. This uprising was not ignited by the fierce resistance of the Students Against Discrimination's anti-quota movement of 2024 alone, rather it was the culmination of a relentless, fifteen-year battle waged by political and Islamist factions. This paper depicts the contributions of Islamist groups, particularly madrasah students in this uprising. It will showcase their subsequent neglect and the oppression they faced under Hasina's tenure. Additionally, the paper discusses their significance and relevance in Bangladesh's politics and society. It traces their historical role in fighting exploitation in this land. It also explains the factors that have led to their declining influence after the Monsoon Revolution. The presented analysis is based on news reports, academic discussions, and historical records. The paper projects a comprehensive analysis of the complex dynamics affecting Islamist groups. It explores their evolving role in Bangladesh's political landscape.

title: Financial Exclusion and the Distributional Limits of Monetary Policy

detail.title: Financial Exclusion and the Distributional Limits of Monetary Policy
detail.abstract: In economies where a portion of the population transacts through mobile money and the other portion strictly uses only cash, can any single interest rate rule serve both groups well? I develop a two-agent New Keynesian model calibrated to Ghana in which included households manage liquidity through mobile money under Baumol-Tobin demand, while excluded households depend on government transfers under fiscal dominance. I find a critical threshold at approximately 70 percent financial exclusion. Below it, aggressive inflation targeting is optimal for both household types. Above it, the welfare surface for included households develops an interior optimum, the optimal Taylor rule diverges across groups, and no single rule resolves the conflict. The distributional cost of monetary policy is convex in exclusion: the welfare variance ratio between household types rises from 7.6:1 at 50 percent exclusion to 98:1 at 80 percent, the range observed across Sub-Saharan Africa. Aggregate welfare statistics mask this entirely. The trade-off is reducible only through financial inclusion, not through monetary policy design.

title: Population Aging, Regional Integration, and Economic Growth Across U.S. Counties *
affiliations: Colorado State University, Fort Collins, Colorado State University, Fort Collins and Colorado State University, Fort Collins

detail.title: Population Aging, Regional Integration, and Economic Growth Across U.S. Counties *

declarations.funderStatement: Economic Development Administration University Center award ED23DEN0G0062

detail.abstract: This paper examines how the economic effects of population aging vary across space. Using U.S. county data from 2000 to 2020, we estimate the impact of changes in the share of adults aged 60 and older on GDP per capita growth. We instrument for aging using lagged age structure from historic censuses to address endogeneity. We find that a 10 percent increase in the 60+ population share reduces GDP per capita by roughly 4-5 percent, but this average masks substantial spatial heterogeneity. Aging has little measurable effect in large, economically integrated labor markets, while generating sizable growth declines in smaller and more isolated regions. Sectoral analysis reveals contractions in agriculture, construction, and manufacturing alongside expansions in health care and professional services; however, only economically integrated counties appear able to offset sectoral contraction and avoid aggregate losses. These results suggest that the local consequences of demographic aging depend not only on industrial structure but also on regional integration and labor market connectivity.

title: Resolving Human-Elephant Conflicts: Bridging Human Rights with Environmental Law

detail.title: Resolving Human-Elephant Conflicts: Bridging Human Rights with Environmental Law

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: Human-elephant conflict (HEC) in Bangladesh represents a critical intersection of environmental degradation, wildlife protection, and human rights obligations. Increasing encounters, particularly in the Mymensingh border region, have resulted in significant human fatalities, economic losses, and retaliatory killing of elephants. This paper examines the legal and policy dimensions of HEC through the lens of environmental law, animal law, and constitutional human rights, arguing that current governance frameworks inadequately address the root causes of conflict. While Bangladesh has adopted international commitments such as the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and CITES, domestic implementation remains weak, particularly in relation to habitat corridor protection and sustainable mitigation strategies. The study evaluates both harmful and non-lethal deterrent mechanisms, advocating for ecologically sustainable solutions such as beehive fencing, chili-based deterrents, and community-based early warning systems. It concludes that an integrated, rights-based approach-combining habitat restoration, legal reform, and community participation-is essential for achieving long-term human-elephant coexistence.

title: A Theory of Trust in Institutions
affiliations: Yale University - Law School and Hebrew University of Jerusalem - Faculty of Law

detail.title: A Theory of Trust in Institutions
detail.abstract: We identify a structural source of declining trust in major institutions that arises from success rather than failure. Institutions build trust by adhering to a mandate, but that trust transforms institutions into platforms that amplify insiders' influence regardless of what they do. This amplification endogenously activates non-mandated activity at the margin, causing trust to decline as institutions become more influential. We refer to this mechanism as elite drift. Increasing effort in the mandated task cannot raise long-run trust, because higher trust also strengthens incentives for mandate-divergent activity. More generally, increases in institutional influence, whether through greater reach or more effective insiders, reduce trust unless mandate enforcement tightens in tandem. When outsiders imperfectly attribute outputs across peer institutions, trust spillovers arise, and elite drift at one institution can raise trust at others. These dynamics persist even when the mandate adjusts endogenously. Our framework provides a theory of institutional trust grounded in organizational design rather than differences in public beliefs.

title: Understanding Socio-Economic Struggles: A Study of the Experience of the Poor in Selected Sub-Saharan African Countries

detail.title: Understanding Socio-Economic Struggles: A Study of the Experience of the Poor in Selected Sub-Saharan African Countries

keywords: Economic development and Poverty. JEL Classification: E00

detail.abstract: The study shows the exclusion of the poor in various governance programmes. It analyses some developing countries in Africa. In most of these countries, the poor are excluded from the economic policies implemented by their governments. The analysis shows that there is evidence of ongoing and persistent poverty, which is strongly supported by exclusive economic policies in line with extractive political institutions, but there is also a kind of institutional ignorance and discrimination of opportunities that has been strongly supported by patterns of rejection in the first place. There are also reasons why poor countries are overly dependent on Western countries to a significant degree. This dependence, however, makes a significant part of these countries corrupt and strongly aligned with exclusive policies and extractive institutions.

title:
Institutional Resilience and Democratic Sustainability in
Post-Transition Europe: Lesson from Romania and Central Eastern Europe

detail.title:
Institutional Resilience and Democratic Sustainability in
Post-Transition Europe: Lesson from Romania and Central Eastern Europe

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: This paper conceptualizes institutional resilience as a core condition of democratic sustainability in post-transition Europe. Building on neo-institutionalist approaches and recent scholarship on democratic resilience, we argue that democracies endure when three capacities align: policy coherence, procedural legitimacy, and civic/monitory participation. Using a comparative, theory-guided design, we analyze Romania, Poland, Hungary, and Slovakia (2007-2025), triangulating V-Dem/Eurostat indicators with documentary evidence (EU Rule of Law reports, CEPEJ) and interpretive analysis. Romania illustrates "reactive resilience" anchored in judicial independence and civic vigilance; Slovakia shows "restorative resilience" after corruption scandals; Poland exhibits "societal compensatory resilience," where civic mobilization offsets institutional regression; Hungary demonstrates "instrumental resilience without democracy," combining administrative capacity with normative decay. We integrate these findings into a three-dimensional model-institutional, normative, and communicative-showing how feedback loops convert crisis into learning. The paper concludes that sustainable democracy depends less on constitutional design alone and more on the institutionalization of learning: redundant veto points, impartial procedures that generate trust, and a monitory public sphere that sustains continuous accountability. For EU policy, the shift from conditionality to capacity (e.g., RRF) can foster endogenous resilience when supranational norms are domestically internalized rather than externally imposed.

title: Getting the Target Right in Return Prediction
affiliations: Fordham university and MBS School of Business

detail.title: Getting the Target Right in Return Prediction

declarations.funderStatement: Adam Zaremba acknowledges the support of the National Science Centre of Poland [grant no. 2022/45/B/HS4/00451].

detail.abstract: We show that a largely overlooked design choice-how returns are defined as prediction targets-drives machine learning performance in stock returns. Using a large international panel of equities from 35 markets over 1994 to 2024, we compare transformations applied to stock characteristics and target returns. Transforming the target from raw to standardized or rank-based returns nearly triples predictive accuracy and doubles portfolio returns. Feature transformations play a secondary role. Rank-based targets perform best on average but discard information about return magnitudes, leading to underperformance when dispersion or skewness is high, particularly among micro-cap stocks. The optimal transformation varies across markets and over time.

title: DETECTING LATENT VOLATILITY CONTAGION: A PROJECTED SCORE ESTIMATOR FOR ROUGH VOLATILITY MODELS

detail.title: DETECTING LATENT VOLATILITY CONTAGION: A PROJECTED SCORE ESTIMATOR FOR ROUGH VOLATILITY MODELS

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a feasible estimator for the source-screened latent contagion object isolated in the first two papers and applies it to a balanced Oxford-Man realized-volatility panel of eight global equity indices. Starting from the reduced local Gaussian block experiment, it represents local alternatives by covariance derivatives, removes the target-only tangent space, and estimates the remaining source-screened component with a low-dimensional projected covariance-score GMM statistic. The paper derives the projected-score geometry, proves the associated local Gaussian efficiency, rough-regime projected-rank, pilot-adaptive transfer, and uniform minimax results, and validates the implementation in synthetic experiments using closed-form information and noncentrality constants. In the Oxford-Man application, estimated physical-measure roughness lies between about 0.04 and 0.09 across the panel, with H_P approximately 0.071 for SPX, while the full-sample directed contagion map is dense and economically informative through intensity ranking and rolling stability rather than sparse edge selection. The paper closes the trilogy with a feasible estimator, a validation protocol, and a real-data physical-measure application, while leaving matched option-panel P/Q classification for later work.

title: Eco-Normalization as Diagnostic Architecture: A Cross-Case Analysis of Framework Requirements for Detecting Implementation Failure

detail.title: Eco-Normalization as Diagnostic Architecture: A Cross-Case Analysis of Framework Requirements for Detecting Implementation Failure

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Gillian Kerr, PhD, was commissioned to undertake this work and was financially compensated for their time. Deena M. Hamza, PhD, is the creator of the Eco-Normalization framework and has an invested (non-financial) interest in studying its utility.
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: New Frontiers Research Fund - Exploration (NFRFE-2021-00540)

detail.abstract: The Eco-Normalization Framework (ENF) (Hamza & Regehr, 2021) provides an integrating architecture for proactively (and retrospectively) assessing whether innovations become genuinely embedded in practice. The diagnostic power of ENF increases when complementary frameworks address the specific failure mechanisms guided by holistic inquiry. This structured retrospective analysis of ten published implementation studies across five sectors (i.e., healthcare, medical education, software engineering, criminal justice, and community public health) identifies five complementary frameworks that, layered within ENF's diagnostic structure, detected the range of failure patterns documented across these cases. The resulting architecture is a structured hypothesis derived from cross-case evidence, not a validated classification system, and provides the analytical foundation for a practitioner-facing diagnostic tool. Normalization Process Theory and Interest Holder Mapping proved universally relevant across all ten cases. Backwards Design, COMB , and PDSA Cycles demonstrated strong but context-dependent relevance. Five recurring failure patterns, specifically surface adoption, context blindness, champion dependency, aspiration mismatch, and parallel process, were traceable across cases and systematically mappable to specific framework gaps. Each framework maps onto a distinct area of inquiry within ENF's architecture, which functions as an integrating lens, borrowing from NPT's embedding mechanisms, CFIR's systems-level determinants, and Reflexive Monitoring in Action's learning discipline within a single diagnostic structure rather than as a competing framework. This suggests a practitioner tool design in which foundational diagnostics (NPT, Interest Holder Mapping) run by default while conditional diagnostics (Backwards Design, COMB , PDSA) are triggered by implementation characteristics. The architecture was derived from cases in predominantly high-income, English-speaking settings; its applicability to other contexts remains to be explored.

title: Senior Citizen Assistance System: A Humanized Smart Mobile and IoT-Based Eldercare Framework

detail.title: Senior Citizen Assistance System: A Humanized Smart Mobile and IoT-Based Eldercare Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that there are no personal, financial, or professional conflicts of interest that could have influenced the outcomes of this study. The research was conducted independently as part of an academic project, and all results presented are unbiased and solely based on the system design and implementation.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve direct clinical trials or human subject experimentation. Any testing performed was limited to simulation or controlled environments. No personal or sensitive data of individuals was collected or stored without consent. Therefore, formal ethical approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted as part of a final year academic project and did not receive any external funding from public, commercial, or non-profit organizations. All resources used in the development of the system were self-supported or provided by the institution.

detail.abstract: We live in a world where the pace of daily life has accelerated dramatically, yet our elderly loved ones require more attention, patience, and care than ever before. The mismatch between what senior citizens need and what modern families can actually provide has become one of the quiet crises of our generation. This paper presents the Senior Citizen Assistance System (SCAS)a practical, affordable, and genuinely useful solution built on Android mobile technology and the Internet of Things (IoT). At its heart, SCAS is designed to bridge the gap between elderly individuals living with limited mobility or chronic illness and the caregivers who want to keep them safe from a distance. The system brings together automated medicine dispensing with smart schedules, continuous health monitoring through wearable sensors, an emergency panic alert with GPS location sharing, smartphone-based fall detection using accelerometer data, sleep cycle tracking, on-demand live video supervision, and an intelligent doctor recommendation engine trained on a decision tree algorithm. The hardware layer uses NodeMCU (ESP8266), Arduino Mega, and Raspberry Pi 3all widely available, low-cost components. Two purpose-built Android applicationsone for the senior citizen and one for the caregiverremain connected in real time through Firebase cloud synchronization. Evaluation in real-world conditions demonstrated a medicine dispensing success rate of 90%, emergency panic alert delivery of 85%, fall detection accuracy of 88%, health monitoring packet reliability of 97%, and doctor recommendation relevance of 75%. SCAS is not just another academic prototypeit is a meaningful step toward making dignified, technologyassisted aging accessible to families who need it most.

title: Navigating the crowdfunding landscape: a study of knowledge trajectories based on main path analysis
affiliations: Széchenyi István University, Kautz Gyula Faculty of Economics, Department of Logistics and Forwarding, Students, Higher Institute of Computer Science of El Manar, Tor Vergata University, Cranfield University - Logistics and Supply Chain Management and MODUL University Vienna

detail.title: Navigating the crowdfunding landscape: a study of knowledge trajectories based on main path analysis

keywords: Main path analysis Paper type Literature review

detail.abstract:
Purpose-Crowdfunding (CF) has become an increasingly popular means of financing for entrepreneurs and has attracted significant attention from both researchers and practitioners in recent years. The purpose of this study is to investigate the core content and knowledge diffusion paths in the CF field. Specifically, we aim to identify the main topics and themes that have emerged in this field and to trace the evolution of CF knowledge over time.

Design/methodology/approach-This study employs co-word clustering and main path analysis (MPA) to examine the historical development of CF research based on 1,528 journal articles retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection database.

Findings-The results of the analysis reveal that CF research focuses on seven themes: sustainability, entrepreneurial finance, entrepreneurship, fintech, social entrepreneurship, social capital, and microcredits. The analysis of the four main paths reveals that equity CF has been the dominant topic in the past years. Recently, CF research has tended to focus on topics such as fintech, the COVID-19 pandemic, competition, Brexit, and policy response.

Originality/value-To the authors' best knowledge, this is the first attempt to explore knowledge diffusion dynamics in the CF field. Overall, the study offers a structure for analyzing the paths through which knowledge is diffused, enabling scholars to effectively manage a large volume of research papers and gain a deeper understanding of the historical, current, and future trends in the development of CF.

detail.abstract: German Abstract: Die Metapher des „Pflügens mit fremdem Kalbe“ (Lobe 1917) war erstaunlich wirkmächtig und wird bis heute für die Rufausnutzung im UWG-Nachahmungsschutz rezipiert. Vergessen ist aber, dass die Metapher im Zusammenhang mit der vergleichenden Werbung geprägt wurde. Ihr wird eine alttestamentarische Grundlage (Ri 14,18) unterstellt. Der Beitrag verfolgt diese Referenz in der christlichen und jüdischen Theologie. title: Intermediary Margins and Drug Costs: Evidence from PBM Spread-Pricing Bans
affiliations: , Bocconi University, Bocconi University - Department of Policy Analysis and Public Management and Yale University

detail.title: Intermediary Margins and Drug Costs: Evidence from PBM Spread-Pricing Bans
detail.abstract: Pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) often use spread pricing, charging health plans more for a drug than they reimburse pharmacies and retaining the difference. We study how state bans on spread pricing affect negotiated prices and beneficiary costs in Medicare Part D. Using staggered policy adoption between 2020 and 2025, we estimate event-study difference-indifferences models on plan-county-year data linked to drug acquisition-cost benchmarks. We find that spread-pricing bans reduce beneficiary cost sharing and total annual beneficiary costs, with little change in acquisition-cost measures. At the same time, observed negotiated prices rise modestly. The results suggest that these policies primarily compress intermediary margins and reallocate payments within the drug supply chain rather than lowering underlying acquisition costs. The findings show that regulating PBM pricing practices can reduce patients' financial burden even when observed plan-facing prices do not fall.

title: The Economics of Representation: Why FHIR Compliance Costs Without Clinical Return

detail.title: The Economics of Representation: Why FHIR Compliance Costs Without Clinical Return
detail.abstract: Background. The European Health Data Space and national digital-health strategies treat Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) as the minimum viable representation standard for clinical artificial intelligence, with compliance obligations propagating to primary-care practices across the EU-27, the United Kingdom, and adjacent jurisdictions. The clinical premium attributed to FHIR adoption has been asserted rather than measured. Objective. To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of FHIR adoption, compared with flat tabular text (status quo) and with openEHR archetype-rich structuring, as input representations for small-language-model primary-care pipelines, and to translate the finding into procurement and policy recommendations. Methods. We extend standard incremental cost-effectiveness analysis to representation depth as an intervention. Effectiveness is taken from a recent paired three-arm simulation of 50 synthetic primary-care patients with three repeats per arm, yielding semantic F1 as a dimensionless fidelity proxy (Stummer 2026). Costs follow Fermi methodology previously applied to ontological-drift cost estimation (Stummer 2026b), using Eurostat and OECD practice counts, published per-practice digital-infrastructure compliance estimates, and national-budget anchors for Germany and the United Kingdom. Results. Mean semantic 𝐹 1 was 0.193 under flat text (95 per cent confidence interval 0.164 to 0.223), 0.198 under FHIR (0.177 to 0.218), and 0.228 under openEHR (0.203 to 0.254). The paired Cohen's 𝑑 for FHIRflat was 0.033 with a 95 per cent confidence interval spanning zero (-0.244 to +0.310). The paired Cohen's 𝑑 for openEHR-FHIR was 0.329 (+0.044 to +0.613), with the interval excluding zero. EU-wide FHIR-compliance spend for primary care under European Health Data Space mandates is estimated at EUR 3 to 7 billion per year, central estimate EUR 4.5 billion. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of FHIR over flat, expressed as euros per 0.01 𝐹 1 gain, is of the order of EUR 1.1 trillion per 𝐹 1 point, compared with EUR 48 to 97 billion per 𝐹 1 point for openEHR over FHIR. Under the willingness-to-pay thresholds examined in this analysis, calibrated against healthoutcome proxies, the FHIR-over-flat comparison fails to achieve dominance in more than approximately 10 per cent of parameter configurations; openEHR-over-FHIR achieves dominance in approximately 55 per cent. Conclusion. FHIR adoption under European Health Data Space mandates pays the compliance cost of structured exchange without producing a measurable clinical-fidelity gain over flat text in the primary-care small-language-model setting. Archetype-based representation does produce a measurable gain. Three complementary policy pathways follow: European Health Data Space revision to specify archetype-level representation as the semantic-fidelity minimum, national procurement policy to condition generalpractitioner information-technology funding on archetype adoption, and indemnitypremium risk-adjustment by representation depth. Limitations: semantic F1 is a proxy for clinical outcome and is not calibrated to qualityadjusted life years; the Fermi cost estimates are order-of-magnitude; the evidence base is small-language-model and synthetic-patient specific; the analysis is European and does not generalise to the United States or Asia.

title: Resources, Time, and Structural Integrity: A Four-Layer Ex-Ante Verification Framework for Climate Finance VERA-TCV™ — Empirical Validation Across Five GCF Projects

detail.title: Resources, Time, and Structural Integrity: A Four-Layer Ex-Ante Verification Framework for Climate Finance VERA-TCV™ — Empirical Validation Across Five GCF Projects

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This research did not involve human participants, human tissue, or personal data collection. All data used in this study are derived from publicly available GCF project documents, Annual Performance Reports, and IEU LORTA evaluation reports. Ethics approval was therefore not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted independently and received no external funding from any government agency, international organization, or private entity.

detail.abstract:
Climate finance evaluation frameworks have long relied on ex-post performance measurement and self-reported compliance, leaving structural design failures undetected until implementation has already begun. This paper introduces VERA-TCV™, a four-layer ex-ante structural verification framework that operationalizes a behavioral premise established in Meatball Theory (Hur, 2025): human self-interest is not a flaw to be corrected, but a structural constant to be embedded within system design. The central argument is that climate finance evaluation must shift from success probability prediction to failure mode identification — asking not whether a project's intentions are virtuous, but whether its architecture is capable of producing the intended outcome despite human behavioral constraints and environmental fragility.

VERA-TCV™ consists of four independent models applied sequentially across the causal layers of
a Theory of Change. VERA™ verifies intent fidelity and reality anchoring at the input layer. ToC:f(x)™ verifies causal structural integrity from activity to output. C-FAIR™ assesses the environmental and financial conditions under which outputs can translate into outcomes. VORTA™ quantifies the social value realization from outcomes to impact. Each model operates as an independent deterministic engine; failure at any layer is structurally separable from performance at others.

The framework is validated against five GCF-funded projects across four continents — FP004 Bangladesh, FP017 Chile, FP026 Madagascar, FP069 Bangladesh, and FP101 Belize — spanning sectors from coastal adaptation to forest conservation and rural resilience. Pre-assessment judgments derived solely from funding proposal documents are mapped against Annual Performance Report time-series data, yielding directional accuracy rates of 86 to 100 percent across cases with five to seven year verification horizons. Cross-validation against IEU LORTA randomized control trial evaluations for FP026 and FP069 confirms methodological complementarity: where LORTA measures treatment effects in components that functioned, VERA-TCV™ identifies structural failure in components that did not — including failure modes that randomized designs are structurally unable to detect.

These findings suggest that structural design quality and environmental delivery capacity are separable dimensions of climate project performance, and that their separation is identifiable ex-ante. The recurrence of identical structural signals — C-FAIR S2 capacity weakness, ToC:f(x) causal exclusivity gaps, and VERA reality anchoring failures — across projects with heterogeneous sectors, regions, and implementing entities indicates a portfolio-level pattern rather than isolated project failures. VERA-TCV™ offers a replicable audit methodology for climate finance design verification,
with implications for project approval, portfolio diagnostics, and the development of structural integrity standards in concessional finance.

title: Decentralization Theater: A Three-Layer Taxonomy of Competing Forms of Centralization in DeFi

detail.title: Decentralization Theater: A Three-Layer Taxonomy of Competing Forms of Centralization in DeFi

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a theoretical and empirical paper using only publicly available on-chain data; no human subjects or personal data were involved.
declarations.funderStatement: None. This research was conducted independently with no external funding.

detail.abstract: "Decentralization" in on-chain finance has become theater: a rhetorical banner that masks the competing forms of centralization actually governing protocol behavior, producing both judicial overreach (invalidated in Van Loon v. Department of the Treasury) and regulatory paralysis (the SEC's withdrawn investigation of Uniswap Labs). Drawing on Oliver Williamson's transactioncost theory of economic governance, this Article proposes a three-layer taxonomy of DeFi as three discrete structural equilibria: Layer 1 (crypto-native, corresponding to Williamson's market), Layer 2 (hybrid, tokenized voting and delegated authority), and Layer 3 (permissionedinstitutional, corresponding to Williamson's hierarchy)-operationalized through a multidimensional coding scheme covering validator concentration, governance entropy, asset whitelisting, user permissioning, dependency profile, and legal-entity exposure. The taxonomy is validated through a triple-event study of OFAC's 2022 sanctions on Tornado Cash, the 2023 district-court affirmance, and the 2025 delisting following the Fifth Circuit's reversal, using layershare time series constructed from DeFiLlama and RWA.xyz data. Activity redistributes across layers predictably under each shock-a pattern that a binary or spectrum framework cannot produce-and the mismatch between regulatory tools and governance forms is not a failure of agency imagination but the predictable cost of asking the wrong question; replacing "is this decentralized?" with "which layer is this?" converts the current enforcement impasse into a tractable matching problem between tool and tier.

title: Comprehensive Classification of Statistical Methods: A Hierarchical Taxonomy from Foundations to Research Frontiers

detail.title: Comprehensive Classification of Statistical Methods: A Hierarchical Taxonomy from Foundations to Research Frontiers

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, patient data, or animal subjects. Therefore, ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Statistical methodology has evolved into a vast and highly fragmented landscape spanning classical inference, Bayesian analysis, causal identification, time series econometrics, and modern machine learning. While this expansion reflects the discipline's intellectual richness, it has also produced conceptual silos, incompatible notational systems, divergent philosophical commitments, and limited crossreferential engagement-consequences that impede both pedagogical transmission and applied research. This paper develops a comprehensive, mathematically rigorous hierarchical taxonomy that unifies this fragmented landscape into a coherent conceptual framework. The exposition is organized into five interconnected domains: Descriptive Statistics (measures of central tendency, dispersion, shape, and graphical methods); Inferential Statistics (estimation theory, hypothesis testing, and regression analysis); Advanced Graduate-Level Statistics (multivariate analysis, time series, Bayesian inference, survival analysis, and robust methods); Doctoral and Research-Level Statistics (high-dimensional inference, causal identification, machine learning, and computational statistics); and an Application Summary contextualizing these methods across clinical trials, economics, genomics, and other domains. A central contribution is the explicit integration of traditionally separated domains, demonstrating that seemingly distinct techniques share common underlying principles rooted in probability theory, optimization, and the data-generating process. Each methodological class is developed with formal mathematical foundations, explicit assumptions, diagnostic considerations, and real-world applications. This work serves as both a unifying reference for researchers and a rigorous conceptual guide for advanced study in modern statistical science.

title: Climate Change and Human Development in India: A District-level Spatial Econometric Analysis

detail.title: Climate Change and Human Development in India: A District-level Spatial Econometric Analysis
detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of climate change on human development across districts in India using the spatial econometric models. Focusing on three dimensions of human development index such as, education, health, and livelihood for the pre-and post-COVID years of 2015 and 2022, it employs spatial autoregressive (SAR) and spatial error (SEM) models to observe both direct and spillover effects. The findings reveal that climate exposure variables such as rainfall and soil quality positively influence education and livelihood conditions over space and time, while rising temperature adversely affects health outcomes. Significant spatial association indicates that the development process as well as the climatic risks in India are interrelated at the regional-level. The results highlight strong regional disparities and highlight the urgent need for coordinated policy responses to achieve sustainable human development following the present shifting climate conditions in India.

title: WAGE-Bench: Measuring the Economic Value of AI in Real Work *
affiliations: University of California Berkeley, Haas School of Business

detail.title: WAGE-Bench: Measuring the Economic Value of AI in Real Work *
detail.abstract: This paper introduces WAGE-Bench, a new framework for evaluating artificial intelligence based on the practical economic value it creates in human work. Standard benchmarks measure technical capability but reveal little about how much AI actually reduces the cost of completing real tasks. WAGE-Bench addresses this gap by eliciting individuals' willingness to accept compensation for performing realistic tasks under alternative AI conditions-without AI, with AI assistance, or with alternative models. Differences in willingness to accept yield a common monetary metric of AI's practical value, enabling comparisons across models, tasks, occupations, and user populations. The framework occupies a middle ground between conventional benchmarks and randomized controlled trials: cheaper, faster, and more scalable than RCTs, yet more closely tied to real-world usefulness than standard benchmarks. We develop the framework conceptually and illustrate its feasibility through a pilot experiment in which undergraduate students value familiar tasks with and without AI access. The pilot reveals substantial variation in the perceived value of AI across tasks, with the largest gains concentrated in technical and cognitively demanding activities.

title: Thermo-Informational Accounting (TIA): A Dual-Component Value Framework for Post-Scarcity Economies -Originally Proposed as the Joule-Byte Synthesis -A Post-Monetary Framework for Type-I Civilization

detail.title: Thermo-Informational Accounting (TIA): A Dual-Component Value Framework for Post-Scarcity Economies -Originally Proposed as the Joule-Byte Synthesis -A Post-Monetary Framework for Type-I Civilization
detail.abstract: Modern economic systems measure value through socially constructed monetary instruments that emerged under conditions of material scarcity. As technological civilization advances toward energy abundance and knowledge-intensive production, these instruments become progressively misaligned with the physical basis of economic activity. This paper proposes Thermo-Informational Accounting (TIA)-a conceptual accounting framework grounding economic value in two physically meaningful components: Exergy (usable energy, in Joules) and Functional Information (codified knowledge with demonstrated productive capacity, valued in energy-equivalent units). Three mathematically grounded propositions are developed: a thermodynamic efficiency anchor (η = Ex_min / Ex), a production exergy function (Ex = f(X,T,M,I)), and an IP depreciation model (V_j(t) = V_j(0)•e^(-λt)). The framework is presented as a complementary measurement standard-not a replacement for monetary systems-intended to operate alongside conventional accounting during a multi-century transition. Core limitations, including the absence of a fully operationalizable functional information measure and unresolved commons governance, are explicitly acknowledged as open research problems.

title: STRUCTURAL TRANSFORMATION OF THE BALANCE SHEET OF RELIANCE INFRASTRUCTURE LIMITED: AN EMPIRICAL ANALYSIS (2014-2025)

detail.title: STRUCTURAL TRANSFORMATION OF THE BALANCE SHEET OF RELIANCE INFRASTRUCTURE LIMITED: AN EMPIRICAL ANALYSIS (2014-2025)

keywords: Indian Corporate Sector JEL Classification: G32 (Financing Policy

detail.abstract: Purpose: This study examines the structural transformation of the balance sheet of Reliance Infrastructure Limited (RIL) over 2014-2025, a decade marked by aggressive expansion, sectoral diversification, pandemic disruption, and post-crisis restructuring. Design/Methodology/Approach: Using secondary data from published financial statements, this study applies descriptive statistics, trend analysis, correlation heatmaps, ANOVA, multiple regression analysis, simultaneous equation modelling, and selected machine learning techniques to examine interrelationships between leverage, liquidity, asset growth, and profitability. Findings: RIL's balance sheet evolution reflects strategic leverage during expansion phases, followed by measured deleveraging supported by diversified revenue streams and improved operational efficiency. Liquidity patterns reveal adaptive financial management during crisis periods, particularly around the COVID-19 shock. Econometric results confirm statistically significant interdependencies between debt and profitability, while machine learning models enhance predictive understanding. Practical Implications: The integrated framework offers practitioners and policymakers a replicable model for evaluating the long-term financial architecture of large diversified conglomerates in emerging markets. Originality/Value: By integrating traditional financial analysis with advanced modelling tools within a single empirical framework, this study contributes a holistic methodology for evaluating balance sheet transformation in diversified emerging-market conglomerates over a decade-long horizon.

title: Irreversibility Field Anatomy: Probability Currents, Housekeeping-Excess Decomposition, and Fundamental Bounds on Strategy Capacity

detail.title: Irreversibility Field Anatomy: Probability Currents, Housekeeping-Excess Decomposition, and Fundamental Bounds on Strategy Capacity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. This research was conducted independently with no institutional affiliation in finance, no external funding, and no relationships with any organization that could have influenced the study. All data sources are publicly available. No proprietary or non-public information was used.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses only publicly available financial market data (equity returns, option chain data, publicly reported macroeconomic indicators). No human subjects, patient data, clinical trials, surveys, or personally identifiable information were involved. Ethics approval is not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. All computational resources, data subscriptions, and infrastructure costs were self-funded by the author. Data sources used: Yahoo Finance (equity returns, option chains), CBOE delayed feeds, FRED API. No grants, institutional support, or third-party funding of any kind.

detail.abstract: We introduce the Irreversibility Field Anatomy (IFA), a quantitative research framework that characterizes equity markets as thermodynamic non-equilibrium systems. The framework constructs three empirical objects from return covariance matrices alone: (1) the probability current field J(x; t), measuring net probability flux in state space; (2) the entropy production rate (EPR) field Φ, which is strictly positive for irreversible dynamics and zero only under detailed balance; and (3) a Hatano-Sasa decomposition of EPR into housekeeping entropy (σhk, the friction cost of maintaining the current correlation topology) and excess entropy (σex, the information cost of topology change). A Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation bound establishes that no linear trading strategy can exceed SRmax(τ) = √(τ•Φ/2) at timescale τ. We validate the framework across five equity universes (S&P 500, GICS Sectors, Macro Futures, S&P Financials, S&P Technology) using 104/104 pre-registered falsification tests. The EPR of the S&P 500 exceeds the symmetric-OU null by z = 398 standard deviations and is orthogonal to realized volatility (Spearman ρ = 0.131). The Hatano-Sasa decomposition successfully classifies the 2008 Global Financial Crisis as friction-dominated and COVID-19 as information-dominated at the sector and macro level, with a decisive reldiff = 0.65 for macro futures. The decomposition fails for individual-stock universes (N = 16 to 89), where correlated crisis sell-offs compress the distinguishing signal, constituting a methodological boundary result. The per-asset TUR ceiling SRmax_pa(21d) = 1.19 for the S&P 500 lies within the empirically realized range for systematic strategies. We commit to honest reporting of all preregistered falsification tests: 4/5 hard kills pass for large-N universes; 5/5 pass for sector and macro aggregates.

detail.abstract: This paper critically examines structural deficiencies within the Indo-U.S. Bilateral Trade Arrangement (BTA) during the first quarter of 2026, with particular attention to its distributive consequences across Indian agriculture and allied sectors, including automobiles, fertilisers, pharmaceuticals, petrochemicals, and technology. Situating the analysis within the evolving post-pandemic global political economy, it argues that emerging geopolitical realignments are likely to reconfigure global hierarchies over the coming decades. Drawing on Putnam's Two-Level Game framework, the study conceptualises trade negotiations as diplomatic interdependent processes shaped by domestic political constraints and international strategic imperatives. Historical parallels from pre-Second World War geoeconomic tensions illustrate how coercive economic trade instruments can exacerbate systemic instability. The paper contends that asymmetrical trade dependence, subject expertise and empirical negotiation wing heightens India's vulnerability to external shocks and policy coercion. The literature strongly suggests that the 1970s and 1980s were characterised by relatively "natural" trade policies. It ultimately concludes by proposing strategic interventions aimed at strengthening foreign policy autonomy, academic governance, institutional resilience, and macroeconomic stability.

title: Residential Integration, Brain Drain, and Remittances in the Caribbean Diaspora: An Immigration Systems Approach

detail.title: Residential Integration, Brain Drain, and Remittances in the Caribbean Diaspora: An Immigration Systems Approach
detail.abstract: Does the immigration system that best integrates migrants into the destination society simultaneously minimise their economic contributions to the islands that produced them? This article tests that hypothesis in the Caribbean-a laboratory uniquely suited to the purpose: the same islands send migrants to three destination systems of sharply contrasting selectivity, enabling a comparative design that holds cultural and historical context broadly constant while varying the institutional filter. Using central bank remittance data corrected for informality, residential dissimilarity indices from Statistics Canada Census 2021, ONS Census 2021, and ACS 5-year 2023, and a local integration quality measure at census tract level, we examine nine corridors connecting Jamaica, Haiti, and Trinidad & Tobago to Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States. The principal finding is a 3.6× differential in remittances per emigrant between the Jamaican-UK and Jamaican-Canada corridors, robust to all informality correction factors tested because the ratio is algebraically invariant to a uniform correction. This differential is not explained by current residential geography: D(Jamaica-born, Toronto) ≈ D(Jamaica-born, London) at moderate levels while remittance intensity diverges by 3.6×. The primary explanatory mechanism is the historical social infrastructure generated by Windrush-era racialised exclusion, whose psychosocial legacy persists in remittance behaviour beyond the residential conditions that produced it. The Haitian corridors qualify the hypothesis; Trinidad & Tobago identifies an origin-income boundary condition; and Barbados-whose corridor-level data are not published-constitutes a structural argument in itself: the island most penalised by the mechanism is least equipped to document it. The article proposes three compensatory policy instruments and identifies the gendered structure of Caribbean migration and the France-Martinique/Guadeloupe corridor as priorities for future research.

title: Evil Versus Rage: Distinguishing Moral Judgment from Clinical Understanding in Violent Behavior

detail.title: Evil Versus Rage: Distinguishing Moral Judgment from Clinical Understanding in Violent Behavior

declarations.declarationOfInterest: na
declarations.ethicsApproval: na
declarations.funderStatement: na

detail.abstract: Violent behavior is often interpreted through two primary lenses; moral judgement and clinical understanding. While society frequently labels acts of violence as "evil", such interpretations may overlook the role of rage as an intense emotional and psychological state shaped by trauma, stress, and impaired emotional regulation. This paper explores how violent actions can be understood through the interaction between moral condemnation and clinical explanations of rage, including the inability to manage emotional responses, leading to reactions that are disproportionately intense or very inappropriate actions by an individual often felling overwhelmed or flooded by emotions and mental health conditions. Sociocultural influences are given certain attention, including stigma surrounding mental health, norms related to masculinity, religious beliefs and systemic inequities that shape how individuals interpret, express, and respond to emotional distress. These factors may be especially influential within marginalized communities, including Black communities regardless of education, economic or political affiliation, where historical mistrust of healthcare systems and cultural frameworks influence help-seeking behaviors and perceptions of mental illness. By examining violence through both moral and clinical perspectives, this paper argues for a balanced approach that promotes accountability while also recognizing the role of rage and environmental stressors in shaping behavior. Understanding this dual framework is essential for improving prevention strategies, reducing stigma and enhancing culturally competent counseling practices.

title: Programmable Waterfall Enforcement and the Convexity Swap: On-Chain Derivative Infrastructure for Structured Credit

detail.title: Programmable Waterfall Enforcement and the Convexity Swap: On-Chain Derivative Infrastructure for Structured Credit
detail.abstract:
Tokenized structured credit products can now be issued, custodied, and monitored on-chain at institutional scale. What remains discretionary is waterfall enforcement: the act of suspending equity distributions, diverting cash to reserves, and accelerating senior principal repayment when overcollateralization or interest coverage triggers breach. In the currently observable tokenized structured credit products, these decisions are made by committees operating on governance timescales—days or weeks after market conditions have already propagated through duration, spread, and liquidity.

This paper closes the enforcement gap through three contributions. First, a formal waterfall specification defines the Deterministic Waterfall Engine as a finite state transducer with provable invariants: sequential priority preservation, bounded trigger response within one evaluation interval, and governance non-interference. Second, a smooth prepayment intensity model completes the negative convexity result deferred from Paper II, establishing sufficient conditions for negative second-derivative behavior (d²P*/dr² < 0) under mortgage-style CPR behavior. Third, the Convexity Swap—a derivative instrument that settles against the realized curvature of the deterministic policy surface—specifies non-discretionary, on-chain-settled hedging for the convexity exposure created by the instrument class introduced in Papers I and II; its market formation remains contingent on broader institutional adoption of the underlying architecture.

Empirical validation under the 2022 rate shock illustrates the enforcement dividend. On an $80 Senior / $20 Equity stack simulated over 36 months under actual 2022–2024 composite rate data, the enforced waterfall redirected $23 of additional Senior principal to accelerated paydown—a 3.6× increase over the static waterfall's scheduled amortization—and suspended $24 of Equity distributions, routing them to Senior protection. At the 36-month horizon, the enforced waterfall had returned $7 more of Senior principal than the static case under identical stress. The basis between policy surface curvature and instrument price curvature is characterized explicitly, with a computable hedge ratio derived from on-chain observables. Integration architectures for Morpho Blue and Aave are developed, with Morpho's immutable-market design identified as the natural complement to deterministic credit-state systems.

The trilogy now specifies the core deterministic stack for on-chain structured credit: margin framework (Paper I), instruments (Paper II), and enforcement with hedging (this paper). Market formation and institutional deployment remain the next stage.

title: SMINORA EcoTech : un écosystème numérique de standardisation volontaire et de transparence professionnelle pour les services non réglementés

detail.title: SMINORA EcoTech : un écosystème numérique de standardisation volontaire et de transparence professionnelle pour les services non réglementés

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of SMINORA EcoTech and has a direct interest in the development of the described system.

detail.abstract: Le secteur des services esthétiques non réglementés-prothésie ongulaire, coiffure, massage, cosmétologie-constitue un marché mondial caractérisé par une asymétrie d'information structurelle et des risques sanitaires silencieux (agents pathogènes viraux asymptomatiques : hépatites B et C, VIH, HPV ; OMS, 2020 ; ECDC, 2022). Cet article présente SMINORA EcoTech, un écosystème numérique innovant fondé sur une architecture technologique progressive (QR code, NFC, capteurs, intelligence artificielle) et un standard de qualité volontaire protégé par dépôt de propriété intellectuelle (INPI France + RU Reg.). Le système de Proof Levels (1 à 5) constitue le coeur de l'innovation : il transforme des biens de croyance non vérifiables en données objectives accessibles en temps réel, avec une trajectoire vers un scoring automatisé par intelligence artificielle (SMINORA IA). L'architecture modulaire Core + Modules permet une extension sans obstacle à tout secteur de services à relation client directe. L'analyse d'un marché mondial non couvert par un tel standard, conétayée par des échanges avec des professionnels dans de multiples pays, confirme le potentiel d'expansion internationale. Le dispositif génère un double effet économique et social : autoRégulation du marché sans coûts étatiques et allègement de la charge sanitaire publique.
