detail.abstract: Recreational marijuana legalization broadens adult access, but users at different ages likely face very different consequences. We estimate the effects of recreational marijuana laws (RMLs) on mental health, behavior, and labor market outcomes using a difference-indifferences imputation strategy on state-year-age-group panel data from 2003-2024 across US states. RMLs raise past-year marijuana use roughly twice as much among 18-25 year olds as among adults 26 and older (6.4 versus 3.3 percentage points). This differential exposure by age helps explain the pattern in our results: the average effect on mental health is null, but this masks a sharp asymmetry. Young adults under 25 report more poor mental health days, exercise less, and become more likely to experience long-term unemployment, amounting to roughly 107,000 additional young adults in unemployment spells over one year across RML states. Adults over 50 report less joint pain, exercise more, and show suggestive income gains. The coherence across five outcomes points to two agespecific channels: cannabis exposure during neurological development for young adults, and pain management for older adults. The findings imply that a uniform adult access model for marijuana legalization produces costs concentrated among younger adults and benefits among older adults.

title: Policy-Driven or Finance-Driven? Dynamic Evidence on China's NEV Market

detail.title: Policy-Driven or Finance-Driven? Dynamic Evidence on China's NEV Market
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the relative dominance of industrial policy versus financial conditions in driving China's New Energy Vehicle (NEV) passenger market. Utilizing a monthly dataset from January 2017 to February 2026, we estimate a Vector Autoregression (VAR) model incorporating NEV sales growth, domestic interbank rates (SHIBOR), global risk sentiment (VIX), and commodity price dynamics (CRB). We explicitly model policy regime shifts through six exogenous dummies capturing major subsidy reforms, the COVID-19 shock, and strategic tax incentive extensions. Our results indicate that financial and global variables yield only transitory and economically marginal effects on NEV sales, suggesting that the sector is partially insulated from global market volatility. Conversely, policy-related shocks exert statistically significant and persistent influence, particularly during the 2019 subsidy overhaul and the post-2023 demand contraction following subsidy termination. Forecast error variance decomposition confirms that policy-driven variation accounts for the vast majority of NEV sales dynamics, dwarfing the explanatory power of credit conditions or international risk factors. These findings establish that China's NEV sector operates under a policydominant regime rather than a finance-driven one. This structural insulation provides a critical empirical foundation for understanding how industrial policy acts as a buffer in the context of global financial decoupling, offering essential insights for green industrial transition and emerging market policy design in an increasingly volatile global environment.

detail.abstract: This study investigates the effect of geopolitical risk and investor attention on stock market volatility in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries from 2019-2024. Using COVID-19 deaths and Google Search Volume Index (SVI) data related to the Russo-Ukraine war, and the Gaza conflict as proxies for investor sentiment, this analysis explores the relation between market volatility and sentiment. Fixed-effects panel regressions and country-level models reveal that COVID-19 deaths and attention to the Russo-Ukrainian war significantly increase market volatility, while attention to the Gaza conflict is associated with weaker or negative effects. The U.A.E. exhibits a distinct pattern, showing reduced volatility during heightened war-related attention, consistent with its role as a regional financial safe haven. These findings highlight the importance of digital information flows in transmitting geopolitical risk to financial markets.

detail.abstract: The social media business model is based on maximising data harvesting, which is monetised through advertising. To this end, social media firms resort to addictive design features. This addiction promotes excessive use of the platform and results in mental health harm. While some jurisdictions have attempted to curb addictive features through existing laws, such as torts, and new regulations, the viability of competition law in curbing addiction-causing business models by dominant firm(s) has not received the required attention. This paper argues, building on the German Facebook case, that the use of addictive features impairs user autonomy, which is the core of 'freely given' consent within the meaning of data protection laws, and hence results in exploitative abuse. The paper also suggests concomitant remedies. A simple cease-and-desist order is not an effective remedy in the specific context. It rather requires an iterative and participative approach to craft fair and healthy design. The paper argues for pursuing corrective justice through private law enforcement and creating a Mental Health Redressal Fund through the public competition law framework.

title: Stakeholder Populism, Campaign GM, and the Economic Education of the Public
affiliations: University of Warwick - Warwick Law School and George Washington University - Department of Strategic Management & Public Policy

detail.title: Stakeholder Populism, Campaign GM, and the Economic Education of the Public
detail.abstract: Populism does not sit well with corporate social responsibility because it tends to collapse all stakeholders into one group, "the people." We consider an alternative relationship between populism and corporate social responsibility, which we capture in the notion of stakeholder populism. We show how, in a historically contingent time and place-the late 1960s and early 1970s in the United States-a group of activist lawyers known as the Project on Corporate Responsibility posited themselves as representatives of "the people," understood as the numerous stakeholders of the American corporation, and campaigned to impose socially responsible behavior on the management of General Motors (GM) and subsequently other large US corporations. Setting the Project against the broader mutations of postwar liberalism, we draw on new archival material to trace the making of Campaign GM and consider how this turning point in the history of corporate governance was also a catalyst for the regrouping of the business establishment and the strategic reorientation of its efforts toward the economic education of the public.

title: Experimental and Analytical Evaluation of Urban Heat Mitigation Strategies in Islamabad: A Policy-Oriented City-Scale Modeling Approach

detail.title: Experimental and Analytical Evaluation of Urban Heat Mitigation Strategies in Islamabad: A Policy-Oriented City-Scale Modeling Approach
detail.abstract: Urban heat is a major environmental and urban planning challenge emerging in many rapidly growing cities, particularly those experiencing rapid, unregulated expansion and increased area of impervious surfaces. Islamabad, although originally planned and designed with some level of green infrastructure, has begun to exhibit signs of urban warming (e.g., increased high temperatures) due to increasing density of infrastructure, land-use changes, and loss of vegetation cover in growing areas. This study examines the degree to which urban heat mitigation strategies can be expected to decrease peak surface temperature in Islamabad using a combined empirical and analytical approach. Data collected in the field are used to obtain surface temperature measurements for several different urban material types (e.g., asphalt, concrete, vegetated surfaces, shaded surface areas and rooftops) in peak summer solar conditions. These measurements are then used as baseline inputs to an analytical model that takes into account the thermal effect of three different urban heat mitigation strategies: (i) increasing the coverage of tree canopy in urban areas, (ii) implementing high reflectivity (generally called "cool") roofing systems, and (iii) replacing conventional pavements with more reflective paving materials. A scenario analysis was performed to evaluate the comparative reduction of peak surface temperature under three types of strategies both individually and in combination. A cost-benefit analysis was also assimilated into this study to evaluate the economic benefits of each strategy in relation to the degree of cooling that would be achieved through its implementation.

title: Women in Kerala: Religious Tradition and Developmental Disaster

detail.title: Women in Kerala: Religious Tradition and Developmental Disaster
detail.abstract: This paper examines the historical evolution of women's lived experiences within the Kerala development model, a framework widely celebrated for prioritizing human development indicators such as education and healthcare despite modest economic output. Drawing on primary sources — including historical newspapers (The Times of India, India Abroad), the Malayalam women's magazine Lakshmi Bhai, oral histories from the Cochin Royal Family and Christ University, religious and colonial records, and census and legislative documents — alongside a substantial secondary literature, the study investigates why advancements in female literacy and health in Kerala coexist with persistently high rates of gender-based violence, suicide, and domestic subordination. By comparing four religious communities — upper-caste Nair Hindus, lower-caste Ezhava Hindus, Muslim Mappilas, and Syro-Malabar Christians — the paper argues that religion is the predominant distinguishing factor shaping Malayalee women's access to education, inheritance, labor, and public life. Across otherwise distinct traditions, however, a common pattern emerges: women's education has historically been oriented toward service and domesticity rather than independent livelihood. The paper contends that understanding these entrenched, religiously-inflected gender hierarchies is essential for interpreting the paradox at the heart of the Kerala model and for designing reforms that translate human-capital gains into substantive gender equality.

title: Veil at Scale: Anonymity, Collective Action, and John Rawls

detail.title: Veil at Scale: Anonymity, Collective Action, and John Rawls

keywords: and John Rawls JEL Classication: D72

detail.abstract: Rawls's veil of ignorance is routinely pierced by tribal identity, which gives citizens a concrete view of where they stand. I formalize an old paradox: the free-rider problem, usually decried as a collective-action pathology, can reconstruct the veil. When polity size N grows, pivot probability shrinks as 1/ √ N and tribal instrumental payo vanishes. What remains is the tension between in-group sanction (scaled by ballot observability) and an intrinsic fairness preference. I characterize a critical region in which scale and anonymity jointly tip voters toward the universal policy, and derive seven testable implications spanning ballot reform, proxy-vote disclosure, jury design, and socialmedia de-anonymization.

detail.abstract: Income inequality and unequal access to economic and social opportunities remain persistent challenges in the Global South, with gender-based disparities constituting one of the most entrenched forms of inequality. Despite sustained economic growth in several developing economies, women continue to face systematic disadvantages in education, employment, income generation, asset ownership, and decision-making power. These disparities not only reinforce income inequality but also constrain inclusive and sustainable development. This study undertakes a comparative crosscountry analysis to examine how opportunity gaps in education, health, and employment-together with gender empowerment-shape income inequality outcomes in the Global South. Using balanced and unbalanced panel data for 20-30 Global South countries over the period 2000-2024, the study constructs a composite Opportunity Gap Index capturing educational access and attainment, health outcomes and financial protection, and labour market inclusion and quality. Income inequality is measured using the Gini coefficient and alternative distributional indicators to ensure robustness. Employing fixed-effects, random-effects, and dynamic panel estimation techniques, the findings reveal that wider opportunity gaps are significantly associated with higher income inequality. Education-related opportunity gaps emerge as the most influential dimension, followed by employment and health disparities. The results further indicate that higher levels of gender empowerment-proxied by female labour force participation, educational attainment, and composite gender indices-significantly reduce income inequality and improve access to economic opportunities. Institutional quality and social protection spending are found to mitigate the inequality-enhancing effects of opportunity gaps. By integrating income inequality, opportunity gaps, and gender empowerment within a unified analytical framework, this study advances the literature in development and gender economics by moving beyond income-centric explanations and highlighting the structural role of unequal opportunities. The findings underscore the critical importance of gender-responsive investments in human capital, labour market formalization, and equitable health financing to achieve inclusive growth and advance the Sustainable Development Goals in the Global South.

detail.abstract:
This report offers a practical guide for engaging stakeholders to promote environmentally sustainable practices and Plant-based Innovation, defined broadly to include diversified proteins, agricultural technology, food-waste reduction, and nature-based materials.

Through six case studies, the report examines what stakeholder advocacy tactics have succeeded and what has not. The cases include Engine No. 1's campaign against ExxonMobil, Carl Icahn's proxy fight with McDonald's, FAIRR's institutional-investor engagement on sustainable proteins, As You Sow's work on antimicrobial resistance, the Humane Society's proposals with Tyson Foods, and Mighty Earth's deforestation campaigns against JBS.

It traces historical developments in corporate shareholder activism (drawing on Sarah Soule's research on combining insider and outsider tactics), reviews the science supporting Plant-based Innovation as a climate and biodiversity solution, and analyzes the corporate playbook of delay, experimentation, and front-group misinformation used to resist change.

The report concludes with five recommendations: define objectives and benchmarks; frame requests in terms of financial materiality; build large and diverse coalitions; escalate strategically; and maintain ongoing pressure. An appendix provides a sample engagement letter.

title: Legal identity documentation and socioeconomic inclusion among forcibly displaced persons: Evidence from 31 host countries

detail.title: Legal identity documentation and socioeconomic inclusion among forcibly displaced persons: Evidence from 31 host countries
detail.abstract: Legal identity documentation is essential for accessing rights, services, and formal economic activity. Yet crosscountry evidence on its link to the socioeconomic inclusion of forcibly displaced persons remains limited. This study estimates this relationship using harmonized microdata from 34 UNHCR Results Monitoring Surveys (2022-2024) in 31 host countries and shows that possession of documentation is consistently associated with better outcomes across multiple domains, including higher school enrollment, greater financial inclusion, improved housing, increased social protection coverage, improved child and maternal health, and notably higher employment. These patterns hold for both refugees and asylum seekers and for internally displaced persons, although the incremental association of documentation is systematically smaller in camps-especially for employment, income, and access to formal financial services-than in out-of-camp settings. The findings point to a broad "legal identity dividend," while underscoring that documentation is necessary but not sufficient to secure full inclusion in restrictive settings

title: A Cause-and-Effect Relation between Natural Resources, Government Policies, and Agricultural Economics

detail.title: A Cause-and-Effect Relation between Natural Resources, Government Policies, and Agricultural Economics
detail.abstract: This research is being conducted to answer the basic question of the degrading condition of the agriculture sector in Punjab. This land has helped people to sustain their lives for centuries. But there has been a continual decline in its productivity, size and sustenance. The high dependence on rice-wheat cultivation cycle and overexploitation of land has led to certain unforeseen complex problems. The rapidly depleting water table and high toxicity of soil from over-use of fertilizers and pesticides has led to multiple health issues, which is reflected in the high incidence of cancer and organ failures. The basic cause is the lack of diversification of crops. Diversification has been avoided by farmers due to some hidden facts. These hidden facts will be unveiled in this research paper. The title of this article-"A Cause-and-Effect Relation between Natural Resources, Government Policies, and Agricultural Economics" has been selected to define the join the scattered dots of government influence, economic loss in agriculture and degradation of land. To make it easy to understand, this hypothesis has been made by using microeconomic concepts and graphical representation. This hypothesis will help economists make more refined policies for the agrarian sector. Even students can take measures to support the farmers. Together, these insights aim to guide future efforts toward a more sustainable and inclusive agricultural model in Punjab.

title: Exploring Food Supply Chain Trends in the COVID-19 Era: A Bibliometric Review
affiliations: Széchenyi István University, Kautz Gyula Faculty of Economics, Department of Logistics and Forwarding, Students, Higher Institute of Computer Science of El Manar, University of Rome Tor Vergata, MODUL University Vienna, Edith Cowan University and Cranfield University

detail.title: Exploring Food Supply Chain Trends in the COVID-19 Era: A Bibliometric Review
detail.abstract: Recently, the food supply chain (FSC) has been severely disrupted due to the COVID-19 pandemic, putting the vital flow of food products from farmers and producers to the ultimate consumers at risk. Furthermore, due to the pandemic, several food organizations have been prompted to rethink their strategies for the future. Although the literature on FSC research in the COVID-19 era is increasing, no attempt has been made to summarize this stream of research using bibliometric techniques. This paper fills this knowledge gap and looks at the current scholarly discourse around the FSC and COVID-19. Applying bibliometric techniques, 287 journal articles were extracted from Scopus and analyzed to determine the temporal evolution of FSC research, the most productive journals, researchers, countries, and the most relevant keywords and publications. To construct a keyword co-occurrence network and categorize the relevant literature, we used the computer program VOSviewer. The findings demonstrate the rapid expansion of FSC research during the COVID-19 pandemic. In addition, the top authors, publications, and nations for scientific output were also determined. Keyword co-occurrence network and detailed qualitative analysis both illustrate that FSC research revolves around six main themes: the impact of COVID-19 on the FSC and agriculture, FSC resilience, food waste and insecurity, fisheries and aquaculture, blockchain technology, and governance and innovation. This study represents the first effort to map worldwide FSC research in the COVID-19 era and draw on a comprehensive collection of journal articles and bibliometric approaches. It offers academics, practitioners, and decision-makers a snapshot of the state of the art in the FSC field and points to where further research is needed.

detail.abstract: We test the Permanent Income Hypothesis using three near-simultaneous macroeconomic shocks in Nigeria (2023-2024): the naira-redesign cash crisis, the fuel subsidy removal, and the Dangote Refinery commissioning. Each shock isolates a distinct consumption-smoothing mechanism. Using household panel data and difference-indifferences , we find that liquidity-constrained households experienced a consumption collapse more than 60 percent larger than financially included households, an order of magnitude beyond comparable estimates from high-income settings. The result is robust to alternative specifications, survives bounds on selection bias, and holds across all wealth quartiles. Pre-trend validation using four waves of the GHS-Panel (2010-2018) confirms parallel consumption trajectories over eight years before the shocks, corroborated by six rounds of a national phone survey measuring food insecurity. Households perceiving the subsidy removal as beneficial exhibit smoother consumption adjustment, consistent with forward-looking expectations updating. Refinery proximity is associated with higher consumption, consistent with precautionary-savings release, though entangled with baseline regional inequality. A formal Euler equation test rejects consumption smoothing, with the rejection concentrated among constrained households. The findings establish that financial inclusion is a precondition for welfare-preserving fiscal reform in developing economies.

title: A Note on the Economic Cost of Exponential-Utility Tractability in Incomplete Markets

detail.title: A Note on the Economic Cost of Exponential-Utility Tractability in Incomplete Markets
detail.abstract: Exponential utility is the standard analytic device for pricing non-traded exposures in incomplete markets, valued for the closed forms it delivers. The tractability is not free: it forces the local price of skewness to equal the local price of variance, suppressing a dimension of preference that decreasing absolute risk aversion treats as informative. This note measures what the suppression costs. Statically, the curvature-matched exponential certainty equivalent is exact through second order but errs at third order through a signed correction governed by the prudence gap and the skewness of the payoff; the correction is zero precisely when the investor has exponential utility. Dynamically, in a stopping problem where an illiquid position is exposed to forced liquidation at less favourable terms, exponential utility removes wealth from the stopping boundary, while decreasing absolute risk aversion restores it: the threshold is nondecreasing in wealth, and the same prudence-gap mechanism that drives the static error makes the exponential benchmark locally too patient when forced liquidation skews the continuation payoff to the left.

title: Are You Intelligent? Perhaps You Should Think Again! (Why Greater Intelligence Is No Vaccine Against Error)

detail.title: Are You Intelligent? Perhaps You Should Think Again! (Why Greater Intelligence Is No Vaccine Against Error)
detail.abstract:
This essay explores why highly educated, intelligent, and cultivated elites, from the intellectuals of the 1789 French Revolution to Silicon Valley elites and economists predicting the 2008 financial crisis, consistently fail in judgment, prediction, and foresight. Drawing on empirical research in psychology, sociology, and behavioral economics, the study argues that the fallibility of elites does not stem from a lack of intelligence but from four structural mechanisms. First, concealed cognitive bias, where greater intelligence enables more sophisticated self-deception. Second, group identity, where intelligence is deployed to defend preexisting beliefs rather than seek truth. Third, specialist tunnel vision, where deep expertise blinds peripheral awareness. Fourth, distance from real-world consequences, where elites face no "skin in the game."

The central claim is that higher intelligence does not eliminate error but can deepen and entrench it. Historical and contemporary evidence demonstrates that elites, despite their cognitive advantages, often fall victim to motivated reasoning, identity-protective cognition, and systemic blind spots. The essay concludes that intellectual humility, epistemic vigilance, and institutional safeguards, such as accountability, transparency, and diverse feedback mechanisms, are essential to mitigate these risks.

This analysis contributes to the philosophy of mind, moral psychology, and political philosophy by offering a framework for understanding the limits of human rationality and the moral responsibilities of intellectual elites in shaping societal outcomes.

title: Multi-agent Adaptive Mechanism Design
affiliations: , Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - School of Engineering, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Institute for Data, Systems, and Society (IDSS) and University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign

detail.title: Multi-agent Adaptive Mechanism Design
detail.abstract: We study the sequential mechanism design problem in which a principal seeks to elicit truthful reports from multiple rational agents while starting with no prior knowledge of agents' beliefs. We introduce Distributionally Robust Adaptive Mechanism (DRAM), a general framework combining insights from both mechanism design and online learning to jointly address truthfulness and cost-optimality. Throughout the sequential game, the mechanism would estimate agents' beliefs, then iteratively updates a distributionally robust linear program with shrinking ambiguity sets to reduce payments while preserving truthfulness. Our mechanism guarantees truthful reporting with high probability while achieving \tilde{O}(N\sqrt{T}) cumulative regret, and we establish a matching lower bound showing that no feasible adaptive mechanism can asymptotically do better. The framework generalizes to plug-in estimators (DRAM+), supporting structured priors and delayed feedback. To our knowledge, this is the first adaptive mechanism under the general settings that maintains truthfulness and achieves optimal regret when incentive constraints are unknown and must be learned.

title: Measuring Uncertainty in the Small Firm Economy: Evidence from the UK Small-Cap Market

detail.title: Measuring Uncertainty in the Small Firm Economy: Evidence from the UK Small-Cap Market
detail.abstract: Uncertainty is central to many areas of entrepreneurship, from investment, hiring, and financing decisions, yet most widely used uncertainty proxies are macro wide or policy focused and often reflect the behaviour of large listed firms. This paper constructs a small-firm equity-uncertainty index for the UK using the FTSE Small Cap. The index follows the logic of modern uncertainty measurement: uncertainty is the conditional volatility of outcomes that are hard to forecast, rather than realised volatility of the series itself. Using monthly FTSE SmallCap returns, we first estimate predictable components via an autoregressive model and then measure uncertainty as the volatility of the forecast error. Two operational estimators are produced: a rolling window estimate and an exponentially weighted moving average estimate. The resulting index captures prominent UK and global stress episodes and offers a targeted proxy for uncertainty faced by smaller listed firms. It also differs from popular market wide uncertainty measures, with smaller sensitivity to episodes largely concentrated in large growth equities. The index is easy to update, transparent, and designed to support empirical work on small firm returns, small firm financing conditions, and the broader small business cycle.

title: Beyond Economic Growth: A Multidimensional Index-Based Analysis of Sustainable Livelihood Security in India
affiliations: College Of Agriculture, Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya

detail.title: Beyond Economic Growth: A Multidimensional Index-Based Analysis of Sustainable Livelihood Security in India
detail.abstract: Background: Rural India is characterized by significant spatial disparities in economic opportunities, social development, and ecological sustainability, which collectively influence the resilience of livelihood systems. Despite sustained economic growth, rural livelihoods continue to face challenges arising from resource degradation, infrastructural gaps, and uneven access to human and physical capital. This necessitates a multidimensional assessment framework to better understand livelihood security beyond income-based measures. Aims: The study aims to construct a Sustainable Livelihood Security Index (SLSI) and assess interstate variations in livelihood security across India, while examining the relative contribution of ecological, economic, and social dimensions in shaping overall livelihood outcomes. Study Design: The study adopts a quantitative, index-based analytical framework using secondary data and composite index methodology. Place and Duration of Study: The study covers major Indian states using the most recent available secondary data from national sources. Methodology: The Sustainable Livelihood Security Index (SLSI) was constructed by integrating three core dimensions; ecological security, economic efficiency, and social equity. Relevant indicators under each dimension were selected based on conceptual relevance and data availability. The indicators were normalized using the min-max method and aggregated to compute dimension-specific indices. The overall SLSI was derived as the arithmetic mean of the three components. The resulting indices were used to assess interstate disparities and examine the relative influence of each dimension on livelihood security. Results: The findings reveal substantial interstate variation in livelihood security, reflecting uneven development across ecological, economic, and social dimensions. States with stronger social development indicators tend to achieve higher overall livelihood security, even when economic performance is moderate. In contrast, states with relatively high economic output often exhibit lower sustainability due to ecological stress and weaker social outcomes. The results further indicate that livelihood security is not determined by any single dimension but by the balanced interaction of all three components. Conclusion: The study demonstrates that sustainable livelihood security is inherently multidimensional and cannot be adequately captured through economic indicators alone. A balanced integration of ecological sustainability, economic performance, and social development is essential for improving livelihood outcomes. The index-based approach provides a robust framework for comparative analysis and contributes to a more comprehensive understanding of rural livelihood sustainability in India.

detail.abstract: We estimate a continuous-time life-cycle model in which labor-market shocks affect health through non-convex medical repair. Using PSID, MEPS, and RAND HRS data, we show that financially fragile households respond to adverse shocks by moving closer to subsistence, working more intensely, and delaying high-return treatment. In the model's main application, skill-biased technical change widens inequality not only through wages but also through endogenous repair failure, generating concentrated lower-tail losses in health, survival, and welfare. Relaxing repair barriers offsets a meaningful share of that damage, and a parsimonious general-equilibrium environment preserves the mechanism.

detail.abstract: The modern corporate conversation about workplace grief rests on a small set of widely repeated statistics, several of which are misattributed, methodologically opaque, or entirely unrelated to grief. The most commonly cited figure, $225.8 billion in annual employer losses attributed to grief, originates from a 2003 productivity audit covering all health conditions and was reframed as a grief-specific cost by a CDC Foundation press release more than a decade later. Other figures that anchor HR discourse, including a claimed 91 percent productivity drop and a manager identification rate of only 11 percent, trace to vendor reports and trade blog posts with no disclosed methodology. The weakness of these popular claims, however, should not be mistaken for weakness in the underlying field. A defensible peer-reviewed evidence base, developed through neuroimaging studies, prospective longitudinal cohorts, and rigorous meta-analyses, shows that bereavement affects cognition, physical health, work functioning, and workforce equity in ways that are material to employers and organizationally mishandled at scale. This paper separates what the research actually supports from what is merely repeated in HR discourse, proposes a five-dimension corporate bereavement readiness framework grounded in impairment, equity, and operational response, and identifies three priority research gaps: bereavement-attributable turnover, evidence-based return-to-work protocols, and independent evaluation of employer grief support platforms.

title: Effect of regulation on corporate governance practices and the quality of justifications of Brazilian companies
affiliations: Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS), Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS) - Department of Economics and Accounting and Federal University of Santa Catarina (UFSC)

detail.title: Effect of regulation on corporate governance practices and the quality of justifications of Brazilian companies
detail.abstract: Purpose-This study aims to investigate the influence of regulation on the adoption of corporate governance practices and the quality of justifications provided by Brazilian publicly traded companies under the "comply or explain" model. Design/methodology/approach-Based on a longitudinal analysis of 476 Corporate Governance Reports from 2020 to 2024, encompassing 12,330 disclosed practices, the study examines six monitoring mechanisms across three core areas: audit committee, internal audit and risk management/internal controls/compliance. From 4,133 cases of partial or nonadoption, qualitative content analysis was conducted using a hybrid model combining supervised machine learning and human validation. Findings-Companies listed on the Novo Mercado segment demonstrated higher rates of formal compliance and gradual improvement in justification quality. However, a persistent gap remains between adoption and meaningful disclosure, especially in other listing segments, where deficient justifications are more frequent. The findings indicate that regulatory obligation positively influences both the adoption of practices and the quality of explanations, though enforcement appears more effective in practice adoption than in disclosure standards. Research limitations/implications-The findings are limited to the Brazilian context, which features a unique regulatory environment and ownership structure. Comparative studies across other emerging markets are recommended. Practical implications-The results highlight the need for stronger regulatory oversight of not only compliance rates but also the substance of justifications. Enhanced guidance could improve the transparency and credibility of disclosures under the "comply or explain" framework. Social implications-Strengthening governance and disclosure practices fosters investor confidence, enhances market transparency and supports the long-term sustainability of organizations. Originality/value-This study contributes novel insights into how regulation shapes both the implementation and justification of corporate governance practices, combining traditional analysis with supervised artificial intelligence (AI) techniques in a major emerging market.

title: Beyond Black and Scholes: Learning About Option Valuation through the Q-Distribution
affiliations: New York University - Stern School of Business

detail.title: Beyond Black and Scholes: Learning About Option Valuation through the Q-Distribution
detail.abstract:
The returns process in the canonical Black-Scholes model produces a lognormal "P" distribution for the future stock price but option prices embody probabilities under a different "Q" distribution. The Q modifies the P to include risk premia and non-lognormal returns expectations. It is these differences that we must understand to move beyond Black and Scholes.

I explore Q versus P in E-mini S&P 500 index futures and options. With huge trading volume, very low transactions costs, and an underlying that is one of the world's most important financial variables, the E-mini is perhaps the best possible market for this study. A major goal is to present methodological innovations that mitigate the large amount of noise in market prices, and allow extraction of valuable information from the Q. Analyzing Q – P produces a number of interest results.
• The Q and the P have systematically different shapes: the Q is fat-tailed for losses on the left, as expected, but the right tail is much thinner than the lognormal. The Q sags below the P for medium-sized losses and gains, which is more consistent with lottery payoff preferences than risk aversion.
• Examining the standard returns-based variables used in no-arbitrage models, I show that some are substantially more important than others and that different portions of the Q and P returns space respond differently to each of them.
• Q - P differences also reveal broad variations over time and across option strikes in market sentiment and tolerance for risk, including effects at daily, weekly, and monthly periodicities.
• Changes in the Q – P difference permit a detailed look at how the market responds to an information event. A look at the behavior of the Q around an FOMC Federal Funds rate announcement adds a rich new set of results to the ongoing research in this area.
• Finally, regarding the accuracy of the Q in predicting the future index level, I find that over more than 20 years, on average the Q has been significantly closer to the distribution of realized returns than the benchmark P.

To support academic research in this promising area, I am happy to make the estimated Q distributions constructed in the paper available on request.

title: INTRO: APERTURA ECONÓMICA DE PHREVO

detail.title: INTRO: APERTURA ECONÓMICA DE PHREVO
detail.abstract: PHREVO — Planetary Human Revolution for Economic Value and Organization — is a post-capitalist economic framework designed as a structural replacement for capitalism rather than a reform of it. Built from the experience and knowledge of the Global South, PHREVO argues that the failure of existing alternative frameworks — from ESG to the SDGs to impact investing — lies not in their values but in their refusal to propose a complete alternative architecture. This paper presents the PHREVO framework in full: its philosophical foundations (dignity as economy, the ethics of care as operational principle), its structural architecture (the 4-16-64 matrix of 4 pillars, 16 domains, and 64 operational instruments), its measurement system (the PHREVO-Score, a six-dimension impact metric designed as an alternative to GDP), its ten policy families covering every domain of economic governance, and three working AI-powered evaluation applications that demonstrate the framework reasoning in real time. PHREVO is currently in early operational deployment through the Dignity Toolkit, a coordination infrastructure for immigrant communities in New York City. This paper invites peer engagement, methodological critique, and collaborative research development.

detail.abstract: We derive a theory of innovation-driven entrepreneurship in which contractual frictions in input markets shape both the implementation and the realized value of innovation. Production requires inputs to be supplied before uncertain revenues are realized, exposing input providers to payment shortfall risk. An innovation is implementable only if a contract simultaneously satisfies the entrepreneur's profitability condition and input providers' participation constraints, generating an implementation frontier that determines which ideas can be brought to market. Trust and liquid wealth act as imperfect substitutes, so contractual frictions shape not only which entrepreneurs can implement innovations, but also how much value can be realized from innovation.

Somatic & Physical Literacy™: A Descriptive Framework…

detail.abstract:
This paper introduces Somatic & Physical Literacy™ (SPL) as a descriptive framework for stabilizing language, accountability, and boundary clarity within the somatic field. It addresses a recurring problem in contemporary somatic and movement-related discourse: the collapse of appearance-level description into interpretation, explanation, and application, often resulting in misclassification, overreach, and implicit authority claims.

Operating under RC Posture™ (descriptive, non-instrumental), the paper defines SPL as an appearance-based literacy that maintains strict separations between what is observed, how it is described, and what is inferred or concluded. It clarifies key distinctions—including appearance versus interpretation, description versus explanation, and posture versus method—and situates these within a broader structural concern regarding drift across discourse environments.

The paper does not propose a method, therapeutic model, or evaluative framework. Instead, it establishes SPL as a descriptive accountability structure designed to preserve epistemic restraint and prevent the conversion of descriptive language into guidance, intervention, or authority. Its contribution is the stabilization of a vocabulary and boundary grammar that enables clearer communication, reduces misclassification, and supports citation-level precision within somatic and adjacent interdisciplinary domains.

title: Multi-Scale Crash Detection via RG Flow of Instanton Action

detail.title: Multi-Scale Crash Detection via RG Flow of Instanton Action
detail.abstract: We introduce a scale-dependent crash probability model by computing the instanton action at multiple observation timescales using renormalization group (RG) flow equations for financial correlations. The Epps effect-the empirical increase of cross-asset correlations with observation timescale-modifies the double-well potential barrier in correlation space, causing the tunneling rate to vary across scales. The instanton action S(inst)(l), computed at RG scale l = log(T/T₀), yields a "tunneling acceleration" signal α(crash) =-dS(inst)/dl that detects anomalous barrier erosion across timescales before it manifests at daily frequencies. We derive the RG-instanton equations, establish conditions under which α(crash) > 0 constitutes an early warning, and propose an empirical validation protocol on historical crash episodes (2008, 2020 COVID, 2022 rate shock). To our knowledge, the combination of renormalization group flow with instanton tunneling calculus for financial crash prediction has no published precedent.

title: Citation Counts and the Applicable Economic Standard: Why Patent Citation Analysis Cannot Satisfy Garretson's Apportionment Requirement

detail.title: Citation Counts and the Applicable Economic Standard: Why Patent Citation Analysis Cannot Satisfy Garretson's Apportionment Requirement

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that he has no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human subjects, patients, or participants. The analysis is based on publicly available legal decisions, statutory law, and aggregated industry success rates. Therefore, ethical approval and written informed consent were not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Patent citation analysis ("PCA") measures a different economic quantity than Garretson's apportionment requirement demands. The method measures bibliometric influence within a patent citation network-a metric that research has shown correlates with patent renewal decisions and aggregate licensing revenues at the individual patent level. Patent damages law requires measuring something different: the incremental value that the specific patented feature contributes to the specific accused product relative to available non-infringing alternatives. Garretson v. Clark, 111 U.S. 120 (1884), established well over a century ago that the patent owner must give evidence tending to separate or apportion the patented feature's contribution to the accused product's value, and that such evidence must be reliable and tangible. The Federal Circuit has operationalized that requirement to mean specifically evidence of the incremental value the patented feature adds to the accused product. PCA cannot satisfy Garretson's requirement as operationalized because it supplies evidence of a different economic quantity-bibliometric influence correlated with patent renewal value-rather than the product-specific incremental contribution the law requires. That gap is structural, not technical: no adjustment for patent age, technology class, self-citations, or observation date bridges a conceptual divide between measuring network position and measuring incremental product contribution. No prior court has evaluated PCA against Garretson's requirement as the Federal Circuit has consistently operationalized it. The economic critique developed here emerges from the author's experience as a damages expert in pharmaceutical and biotechnology patent litigation, where PCA has appeared as a royalty adjustment tool for early-stage comparable licenses, and the argument has not been developed in the legal literature in this form until now.

title: AI and the Economy: The Four Rates Which Define The Future (Short Version 1 )
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: AI and the Economy: The Four Rates Which Define The Future (Short Version 1 )
detail.abstract: AI will displace 22-25 million workers and generate more than enough prosperity to support every one of them. The $2.9 trillion in productivity gains will more than offset the displaced wage bill. We show that a faster, more capable AI makes actually the fiscal position stronger while leaving the number of displaced workers unchanged. AI will be more deflationary than the China trade shock, and more permanent. The combined supply and demand channels produce an average deflationary impulse of approximately-0.75% per year; roughly 50% larger than China's peak contribution to US disinflation (hitting services rather than goods). AI's footprint is already measurable in current data. We document $655 billion in excess productivity above pre-2022 trend, 2.5 million missing jobs in high-exposure sectors, and wages decoupling from productivity in direct proportion to each sector's automation ceiling. The economic debate about AI has produced a wide range of estimates and almost no coherent framework. This paper resolves both. Via a single framework, we endogenously derive the impact of AI on GDP, jobs, prices, and vendor economics producing internally consistent forecasts.

title: When the Chair Speaks: Firm-Level Pricing of FOMC Press Conferences

detail.title: When the Chair Speaks: Firm-Level Pricing of FOMC Press Conferences
detail.abstract: The modern FOMC day is two communication events thirty minutes apart: the written policy statement and the Chair's press conference. I measure each firm's option-implied response to the press conference, separately from its response to the statement, and price that response in the cross-section of FOMC-day stock returns. Firms with stronger press-conference exposure earn an FOMC-day long-short premium of 78 basis points per event, more than an order of magnitude larger than the statement-window counterpart, rising to 115 basis points in the post-2018 Powell era, when press-conference shocks grew materially larger. Yet the payoff structure is asymmetric: the premium is collected on dovish press-conference surprises and lost on hawkish ones — a pattern consistent with an insurance-style tail-risk premium, though a one-sided belief-updating channel would produce the same sign asymmetry. The press conference, not the written statement, is where firm-level monetary-policy risk is priced in the cross-section.

title: TRUMP'S TARIFFS AND THE CONSUMER BURDEN: A HIDDEN COST ANALYSIS

detail.title: TRUMP'S TARIFFS AND THE CONSUMER BURDEN: A HIDDEN COST ANALYSIS
detail.abstract: The effectiveness of tariffs as a policy tool continues to provoke global debate, particularly in light of the Trump tariffs. While the tariffs were introduced with the stated objective of incentivising consumers to shift toward more affordable domestic alternatives, this rationale rests on the flawed assumption that domestic prices remain unaffected by trade barriers. In practice, both imported and domestic goods saw price increases, with consumers bearing the financial burden. Moreover, while such policies may temporarily bolster employment in targeted sectors like steel and aluminium, they often result in net job losses due to disruptions in downstream industries such as manufacturing, construction, and retail sectors more labour-intensive and consumer-facing. This paper further examines overlooked retaliatory measures imposed by trade partners, which adversely impact U.S. exports and reduce global demand for American goods, thereby undermining the broader economy. Through a microeconomic lens, this study analyses how these dynamics converge to harm global consumers, particularly those in low- and middle-income groups. The findings reveal that the intended protective effects of tariffs are offset by inflationary pressures, job insecurity, and diminished consumer choice. Ultimately, the article questions whether such trade interventions achieve their objectives or merely redistribute economic strain from state to citizen. KEYWORDS: Consumer Costs, Trade Policy, Retaliatory Tariffs, Protectionism, Job Displacement

title: The Missing Half of the Queue: Why FERC Should Require Load-Side Interconnection Queue Disclosure

detail.title: The Missing Half of the Queue: Why FERC Should Require Load-Side Interconnection Queue Disclosure
detail.abstract: The U.S. generation interconnection queue is public record. The equivalent record for large load customers, including data centers seeking to connect at scales of hundreds of megawatts, is not. This brief argues that the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission should extend to the load side the same disclosure standard it established for generation interconnection over the past three decades. Drawing on a companion empirical paper (SSRN 6446446), the brief quantifies the cost of the current data gap, traces the regulatory history of generation-side transparency from FERC Orders 888 through 2023, documents emerging state-level precedents in Texas and Georgia, and identifies the tariff amendment mechanism through which FERC could act without new legislation.

title: Rational Foreclosure: A Stochastic Reference Point Model of Aspirational Abandonment under Positional Drift

detail.title: Rational Foreclosure: A Stochastic Reference Point Model of Aspirational Abandonment under Positional Drift

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial or personal relationships that could have influenced this study. This paper was developed with assistance from AI systems (Anthropic's Claude and DeepSeek). The formal proof in Appendix A was produced through an iterative adversarial process between the two systems. Full details are in the Acknowledgment section of the paper.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract:
The behavioral economics consensus holds that when people abandon long-term goals, they are making a mistake. Present bias, scarcity-induced bandwidth depletion, and insufficient self-control are the standard diagnoses; commitment devices and nudges are the standard prescriptions. This paper shows that for a specific and identifiable class of agents, the standard diagnosis is wrong and the standard prescription causes harm.

An agent with deterministic wealth accumulation faces a socially salient reference position evolving as a geometric Brownian motion. The agent chooses both a consumption process and a stopping time at which to permanently exit the positional race. Under log consumption utility and Kahneman-Tversky loss-averse preferences over the proportional wealth-to-reference gap, the value function reduces to a one-dimensional free-boundary problem in the wealth-to-reference ratio. Existence and uniqueness of the optimal stopping boundary is established as a formal theorem (Theorem 1) via viscosity solution methods, with numerical verification across three calibrated parameter sets and a full replication bundle deposited at Harvard Dataverse (doi:10.7910/DVN/V5NSZX).

The headline result inverts a foundational policy intuition. Higher reference volatility delays abandonment rather than accelerating it, because uncertainty about the moving target raises the option value of waiting. Policies designed to stabilize positional benchmarks — housing prices, wage ladders, promotion schedules — destroy this option value and accelerate exit among already-foreclosed agents. A welfare reversal follows: patience-inducing interventions that force continuation past the optimal boundary are strictly welfare-reducing, with losses that grow quadratically in the size of the displacement. The framework challenges the theoretical foundation of the nudge literature by showing that a class of observed present-biased behavior is the rational exercise of an optimal stopping rule, not a bias to be corrected.

title: Female-Managed Funds and Female-Led Firms: Allocation, Attention, and Affinity
affiliations: North Carolina State University, Mays Business School at Texas A&M University and

detail.title: Female-Managed Funds and Female-Led Firms: Allocation, Attention, and Affinity
detail.abstract: Identity-linked investing is often read as taste. We show otherwise. Across U.S. equity mutual funds, female managers overweight female-CEO firms by 0.13 percentage points of TNA (about 5% of mean exposure). After female-manager appointments, exposure rises by 0.31 percentage points. A taste-based affinity view predicts ESG co-tilts or return sacrifice; we find no support for either. Instead, the tilt is strongest in geographically proximate female-led firms and is accompanied by lower public-information acquisition (EDGAR downloads are lower), consistent with a comparative advantage in information processing and monitoring.

title: Migration diplomacy in the Gulf -non-state actors, cross-border mobility, and the United Arab Emirates

detail.title: Migration diplomacy in the Gulf -non-state actors, cross-border mobility, and the United Arab Emirates
detail.abstract: What is the role of non-state actors in the international politics of labour migration in the Gulf Cooperation Council countries? This paper employs a ‘migration diplomacy’ framework in order to examine the politics of regional mobility while interrogating the assumed centrality of the state in this process. It focuses on labour migration into the United Arab Emirates and draws on a range of primary sources in order to identify four types of non-state actors that seek to maximise their interests within the workings of Emirati migration diplomacy: public-private partnerships, namely the Tadbeer (‘procurement’) centres; corporations within the Emirati construction sector; business elites managing subcontracting companies; and, finally, non-governmental organisations and foreign consulting firms. The paper identifies how each of these four sets of actors pursues strategies that are able to strengthen, supplant, or undermine the state’s formal migration diplomacy aims. Furthermore, the Emirati case debunks the myth of the state as a centre of power in Gulf migration management via the kafāla (‘sponsorship’) system. Overall, the paper demonstates how a range of non-state actors can navigate migration management policymaking, thereby underlining the complexity of Gulf migration diplomacy.

title: PROTECTION OF DIGNITY AT WORK IN THE CONTEXT OF PERSONAL DATA PROCESSING THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE

detail.title: PROTECTION OF DIGNITY AT WORK IN THE CONTEXT OF PERSONAL DATA PROCESSING THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
detail.abstract: The protection of dignity at work represents a fundamental principle in both international and national labor regulations. The use of artificial intelligence to process personal data presents unique characteristics and risks in the context of labor relations, particularly from the perspective of dignity in the workplace. This article aims to explore some of these risks, referring to potential impacts on workers' personal lives, exposure to discrimination that affect dignity at work, and identify some mitigating measures. These practices could lead to illegal conduct that, while not intended by employers, might be overlooked, accepted, or even impossible to detect. In these cases, employer liability for the use of such technical means becomes significant.

title: The Size Mechanism Hypothesis: Capital Absorption Time, Not Information Diffusion Speed, Determines Trend Magnitude in Foreign Exchange Markets

detail.title: The Size Mechanism Hypothesis: Capital Absorption Time, Not Information Diffusion Speed, Determines Trend Magnitude in Foreign Exchange Markets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. The research was conducted independently using the author's own live trading data.

detail.abstract: The standard explanation for momentum attributes trend persistence to slow information diffusion among heterogeneous investors. This paper proposes and tests an alternative: trends persist because large capital repositioning takes time to be absorbed by available liquidity. The key empirical prediction is that trade duration, not economic surprise magnitude, should determine trend outcomes. Using 35,072 economic calendar events matched to 3,271 algorithmic trading signals across six USD currency pairs (2019-2026), four sequential tests consistently support the capital absorption mechanism: duration explains 10.1% of outcome variance while economic surprise explains 0.02% (ratio 50:1). Cross-market replication on the S&P 500 (3,884 US macro events, 887 trades) produces a 507:1 ratio, with surprise statistically indistinguishable from zero (p 1 The Size Mechanism Hypothesis = 0.64). The results challenge the informational foundations of momentum as described since Jegadeesh and Titman (1993).

title: The Co-Evolutionary Information-Capital System: Dual Prisoner's Dilemma, Coupled Dynamics, and a Game-Theoretic Foundation for Market Microstructure

detail.title: The Co-Evolutionary Information-Capital System: Dual Prisoner's Dilemma, Coupled Dynamics, and a Game-Theoretic Foundation for Market Microstructure

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. The research was conducted independently using the author's own live trading data.

detail.abstract: We develop a unified theory of co-evolutionary market dynamics built vertically from micro-level strategic incentives to macro-level observable phenomena. Market participants simultaneously play two prisoner's dilemmas: a strategy game (fundamental analysis vs momentum trading) and a speed game (patient execution vs front-running). We derive the payoff ordering T > R > P > S from market microstructure primitives. The population outcome of these games determines the four excitation parameters of a bivariate Hawkes process modelling the co-evolution of information and capital flows: the branching matrix G is the outer product of the two game outcomes, and its spectral radius ρ(G)-the order parameter for regime transitions-is an emergent property of the population game. The bivariate Hawkes dynamics feed into a coupled stochastic system where inventory I(t) and liquidity λ(t) co-evolve. We prove existence and uniqueness of strong solutions (Theorem 1), establish V-uniform ergodicity when δ² < 4γλ_min with explicit Lyapunov constants (Theorem 2), and characterise stationary moments with bounded error terms (Theorem 3). The phase diagram partitions parameter space into stable, quasi-oscillatory, and explosive regimes, with the boundary connected to the empirical phase transition (Z* ≈ 2σ, t = 20.41).

title: Regulatory Learning by Design
affiliations: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

detail.title: Regulatory Learning by Design
detail.abstract: Although ex-ante cost-benefit analysis is standard in rulemaking, many regulatory impacts can only be measured after a rule takes effect. This paper argues that regulations should be designed with ex-post evaluation in mind. We propose two main strategies to enhance such evaluation: differentiated implementation – through tiering, staggered rollout, or randomization — which creates treatment and control groups that support causal identification; and dual reporting, which preserves data continuity across definitional changes. We also recommend embedding evaluation staff early in the rulemaking process and investing in data infrastructure for external researchers. Together, these practices would improve regulatory accountability and lead to better, more evidence-based policy.

title: Auction Market Theory as an Emergent Property of Inventory Dynamics: The First Formal Mathematical Treatment

detail.title: Auction Market Theory as an Emergent Property of Inventory Dynamics: The First Formal Mathematical Treatment

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. The research was conducted independently using the author's own live trading data.

detail.abstract: Auction Market Theory (AMT), introduced by Steidlmayer (1984) at the Chicago Board of Trade, has been used by professional traders for four decades to interpret market structure through volume profile analysis. Despite widespread practitioner adoption, AMT has never received a formal mathematical treatment in the academic literature. This paper provides one. Using a two-equation stochastic system-an inventory process with Hawkes self-exciting arrivals and a linear price impact process-we show that every core AMT concept (value, value area, point of control, balance, imbalance, initiative activity, responsive activity, single prints, and excess) emerges as an analytically derivable property of the system. The volume profile is the stationary distribution of the price process during balance; the 70% value area is its confidence interval; the point of control is its mode. The balance-to-imbalance transition is a phase transition at a critical inventory 1 Auction Market Theory as Emergent Property threshold. The magnitude-direction separation theorem-which states that magnitude clusters while direction does not-is the formal content of Steidlmayer's central insight that the profile reveals structure but not direction. Empirical validation from 44,035 hourly FX bars and 17,716 gap-fade trades across 26 years confirms the predicted mapping. The paper bridges a persistent gap between practitioner market microstructure and academic theory.

title: The Theory of Tariff Incidence: Alexander Hamilton and His Nineteenth-Century Protectionist Followers

detail.title: The Theory of Tariff Incidence: Alexander Hamilton and His Nineteenth-Century Protectionist Followers
detail.abstract: Alexander Hamilton's treatment of the tariff features most prominently in his celebrated 1791 Report on Manufactures, yet Hamilton's views on the subject extend well beyond this text. His lesser-known works, Continentalist No. 5 and his Report on the Impost, contain an impressive analysis of tariff incidence grounded in market competition. According to Hamilton, it is the competition between purchase and sale of commodities which conditions whether the incidence of a tariff will be shouldered more by domestic consumers or by foreign producers. By the nineteenth century, followers of Hamilton, including Daniel Raymond, Ellis H. Roberts, Van Buren Denslow, and Henry M. Hoyt, transformed this insight into a dynamic theory which contends that the incidence of a protective tariff has a tendency to shift with industrial development. According to this theory, tariffs on infant industries fall primarily on domestic consumers, thereby naturally providing maximum protection when industries need it most. However, as industries mature and domestic supply increases, tariff incidence will increasingly shift toward foreign producers, thereby reducing the burden on consumers over time. In developing this theory, nineteenth-century American Protectionists offered a sophisticated defence against the claim that tariff incidence falls exclusively on domestic consumers.

title: THE MAGNITUDE-DIRECTION SEPARATION THEOREM Magnitude Clusters, Direction Does Not: A Universal Property of Self-Exciting Point Processes

detail.title: THE MAGNITUDE-DIRECTION SEPARATION THEOREM Magnitude Clusters, Direction Does Not: A Universal Property of Self-Exciting Point Processes

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. The research was conducted independently using the author's own live trading data.

detail.abstract: We establish a general property of marked self-exciting point processes: the magnitude of consecutive events exhibits positive autocorrelation (AC1 > 0) while the direction of consecutive changes exhibits non-positive autocorrelation (AC1 ≤ 0). We prove this separation theorem for the Hawkes process class and verify it empirically across four domains: foreign exchange markets (264,000 H1 bars and 41,000 D1 bars across six currency pairs, 2000-2026), seismology (37,650 earthquakes in Southern California, 2010-2025), and neuroscience (1.19 million spikes from 257 mouse cortical neurons and 24,535 spikes from 16 human hippocampal neurons). The theorem holds without exception across all seven datasets. Magnitude AC1 ranges from +0.055 to +0.315; direction AC1 ranges from-0.316 to-0.016. We derive a closed-form expression relating the magnitude AC1 to the Hawkes branching ratio and show that the direction result follows from the conditional independence of event signs given the intensity process. The theorem resolves an active debate in seismology regarding magnitude independence and provides a unified explanation for volatility clustering in finance, aftershock patterns in geophysics, and burst dynamics in neural spike trains.

title: Presentation on Why Some Futures Markets Thrive and Others Die

detail.title: Presentation on Why Some Futures Markets Thrive and Others Die
detail.abstract: Hilary Till provided this presentation in Chicago at the NCCC-134 Conference on Applied Commodity Price Analysis, Forecasting, and Market Risk Management in April 2026.  Futures trading can be seen as a game where the competing players, the hedgers and the speculators, each have sufficient economic reasons to participate. The referee of this game, the government authorities, has the power to stop the game, if there is not a convincing economic rationale for a futures contract’s existence. Therefore, a futures contract can succeed only if it responds to a commercial hedging need, and if speculators are able to manage the risk of taking on the hedger’s positions. In addition, a convincing case must be made that the contract serves an economic purpose; otherwise the contract is at risk to either being banned or heavily curtailed.

title: Small Firms are Not All Alike: Return and Financial Health Heterogeneity Within the Smallest Decile

detail.title: Small Firms are Not All Alike: Return and Financial Health Heterogeneity Within the Smallest Decile
detail.abstract: This study examines how financial characteristics vary within the smallest marketequity decile of U.S. listed nonfinancial firms and how that variation relates to portfolio returns. Using CRSP and Compustat data from July 1963 to June 2024, we subdivide the smallest decile into two halves (10A, 10B) and four quartiles (10W, 10X, 10Y, 10Z) and compare seven accounting ratios and portfolio returns across the subgroups. We document pronounced heterogeneity in returns and financial characteristics: valueweighted mean annual returns decline from 49.0% in the largest quartile to-37.0% in the smallest. Profit margin, return on common equity, dividend payout, and growth in net operating assets deteriorate monotonically with decreasing size, while leverage differences are weak and economically small. Within every subgroup, relatively smaller firms systematically outperform relatively larger firms by 4.09 to 12.35 percentage points per month, and portfolio weight concentration in the smallest quartile is 85% above equalweighting. These patterns help reconcile the longstanding divergence between valueand equal-weighted size premiums and indicate that profitability-not balance-sheet leverage-is the financial characteristic most strongly associated with return outcomes in the microcap segment.

title: Global Reflection Economic Theory "Gre"

detail.title: Global Reflection Economic Theory "Gre"

keywords: Toward a Participatory Economy of Trust

detail.abstract:
The Global Reflection Economic Theory (GRE) introduces a new paradigm in economic governance that replaces the exhausted binary of fiscal austerity and conventional Keynesian stimulus with a logic of reflexive co-production between state and society. Synthesizing institutional economics, Doughnut Economics, the entrepreneurial state literature, and AI-enabled governance, GRE establishes three interlocking mechanisms that together constitute a complete operational architecture: (1) Economic Asset Recycling, which activates dormant sovereign assets through transparent leasing and partnership structures without relinquishing public ownership; (2) Trust Capital (TC), formalized as a quantifiable macroeconomic variable that directly shapes money velocity, tax compliance, credit formation, and institutional resilience; and (3) the Reflection Index (RI = TC × AP × GE), a composite indicator of systemic economic health that integrates trust, asset productivity, and governance efficiency into a single, measurable metric.
By positioning the citizen as both co-owner and active co-producer of national output, GRE advances beyond post-growth critiques and traditional demand-management models alike. It delivers a rigorous, phased implementation roadmap and offers immediate policy relevance for resource-rich states, emerging economies, and international institutions seeking growth models that are simultaneously inclusive, ecologically sustainable, and institutionally robust.

title: Blitzkrieg and Zombies: Central Bank Intervention, Negative Selection, and the Information-Capital Game in Foreign Exchange Markets

detail.title: Blitzkrieg and Zombies: Central Bank Intervention, Negative Selection, and the Information-Capital Game in Foreign Exchange Markets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. The research was conducted independently using the author's own live trading data.

detail.abstract: This paper models financial markets as a two-player game between Capital (size, brute-force repositioning) and Information (timing, asymmetric signal exploitation), with the State acting as a referee whose sole function is to prevent mutual defection. The referee possesses only one tool-capital injection-and is structurally blind to information quality. Using the Strategy Performance Markov Chain (SPMC) framework to detect game-theoretic regime states, I decompose central bank intervention into two phases: a blitzkrieg deployment phase (fast, overwhelming) that arrests acute crisis, and a maintenance phase whose duration determines negative selection damage. Empirical tests on 16 FX pairs at hourly resolution across the 2019 Repo and 2020 COVID QE episodes reveal that: (1) larger, faster interventions improve aggregate regime quality (r =-0.993, p = 0.0007 for balance sheet expansion vs. expected bad-state duration); (2) spread volatility diverges from spread level during intervention, rising 4× and continuing to worsen 12 months post-intervention; (3) PCA1 variance (USD factor dominance) jumps from 40% to 65% during intervention and never reverts; (4) SMA strategy performance degrades monotonically through and after

title: Negotiating Sustainable Energy Development: A Case for ESG Legal Reform in Nigeria

detail.title: Negotiating Sustainable Energy Development: A Case for ESG Legal Reform in Nigeria
detail.abstract:
Nigeria faces a structural tension between its dependence on fossil fuel revenues and its legal commitments to a net-zero future. This article argues that the success of Nigeria's energy transition will depend, in significant part, on how effectively environmental, social and governance (ESG) considerations are embedded within its corporate and capital markets law. The current framework is characterised by fragmented climate and financial regulation, weak integration of ESG into directors' fiduciary duties, underdeveloped fiscal incentives for transition projects, and the absence of a comprehensive green and transition finance taxonomy. Drawing on comparative developments in the United Kingdom and United States, the article makes the case for a shift from largely hortatory soft law toward a coherent, enforceable ESG regime. 

Doctrinal and comparative analysis is used to develop a reform agenda along five dimensions: (i) enactment of a unified national ESG statute; (ii) a context-specific transition finance taxonomy; (iii) statutory clarification of ESG‑related directors’ duties; (iv) targeted, performance‑based fiscal incentives; and (v) mandatory, International Sustainability Standards Board‑aligned disclosure for listed and systemically important firms. The article concludes that a carefully designed ESG framework can help reconcile Nigeria’s dual imperatives of energy security and sustainable development, while making the jurisdiction more attractive to global climate and transition finance.
