title: Observable and Latent Regime Structure in Intraday Gap Reversals: A Taxonomy of Strategy-Level Regime Dependence

detail.title: Observable and Latent Regime Structure in Intraday Gap Reversals: A Taxonomy of Strategy-Level Regime Dependence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. The research was conducted independently using the author's own live trading data.

keywords: auction market theory JEL Classification: G12

detail.abstract: This paper introduces a taxonomy of regime dependence in trading strategies, distinguishing between observable-regime strategies, where the conditioning variable is known at trade entry, and latent-regime strategies, where the relevant regime must be inferred from outcome history. The distinction has a precise statistical consequence: observable-regime strategies produce conditionally i.i.d. trade outcomes (no autocorrelation), while latent-regime strategies produce autocorrelated outcomes (exploitable by performance filters). Using intraday gap-reversal strategies on daily FX bars as the empirical setting, I demonstrate the taxonomy by decomposing gaps relative to a macro trend indicator into two structurally distinct populations. Gaps opposing the prevailing trend represent responsive market activity and exhibit strong mean-reversion (profit factor 1.59, 17,716 trades, 26 years of out-of-sample data, zero losing years). Gaps aligned with the 1 Observable and Latent Regime Structure trend represent initiative activity and do not revert (profit factor 0.74). The observable regime variable (trend direction at entry) fully accounts for the performance difference: within each subpopulation, outcomes are i.i.d. with no residual autocorrelation, confirming that the strategy's edge derives from correct regime classification rather than from temporal persistence. Crossmarket replication on a European equity index confirms the decomposition at the daily timeframe. The taxonomy provides a theoretical framework for understanding when performance filters (such as Markov regime models) add value and when they are unnecessary.

title: Cyber Incident Response in UK Building Societies

detail.title: Cyber Incident Response in UK Building Societies
detail.abstract: Building societies hold an unusual position in UK financial services. They are member-owned mutual institutions, answerable to their members rather than shareholders, and operating under a legislative framework (the Building Societies Act 1986) that has changed little since its passage. The cyber threats they face bear no relationship to that settled character. A ransomware operator does not distinguish between a FTSE-listed bank and a regional mutual with eight branches; the fraud that flows from compromised credentials costs victims regardless of whether their account is held at a major high-street lender or a 50,000-member society in the north of England. What differs markedly is the resource available to respond. A building society with half a billion pounds in assets might employ a single dedicated information security professional, who is simultaneously the CISO, the incident response team, the governance lead, and the person who answers the phone at two in the morning when something goes wrong. This paper is written for that practitioner, and for the institutions they serve. Drawing on experience within UK mutual financial institutions, it maps the regulatory obligations governing incident response, including FCA SYSC and PS21/3, PRA SS1/21 (on operational resilience) and SS2/21 (on outsourcing and third-party risk), UK GDPR, the NIS Regulations 2018, and DORA in its indirect application through UK supply chains, and is candid about the gap between what those frameworks assume and what smaller societies can realistically deliver. Against that analysis, the paper proposes a tiered Bronze-Silver-Gold incident response framework adapted specifically for the building society context, examines ransomware, business email compromise, and supply chain incidents as the scenarios most likely to cause serious harm, and sets out a maturity roadmap that builds credible, regulator-ready capability without requiring wholesale technology investment or additional headcount.

title: SEMI-PARAMETRIC MARKOV CHAIN ANALYSIS OF STRATEGY PERFORMANCE REGIMES IN ALGORITHMIC FOREX TRADING

detail.title: SEMI-PARAMETRIC MARKOV CHAIN ANALYSIS OF STRATEGY PERFORMANCE REGIMES IN ALGORITHMIC FOREX TRADING

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. The research was conducted independently using the author's own live trading data.

keywords: markov switching model JEL Classification: C41

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Semi-Parametric Markov Chain (SPMC) framework for modeling strategy-specific performance regimes in algorithmic forex trading. Unlike conventional regime detection methods that operate on price return sequences, SPMC is fitted directly on the sequence of strategy trade outcomes, modeling performance persistence as a first-order (and, where warranted, second-order) Markov process. Using a dataset of 10,252 trades across six major currency pairs spanning 2019 to 2026, generated by a mean-reversion strategy with a rolling-performance filter, we estimate the SPMC transition matrix, test the Markov property, derive the stationary distribution, and compare the optimal Bayesian filter implied by the chain against the practitioner heuristic it formalizes. Key findings include highly symmetric state persistence (pₒₒ = p₂₂ = 0.793-0.794), rejection of the first-order Markov property in favor of a second-order specification, stationary distribution predictions consistent with empirical regime proportions, and an approximately ten percent improvement in cumulative performance under the optimal Bayesian filter. Critically, SPMC transition dynamics are shown to be empirically orthogonal to those of a price-based Markov Switching Model estimated over the same period, confirming that strategy performance regimes and market volatility regimes are distinct phenomena. The framework offers a principled, strategy-agnostic approach to adaptive trade filtering and contributes a novel intersection between financial regime-detection econometrics and algorithmic strategy evaluation.

title: Instructor Value-Added in Post-Secondary Education *
affiliations: , Stanford University - Hoover Institution and Brigham Young University

detail.title: Instructor Value-Added in Post-Secondary Education *
detail.abstract: Value-added methods are widely used in economics to measure how heterogeneous agents contribute to outcomes, but their credibility hinges on quasi-random exposure to those agents. In higher education, this condition fails: when students select courses and instructors based on unobserved characteristics, conventional value-added estimates will be biased. We develop a method that groups students with similar course histories and identifies instructor effects within these groups by comparing outcomes among students in the same course with different instructors. Using a policy at Purdue University, we show our estimates perform as well as those based on conditional random assignment. The method can be applied at any university; applying the method to data from nearly all public universities in Texas, we show it substantially reduces forecast bias. Instructor quality significantly affects future grades and earnings: a one standard deviation improvement raises next-semester GPA by 0.05 points and earnings by 5%. About half of instructor's effect on earnings operates through major choice.Valueadded is only weakly correlated with student evaluations, and replacing the bottom 5% of instructors based on value-added to earnings instead of evaluations could increase affected students' earnings by up to 4%.

title: Reviving The Police Legal Advisor as the Missing Piece to the Police Oversight Puzzle
affiliations: Lincoln Memorial University Duncan School of Law

detail.title: Reviving The Police Legal Advisor as the Missing Piece to the Police Oversight Puzzle

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This article was created in connection with the author’s tenure as a 2025–2026 Research Fellow for the American Bar Association’s Legal Education Police Practices Consortium (LEPPC). The LEPPC is a collaborative initiative between the ABA and participating law schools dedicated to understanding and addressing complex legal issues in policing, including police conduct, oversight, and the evolving nature of law enforcement (visit www.abalegaledpoliceconsortium.org for more information on the Consortium). This research was developed as a contribution to the Consortium’s national effort to advance policies and practices that support effective, civil, and human rights-compliant policing throughout the United States, specifically focusing on advancing constitutional policing and enhancing legal training for law enforcement officers.

detail.abstract:
Police misconduct exacts a devastating human and financial toll, frequently stemming from a fundamental “knowledge gap” regarding investigative constitutional criminal procedure. Standard police academy training is fleeting and in-service legal training is structurally inadequate to equip law enforcement officers with the continuous, practical legal instruction necessary to lawfully serve modern policing. To fill this pedagogical void, law enforcement agencies have historically relied on ad hoc guidance from local prosecutors or the retrospective accountability imposed by municipal insurers, civil liability, civilian review boards, and Department of Justice (DOJ) consent decrees. However, these existing mechanisms consistently fail to prevent unconstitutional policing. Prosecutors are ethically, structurally, and practically bound to their adversarial role of securing convictions, leaving them ill-suited to serve as objective, daily legal educators. Furthermore, external oversight mechanisms remain inherently reactive, intervening only after a constitutional injury has occurred and staggering municipal liability has accrued.

To bridge this critical pedagogical gap and proactively prevent unconstitutional policing, this article proposes that law enforcement agencies must embed an Independent Police Legal Advisor (IPLA) directly into their daily operations. Operating as an independent general counsel whose sole institutional allegiance is to constitutional compliance, the IPLA serves a vital translational function. By shifting police training paradigms toward constructivist adult learning (andragogy) principles, the IPLA translates complex, fact-bound appellate decisions into immediate, actionable training bulletins and operational guidance. Moreover, widespread adoption of the IPLA model represents a highly cost-effective risk management strategy. When contrasted against the exorbitant, multi-million-dollar burdens of federal consent decrees and civil liability payouts, the preventative salary of a single in-house attorney is a negligible expenditure. For smaller municipalities and elected sheriffs resistant to oversight, this model can be successfully implemented as a shared “circuit” advisor subsidized through intergovernmental risk pools and federal grants. Ultimately, the integration of the IPLA transforms law enforcement agencies into proactive learning organizations, ensuring that constitutional compliance becomes permanently institutionalized from within rather than temporarily and reactively imposed from the outside.

title: Commons or Tollgate? The Private Enclosure of Digital Infrastructure

detail.title: Commons or Tollgate? The Private Enclosure of Digital Infrastructure
detail.abstract: Why do most middle-income countries fail to build public digital infrastructure even when the engineering is within reach? I develop a model in which societies settle disputes using two technologiesa public ledger that veries signed facts cheaply, and institutions that adjudicate human judgments expensively. Three departures from standard public-goods theorystage-local visibility, a claim decomposition, and two-type heterogeneitydeliver three testable predictions: the welfare cost of under-investment is inverted-U in development stage; the opportunity to build is time-limited by private enclosure of the digital commons; and ledger infrastructure generates regressive fraud externalities. Winning the race against enclosure requires two investments: build the rails, and sta the police station.

title: CLASSCONNECT
affiliations: Rizvi College, Rizvi College, Rizvi College and Rizvi College

detail.title: CLASSCONNECT
detail.abstract:
Class Connect is a web-based student-teacher connectivity platform developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python (Flask), and SQLite. Traditional methods of finding tuition teachers, such as word-of-mouth or local advertisements, are often inefficient, unorganized, and lack transparency. Existing online platforms may provide tutor listings, but they often fail to focus on localized search and personalized student requirements.

Class Connect addresses these limitations by providing a centralized system where students can discover nearby tutors based on subject expertise, location, and ratings. The platform ensures an efficient and structured approach to connecting students with teachers by maintaining organized digital profiles and enabling easy accessibility.

The system’s core workflow consists of three major components: (1) User Authentication Module, which allows secure login and registration for both students and teachers; (2) Teacher Management System, where teachers can create profiles, upload resumes, and specify subjects and qualifications; and (3) Location-Based Search and Rating System, which enables students to find suitable tutors within a specific area and evaluate them based on ratings and feedback.

Key features of the platform include secure account management, dynamic teacher search, resume upload functionality, rating and review system, and a user-friendly interface for seamless interaction. The application is lightweight, easy to deploy, and suitable for local-level educational ecosystems due to its use of SQLite as the database.

Overall, Class Connect improves accessibility to quality education by digitizing the process of finding tutors, reducing manual effort, and enhancing transparency between students and teachers.

title: The Digital Markets Act and Artificial Intelligence: Embedded Functionality, Dual-Track Enforcement, and the 2026 Review

detail.title: The Digital Markets Act and Artificial Intelligence: Embedded Functionality, Dual-Track Enforcement, and the 2026 Review

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced my study.

detail.abstract: The DMA already governs substantial gatekeeper AI deployment through the embedded-functionality doctrine: where an AI function is integrated into a designated core platform service and shares its service identity, existing obligations on self-preferencing, data combination, bundling, and interoperability apply without any new designation. • Article 6(5) DMA-not Article 6(1)(a) as sometimes cited-governs self-preferencing; its extension to AIgenerated answer composition is an open specification question, not a settled conclusion, because the provision is textually confined to 'ranking and related indexing and crawling'. • Under Article 1(6) DMA, the Regulation and Article 102 TFEU operate as complementary tracks: the DMA governs where AI conduct maps onto listed obligations; Article 102 supplies the more adaptable instrument for AI practices outside the closed catalogue; and the AI Act adds a parallel safety and governance layer. • The 2026 review under Article 53 is the decisive legal moment-it must resolve whether AI assistants satisfying Article 2(2)(h) thresholds warrant formal designation, whether model-distribution channels require targeted obligations, and whether Article 6(5)'s 'ranking' standard can be extended to answer-engine environments without legislative amendment.

title: Price Differences Between In-Store Shopping and Online Shopping

detail.title: Price Differences Between In-Store Shopping and Online Shopping
detail.abstract: In this paper, the information presented will briefly touch on how the prices differ between instore and online shops. Firstly, I had to collect the data by going into both the online and local instore DICKS and JCPenney to find out what the prices are for four different products. Then, the data needed to be found online through how other people have done research on the topic. So, I went online and searched many things to find out how the prices differed. Once that data was collected, I researched and found out how all these aspects and inputs affected the consumer and producer surplus overall. To do so, I researched and used the equations that I knew to calculate an estimate of the PS and CS between the four products that I chose between the two stores. I learned that between in-store and online prices, there are so many factors that change how the price is set. Such as maintaining the local store, dealing with customers, and unbought items on the shelves. It was also interesting to learn that both the consumer and producer surplus is greater online. Though this may be the case, the economic surplus is a very small amount of money more.

title: Are You 18? Age Verification and Adult-only Consumption in the US
affiliations: Indian School of Business, , University of Padua - Department of Economics and Management, Rotman School of Management, Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR) and The University of Manchester

detail.title: Are You 18? Age Verification and Adult-only Consumption in the US
detail.abstract: Several U.S. states now require age verification for accessing online pornography. We compile domain-state-week traffic for major adult platforms across fifteen states and estimate the causal impact of age verification laws using a difference-indifferences design with staggered adoption. In treated states, platforms that implemented ageverification gates experienced large declines in observed visit (e.g., xHamster), while large free-access sites that remained ungated during the sample period (e.g., XNXX, XVideos) gained 35-40%, consistent with substantial cross-platform substitution. By contrast, registration-and payment-based platforms (e.g., OnlyFans, Stripchat) exhibit smaller changes, consistent with lower marginal frictions when users are already authenticated. Overall, the evidence suggests that age-verification laws can reallocate observed traffic across major platforms in our sample while reducing visits to adopting and blocked domains.

title: Analysis Of the Role of Individuals In a Team and Organization

detail.title: Analysis Of the Role of Individuals In a Team and Organization
detail.abstract: The role of individuals in a team is multidimensional and is an important factor in the success of the organization. Individuals not only function as technical implementers, but also as value carriers, strategic communicators, innovators, as well as agents of change that affect team dynamics. Research shows that there is a positive relationship between self-transcendence values (STV) and environmentally sustainable work behavior (ESWB), which is mediated by innovative work attitudes (IWA). In addition, the role of allyship strengthens an inclusive work climate, improves member well-being, and maintains the organization's image. The typology of individual roles such as embodier, promoter, defender, relationship builder, scout, sensemaker, and critic emphasizes that personal contributions include aspects of values, communication, care, and social involvement. By strengthening personal values, innovative attitudes, effective communication, and management of social dynamics, individual roles can be optimized to create a healthy, safe, and sustainable work environment.

title: xtdpthresh: Dynamic panel threshold regression for unbalanced panels, with endogenous regressors and continuity-robust inference *
affiliations: Vietnam National University - Ho Chi Minh City (VNU-HCM) - International University and

detail.title: xtdpthresh: Dynamic panel threshold regression for unbalanced panels, with endogenous regressors and continuity-robust inference *

declarations.declarationOfInterest: All authors certify that they have no affiliations with or involvement in any organization or entity with any financial interest or non-financial interest in the subject matter or materials discussed in this manuscript.
declarations.funderStatement: The authors did not receive any funding for this work.

detail.abstract: We introduce `xtdpthresh`, a Stata command for estimating the dynamic panel threshold model of Seo and Shin (2016) on unbalanced panels. The command supports three transformations — first-difference (FD), forward orthogonal deviations (FOD; Arellano and Bover 1995), and system GMM (Blundell and Bond 1998) — with user control over the instrument set via `collapse` and `maxlag()` in the style of `xtabond2` (Roodman 2009). Threshold-parameter inference follows the grid-inversion framework of Gong and Seo (2026, §4.1) combined with the fast-bootstrap convention of `xthenreg` (Seo, Kim, and Kim 2019, the reference Stata implementation of Seo-Shin 2016), which uses unit-level wild residual weights, a fixed first-stage GMM weight matrix, and one-step bootstrap GMM per draw. This scheme is 30-60-fold faster than the exact cluster-resample Algorithm 1 of Gong-Seo and matches what Stata threshold users are already accustomed to from `xthenreg`; Gong-Seo uniform-validity (Theorem I.1) is proved for the exact algorithm, while we document empirical coverage near nominal in a Monte Carlo on the canonical Seo-Shin Tong-SETAR data-generating process as evidence for the fast scheme's practical validity. The command extends the fast-bootstrap scheme beyond the sup-Wald linearity test of `xthenreg` to the grid-inversion threshold CI and the continuity test of Gong-Seo, and to the FOD and system GMM configurations for which formal bootstrap validity is not yet established in the literature. We illustrate the command on Hansen's (1999) firm investment data, on an artificially unbalanced variant of that dataset, and on FDIC Call Report data for 500 U.S. commercial banks over 36 quarters, 2015-2023. A small Monte Carlo documents 95% grid-bootstrap coverage between 0.90 and 0.99 across the three transformations on balanced and unbalanced panels, with FD closest to nominal; we treat this as empirical support for, rather than proof of, the validity of the bootstrap under FOD and system GMM. The command fills a gap in the dynamic panel threshold toolkit: to our knowledge, it is the first Stata implementation to combine unbalanced-panel support, an endogenous threshold via user-supplied instruments, Blundell-Bond system GMM, and continuity-robust grid bootstrap inference in a single interface.

title: Technology and finance integration policies and corporate employment decisions

detail.title: Technology and finance integration policies and corporate employment decisions

keywords: The technology and finance integration policy

detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of technology and finance integration policies on corporate employment decisions. Using a dataset of 4,367 A-share non-financial listed companies across 259 prefecture-level cities in China from 2003 to 2023, we adopt a multi-period difference-indifferences approach and find that these pilot policies significantly increase firms' employment size and the proportion of technical production personnel, while reducing average salaries and driving wage structure toward market equilibrium. This finding is robust to placebo tests, parallel trend checks, propensity score matching, and other robustness verifications. Mechanism analysis reveals two transmission channels: easing financing constraints by optimizing the multi-level financing system, and enhancing profitability by facilitating the transformation of technological achievements. Moreover, the policy impact exhibits heterogeneity across regional financial deepening levels, firm types (high-tech vs. non-high-tech), and enterprise life cycles. These findings emphasize the role of technology-finance integration in stabilizing employment and optimizing labor allocation. And offered important policy implications for advancing the finance sector development, coordinate policy objectives, and optimize policy formulation in the future.

title: Formalizing Collapse Through Excess

detail.title: Formalizing Collapse Through Excess
detail.abstract: Complex adaptive systems frequently exhibit a puzzling pattern: apparent stability under growing pressure, followed by sudden, catastrophic failure. Previous work proposed the Capacity-Load Mismatch (CLM) framework as a conceptual lens for understanding this dynamic, identifying tempo, the rate at which load is introduced, as a critical but undertheorized variable [2]. However, that initial formulation relied on a linear approximation that could not capture the nonlinear phenomena it described. This paper bridges that gap. I develop a minimal dynamical system model in which regulatory capacity degrades nonlinearly under tempo-weighted stress, governed by a Hill-type response function. Analysis of this model reveals three phenomena that the linear approximation could not produce. First, the system undergoes a saddle-node bifurcation at a critical tempo threshold, a mathematically precise tipping point beyond which the stable state ceases to exist and collapse becomes inevitable. Second, the model exhibits hysteresis: recovery from collapse requires reducing tempo significantly below the level that caused the transition, formalizing the observation that the path out of failure is harder than the path in. Third, the model reproduces critical slowing down, the progressive lengthening of recovery times as the system approaches its threshold, providing a formal basis for early warning detection. 1 Parameter sensitivity analysis demonstrates that these phenomena are structurally robust: they persist across wide ranges of parameter values, confirming that collapse through excess is a general property of the model architecture rather than an artifact of specific parameter choices. Cross-domain parameter mapping illustrates how ecological, neural, relational, and planetary systems can be represented as distinct parameterizations of the same underlying dynamical structure. An interactive computational simulation accompanies this paper as supplementary material, enabling readers to explore the model's behavior directly.

title: Interaction-Adjusted Concentration: A Quadratic Generalization of the HHI
affiliations: and Chinese University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Interaction-Adjusted Concentration: A Quadratic Generalization of the HHI
detail.abstract: Conventional concentration measures like the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) assume product homogeneity, failing to distinguish markets with varying degrees of substitutability and complementarity. We generalize the HHI by axiomatically deriving quadratic concentration and welfare indices that incorporate pairwise interactions. We also provide welfare-theoretic foundations for their applications in differentiated-product markets. A key insight from the quadratic concentration index is its relationship with surplus distribution: for substitutes, higher concentration correlates with a higher producers’ share—mirroring the classic HHI result—but the relationship reverses for complements. This implies stricter scrutiny for substitute-heavy markets and greater leniency for complementary ones. We further develop a parametric family of quadratic welfare indices that directly link to weighted total surplus, enabling tailored welfare standards. Applied to merger analysis, these indices suggest refined screening guidelines: output-increasing mergers warrant minimal review; when output may fall, screening tightens beyond current HHI-based guidelines.

title: Maria V. Tuchina Algorithmic Jurisdiction and the Transformation of the Competence of Judicial Bodies of Integration Associations in Digital Cross-Border
affiliations: Moscow State Institute of International Relations (MGIMO)

detail.title: Maria V. Tuchina Algorithmic Jurisdiction and the Transformation of the Competence of Judicial Bodies of Integration Associations in Digital Cross-Border
detail.abstract:
This paper develops the concept of algorithmic jurisdiction as an analytical framework for understanding how authority is allocated over decisions shaped by algorithms, data, and digital infrastructures operating across multiple legal orders. It argues that digital cross-border ecosystems transform jurisdiction from a territorial model into a networked and functional one, requiring courts to address questions of control over models, data location, explainability, and enforceability rather than merely the place where a dispute arises.

Through a comparative analysis of the European Union, the Eurasian Economic Union, and ASEAN, the paper demonstrates divergent institutional responses to this shift. In the EU, judicial competence expands toward oversight of automated decision-making and platform governance within a multi-level regulatory architecture (GDPR, DSA, AI Act). In the EAEU, jurisdiction evolves through the interpretation of mutual recognition of digital identifiers and cross-border digital infrastructures. In ASEAN, the absence of a permanent supranational court leads to a reliance on soft law and intergovernmental coordination.

The paper identifies key challenges of algorithmic jurisdiction, including evidentiary asymmetries, attribution of liability, cross-border enforcement, and the preservation of due process in automated environments. It concludes by proposing procedural adaptations, including standards for algorithmic evidence, enhanced transparency obligations, and new coordination mechanisms among courts and regulators, aimed at ensuring accountability in digital ecosystems.

title:
Singapore’s Sovereign Anchor to be A Safe Harbour In a Sea of

Change: The Return of Geopolitics as a Determinant of the Success and Viability of Global Cities

detail.title:
Singapore’s Sovereign Anchor to be A Safe Harbour In a Sea of

Change: The Return of Geopolitics as a Determinant of the Success and Viability of Global Cities
detail.abstract: This paper argues the return of geopolitics requires a rethinking of global city theory through the case of Singapore, the world’s only fully sovereign global city-state. Whereas classic global city literature assumes the global city to take a neoliberal form in a rules based international liberal order and emphasises the command-and-control functions within transnational networks of capital where both geopolitics and social contradictions that result from globalised capitalism are typically assumed to fade into the background from economic progress, recent events around the world that has damaged this world order at a fundamental order - not least the the election of Trump, Brexit, and the Hormuz crisis - ultimately relies the sovereign power of the state representing them being able to wield coercion, statecraft, and diplomacy to shape the global order in the city's interest. Using historical sociology and Charles Tilly’s account of state formation, the paper shows how Singapore’s unusual fusion of city, nation, and state facilitates ideologies of communitarianism and survivalism against liberal norms to articulate its own programme for global cityness, which, with the powers of a high modernist state, may have its advantages in a harder-edge era of global competition and distrust.

title:
Authentic Leadership as Inner Development:

Individuation, Social Transformation and Implications for Female Leadership

detail.title:
Authentic Leadership as Inner Development:

Individuation, Social Transformation and Implications for Female Leadership
detail.abstract: This paper reconceptualises authentic leadership as a process of inner development grounded in individuation and psychological integration. Drawing on Jungian psychology, it argues that authenticity emerges through alignment between identity, values and action, rather than through predefined behavioural models. The paper further explores how such processes, while not inherently gender-specific, have significant implications for female leadership within contexts shaped by dominant norms. It proposes that authentic leadership can act as a generative force, enabling individuals to move beyond conditioned expectations and contributing to broader processes of social transformation.

title: AI Uncertainty and the Muting of Monetary Policy Transmission: Evidence from the United States
affiliations: Central Bank of Nigeria, Eastern Mediterranean University and Central Bank of Nigeria

detail.title: AI Uncertainty and the Muting of Monetary Policy Transmission: Evidence from the United States
detail.abstract: This paper documents a structural friction in United States monetary policy transmission generated by abrupt escalations in uncertainty about artificial intelligence. Using state-dependent local projections, we estimate the interaction between high-frequency federal funds rate surprises in the FOMC statement window and turning points in AI uncertainty, constructed as the second difference of the log AI Uncertainty index. The state variable isolates abrupt accelerations in AI discourse and is empirically orthogonal to the VIX, economic policy uncertainty, and the shock itself. Contractionary surprises generate significantly weaker disinflationary responses during AI uncertainty surges: month-on-month inflation interactions are positive and significant at horizons one through six months, with point estimates between 0.49 and 0.82 percentage points. Withinevent decomposition locates the muting in the Federal Reserve's statement-window rate decision rather than in press-conference communication, pointing to the contemporaneous cost-of-capital channel rather than forward guidance as the margin where the friction operates. A horse race against economic policy uncertainty produces a sign reversal on inflation interactions, consistent with the friction being specifically technological; the EPU interaction shows a directional reversal on inflation. The evidence is consistent with a non-resolving general-purpose technology shock generating commitment-based investment irreversibility: firms with AI deployment horizons treat current financing costs as small relative to the option value of technology commitment, while remaining attentive to forward-outlook information. The results imply that central banks operating under constant-transmission-parameter assumptions will systematically mis-calibrate policy during periods of rapid technological transition.

title: Do Export Bans Reshape Food Trade? Evidence from India's Rice Exports to Sub-Saharan Africa

detail.title: Do Export Bans Reshape Food Trade? Evidence from India's Rice Exports to Sub-Saharan Africa
detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether India's 2011 removal of its non-basmati rice export ban produced a persistent reallocation of trade toward Sub-Saharan Africa, and whether that shift was supply-driven rather than the result of a contemporaneous African demand shock. Using UN Comtrade data for 1996-2024, the analysis combines a triple-difference design with exporter-specific trend-break models, relative-share regressions and dynamic event-study specifications. The DDD estimates show a large and statistically significant post-2011 India-SSA divergence in both export shares and values. Exporter-level models confirm a discrete level shift and a sustained acceleration in India's African trajectory. Log-ratio regressions indicate substantial postliberalisation gains relative to Thailand, Vietnam and Pakistan, consistent with competitive displacement. Dynamic estimates reveal that the shift consolidates after 2011 and persists over the following decade. In contrast, aggregate African imports exhibit no positive structural break at liberalisation. The evidence points to a durable, geographically concentrated and supply-driven reconfiguration of trade following India's re-entry into a thin global rice market.

title: Sectoral and aggregate effects of supply chain disruptions in a small open economy
affiliations: Supply Chain Intelligence Institute Austria, Austrian Institute of Economic Research (WIFO), Austrian Institute of Economic Research (WIFO) and Austrian Institute of Economic Research (WIFO)

detail.title: Sectoral and aggregate effects of supply chain disruptions in a small open economy

declarations.funderStatement: On behalf of the Supply Chain Intelligence Institute Austria (ASCII), we acknowledge financial support from the Austrian Federal Ministry for Economy, Energy and Tourism (BMWET) and the Federal State of Upper Austria.

detail.abstract: We present a country-specific measure of supply chain disruptions and compare it with a global counterpart. We identify each measure's macroeconomic role and consider a sectoral extension using the two-digit NACE level of disaggregation and a multi-sector general equilibrium model to assess the contribution of each sector to CPI inflation. Our results indicate that supply chain disruptions elicit substantial contractionary effects both at the macroeconomic level and in most sectors, and that country-level disruptions significantly dominate their global counterparts. The manufacturing sector emerges as the main domestic transmitter of shocks, with significant spillovers to private services. Consumer preferences tend to spread supply chain disruptions fairly evenly across COICOP categories as they pass through to CPI inflation.

detail.abstract: Keating and Shadwick's Omega ratio captures all statistical moments of return distributions but has practical limitations with respect to portfolio optimization. Kapsos et al. simplified the Omega ratio into an expression with better practical application, but its focus as a portfolio optimization tool represents a trade-off with respect to absolute risk-adjusted performance measurement. First, I've transformed the Kapsos form of the Omega ratio in an analogous manner to what Modigliani did with the Sharpe ratio to create an intuitive percentage output scaled against the market. Second, I've deconstructed the Kapsos form of Omega to create a 3 x 1 matrix that measures and intuitively communicates the three fundamental characteristics that define an investment: risk, return, and liquidity.

title:
From Price Formation to Market Trajectories:

A Demand Selection Framework for Divergent Asset Outcomes

detail.title:
From Price Formation to Market Trajectories:

A Demand Selection Framework for Divergent Asset Outcomes

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants or require ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Collectible asset markets frequently exhibit divergent long-term outcomes despite sharing broadly similar characteristics such as scarcity, symbolic meaning, and market visibility. While existing approaches often focus on valuation or price formation, they offer limited explanation for why some assets experience explosive growth, others stabilize, and still others contract, fragment, or disappear.

Building on the Demand Selection Model developed in prior work, this paper extends the analysis from price formation to market trajectories. It argues that divergence is not incidental, but arises systematically from differences in how demand is structured, sequenced, transmitted, and sustained over time. In particular, the interaction between natural demand and wealth-driven demand, together with the timing of their emergence and the conditions under which value is transmitted across the market, generates distinct outcome patterns.

To operationalize this argument, the paper develops a typology of eight asset outcome types, including explosive, institutionally structured, brand-sustained, cultural-interpretive, generational-demand, contracting, obsolescent, and structurally misaligned markets. It further identifies four core mechanisms—demand composition, temporal sequencing, value transmission, and competitive redistribution—that explain how these outcomes arise.

The framework provides a unified basis for comparing heterogeneous asset markets and offers a process-based alternative to object-level explanations. The framework suggests that market trajectories are shaped not only by value recognition, but by how demand is structured and sustained over time.

title: An Innovation Garden for Farmers' Plant Breeding? Inspiration from the Regulatory Sandbox

detail.title: An Innovation Garden for Farmers' Plant Breeding? Inspiration from the Regulatory Sandbox
detail.abstract: While farmers continue to engage in plant breeding, contemporary plant innovation laws-namely patent law and plant variety protection (PVP)-increasingly limit their freedom to operate. Patents on plant-related inventions can restrict access to breeding material in the absence of a full breeders' exemption. Furthermore, the breeders' exemption under PVP law still involves legal uncertainty because newly developed varieties may risk infringing the rights of the initial PVP holder. Combined with other laws governing the circulation of seeds-such as seed marketing legislation and plant health regulations-these frameworks can create difficulties for farmers' breeding projects. Focusing specifically on intellectual property (IP) law, this article proposes the concept of an Innovation Garden, inspired by the regulatory sandbox. The Innovation Garden would provide farmer-breeders with a legally secure space for plant breeding through the necessary tailoring of regulatory requirements. It would also enhance legal certainty by offering guidance on potential infringement and compliance risks. By examining the challenges and possible mitigating measures, the article argues that such a regime is legally feasible and capable of supporting farmers' innovation.

title: AN INTEGRATIVE ANALYSIS OF INDIVIDUAL BEHAVIOR AND GROUP DYNAMICS ON THE PERFORMANCE OF MODERN ORGANIZATIONS

detail.title: AN INTEGRATIVE ANALYSIS OF INDIVIDUAL BEHAVIOR AND GROUP DYNAMICS ON THE PERFORMANCE OF MODERN ORGANIZATIONS
detail.abstract: The purpose of this study is to comprehend the dynamics of team and individual beha vior in organizations and how they affect productivity.A review of the literature is the approach taken, looking at numerous pertinent scientific sources. The study's findings show that personality traits, skills, motivation, work ideals, and e motions all have an impact on an individual's behavior. In the meanwhile, decisionmaking, trust, leadership, and communication all affect team dynamics. Performance is also impacted by organizational processes like culture, structure, and o rganizational transformation.The success of the organization in accomplishing its obje ctives is determined by the interactions among individuals, teams, and the organizatio n as a whole.

title: The Activation Trap: A Hybrid Model of Inactive Capital, Symbolic Modernisation, And Low-Equilibrium Dynamics in Aid-Dependent South

detail.title: The Activation Trap: A Hybrid Model of Inactive Capital, Symbolic Modernisation, And Low-Equilibrium Dynamics in Aid-Dependent South

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial, institutional, or personal conflicts of interest related to the research, writing, or dissemination of this manuscript. The work is produced independently as part of an ongoing theoretical catalogue.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a hybrid theoretical model to explain why many economies accumulate education, infrastructure, and administrative capacity yet remain technologically stagnant. The model reframes underdevelopment as a problem of activation rather than accumulation. Using an evolutionary-game-theoretic framework, the paper shows that individuals face a strategic choice between innovation and conformity, and that institutional incentives in low-activation economies overwhelmingly reward conformity. Innovation becomes viable only after a critical activation threshold is reached, but symbolic modernisationprestige-driven, non-productive forms of modernity-raises this threshold and locks the system into a low-equilibrium state. The model integrates insights from Baran's concept of potential surplus, Pritchett's education-productivity paradox, and institutional theories of growth. It explains why pilot projects fail to scale, why human capital remains underutilised, and why administrative sectors absorb talent. The activation trap provides a unified framework for understanding persistent development failures in aid-dependent economies and offers a new lens for analysing the political economy of structural transformation.

title: IMPACTS DES INFRASTRUCTURES ÉNERGÉTIQUES SUR LA PRODUCTIVITÉ EN AFRIQUE SUB-SAHARIENNE

detail.title: IMPACTS DES INFRASTRUCTURES ÉNERGÉTIQUES SUR LA PRODUCTIVITÉ EN AFRIQUE SUB-SAHARIENNE
detail.abstract:
> In this study, we examine the relationship between energy
infrastructure development and industrial productivity in sub-Saharan
Africa over the period 2005-2019. Using various econometric methods
on a panel of 46 countries, we analyze the impact of energy intensity,
access to electricty, and the electricity infrastructure development
index on industrial value added and total factor productivity. Our
results indicate a complex and sometimes counter-intuitive
relationship ; the electricity infrastructure development index and
access to electricity show negative effects on industrial value added in
certain spécifications, while energy efficiency appears as an essential
positive factor for productivity across all regions. Regional analysis
reveals strong heterogeneity in effects, with East Africa benefiting
significantly from electrical infrastructure, in contrast to Southern and
Central Africa. Institutional factors such as corruption plays an
important moderating role, particularly in Central Africa. Our results
suggest that energy infrastructure developement policies must be
accompanied by measures aimes at improving energy efficiency,
reducing energy access costs, and strenghtening the quality of
institutions to maximize their impact on industrial productivity.

title: Enforcement-Generated Selection in Arms Trafficking Data: A Measurement Diagnostic for Compliance Monitoring

detail.title: Enforcement-Generated Selection in Arms Trafficking Data: A Measurement Diagnostic for Compliance Monitoring
detail.abstract: When enforcement pressures shape who gets caught, and not just how many, enforcement data may reverse rather than attenuate the observed relationship between policy and outcome. Using the iTrace weapons database, this paper documents this risk in an Iraq-centered setting where all within-country identifying variation comes from Iraq. Embargo-exposed items show greater supply-chain complexity (+0.684 waypoints) but lower observed opacity (−0.140). Restricting to well-traced items (pooled weapons and ammunition; n = 265; trace_quality ∈ {confirmed_id, traced}) reverses the opacity coefficient to +0.118. Because wild-cluster bootstrap intervals cross zero for the main estimates, the contribution is diagnostic but not causal. Sign divergence across trace-quality strata is evidence consistent with enforcement-generated selection and difficult to reconcile with classical attenuation. The paper proposes trace-quality stratification as a portable protocol for analysts using enforcement-generated data.

title: Gambling for Retirement: The Economics of Savings Lotteries
affiliations: University of Florida, University of Michigan, Bocconi University and World Bank

detail.title: Gambling for Retirement: The Economics of Savings Lotteries
detail.abstract: Governments frequently use lottery-like incentives to encourage socially desirable behavior (“Pigouvian lotteries”). We study lotteries that encourage retirement savings in a nationwide field experiment with over 380,000 participants in Colombia's public pension system. Lotteries increase savings during the qualification period, but this effect is almost entirely offset by subsequent declines in savings, as workers strategically shift the timing of deposits. Lotteries also crowd out demand for valuable life and disability insurance and disproportionately benefit wealthier participants. A complementary experiment on deterministic savings subsidies (“matches”) shows they are more cost-effective than lotteries and generate lasting habit formation in savings. More broadly, our findings illustrate that spillovers across choice domains and over time can fundamentally reshape the welfare implications of behavioral policies.

title: ORGAM: A DIGITAL PLATFORM FOR INCLUSIVE ORGANIC FARMING

detail.title: ORGAM: A DIGITAL PLATFORM FOR INCLUSIVE ORGANIC FARMING
detail.abstract: Organic farming has gained global recognition as a sustainable approach to agriculture; however, small-scale farmers continue to face challenges such as limited market access, insufficient investment, and unclear collaboration agreements. This study aims to address these issues through the development of ORGAM, a web-based and mobile-responsive platform designed to connect organic farmers, consumers, investors, and landowners. The study utilized a developmental research design incorporating system design, user testing, and evaluation. Data were collected through surveys and user acceptance testing involving selected participants from Davao del Sur. Results indicate that ORGAM improves accessibility to markets, enhances communication among stakeholders, and increases transparency in collaboration agreements. The platform also demonstrated potential to improve farmers’ income and operational efficiency. The study concludes that digital platforms like ORGAM can significantly contribute to strengthening the organic farming ecosystem by integrating marketplace, collaboration, and monitoring tools into a unified system.

title: Banking-Sector Climate Transition Risk and Corporate Climate Exposure
affiliations: Swinburne University of Technology, Swinburne University of Technology and Swinburne University of Technology - Department of Accounting, Economics, and Finance

detail.title: Banking-Sector Climate Transition Risk and Corporate Climate Exposure
detail.abstract: Banking-sector climate transition risk propagates to nonfinancial firms through the credit channel, reaching the broader economy before financial losses appear on bank balance sheets. In a panel of over 3,500 U.S. firms from 2001 to 2024, a one-standard-deviation increase in the banking sector's aggregate climate-related capital shortfall is associated with a 14.8% increase in overall firm-level climate discussion in earnings calls and a 60.0% increase in discussion of climate regulation and carbon policy, relative to sample means. Discussion of physical climate hazards shows no association, differentiating a transition-specific credit channel from a general information spillover. The effect concentrates among firms with active bank borrowing and carbon-intensive firms and attenuates for firms with greater equity-market access. Transmission originates from publicly listed banks and is absent for privately held banks. These findings suggest that climate stress tests focused on direct loan losses substantially underestimate the systemic reach of transition risk.

title: Metacognition and Human Productive Potential: How Intelligence and Metacognition could explain Productivity?

detail.abstract: This paper undertakes an inquiry into the metacognitive aspects of the mind related to human productive potential, and examines the link between metacognition and intelligence. It reinforces the value of the metacognitive pathways to higher productivity through deep noetics, learning, and inculcation of deep habitshabits that induce perceptible changes in the organisation of the brain neural network patterns. It is presumed that all these changes affect human intelligence in a productive manner. In this paper, first, we try to establish theoretical relationship between metacognition and human intelligence. Following this, we discuss about the human brain as the dominant source of intelligent behavior. Our attempt touches upon these aspects, and we further propose linking metacognition with intelligence and learning as a function of productivity.

title: The Solvency Gap: A Quantitative Diagnostic of the "Profitless Prosperity" in European Football

detail.title: The Solvency Gap: A Quantitative Diagnostic of the "Profitless Prosperity" in European Football
detail.abstract:
This report provides a quantitative diagnostic of the profitless prosperity currently defining the European football industry. Despite achieving record-breaking revenues of 38 billion euros in the 2023/24 season, the sector remains plagued by operational insolvency and fragile unit economics. Through an analysis of data from UEFA and Deloitte, the study identifies a revenue pivot: the era of double-digit broadcast growth has concluded, forcing clubs to transition toward active income generated through commercial activities and modernised match-day infrastructure.

However, this growth is being neutralised by a structural cost disease. Rising income is immediately offset by escalating player and non-player wages, a 15% surge in operating expenses (OPEX), and significant capital expenditure (CAPEX) required for stadium modernisation. Furthermore, a silent debt crisis is emerging; while total industry debt has reached 28.1 billon euros, clubs are increasingly reliant on 7.9 billion euros in transfer payables, essentially vendor financing for player acquisitions, which affects future cash flows.

title: The Power of Focus: How Inventor-base Concentration Drives Firm Performance? *
affiliations: Wilfrid Laurier University - Lazaridis School of Business & Economics

detail.title: The Power of Focus: How Inventor-base Concentration Drives Firm Performance? *

declarations.funderStatement: I acknowledge financial support from the Lazaridis Institute and the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (Grant Numbers: 435-2024-0363).

keywords: cost of equity JEL classification: G34

detail.abstract: Using data on inventor career trajectories across U.S. public firms, we find that a more concentrated inventor base enhances firms' operating performance. This relationship remains robust across multiple model specifications. Examining two potential mechanisms-the Product Competitiveness Hypothesis and the Labor Efficiency Hypothesis-we show that greater concentration reduces labor-related expenses. Furthermore, we find that firms with concentrated inventor bases exhibit lower operating leverage and a reduced cost of equity. These findings underscore the importance of human capital strategies in assessing firms' operating performance.

title: Strategic Alliances and Partnerships as a Competitiveness Driver for the Russian Steel Industry
affiliations: Moscow State Institute of International Relations (MGIMO)

detail.title: Strategic Alliances and Partnerships as a Competitiveness Driver for the Russian Steel Industry

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The uploaded manuscript does not identify any specific conflict of interest, so this is the appropriate standard statement unless there is an undisclosed personal or financial relationship that should be added.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study did not involve patients, human participants, or case reports requiring written consent. It was based on industry data analysis, case studies of companies and institutions, and content analysis of publicly available corporate and industry materials.
declarations.funderStatement: Based on the uploaded manuscript, no specific funding source is identified. A suitable brief statement is: “This research received no external funding.”

detail.abstract: The Russian steel industry, historically accounting for between 4-6% of global crude steel output, has experienced significant structural pressures since 2022 due to sanctions, logistical disruptions and restrictions on access to foreign technology and financing. In this environment, traditional growth strategies such as vertical integration and acquisitions have become less feasible, prompting firms to increasingly rely on strategic alliances and partnerships as a mechanism for ensuring resource access, technological development and market stability. This paper examines the role of alliances within the Russian steel sector through an analytical overview of the global industry context and a set of detailed case studies, including NLMK-OMK cooperation in largediameter pipe (LDP) production, Severstal-Gazprom scientific and technological partnerships, the activities of the Industrial Competence Center "Metallurgy," the development of the steel construction market through ARSS, and university-industry collaboration models. Findings indicate that alliances help reduce transaction costs, accelerate technological adoption, stabilize supply chains and support industry-wide modernization efforts. The study argues that cooperative models are emerging as a necessary condition for maintaining competitiveness in the "new normal" of global fragmentation.

title: A Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for Detecting Trade-Based Money Laundering (TBML) in Cross-Border Finance: Bridging Compliance and Technology

keywords: RegTech JEL Classification: G28 (Government Policy and Regulation)

detail.abstract: Trade-Based Money Laundering (TBML) represents one of the most sophisticated mechanisms of illicit financial value transfer in the global economy, responsible for an estimated USD 1.6 trillion in annual illicit flows and constituting 3-5% of all illegal financial transactions worldwide [1,2]. Existing Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Transaction Monitoring Systems, predominantly rule-based, generate falsepositive rates of 90-95%, imposing a global compliance cost exceeding USD 274 billion annually [3,4]. This paper proposes a Hybrid Machine Learning (HML) framework that integrates supervised ensemble learning-Gradient Boosting Machines (XGBoost) and Random Forest-with unsupervised anomaly detection-Isolation Forest and Autoencoder Neural Networks-for TBML detection in cross-border trade finance data. A six-category domain-informed feature engineering pipeline incorporates Commodity Price Deviation Scoring (CPDS), Jurisdictional Risk Scoring (JRS), Documentary Consistency Scoring (DCS), Behavioral Drift Scoring (BDS), counterparty network topology features, adaptable solution for financial institutions navigating the compliance-technology frontier in crossborder finance.

title: From rhetoric to results: Governor charisma increases economic output
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Lausanne - Department of Organizational Behavior and University of Lausanne

detail.title: From rhetoric to results: Governor charisma increases economic output

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: The causal impact of charisma in high-stakes economic settings is difficult to establish. We showcase a novel approach by exploiting a dataset using close-call U.S. gubernatorial elections. We exploit the randomness provided by such elections to estimate the causal effect of charisma on state-level economic variables. We account for fixed effects (constant terms) at the state and year level, and controlling for important observables, demonstrate an economically meaningful effect for charisma on state output. For example, ceteris paribus, a winner who is 10% more charismatic than the mean of governors, against an opponent at the average, increases state-level GDP by 0.78% each year of a four-year term. Potential mechanisms include state spending increases (i.e. the fiscal multiplier) and new business creation.

title: The 425× Premium and the 85:1 Discount Are the Same Trade: A Partition Framework for Pricing Chinese AI Equity Across Private and Public Markets

detail.title: The 425× Premium and the 85:1 Discount Are the Same Trade: A Partition Framework for Pricing Chinese AI Equity Across Private and Public Markets
detail.abstract: This paper documents and explains a simultaneous pricing anomaly in the 2026 global market for Chinese frontier artificial intelligence (AI) equity. In private markets, DeepSeek is raising its first external funding round at approximately $10 billion, against OpenAI’s post-money valuation of $852 billion — an 85-to-1 ratio applied to two companies the 2026 Stanford AI Index places 2.7 percentage points apart on capability benchmarks. In public markets, MiniMax trades on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange at a price-to-sales (P/S) multiple of approximately 425× on its $79 million 2025 revenue against a $33.6 billion market capitalisation, while OpenAI’s private round implies roughly 35× sales, Anthropic’s 13×, and Nvidia’s public-market multiple is approximately 26×. The same asset class — Chinese frontier AI — is priced at a 91 percent discount in one venue and an order-of-magnitude premium in another, at the same moment in time. I argue that neither market is in error: they are pricing different objects, because they are populated by different buyers operating under non-overlapping mandates. I develop a framework — the Partition Map — that sorts the global AI equity space into four quadrants by asset class and access venue, each with a distinct dominant pricing pool. I isolate the mechanism producing the global-private quadrant’s discount, which I term the Mandate Discount, and document its construction through 2025 via systematic 13F-visible withdrawal of U.S. institutional capital (Appaloosa, Bridgewater, Scion). I argue that the public-market premium is produced by a closed pricing loop in which scarcity dynamics dominate. The paper specifies convergence conditions, testable predictions, and three realistic bridging mechanisms — Middle Eastern sovereign capital, Stock Connect expansion, and privatisation followed by A-share relisting. I acknowledge a bidirectional causality: the partition is not only an effect of capital withdrawal but also a cause of further withdrawal, producing a self-fulfilling equilibrium.

title: Project MAXIMUM BOOST: Flying-Car Racing as the Regulatory, Certification, and Constitutional Pathway to Maximum Freedom in Advanced Air Mobility

detail.title: Project MAXIMUM BOOST: Flying-Car Racing as the Regulatory, Certification, and Constitutional Pathway to Maximum Freedom in Advanced Air Mobility
detail.abstract: This paper argues that the fastest, lowest-cost, and most democratically legitimate path to scaled Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) in the United States is competitive, fully unmanned flying-car motorsportspecifically the X1Racing Project MAXIMUM BOOST framework, an $11.0 billion federal program executing over a seven-year expenditure timeline in which $2.2 billion is released up-front and $8.8 billion is matched dollar-for-dollar against corporate racing sponsorship beginning immediately. The argument rests on five linked claims. First, the retained constitutional right of unimpeded mobility, established by the Supreme Court in Crandall v. Nevada (1868) and reaffirmed in Saenz v. Roe (1999), should be read to presumptively include personal air mobility once an ordinary-means threshold is met; the practical consequence is that a state-issued driver's license, paired with a qualified AI co-pilot, should be the licensing default rather than a multi-year FAA certification program, and any surface location that the certified AI system assesses as meeting vertiport safety criteria should be operable as a vertiport by default under the same constitutional presumption. Second, entertainment-funded, exclusively unmanned racing-featuring designated "danger zones" in which AI stabilization authority is deliberately reduced to generate spectatorgrade collisions and failure modes-is the only known environment that can produce the density, coverage, and adversarial edge-case richness of flight telemetry required to certify an AI co-pilot at that threshold. Because no human is on board the racing airframes, the program is free to operate aggressively into the failure envelope that civil test campaigns are ethically forbidden to enter; Project MAXIMUM BOOST functions, in this respect, as the continuously-operated civil aviation proving ground that civil aviation has never had. Third, a decomposition of general-aviation fatal-accident causes indicates that an AI co-pilot with airframe-envelope authority, geospatial awareness, and weather integration is capable of driving the personal-eVTOL fatality rate below the U.S. pedestrian-fatality rate per mile-supporting the claim that AIco-piloted hybrid-electric flight can be safer than walking. Fourth, three existing regulatory mechanismsthe FAA's MOSAIC final rule (effective 22 October 2025 for sport-pilot privileges; 24 July 2026 for aircraft certification), the Department of War Acquisition Transformation Strategy (7 November 2025), and the Executive Branch commitment to expedited approvals for domestic investments of USD 1 billion or greater-together form a complete regulatory on-ramp requiring no new statute. Fifth, a well-to-wheel energy analysis shows that racing-derived super-efficient hybrid-electric powertrains outperform grid-charged pure-electric alternatives on both thermal efficiency and mission range, and a performance-based racing rulebook admitting free-piston linear generator (FPLG) and other non-crankshaft architectures can drive brake thermal efficiency from a 60% near-term floor toward a 70%+ championship-level horizon-pulling these technologies into civil service a decade ahead of any conventional certification path. The paper draws its model of technology acceleration from two precedents: the century-long transfer of motorsport innovation to passenger-car safety, and the Apollo-era space race, whose combination of public spectacle,

title:
The $6 Trillion Blind Spot:

How Western-Centric Bias in Frontier AI Systems Misreads Islamic Finance Expertise

detail.title:
The $6 Trillion Blind Spot:

How Western-Centric Bias in Frontier AI Systems Misreads Islamic Finance Expertise

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I have no personal or financial relationship with people or organizations that may be perceived to influence the study

detail.abstract: This policy brief documents and analyses a category error made by a frontier large language model (LLM) in a professional evaluation context: the misclassification of Islamic Finance expertise as credential dilution rather than strategic competency. Drawing on the author's direct experience as a finance practitioner operating across Nigerian, UK, and sovereign public-sector contexts, the brief argues that this failure is not incidental but structuralrooted in Western-centric training data that renders a $5.98 trillion global industry illegible to AI systems being deployed in hiring, credit, and investment advisory contexts. The 2004 Saxony-Anhalt EUR 100M Sukuk al-Ijara is deployed as a forensic test case to expose the specific reasoning failure. The brief concludes with recommendations for AI developers, financial regulators, and Islamic finance governance bodies.

title: Stochastic Optimal Portfolio Allocation under Transaction Costs: A Classical vs Quantum Optimization Approach
affiliations: Symbiosis International University - Symbiosis Institute of Business Management (SIBM), Students

detail.title: Stochastic Optimal Portfolio Allocation under Transaction Costs: A Classical vs Quantum Optimization Approach
detail.abstract: This paper studies optimal portfolio allocation under proportional transaction costs in a stochastic continuous-time framework. We model asset dynamics using geometric Brownian motion and formulate the investor's problem as a utility maximization problem under trading frictions. The resulting stochastic control problem is characterized via the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, which becomes nonlinear and intractable in closed form due to transaction costs. To overcome this, we implement Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate approximate optimal strategies and compare them against a discretized formulation recast as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem. The QUBO model is solved using both classical and quantum-inspired approaches. Results show that while classical methods remain robust, quantum optimization provides a promising framework for high-dimensional extensions.

title: Tuning in to Frequencies: How Global Assets Align U.S. Put-Call Parity Residuals

detail.title: Tuning in to Frequencies: How Global Assets Align U.S. Put-Call Parity Residuals
detail.abstract: Put-call parity holds under risk-neutral pricing, yet enforcement exposes arbitrageurs to path-dependent capital costs. The carry gap-the annualized wedge between option-implied and OIS discount factors-is a Q-measure object, but P-measure investment opportunities may shape its enforcement burden. We document this alignment in SPX and RUT options: low-frequency global asset returns raise in-sample R 2 by 0.093 and 0.082 and lift pooled out-of-sample R 2 from 0.221 to 0.364 (SPX) and 0.171 to 0.309 (RUT). Effective horizons differ by asset-IEFA (70 days), IGOV (400 days), IAU (336 days)-and asset terms largely absorb the OIS baseline, providing systematic evidence of a P→Q channel.

title: The Matched Filter Principle for Trading Strategy Regime Detection: Tail Index as the Universal Threshold Between Filter Designs

detail.title: The Matched Filter Principle for Trading Strategy Regime Detection: Tail Index as the Universal Threshold Between Filter Designs

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. The research was conducted independently using the author's own live trading data.

detail.abstract: The optimal regime detection filter for a trading strategy must match the distributional structure of the strategy's return sequence. Applying a mismatched filter produces degenerate or spurious regime signals; applying a matched filter extracts maximum information from the performance history. This paper formalises the Matched Filter Principle by connecting the signal processing matched filter theorem to the Neyman-Pearson framework for regime detection in trade outcome sequences. The tail index α of the return distribution determines which filter design is optimal: strategies with α > 2 (finite variance, approximately Gaussian) are optimally filtered by rollingmean estimators such as the Semi-Parametric Markov Chain (SPMC), while strategies with α ≤ 2 (infinite or borderline-infinite variance, Pareto/power-law) cause rolling-mean filters to degenerate because the sample mean is no longer a reliable estimator. Empirical validation uses 143 look-1 The Matched Filter Principle ahead-free strategy-filter combinations across six USD currency pairs (2019-2026). Meanreversion strategies produce tail index α ≈ 3.7-4.4 and strong SPMC performance (Δ Sharpe = +10.5%); trend-following strategies produce α ≈ 1.5-2.4 and degenerate SPMC signals (the filter labels the extreme tail as a "regime" rather than detecting genuine state persistence). The α = 2 threshold that separates reliable from unreliable rolling-mean estimation may also separate meanreverting from trending market conditions, connecting filter design, strategy type, and market efficiency through a single distributional parameter.

title: A Directed-Search Theory of Durable Goods Replacement

detail.title: A Directed-Search Theory of Durable Goods Replacement
detail.abstract: How do interest rates affect durable-goods markets in general equilibrium? I develop a directed-search model of differentiated durables in which state-dependent failure rates sort ex ante identical buyers and sellers across submarkets. Buyers' optimal policy partitions the state space into non-degenerate action and inaction regions with target quality monotonic in the holding, and market tightness decreasing in quality. Calibrated to U.S. vehicle microdata, the model predicts that a decline in the interest rate triggers a short-run overshoot of durable expenditure; firms reallocate production toward higherquality submarkets, and the economy converges to a stationary equilibrium of less frequent, higher-quality purchases.

title: Price discovery after circuit breaker exhaustion: evidence from the National Stock Exchange of India

detail.title: Price discovery after circuit breaker exhaustion: evidence from the National Stock Exchange of India
detail.abstract: This paper examines next-day price discovery following circuit breaker exhaustion on the National Stock Exchange of India. Using daily bhavcopy data for 3,363 equity securities over 2008 to 2024, circuit hits are identified as days on which the intraday high equals the intraday low. Decomposing returns into an opening gap and intraday drift reveals systematic overshooting: after an upper circuit, the price overshoots 1.86% at the open with a 0.23% intraday reversal. The overshoot has grown monotonically across three periods and concentrates in liquid stocks. Clustered standard errors and a near-miss placebo confirm robustness. A pre-open call auction is proposed.
