declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study does not involve human participants, human data, or animal subjects. The analysis is based entirely on publicly available on-chain transaction data and market price data from cryptocurrency exchanges.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The research was conducted independently by the author without external financial support.

detail.abstract: Token unlock events-scheduled releases of previously restricted cryptocurrency supplyrepresent one of the most predictable, yet paradoxically unmitigated, supply shocks in digital asset markets. Keyrock (2024) analyzed over 16,000 unlock events and documented a 90% negative price impact within a 30-day window, establishing the broad pattern of underperformance. However, this aggregate result leaves two empirical questions unresolved: first, within the 30-day window, when is the selling pressure concentrated? Second, does the effect persist after controlling for Bitcoin market beta? This paper offers preliminary evidence on both questions using a hand-collected sample of 52 major token unlock events on Binance-listed assets between January 2023 and December 2025. We document three findings. First, 46 of 52 events (88.5%; binomial test p = 2.2 × 10⁻⁹; robust to Bonferroni correction across 17 formal hypothesis tests) exhibit negative returns within 72 hours of unlock, with a mean return of-16.97%. The similarity between our 72hour rate and Keyrock's 30-day rate (90%) is suggestive of temporal concentration, though we emphasize this is a qualitative cross-study comparison across non-overlapping samples. Second, the same 88.5% of events underperform Bitcoin on a relative basis; one-way ANOVA across five Bitcoin regimes finds no statistically significant modulation of the effect (F-test p = 0.24). Robustness checks using Ethereum and a top-10 market-cap-weighted index yield qualitatively similar results. Third, we report an exploratory, hypothesisgenerating observation: within our sample, all 14 events occurring within a 60-day window around the 365-day post-listing anniversary exhibit negative returns. We emphasize this pattern was identified post-hoc and any nominal p-value is not interpretable as a valid test; pre-registered out-of-sample replication is required. We interpret these findings through a supply shock hypothesis. Notwithstanding the correlational nature of the evidence, the consistency of the effect across Bitcoin regimes, recipient categories, and alternative benchmarks suggests that unlock-specific selling pressure is the most parsimonious explanation among those we considered. Replication data and analysis code are publicly available.

title:
O construcție alternativă: Alianța Dreptate și Adevăr

An Alternative Construction: The Justice and Truth Alliance

detail.title:
O construcție alternativă: Alianța Dreptate și Adevăr

An Alternative Construction: The Justice and Truth Alliance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This article examines the political and electoral context that led to the formation of the Justice and Truth Alliance (Alianța DA) in Romania in 2003, analysing it as a strategic response to the structural dominance of the Social Democrat Party (PSD) and to the crisis of confidence affecting the Romanian party system as a whole. Drawing on longitudinal polling data from the FSD Barometer of Public Opinion, the article traces the descending trend in citizens' trust towards political leaders and parties, identifying three typological patterns in the relationship between leaders and parties: direct proportional correlation, inverse proportional correlation, and non-correlation. These patterns are analysed in detail for PSD, PD, and PNL, revealing the distinct vulnerabilities of each formation. In the case of PSD, the article identifies an inverse proportional correlation in which voting intention for the party consistently exceeds confidence in its leader, a unique feature among Romanian parties that reflects the party's organisational strength and clientelistic networks. By contrast, PD and PNL are shown to be highly dependent on their leaders' personal popularity, making leadership crises directly damaging to their electoral prospects. The article argues that the electoral ceiling faced by the two main opposition parties — separated from PSD by roughly 10 percentage points — created strong incentives for alliance-building. It concludes that while the Alianța DA represents a viable alternative construction, its long-term stability will depend on its capacity to transcend the personalistic logic of Romanian party politics and develop genuine institutional cohesion.

title: AllInTrade: The Missing Economics of a Trade

detail.title: AllInTrade: The Missing Economics of a Trade

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is employed by CACEIS, a European asset servicer. The views expressed herein are solely the author's and do not represent those of CACEIS or its affiliates. No institutional funding supported this research. No CACEIS-specific product, service, or data source is discussed. All data used are independently sourced under separate licenses with Virtu Financial (Global Cost Review) and EquiLend Data & Analytics (DataLend), used solely for academic research purposes. No raw licensed data are redistributed; only derived summary statistics are reported.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses aggregated financial market data (equity prices, index memberships, aggregated securities-lending statistics, and aggregated execution-cost benchmarks) and does not involve human subjects, personal data, or any procedures requiring ethics review.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. No institutional funding was provided by CACEIS or any other organization.

detail.abstract:
An institutional portfolio optimiser sees two of the five economic components that determine a trade's net return. Price-return forecasts and execution costs enter the ex-ante weight decision; the other three — securities-lending income, collateral and funding carry, and operational frictions — are observed by other desks and only after the decision has been made, even though in many non-large-cap universes they match or exceed execution costs.

AllInTrade integrates all five components into the same ex-ante portfolio objective. Compared with an optimiser that uses only price forecasts and execution costs, it overweights names whose lending or collateral economics improve their total-return ranking, and underweights names whose borrow costs or operational hazards do the reverse — within the same risk and tracking-error budget.

Empirically, across three U.S. equity universes tested, the portfolio-level spread scales as the framework predicts: monotonically with universe-level lending-fee dispersion, from a structurally negligible level on S&P 500 (a deliberate lower-bound test) to larger magnitudes on Russell Midcap and Russell 2000. The same logic extends naturally to higher-friction asset classes — emerging-market equities, single-name credit, hard-to-borrow names — where the integration gap is wider and the captured economics correspondingly larger.

The practical implication reshapes the trade itself: the instruction to the broker and a pre-priced lending-and-collateral commitment leave the order-management system as a single coupled order, capturing the economics at the moment they exist rather than days later in custody. An illustrative Russell 2000 deployment walks through the mechanics.

title: Skilled Migration Policy in Thailand: Structural Challenges and Opportunities with a Focus on Indian IT Expatriates
affiliations: and Suresh Gyan Vihar University Jaipur

detail.title: Skilled Migration Policy in Thailand: Structural Challenges and Opportunities with a Focus on Indian IT Expatriates
detail.abstract: Thailand has developed multiple pathways to attract skilled foreign professionals; however, its regulatory framework remains complex and fragmented. This study provides a structured overview of Thailand's skilled migration system, focusing on visa structures, work permit regulations, and institutional coordination. Drawing on secondary policy sources and the existing literature, this study identifies key challenges, including administrative fragmentation, limited labour mobility, and inconsistent eligibility criteria across programmes. It also highlights emerging opportunities related to demographic changes, digitalisation, and policy alignment with investment priorities. With specific reference to Indian expatriates, particularly those in the information technology sector, this study examines how current policies influence the utilisation, mobility, and contribution of skilled foreign talent within Thailand's evolving digital economy. Indian professionals, given their global presence in IT and digital services, provide a relevant lens for assessing the effectiveness of Thailand's migration framework in attracting and retaining specialised skills. This study argues that while Thailand has established several mechanisms to attract talent, greater standardisation, sectoral alignment, and institutional coordination are required to enhance efficiency and global competitiveness.

title: Labour Mobility as a Catalyst for Knowledge Spillovers in Australia
affiliations: and Government of the Commonwealth of Australia - IP Australia

detail.title: Labour Mobility as a Catalyst for Knowledge Spillovers in Australia
detail.abstract: Labor mobility is increasingly recognized as a catalyst for productivity and innovation enhancement. This paper investigates the impact of labour mobility on innovation in Australia, drawing on extensive empirical analysis. At a macro level, enhanced labour mobility fosters improved matching and extended networks, facilitating knowledge exchange among firms. The "learning by hiring" effect, where new hires introduce fresh insights and opportunities, is well-documented, with new employees bringing both private and social knowledge to their new workplace. However, the transferability of social knowledge remains underexplored. The study utilizes comprehensive ABS datasets, including the Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE) and the Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA), covering the period from 2002 to 2022. By constructing a linked employer-employee job-year dataset, the analysis identifies the characteristics of both joining and departing employees and their previous or future employers. Employing a Cobb-Douglas specification, the study assesses the relationship between labour mobility and innovation, finding that the impact of joiners is moderated by the innovation capabilities and size of their previous firm. While joiners from patent-holding firms significantly contribute to innovation outcomes, the effect diminishes as firm size increases. Conversely, the impact of leavers on innovation appears negligible. These findings underscore the importance of labour market dynamism in fostering innovation and suggest that policies aimed at promoting labour mobility may yield substantial benefits for innovation and productivity enhancement in Australia.

title: International Sanctions and Constitutional Compliance
affiliations: University of Hamburg - Institute of Law and Economics, University of Trier - Faculty of Economics and University of Trier - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: International Sanctions and Constitutional Compliance
detail.abstract: Judging governments' responses to international sanctions based on their compliance with a universal human rights standard can be criticized as an imposition of Western values. We propose an alternative benchmark for government action that is not subject to the same potential criticism: whether governments comply with their own national constitutions as codified forms of the social contract. Our analysis of 182 countries from 1962 to 2022 using state-of-the-art panel DiD and event study estimators corroborates our theoretical expectation that government responses depend on regime type. Whereas democracies improve their constitutional compliance under sanction pressure, autocracies start complying even less. These results suggest that sanctions can only make governments comply with their legal commitments if those governments are dependent on broad popular support.

title: Land Reforms in Developing Financial Markets: Lessons from England's Land Enclosures 1750-1830
affiliations: Tel Aviv University - Eitan Berglas School of Economics, , Ben-Gurion University of the Negev and Ben-Gurion University of the Negev

detail.title: Land Reforms in Developing Financial Markets: Lessons from England's Land Enclosures 1750-1830

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The views expressed in this paper solely reflect those of the authors and not necessarily those of the Bank of Israel, or of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago or the Federal Reserve System.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by the Israel Science Foundation (grants No.374/21 and No.51/22).

detail.abstract: Land titling is expected to expand credit by making land pledgeable, but isolating this collateral channel empirically is difficult. We utilize English enclosures from 1750-1830 as a laboratory: privatization of "common waste" created newly mortgageable land, in contrast with "open-field" enclosures which largely reorganized already titled arable land. A stylized model with endogenous default predicts that an influx of newly pledgeable waste land lowers equilibrium collateral requirements, generating a local credit expansion but an increase in bankruptcies. Using a newly digitized universe of personal bankruptcies from the London Gazette, we find that the enclosure of common waste led to higher bankruptcies, particularly in industrial areas and during downturns. Bankruptcies are concentrated among industrial occupations with tight cash-flow cycles. In contrast, enclosures of open-field reduce bankruptcies. The results clarify a key collateral channel through which property reforms can deepen credit while increasing defaults.

title: A Blueprint for Expanding Access to Justice in Los Angeles Superior Court’s Eviction Docket
affiliations: Stanford Law School, Stanford Legal Design Lab, Rhode Center on the Legal Profession, Stanford Law School, Stanford University, Rhode Center on the Legal Profession, Stanford Law School and Stanford Law School

detail.title: A Blueprint for Expanding Access to Justice in Los Angeles Superior Court’s Eviction Docket

declarations.ethicsApproval: Stanford University IRB Protocol # 72977
declarations.funderStatement: This research was made possible through the generous support of Stanford Impact Labs.

detail.abstract:
The civil dockets of U.S. state courts are increasingly dominated by high-volume and low-value but high-stakes cases such as eviction, debt collection and foreclosure.  This Report examines the access-to-justice crisis in high-volume state-court litigation through a detailed study of nearly 150,000 eviction cases in the Los Angeles Superior Court, the nation’s largest trial court. Drawing on court data, interviews, focus groups, ethnographic observation, and audits of digital tools, it shows how these dockets are shaped by corporate landlords, self-represented tenants, and outcomes that are the result of default judgments rather than meaningful participation on the merits. The Report identifies six core problems: fragmented legal protections and help resources, weak court data systems, major knowledge gaps for litigants, uncertainty among court staff about how much assistance they can provide, barriers facing legal aid and community organizations, and digital services that are hard to find, poorly integrated, and difficult to use.  
In response, the Report offers a practical reform agenda centered on four roles courts can play. First, to become a learning organization, the Court should expand its data collection and data-analytic capacity, increase transparency and knowledge sharing practices, and build frameworks for ongoing evaluation of innovations. Second, to become a trusted and effective information hub, the Court should equip its users with centralized, clear, accessible and actionable information about how to navigate the system and meaningfully participate in their cases, including by redesigning key notices. Third, to become a collaboration hub, the Court should facilitate and strengthen the work of justice partners and develop tools to connect court users with appropriate forms of legal help (e.g., through self-service triage and referral tools). Finally, to become a digital hub, the Court should create integrated, user-centered, end-to-end digital pathways for litigants, and develop infrastructure for the responsible deployment of artificial intelligence tools, including litigant-facing assistants and court operations support systems (e.g. for compliance-checks). Altogether, the Report advances a framework for incremental, evidence-based reform that builds on courts’ role leveraging data, design, technology, and institutional partnerships to promote more accessible, equitable, and effective pathways to justice.

title: Fairness as Foundation: A Complete Architecture for Structurally Fair Governance

detail.title: Fairness as Foundation: A Complete Architecture for Structurally Fair Governance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the Founder and President of CARO, the organization that published this work. No external funding or financial conflicts of interest exist.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was self-funded by the author through CARO (Care for Assets, Resources, and Obligations), a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.

detail.abstract:
This paper presents a comprehensive governance philosophy that addresses a question no existing framework has fully answered: why do all democratic systems, across different stages of development and political cultures, produce structural unfairness? The answer advanced here is architectural. Governance fails not because of individual actors, cultural deficiencies, or insufficient resources, but because governance systems are structurally designed to fail — to invert authority and accountability, to subordinate the governed to the governing, and to make structural unfairness the predictable outcome rather than the exceptional case.

The framework constructed — Equitism — holds that every person subject to governance authority holds a Meta-Right to Structural Fairness: an inalienable right not merely to good outcomes from governance, but to governance systems architecturally designed to preserve their equal standing as justificatory agents. The paper provides the complete institutional architecture through which structural fairness can be operationalized: the Fairocracy constitutional system, the FairVote decision mechanism, the Unified Fair Democratic System (UFDS) — a complete constitutional blueprint specifiable to any governance context — and the Universal Governance Framework (UGF), the global extension of the framework to international institutions. It also provides the Fairness Index: a measurement instrument that makes structural fairness empirically assessable.

Bangladesh is used as the primary diagnostic case — the clearest available demonstration of the governance failure mode the framework addresses — while the analysis applies to transitional and mature democracies globally. The framework engages the foundational literature in political philosophy (Rawls, Pettit, Habermas, Forst, Scanlon) while going beyond existing theory toward institutional design obligations and constitutional specification.

title:
Wave Liquidity Redistribution Theory (WLRT) v4.0:
Universal Configuration Dynamics in Multi-Environment Liquidity Systems

detail.title:
Wave Liquidity Redistribution Theory (WLRT) v4.0:
Universal Configuration Dynamics in Multi-Environment Liquidity Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Wave Liquidity Redistribution Theory (WLRT) provides a structural framework for understanding how liquidity is formed, distributed, and transformed across interacting environments.

The theory introduces liquidity as a primary ontological element and models system dynamics through a discrete configuration space governed by admissible transitions. Directed finite configuration structures are formalized within a canonical system (A.D.E.), where system evolution is represented through phase-based dynamics defined in phase time.

WLRT extends this framework by introducing a multi-environment architecture in which informational, financial, execution, and logistics environments are structurally coupled. This allows analysis of system behavior beyond single-domain models and reveals how cross-environment interactions influence stability, fragility, and transition dynamics.

A central contribution of the theory is the formalization of structural fragility as an intrinsic property of the system, along with its diagnostic representation. Cascades and topological constraints of configuration space are introduced as necessary consequences of accumulated fragility and limited admissible transitions.

The theory further defines stability as a structural balance between compensation and fragility, and establishes regimes of applicability that determine when interpretation and action remain structurally valid.

Rather than prescribing specific actions, WLRT enhances decision-making by providing a framework that reduces structural ambiguity, identifies conditions under which interpretations remain reliable, and clarifies the limits beyond which conclusions become inadmissible.

WLRT v4.0 represents a complete and structurally closed formulation of the theory, integrating its ontological, dynamical, architectural, and diagnostic components into a single coherent system.

Canonical monograph release of WLRT v4.0. The full version is archived on Zenodo with DOI:
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19701949

title: Digital Financial Infrastructure and Climate Resilience: Evidence from Mobile Money Adoption
affiliations: Zhejiang University of Finance and Economics (ZUFE), ,  and University of Massachusetts Boston

detail.title: Digital Financial Infrastructure and Climate Resilience: Evidence from Mobile Money Adoption
detail.abstract: Does digital finance help communities withstand drought? We study 132 cities across 34 fragile and conflict-affected states over 2000-2021 using satellite vegetation data. Drought reduces vegetation by 3.8 percent per standard deviation, but cities with mobile money experience significantly less damage-an effect that is stable across specifications. In the encompassing specification, mobile money is the only statistically significant moderator of drought damage. Event studies show that mobile money raises GDP; point estimates suggest substitution away from formal credit, though this effect is imprecisely estimated, consistent with transfers and savings rather than credit intermediation, though the credit evidence is imprecise.

title: Self-censorship in Communist China: Text Analysis of Sermons From State-registered Churches

detail.title: Self-censorship in Communist China: Text Analysis of Sermons From State-registered Churches
detail.abstract: State-registered religion is puzzling because it can be portrayed as both an opponent and a partner of the state. While registered religions need to be receptive to the rules of the government, they also need to satisfy the needs of their congregants. In light of the Communist Party’s increasing repression, I investigate how this complex positioning between the government and the congregation has influenced the content of sermons in state-approved Protestant churches. Using computational text analysis on sermons from a state-approved Protestant church in China between 2009 and 2021, I analyze the pastors’ degree and composition of self-censorship in their receptiveness to changes over time, as well as to politically and religiously sensitive dates. By focusing on sermons shared in state-approved churches, I shed light on the complex positions in which these Party-registered pastors maneuver. This research also contributes to the broader discussion of civil rights and state-society relations in the context of a strong authoritarian state.

title: The Flexibility Illusion of Cryptocurrency Mining
affiliations: University of Witten/Herdecke, University of Witten/Herdecke and University of Witten/Herdecke

detail.title: The Flexibility Illusion of Cryptocurrency Mining

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests.

detail.abstract: Flexible demand is increasingly important in energy systems with high renewable penetration. Bitcoin mining is often cited as a large, theoretically flexible load. Despite electricity consumption rivaling medium-sized industrial economies, the energy market behavior and impacts of Bitcoin miners remain largely unexplored. We exploit the large-scale relocation of Bitcoin mining to Texas, which became the world's largest mining hub following China's 2021 ban, to estimate its effects on local wholesale electricity prices. Combining a novel, hand-collected dataset on mining facility locations with high-frequency wholesale price data, we identify price impacts using a DiD design. We find that miners select into renewable-rich, high-GDP per capita counties with initially lower electricity prices on average. Mining entry has no significant effect on daytime prices but increases nighttime prices by 13.5%, indicating that Bitcoin miners fail to exploit their operational flexibility. Instead they increase baseload demand and reinforce fossil generation during low-renewable periods.

title: Distributions and Drivers of Lifetime Earnings
affiliations: German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin),  and German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin), Students

detail.title: Distributions and Drivers of Lifetime Earnings

keywords: labor market participation JEL codes: C38

detail.abstract: We link administrative pension records with rich household survey data to study the distribution and drivers of lifetime labor earnings in Germany for birth cohorts from 1935 onward. Unlike previous studies, our data capture the entire workforce, including the self-employed, civil servants, and workers with interrupted careers, revealing that conventional sample restrictions overstate earnings and understate inequality. We document large gender gaps, rising male inequality, and declining female inequality across cohorts. We examine the association between lifetime earnings and a comprehensive set of factors spanning childhood conditions, education, and family formation, uncovering strongly gender-differentiated patterns that accumulate dynamically over the life course yet remain stable across cohorts.

title: PUBLIC AND CORPORATE EXPENDITURES IN R&D AND INNOVATIVE CAPACITIES: THE CASES OF GERMANY AND PORTUGAL

detail.title: PUBLIC AND CORPORATE EXPENDITURES IN R&D AND INNOVATIVE CAPACITIES: THE CASES OF GERMANY AND PORTUGAL

declarations.ethicsApproval: O presente estudo não envolveu a participação direta de seres humanos nem a recolha de dados primários junto de indivíduos. A investigação baseou-se exclusivamente na análise de dados secundários de acesso público. Deste modo, não foi necessária a submissão a um comité de ética. Ainda assim, foram respeitados todos os princípios éticos aplicáveis à investigação científica, nomeadamente no que se refere à integridade, rigor e uso responsável da informação.

detail.abstract: This article examines the role of public and business R&D expenditure in promoting innovative capacities, with a specific analysis of the cases of Germany and Portugal. Using data from the European Innovation Scoreboard (2021), we investigated the nature and relationship of R&D spending in both countries. We identified that public expenditure on R&D is mostly directed to activities of a fundamental and applied nature, carried out in educational institutions and technological infrastructures. On the other hand, business R&D activities tend to be more applied and oriented towards experimental development, with the aim of achieving specific previously defined goals. However, it was understood that the innovative capacity of a country does not depend only on the amount of investment in R&D, but on the dynamics implemented by the different sectors. Countries that invest significantly in public and business spending on R&D tend to experience a greater increase in innovation, particularly when these investments are complementary and directed towards the generation of new knowledge that results in techniques or goods with added economic value. Our analyses suggest the importance of an integrated and collaborative approach between the public and private sectors in promoting innovation, highlighting the need for policies that encourage and facilitate such cooperation. In addition, we highlight the relevance of strategic investments in R&D that promote not only scientific advancement, but also its practical application in the economy and society.

title: A "Sharing Hand" or a Gendered Burden? Daughters and Parental Time Allocation in India
affiliations: and Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Kanpur

detail.title: A "Sharing Hand" or a Gendered Burden? Daughters and Parental Time Allocation in India
detail.abstract: Parental time is a critical input into child development, and its allocation within households may vary systematically with the gender composition of children, particularly in settings characterized by persistent son preference. This paper examines how child gender and gender composition are associated with parental time allocation in India. Using nationally representative data from the 2019 and 2024 rounds of the Indian Time Use Survey, we focus on two-child households and estimate pooled cross-sectional models with district and surveyyear fixed effects. We document asymmetric parental responses to the presence of daughters: mothers allocate more time to childcare but reduce time spent in household production, while fathers exhibit limited behavioral adjustment. These patterns are consistent with gendered specialization and intra-household labor substitution, whereby daughters increasingly assume maternal domestic responsibilities as they age, particularly during adolescence. The extent of this substitution is larger in settings with stronger son preference, lower socioeconomic status, and limited access to labor-saving household technologies, highlighting the interaction between social norms and structural constraints. Our findings suggest that daughters partially relax maternal time constraints by absorbing domestic work, but this reallocation likely comes at the expense of their own time use, with implications for human capital accumulation. The results point to a channel through which gender inequalities are reproduced within households and underscore the importance of policies that address both gender norms and constraints on household production.

title: Chasing Ratings, Losing Impact: The Effects of Journal Lists on Publication Patterns in Business and Management
affiliations: University of Reading - ICMA Centre and University of Bristol

detail.title: Chasing Ratings, Losing Impact: The Effects of Journal Lists on Publication Patterns in Business and Management

keywords: business and management fields JEL Codes: C23

detail.abstract: The quality of research papers in business and management is frequently assessed in an automated fashion according to the rating of the journals in which they are published. Using a very large sample of research spanning all fields in business and management studies, we examine the extent to which the prevalence of country-specific journal ratings lists leads authors to focus on ratings, potentially at the expense of the academic influence and article fit of the resulting publication. We find that authors based in the UK or Australia publish disproportionately frequently in journals that have low impact factors within ratings categories measured using their country's journal lists. We argue that such outcomes could have arisen in contexts where measured research performance is prioritised alongside publication in less competitive outlets. We show that this success is on average achieved at the expense of both fit to the journal and citations, which are sacrificed by publishing in lower-impact, higher-rated journals. We find no evidence, however, that work by Australian or UK authors who publish away from their core fields appears in higher rated journals.

title: Effectiveness of Special Economic Zones as a Strategy for Economic Development in Sri Lanka

detail.title: Effectiveness of Special Economic Zones as a Strategy for Economic Development in Sri Lanka
detail.abstract: Economic development is the ultimate destination of human civilization commenced with subsistence agriculture to globally industrialized output, served with artificial intelligence-based services, for the purpose of enhancing standards of living. Uneven distribution of resources in the globe was mapped with an economic intention as in the form of investments to accomplish desired economic development goals in given geographical boundaries without claiming against the natural realities. Nations, governments, and business partners designed deliberate gatherings with respect to clearly defined boundaries as various forms of zones to undertake economic, socio cultural, technological and political paradigms in the long run. The main objectives of the article is to evaluate the effectiveness of special economic zones as a strategy for economic development in Sri Lanka. In addition, it is expected to explore the evolution and scattering of special economic zones in the Asia, to identify the role of special economic zones in Sri Lanka and to investigate challenges and prospects of promoting special economic zones in Sri Lanka. The study is purely based on secondary data and qualitative analytical approach is used to derive conclusions. Investment attempts by Sri Lanka after trade liberalization broaden the scope of industrialization as it led towards novel experience to both production and consumption while making sensible structural changes. Export Processing Zones transferred villages to cities not only adding value to the gross domestic product but also to human lives. The portfolio of especial economic zones of Sri Lanka was expanded with the time but within limited scope of operation. Corruptions, delays, cost inefficiencies and policy mismatch are key challenges for Sri Lanka to overwhelm, in order to attract foreign direct investments. However unmatchable locational advantage, resource endowment, literacy as well as upcoming investment zones like Port-City are the core prospects to position demand for foreign direct investments in the region.

title: Who Controls Restructuring? Control Intensity and Credit Markets in Chapter 11 and Beyond

detail.title: Who Controls Restructuring? Control Intensity and Credit Markets in Chapter 11 and Beyond
detail.abstract: Corporate restructuring systems are typically described in formal legal terms. In practice, however, outcomes are shaped by how control is exercised during the restructuring process. This paper introduces the concept of "control intensity" to examine how decision-making authority is allocated and operationalized across different regimes. It compares the U.S. Chapter 11 system with preventive restructuring frameworks in Italy, France, and Türkiye. The analysis shows that control is increasingly concentrated at early stages-often through financing structures, judicial oversight, and liquidity constraints-rather than through formal governance mechanisms. This shift has direct implications for creditor behavior, transparency, and credit market outcomes. The paper argues for a calibrated approach to control allocation that aligns legal design with operational reality and improves efficiency in cross-border restructuring.

title: Rethinking the Determinants of Fertility Decline
affiliations: Vienna University of Economics and Business

detail.title: Rethinking the Determinants of Fertility Decline
detail.abstract: Global fertility has declined from 5.4 children per woman in 1960 to 2.3 in 2023, with many major economies reaching record lows far below replacement. This decline has occurred across countries with vastly different levels of income, institutions, and cultural backgrounds, challenging explanations based on these traditional variables. Using a panel of 237 countries from 1950 to 2023, I show that widely documented cross-sectional relationships do not carry over to within-country changes over time. For example, female education and female labor force participation-typically negatively associated with fertility across countries-are often positively related to fertility within countries once country and time fixed effects are included. Cultural values and religiosity likewise exhibit little to no within-country association. These findings suggest that traditional explanations of global fertility decline primarily capture crosscountry differences but not within-country changes, complicating policies to reverse low fertility.

title: Dynamic Pigouvian Fees for Orbital Debris: Discount Rate Sensitivity and Altitude-Specific Fee Schedule for 2026-2040

detail.title: Dynamic Pigouvian Fees for Orbital Debris: Discount Rate Sensitivity and Altitude-Specific Fee Schedule for 2026-2040
detail.abstract: We extend the altitude-dependent Orbital Damage Function (ODF) framework (Malik, 2026a) to derive a time-varying Pigouvian fee schedule for orbital debris regulation across the period 2026-2040. Building on our finding that the Social Cost of Orbital Debris (SCOD) varies by two orders of magnitude across low Earth orbit (LEO), we conduct a comprehensive discount rate sensitivity analysis showing that altitude-dependence is robust across social discount rates of 1%-5%. We then derive a time-evolving fee schedule growing at 14% per annum (consistent with Rao et al., 2020) that reflects both the altitude-specificity of debris damage and the increasing congestion of LEO driven by mega-constellation deployment. Our principal finding is that an operator at 800 km faces an optimal annual fee 44× higher than an equivalent operator at 400 km, and that delaying fee implementation by five years increases the socially optimal fee by approximately 40% due to compound debris accumulation. The results directly inform FCC orbital debris mitigation rules (effective September 2024), ESA Zero Debris Charter compliance design, and the pricing basis for orbital debris credit (ODC) markets.

title: The Impact of Central Bank Reactions on Inflationary Price Distress in Sub-Saharan African Economies

detail.title: The Impact of Central Bank Reactions on Inflationary Price Distress in Sub-Saharan African Economies
detail.abstract: This policy brief provides a critical assessment of central bank responses to persistent inflationary pressures and the resulting price distress and welfare deterioration in Sub-Saharan African economies. It argues that inflation in the region is predominantly driven by structural rigidities, supply-side constraints, and recurrent external shocks rather than excess aggregate demand, thereby limiting the effectiveness of conventional monetary policy frameworks. Central banks have largely responded through policy interest rate adjustments, exchange rate management, and liquidity tightening. While these instruments remain essential to macroeconomic stabilization, their effectiveness is weakened by structural bottlenecks such as food production constraints, energy price volatility, infrastructure deficits, and high import dependence. These factors significantly reduce the transmission efficiency of monetary policy and weaken its influence on the underlying drivers of inflation. The analysis highlights that although monetary tightening may support credibility and help anchor inflation expectations, it generates important macroeconomic trade-offs. Higher interest rates tend to suppress investment, restrict credit to the private sector, and dampen aggregate demand, particularly in economies characterized by high informality and limited financial depth. These effects disproportionately affect small and medium enterprises, leading to reduced employment, declining household incomes, and widening inequality, often without meaningful reductions in the prices of essential goods. In addition, exchange rate interventions are constrained by limited foreign reserve buffers and persistent external vulnerabilities, while weak financial systems further impair the transmission of monetary policy signals to the real economy. The policy brief concludes that inflation control cannot be effectively achieved through monetary policy alone. It calls for a coordinated policy framework that integrates credible and flexible monetary policy with disciplined fiscal management and targeted structural reforms. Strategic investments in agriculture, energy systems, and infrastructure are essential to address the structural roots of inflation.

The findings reveal a market characterized by high corporate concentration, with Grupo Nutresa accounting for 46.1% of the sales value. Overall, the results point to a relatively mature market where barriers to entry are not solely dependent on production, but primarily on factors such as distribution and brand positioning. Within this framework, the capillarity of the traditional distribution channel emerges as a critical competitive advantage for established actors.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain for Real-Time Financial Reporting: Automating Accounting, Reducing Fraud, and Enhancing Reliability

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain for Real-Time Financial Reporting: Automating Accounting, Reducing Fraud, and Enhancing Reliability
detail.abstract: Through this study, I examine how we can revolutionize traditional financial reporting processes by integrating blockchain technology, automation, and artificial intelligence (AI) into a single model. Conventional accounting is still characterized by periodic closings, manual reconciliation and retrospective auditing that are known to introduce delays, human errors, and increased exposure to fraud. This study verifies whether a reporting system involving technology can be used to enhance productivity, accuracy and reliability within such limitations. I operated two accounting systems in parallel during a three-month comparative case study with one mediumsized e-commerce company: a traditional manual reporting system and a technology-powered platform where AI automation was enforced on a permissioned blockchain ledger. I analyzed five common indicators of performance (Bizri et al., 2021) which are monthly closing time, rate of transaction error, audit hours, accuracy of fraud detection and cost of reporting which were determined on approximately 10,000 transactions. The results indicate that there is a remarkable improvement of AI-blockchain environment. There was an increase of 29 % in the accuracy of fraud detection, a reduction of 46 in the auditing hours, time saved in the monthly closing of books, the error rates were to be reduced by 76 percent and the costs of reporting were to be reduced by 39. The implications of these findings are as follows: with the help of real-time processing, reinforcing internal controls, and enhancing transparency, combining AI and blockchain can positively influence the financial reporting considerably. But the first incurred expenses and uncertainty on the part of regulations are still major factors to mass adoption.

title: From US Practice to Cross-Border Reality

detail.title: From US Practice to Cross-Border Reality
detail.abstract: This note argues real estate contracts "two papers" in the land sale contract and the deed remains analytically useful, but is incomplete for foreign-linked buyers. For NRIs and nonimmigrant buyers in the United States, the central legal risks often arise outside classical first-year property doctrine: tax residence, source-of-funds compliance, disclosure and title diligence, lender representations, exit withholding, estate tax exposure, and India-side reporting obligations. The better framework is therefore not merely contract plus deed, but contract plus deed plus status, tax classification, title diligence, and cross-border planning.

title: Unequal ecological exchange of water in Mexico: A two level input-output analysis of blue virtual water flows

detail.title: Unequal ecological exchange of water in Mexico: A two level input-output analysis of blue virtual water flows

declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the National Council of Humanities, Sciences and Technologies of Mexico (CONAHCYT) through grant number 852583, as part of their foreign Ph.D. scholarships program.

contentFormat.other: The second chapter of my Ph.D. thesis in economics

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether Mexico's integration into global value chains (GVCs) has produced unequal ecological exchanges (UEE) of blue water resources, both with its main trading partners and across its domestic macro-regions. To this end, we carry out an inter-country and an inter-regional input-output analysis to trace virtual water flows embedded in international and domestic trade for 2018. Results show that Mexico is a net exporter of virtual water to the USA, Canada, the EU27, Japan, and Latin America, driven by agricultural, agri-food, and motor vehicle industries, while importing virtual water from China, Brazil, and India through agricultural, plastics, basic steel, and food processing industries. At the subnational level, international trade emerges as the primary driver of water stress in the North region, and preliminary evidence points to a net transfer of water resources from the South and North-Central towards the North and Central regions, suggesting intranational UEE dynamics. These findings underscore the need for targeted water resource management policies, coordinated public-private investment in water infrastructure, and prioritization of regions whose working populations depend most heavily on water-intensive industries.

title: Ecuador's 2026 Oil Hedge in a High-Volatility World

detail.title: Ecuador's 2026 Oil Hedge in a High-Volatility World
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes Ecuador's 2026 sovereign oil hedging program through a combined quantitative and legal institutional lens. Using a Monte Carlo simulation calibrated to high-volatility market conditions (σ ≈ 35%), the study evaluates fiscal revenue outcomes under four hedging structures: unhedged, Asian put option, collar, and three-way collar. The simulation is grounded in Ecuador's current export profile (approximately 120 million barrels hedged annually), the IMF Extended Fund Facility (EFF) fiscal adjuster (~$23.85 million per $1/barrel), and the operational parameters established by BCE Resolution JPRFM-2026-009-M of March 2026.

title: Strengthening Upstream Circular Economy Governance in Kenya: Policy Recommendations from a Multi-Stakeholder Assessment

detail.title: Strengthening Upstream Circular Economy Governance in Kenya: Policy Recommendations from a Multi-Stakeholder Assessment

keywords: CC BY (Creative Commons Attribution) Upstream circular economy

detail.abstract: Kenya has made significant progress in downstream circular economy (CE) interventions, including waste management policies and recycling programs. However, upstream circular economy (UCE)-designing out waste before it is created-remains nascent. This paper presents findings from the UCERA (Upstream Circular Economy Readiness Assessment) validation workshop held in Nairobi on 1st April 2026, organized by UNIDO, the Ministry of Industry of Kenya, and Demos Helsinki. Drawing on participatory assessment involving six Kenyan government entities (SDTVET, MECCF, SDEP, NEMA, KNCPC, and MITI), the paper identifies key gaps in coordination, policy focus, and skills development. It offers recommendations for strengthening upstream CE governance, including digitizing assessment tools, introducing anonymous feedback mechanisms, leveraging Kenya's mobile money infrastructure (M-PESA), integrating upstream principles into TVET curricula, and planning for a just transition for informal sector workers (e.g., Dandora waste pickers, mitumba traders). The paper concludes that Kenya is ready for upstream CE, provided that enforcement, capacity building, and institutional coordination are prioritized. The findings are relevant to policymakers, development partners, TVET institutions, and researchers working on circular economy transitions in emerging economies.

title: Predictive Value of Within-Strategy Permutation Tests for Forward Selection: Evidence from Over 6 Billion Strategy-Level Permutations Across Three Asset Classes

detail.title: Predictive Value of Within-Strategy Permutation Tests for Forward Selection: Evidence from Over 6 Billion Strategy-Level Permutations Across Three Asset Classes

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. No financial or non-financial interests are related to the subject matter of this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study does not involve human participants, human data, or animals. All analyses use publicly available market data (cryptocurrency exchange data, FX quotes, and commodity futures prices).
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Within-strategy Monte Carlo permutation testing—shuffling a strategy's trade returns to assess significance—rests on an exchangeability assumption that financial time series violate. Does acting on the test's output improve forward strategy selection? We evaluate this across 437,911 strategy configurations (8 indicator families; within-family bar-level PnL correlations average only |ρ| = 0.031, refuting the common assumption of near-duplicate return streams among parameter variants) on nine instruments spanning three asset classes (crypto, forex, commodities) and 160 walk-forward windows, with over 6.1 billion strategy-level permutations. Cross-asset correlations reduce the effective number of independent replications to approximately three to four asset-class clusters, but the negative-lift finding holds within each cluster. Adding MC filtering on top of a simple in-sample profitability gate (IS Profit Factor > 1) produces negative incremental lift—the change in out-of-sample profitability from applying the filter—of −1.2 pp in crypto (95% CI [−1.33, −1.07], p < 10⁻⁴) and −0.6 to −1.5 pp in forex and commodities. While the per-strategy effect is small in isolation, it compounds across the pipeline: a fund evaluating 1,000 strategies per quarter loses approximately 13 profitable candidates from its MC-filtered pool (1,000 × 0.013), and this systematic bias accumulates across evaluation cycles and interacts multiplicatively with large search spaces. The effect is structurally consistent across all conditions tested: a placebo test with matched pass rates produces zero lift (mean ±0.003 pp), confirming it is not a statistical artifact. An IS Profit Factor-stratified analysis confirms that in crypto markets, the negative lift persists within narrow IS PF bins (five of six bins, 93.8% of observations), identifying an independent temporal-selection channel. In forex and commodity markets, the aggregate negative lift is largely attributable to MC anti-selecting on IS PF; once IS PF is controlled, the residual lift is negligible. The primary mechanism in crypto reflects a failure of within-strategy resampling under non-exchangeability: permutation destroys temporal return structure that is orthogonal to forward profitability, inducing adverse selection on regime-dependent compounding rather than signal quality. Additionally, the Profit Factor—the most common selection metric—is provably permutation-invariant and invisible to the test by construction. The finding generalizes across asset classes with fundamentally different microstructure and is confirmed by synthetic experiments under known ground truth.

title: Bureaucratic Capacity and Urban Planning: Evidence from Los Angeles
affiliations: California State University, Northridge - David Nazarian College of Business and Economics, University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) and University of Connecticut

detail.title: Bureaucratic Capacity and Urban Planning: Evidence from Los Angeles
detail.abstract: Using data from the Los Angeles City Planning Commission, we document the role of bureaucratic capacity in influencing urban development outcomes. We show that public opposition and familiarity of cases matter. Cases that are fairly typical are more likely to sail through approvals, but cases exhibiting peculiar features are less likely to be approved and more likely to be delayed. We measure familiarity by how semantically unique the proposal is compared to other proposals of its category. A one standard deviation increase in uniqueness decreases the log odds of approval by 0.283. Public opposition matters as well: a doubling of the number of opposition letters reduces the log odds of approval by 0.137. The results are consistent with a model of bureaucratic choice with public monitoring, reputational risk, and cognitive constraints.

title: Strengthening Financial Stability and Economic Inclusion in the United States Through Strategic Leadership in Cooperative Financial Institutions

detail.title: Strengthening Financial Stability and Economic Inclusion in the United States Through Strategic Leadership in Cooperative Financial Institutions
detail.abstract: Financial stability and economic inclusion remain central priorities within the United States, particularly as financial systems confront increasing complexity, technological disruption, and persistent inequality in access to capital. Credit unions, as cooperative financial institutions, occupy a unique position in advancing these objectives due to their member-focused structure and community-based mission. However, the effectiveness of credit unions in contributing to national economic outcomes is significantly influenced by the quality of executive leadership, organizational culture, and risk governance practices. This article develops a leadership-driven framework that integrates strategic alignment, enterprise risk management, and cultural cohesion as mechanisms for enhancing institutional performance and systemic resilience. Drawing on interdisciplinary literature in financial management, leadership theory, and cooperative economics, the analysis demonstrates that strengthening executive leadership within credit unions represents a scalable solution to improving financial inclusion, supporting small business growth, and enhancing economic stability in underserved communities. The findings highlight the broader national implications of leadership innovation in cooperative finance, positioning it as a critical contributor to sustainable economic development in the United States.

title: Digital Rights Management and Copyright's Paradigm: The Implications of Backdoor Propertisation in Digital Copyright Law for End-Users' Access to Knowledge

detail.title: Digital Rights Management and Copyright's Paradigm: The Implications of Backdoor Propertisation in Digital Copyright Law for End-Users' Access to Knowledge
detail.abstract:
This paper analyses the implications of technical protection measures (TPM) enabled digital rights management systems as a mode of increased intellectual property rights for rightsholders through the backdoor. The analysis considers the implications of the backdoor propertisation of creative works for end-users within copyright’s paradigm, conducted through the lens of the Infosoc Directive’s Article 6(4).

 

   This paper establishes that the ambiguous wording of Art. 6 (4), when implemented into EU member state domestic laws, functions as an avenue for rightsholders to exploit the provision’s ambiguity to increase their IPRs through the backdoor (backdoor propertisation). Through its analysis of the implementation of Article 6 (4) into the UK's Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988's topical s.29A Text and Data-Mining exception, the paper not only strengthens its position that backdoor IPRs place unnecessary burdens on end-users accessing knowledge under copyright’s exceptions and limitations. It is also established that TPMs serve as a mechanism for the backdoor propertisation of creative works.

   This work established the core conceptual framework for the author's research into developing a forward-thinking theory of regime-shifting, serving as the pivotal starting point for nearly a decade of subsequent research into backdoor propertisation and Article 6(4) of the Infosoc Directive.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Data Governance, and the Future of Financial Stability: A Strategic Framework for U.S. Cooperative Financial Institutions

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence, Data Governance, and the Future of Financial Stability: A Strategic Framework for U.S. Cooperative Financial Institutions
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and advanced data analytics are rapidly transforming the financial services sector, creating both unprecedented opportunities and complex systemic risks. While large financial institutions have led the adoption of AI-driven technologies, cooperative financial institutions such as credit unions remain at an earlier stage of integration, creating both a capability gap and a strategic opportunity. This article examines the role of AI and data governance in strengthening financial stability, improving risk management, and expanding financial inclusion within the United States. It develops a leadership-driven framework for the responsible adoption of AI in credit unions, emphasizing ethical data use, regulatory alignment, and institutional resilience. Drawing on interdisciplinary literature in financial technology, risk governance, and organizational leadership, the study argues that advancing AI integration in cooperative financial institutions represents a matter of substantial merit and national importance. The findings highlight how strategic leadership in AI adoption can enhance systemic stability, reduce financial exclusion, and contribute to long-term economic competitiveness in the United States.

title: Climate Risk and Financial System Resilience: The Emerging Role of Credit Unions in Sustainable Economic Development in the United States

detail.title: Climate Risk and Financial System Resilience: The Emerging Role of Credit Unions in Sustainable Economic Development in the United States
detail.abstract: Climate change has emerged as a systemic financial risk with far-reaching implications for asset valuation, credit performance, and economic stability. While large financial institutions have increasingly incorporated climate risk into strategic decision-making, the role of cooperative financial institutions-particularly credit unions-remains underdeveloped in both practice and scholarly discourse. This article examines the integration of climate-related financial risk within credit unions and its broader implications for financial system resilience in the United States. It develops a leadership-driven framework that aligns climate risk governance, strategic lending practices, and community engagement with sustainable economic development objectives. Drawing on interdisciplinary literature in sustainable finance, risk management, and organizational leadership, the study argues that credit unions can play a critical role in mitigating climate-related risks while advancing financial inclusion and local economic resilience. The findings highlight that incorporating climate risk into cooperative financial leadership represents a matter of substantial merit and national importance, contributing to long-term economic stability and environmental sustainability.

declarations.ethicsApproval: The author has no subject-related ethics statement related to this paper.

detail.abstract: Transportation projects that require utility infrastructure relocations along existing rights of way are often delayed because status quo policies misalign incentives: utilities bear full relocation costs while the transportation authority bears full delay costs. This paper argues that a compensation requirement, structured as a contingent payment for timely relocation performance, can resolve this incentive problem and avoid transportation project delays. The paper first characterizes the multi-utility right of way as an anti-commons in which multi-party coordination is held back by fragmented exclusion rights, leading to systematic under-delivery of timely relocation. We then draw a useful parallel between forced relocations and eminent domain as used in land assembly projects. A sequential decision model based on this parallel is presented that demonstrates why utilities are incentivized to delay under the status quo. The model then shows that conditional compensation, designed as payment contingent on timely relocation, induces better outcomes with relocations proceeding on schedule. The policy could succeed with modest compensation, making the policy fiscally feasible as well as incentive compatible.

title: Token Dilution and the Cross-Section of Cryptocurrency Returns

detail.title: Token Dilution and the Cross-Section of Cryptocurrency Returns
detail.abstract: This study investigates whether token supply dilution predicts the cross-section of cryptocurrency returns, establishing a parallel to the share issuance anomaly in equity markets. Using weekly data for 404 cryptocurrencies from November 2020 to March 2026 sourced from the CoinGecko API, three dilution measures are constructed: the oat ratio (circulating supply relative to maximum supply), the FDV premium (fully diluted valuation relative to market capitalization), and the smoothed dilution rate (12-week moving average of circulating supply growth). The empirical analysis yields four main ndings. First, token dilution signicantly predicts crosssectional returns. The FDV premium achieves a Newey-West t-statistic of-3.13 in Fama-MacBeth regressions; the 12-week dilution rate achieves t =-2.79 in a paired specication that combines it with the oat ratio and t =-2.54 when paired with the FDV premium. The ow coecient is statistically indistinguishable across the two pairings (p = 0.65), supporting the internal consistency of the paired design. Portfolio sorts produce annualized long-short spreads of 2532%. Second, aggregate dilution risk is a priced systematic factor: a dilution beta estimated from a two-factor model carries a signicant positive premium (t = +2.88), indicating that coins with higher exposure to aggregate dilution shocks earn higher expected returns. Third, the liquidity amplication hypothesis is not supported: the dilution premium is not signicantly larger among illiquid coins. Fourth, and most substantively, the dilution premium has an identiable economic scope. It is absent in value-weighted regressions but re-emerges after excluding the top-ve blue-chip coins, and it is concentrated in coins in their rst year of trading with no detectable eect in mature coins. This patternpremium absent where analyst attention and arbitrage capital are abundant, premium present where they are scarceis consistent with a limitedattention mechanism rather than mechanical price pressure. The results are robust across bull and bear markets, pre-and post-Bitcoin-ETF subperiods, alternative winsorization cutos, and various sample restrictions. A Wald test of the paired design across seven subsamples fails to reject equality of the ow coecient in six cases. These ndings contribute to the cryptocurrency asset pricing literature by documenting a supply-side anomaly, introducing token dilution risk as a systematic pricing factor, and mapping the economic boundary within which the characteristic premium operates.

title: Progress in Neuroscience Models through Stochastic Differential Equations and AI

detail.title: Progress in Neuroscience Models through Stochastic Differential Equations and AI

declarations.funderStatement: Iden Stein is the main author, Rajit Chatterjea is the second author and the mentor of Iden Stein

detail.abstract: Existing stochastic Hodgkin-Huxley (SHH) models capture single-neuron noise but seldom integrate network-level energy dynamics with AI-assisted parameter inference in a unified, mathematically guaranteed framework. Population-density and moment-closure approaches track statistical moments efficiently yet sacrifice biophysical detail. We address these gaps by proposing a hybrid stochastic neural model that combines Hodgkin-Huxley ion-channel dynamics with Ashkin-Teller-inspired network coupling, probabilistic spiking, and activity-dependent synaptic plasticity governed by Itô stochastic differential equations (SDEs). The biological motivation for the Ashkin-Teller coupling is to capture the two distinct excitatory/inhibitory binary states that coexist within cortical microcircuits, a feature that purely additive synaptic current models cannot represent. We prove existence and uniqueness of strong solutions via Lipschitz continuity and linear-growth verification under Itô's theorem, and establish domain invariance that maintains biologically meaningful state bounds, for single-neuron, two-neuron, and general N-neuron configurations. Machine-learning parameter optimisation is used to infer conductance and plasticity parameters from simulated spike-train statistics; the specific algorithms and evaluation protocols are described in the body of the paper. Euler-Maruyama simulations for N = 1, 2, 5 neurons demonstrate fluctuating membrane potentials, rare spiking events, and emergent low-frequency oscillatory patterns in mean firing rates driven by intrinsic noise and covariance-based plasticity. Qualitative agreement with established SHH channel-noise results and mean-field integrate-and-fire networks is discussed, together with the limitations of the present approach and avenues for empirical validation against publicly available electrophysiology datasets.

detail.abstract: Bài viết phân tích yêu cầu cấp thiết của việc hoàn thiện thể chế pháp luật nhằm đáp ứng mục tiêu phát triển nhanh và bền vững theo tinh thần Nghị quyết Đại hội XIV của Đảng Cộng sản Việt Nam. Trong bối cảnh toàn cầu "hỗn loạn" với sự phân mảnh quản trị đa phương, biến đổi khí hậu gia tăng và các cú sốc hệ thống liên tiếp, pháp luật không còn giữ vai trò điều chỉnh thụ động mà phải chuyển sang mô hình thích ứng, đa trung tâm và lấy chuyển đổi công bằng làm trụ cột. title: Developing a Self-Management Skills Enhancement Program for Primary School Learners
affiliations: Angeles University Foundation and Angeles University Foundation

detail.title: Developing a Self-Management Skills Enhancement Program for Primary School Learners
detail.abstract: This study analyzed the implementation of a self-management skills program and the multifaceted performance of primary school learners at Dongchang Road Primary School, Shandong, China. It aimed to describe learners' demographic profiles by age, gender, and grade level. It also assessed the level of program implementation for self-monitoring, self-evaluation, and self-reinforcement mechanisms. Further, it determined learners' levels of self-control, selfconfidence, and self-worth, identified differences in multifaceted performance across demographic variables, examined the significant effects of self-management skills on multifaceted performance, and developed a proposed self-management skills development program. A descriptive correlational design with regression analysis was used to examine relationships among the variables without manipulation. The participants were in Grades 4-6 of a primary school. The data were analyzed using frequency and percentage, mean and standard deviation, Mann-Whitney U test, Kruskal-Wallis test, and multiple linear regression with bootstrapping. The findings showed that a developmentally appropriate, well-balanced sample had nearly equal representation across all grade levels. The self-management skills program was implemented to a very great extent, and learners demonstrated very high levels of self-control, self-confidence, and self-worth. No significant differences in multifaceted performance were found across age, gender, or grade level. The regression analysis showed that selective, dimension-specific effects on self-evaluation significantly enhanced self-control, whereas selfreinforcement positively influenced self-confidence but was negatively associated with selfcontrol. No self-management component independently predicted self-worth or overall multifaceted performance. Thus, based on the findings, a balanced and integrative selfmanagement skills development program is proposed. It emphasizes reflective self-evaluation, guided reinforcement, and emotionally supportive classroom practices for learners.

Các đề xuất này nhằm nâng tầm Hiến pháp từ văn bản ổn định tĩnh sang khung pháp lý động, khả thi, công bằng và thích ứng, góp phần hiện thực hóa mục tiêu phát triển nhanh và bền vững đến năm 2045.
