declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study is based on the analysis of publicly available political texts and does not involve human participants or personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This study presents an Area Studies analysis of the discursive construction of a negative image of Alliance 90/The Greens in German political discourse following the February 23, 2025 Bundestag elections. Against the backdrop of record-high voter turnout (82.5%), the victory of the CDU/CSU bloc, and the collapse of the "traffic light" coalition, the Greens' electoral result (11.61%, fourth place) triggered intensified critical discourse. Drawing on parliamentary speeches (M. Weiser, AfD) and media texts (T. Handel, Die Tagesschau), the research identifies five dominant delegitimization strategies: catastrophization, irrationalization, historical stigmatization, destructive semantics, and regional marginalization. The analysis reveals that post-2025 criticism has shifted from programmatic debate to ontological delegitimization, wherein the party is problematized not for specific policies but as a bearer of a value model perceived as alien, particularly in eastern German states. The findings contribute to political linguistics, German Area Studies, and comparative discourse analysis.

title: Liquidity as a double-edged sword: US firm responses to oil volatility and Middle East geopolitical conflict

detail.title: Liquidity as a double-edged sword: US firm responses to oil volatility and Middle East geopolitical conflict

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This study examines whether corporate cash holdings provide uniform protection against macroeconomic shocks. Using a panel of US non-financial firms over 2009-2024, we interact predetermined cash holdings with oil price volatility and Middle East conflict. We document that cash enhances profitability during oil uncertainty but is associated with lower profitability during geopolitical conflict. Both effects concentrate among financially constrained firms and align with the precautionary motive framework. Our result remains constant with using an alternate proxy of geopolitical risk and GARCH-based volatility. Results also survive Bartik instrumental variables, a shipping route disruption IV, and a Durbin-Wu-Hausman test. Our findings challenge the assumption that liquidity provides universal insurance against external uncertainty.

title: A Hierarchical Theory of Macrodynamics: Distribution, Stability, and Endogenous Cycles in a Cambridge-Kaleckian Framework

detail.title: A Hierarchical Theory of Macrodynamics: Distribution, Stability, and Endogenous Cycles in a Cambridge-Kaleckian Framework

declarations.funderStatement: The author thanks to CNPQ for its financial support.

detail.abstract:
This thesis presents a hierarchical macrodynamics theory where income distribution, capital accumulation, and macroeconomic stability are interconnected through a Cambridge-Kaleckian framework. Central to this theory are continuous-time dynamical systems, ranging from a two-dimensional Sraffian Supermultiplier model to a complex five-dimensional open-economy system that incorporates fiscal policy and balance-of-payments constraints.

Eleven primary theorems are established. The first theorem demonstrates the unconditional local asymptotic stability of the Sraffian Supermultiplier model, correcting an error in the literature. Subsequent theorems analyze the three-dimensional Cambridge-Kaleckian system, revealing a one-dimensional equilibrium and an explicit threshold for cyclical behavior. The stability of Kaleckian markup dynamics is affirmed, enhancing the theoretical robustness of the model.

The framework also extends to considerations of fiscal policy and international dynamics, confirming that counter-cyclical measures can be harmonized with the Cambridge anchor. Moreover, the thesis shows that the Cambridge-Kaleckian investment function subsumes various existing models, including the New Keynesian framework.

Finally, the application of this theory to the macroeconomic implications of artificial intelligence suggests that AI's impact on stability and distribution remains uncertain, yet a tailored stabilization strategy can enhance robustness in the presence of AI.

title: A High-Performance Monte Carlo Framework for Credit Derivatives Pricing, Implied Dependence, and Model Risk
affiliations: University of Oxford - Said Business School

detail.title: A High-Performance Monte Carlo Framework for Credit Derivatives Pricing, Implied Dependence, and Model Risk
detail.abstract:
We develop a high-performance Monte Carlo framework for pricing credit derivatives, including single-name Credit Default Swaps (CDS) and multi-name basket structures such as First-to-Default and Nth-to-Default products.

The framework combines reduced-form hazard rate modelling with latent dependence captured via a one-factor Gaussian copula, and introduces a structural decomposition in which combinatorial default aggregation is separated from simulation. This enables the construction of an effective basket hazard curve prior to Monte Carlo valuation, significantly reducing computational complexity while remaining fully consistent with calibrated single-name CDS term structures.

The implementation is designed for scalability and numerical efficiency, leveraging quasirandom Sobol sequences, OpenMP parallelisation, and a flattened memory architecture that ensures cache-efficient path evaluation. In the single-name case, pricing reduces to a single uniform draw per path, yielding linear complexity in the number of simulations.

We interpret Monte Carlo pricing as a structural mapping from model primitives-hazard rates, dependence structure, and higher-order features such as jumps or regime shifts-to observable market prices. Within this framework, dependence parameters such as Gaussian copula correlation are not structural constants, but reduced-form objects that absorb multiple sources of systemic risk and model misspecification.

Extensions such as jump dynamics and regime-dependent intensities do not introduce independent pricing signals, but instead reshape the implied dependence structure required to match market prices.

The resulting framework serves both as a production-grade pricing engine and as a research platform for analysing calibration instability, model risk, and the regime dependence of implied credit correlations in multi-name credit markets.

title: Does Artificial Intelligence Keep Firms Out of Trouble? Evidence from Corporate Litigation in China

detail.title: Does Artificial Intelligence Keep Firms Out of Trouble? Evidence from Corporate Litigation in China
detail.abstract: We analyse the effects of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption on corporate litigation risk, exploring longitudinal firm level data from China spanning 2007 to 2024. Using the "Broadband China" policy as an exogenous shock, we find that a one unit increase in AI adoption led to a 14.8% decline in defendant litigation losses and decreased the probability of encountering a catastrophic major lawsuit by 26.5 percentage points. At the same time, we find that AI adoption significantly reduced a firm's dependence on short-term debt and curbed the incidence of corporate fraud. These risk reduction effects were concentrated among non-state-owned enterprises, industry followers, and firms facing high environmental uncertainty. We also show that this deterrence effect was driven entirely by substantive data infrastructure rather than symbolic "AI-washing", and required complementary institutional monitoring to function effectively. Finally, by safeguarding cash flows from legal disputes, more exposed firms significantly increased their long-term R&D investments.

title: Decolonial Constitutionalism
affiliations: The University of the West Indies, Cave Hill Campus

detail.title: Decolonial Constitutionalism
detail.abstract: The author proposes an understanding of decolonial constitutionalism that accounts for the history of slavery, colonialism, and racial capitalism not only as historical injustices but also as constitutive forces of power, knowledge, and being. The 1661 Barbados Slave Code as a “slave constitution” institutionalized racialized violence in the slave society to render the Black human as nonhuman through the law. The author critiques the coloniality of Independence Caribbean constitutions and challenges the reformist approaches to decolonial constitutionalism that fail to disrupt this coloniality. Employing Charles W. Mills's use of the creole concept of smadditizin’—the struggle for recognition of personhood where it was denied because of race—the author advocates for a refounding of Caribbean constitutions. This refounding must center the Caribbean person as “somebody” (smaddy), as individual and collective agents of their own liberation. The author therefore envisages decolonial constitutionalism as a transformative project to create a new blueprint for the way of life of a political community, that is, a constitution that affirms the sovereignty of the people. Decolonial constitutionalism is not merely legal reform; it must be an ontological rupture grounded in Caribbean-centered epistemologies.

title: Segmentación de Empresas para Estrategias de Inversión en Valor: Un Enfoque basado en Fuzzy C-Means y Random Forest

detail.title: Segmentación de Empresas para Estrategias de Inversión en Valor: Un Enfoque basado en Fuzzy C-Means y Random Forest
detail.abstract: El presente estudio tiene como objetivo identificar de manera sistemática empresas potencialmente infravaloradas con fundamentos financieros sólidos. La metodología combina el algoritmo Fuzzy C-means, utilizado para segmentar 322 compañías que componen el índice S&P 500, con el método Random Forest, empleado para determinar la importancia de las variables dentro de la estructura de los grupos. Se identificaron tres conglomerados con diferencias significativas en sus indicadores financieros, lo que revela la utilidad de los métodos propuestos en estrategias de inversión. El índice de rotación de activos y el múltiplo precio sobre ventas resultaron ser variables determinantes, manteniendo su relevancia tanto en 2020 como en 2024.

title: Outcome-Classified Precision Auditing of Filter Rules in Algorithmic DEX Trading: Evidence from 2,400 Rejection Events

detail.title: Outcome-Classified Precision Auditing of Filter Rules in Algorithmic DEX Trading: Evidence from 2,400 Rejection Events

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests. The research was conducted independently without institutional or external funding. The author operates the production trading system from which the dataset was derived and is the sole beneficiary of its performance.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. No human-subjects research is involved. The dataset consists of public on-chain token identifiers and price observations from a public price oracle, as noted in Section IV of the paper.
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded. No external or institutional funding.

detail.abstract: Filter-gated algorithmic trading systems on decentralized exchanges reject the majority of candidate tokens they encounter, yet the in-production precision of these filter rules-whether they save capital more often than they forgo profitable entries-is rarely measured at scale. Prior work by the author introduced a post-rejection follow-up sampling methodology capable of producing the necessary data. The present paper reports the first at-scale precision audit produced by that methodology. Applied to a production multi-strategy trading fleet over a continuous fourteenday observation window, the method yielded approximately 99,000 follow-up samples across approximately 2,400 unique rejection events spanning eight active filter rules. We introduce an outcome classification refinement that credits a rejected candidate's disappearance from the price oracle within a short interval of rejection as an implicit positive save signal, on the premise that such disappearance is the observable signature of the rug-pull and delisting outcomes filter stacks are designed to avoid. Under this refinement, every active filter in the live stack demonstrates a net-positive precision verdict with an aggregate save-to-miss ratio of approximately fifteen to one. Under the conservative alternative that excludes the early-death category, the ratio remains strongly positive at approximately four to one. Early-death events account for roughly half of all classified rejections, a finding that reshapes the filtercalibration problem in this domain toward asymmetric avoidance of a substantial short-lived token population rather than symmetric opportunity-cost balancing.

detail.abstract: Purpose: The primary purpose of this research is to examine the effects of external debt on economic development in South Asia from 1990 to 2020. Based on previous literature, some findings indicate that external debt plays a vital role in economic development, supporting human health, development projects, and humanitarian assistance in disasters and underdeveloped countries, while others are not in favor. Hence, this study aims to assess the impacts of foreign debt on South Asian economies and to offer recommendations for achieving a sound economic status. Methodology: This research is based on cross-sectional data for selected countries in South Asia. The study employs basic tests and techniques such as panel unit root tests, descriptive statistics, panel cointegration, correlation matrix, Granger causality, VIF estimation, heteroscedasticity tests, and ECM. Findings: The outcomes of the analysis confirmed that external debt has negative effects in both the short run and the long run on the economic growth of South Asia. Recommendations: The present study suggests that it is better not to rely too heavily on external loans. Because these countries have to pay a large portion of their GDP. Therefore, the government should manage the budget, avoid unnecessary expenditures, and plan the tax system to increase revenue rather than depending on other states. It is also important to ensure the clarity and accountability of leading bodies and to strengthen public financial management.

title: The Labor-Sovereign Enterprise

detail.title: The Labor-Sovereign Enterprise

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no financial relationships with any organizations relevant to this work. This paper was produced from independent scholarly interest with no external funding or institutional affiliation.
declarations.funderStatement: Self-Funded

detail.abstract: The standard market firm has a structural problem: labor is a cost, and rational operators minimize costs. This is not a moral failure. It is a mechanical one. No wage floor, regulatory constraint, or moral appeal fully resolves an incentive structure in which treating people as expendable is the optimizing move. The solution must operate at the same level as the problem-structural. This paper proposes the Labor-Sovereign Enterprise (LSE), a legal business designation, analogous to nonprofit or benefit corporation status, that imposes five operational requirements on participating firms: a receiver-defined compensation floor, dynamic wage adjustability, a transparent append-only operational ledger, a free communication platform accessible to all workers without operator moderation, and a democratic governance process in which the worker electorate is sovereign and the governance form itself is revisable. These requirements are audited by a polycentric enforcement structure spanning community, state, and governmental bodies.

title: WORKING PAPER | ECONOMIC ANALYTICS & POLICY Probabilistic Macroeconomic Intelligence: A Monte Carlo Framework for Real-Time U.S. Scenario Forecasting and National Economic Risk Assessment

detail.abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic macroeconomic intelligence framework that integrates real-time Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) retrieval, Monte Carlo simulation (N=500 stochastic paths), and large language model (LLM)-driven narrative synthesis into a unified, deployable dashboard architecture. Drawing on eight core U.S. macroeconomic indicators-including CPI inflation, unemployment, the Fed Funds Rate, real GDP growth, the 10Y-2Y Treasury yield spread, the National Financial Conditions Index (NFCI), industrial production, and consumer sentiment-the system generates probabilistic forecasts over rolling 12-36 month horizons with P10-P90 uncertainty quantification. We demonstrate that baseline forecasts project moderate GDP growth (1.71% over 36 months), declining inflation toward the Federal Reserve's 2% target, and a 13% 12-month recession probability under current conditions. Critically, the framework's scenario simulation capability-including financial condition shocks and monetary policy pivots-reveals non-linear systemic sensitivities obscured by conventional point-estimate forecasting. We argue this architecture represents a methodological advance over static econometric tools and has direct implications for fiscal policy design, financial risk management, humanitarian resource allocation, and national economic resilience planning. The system was built and deployed by the author using serverless cloud infrastructure (Cloudflare Workers) and constitutes an original contribution to applied economic intelligence systems.

title: The Future of Money: Agentic AI-integrated Real World Asset Tokenisation
affiliations: NUS High School of Mathematics and Science

detail.title: The Future of Money: Agentic AI-integrated Real World Asset Tokenisation
detail.abstract: This paper quantifies the economic impact of real-world asset tokenisation integrated with agentic artificial intelligence across global financial markets. I develop a Monte Carlo simulation framework calibrated to pilot data to project cost savings under parameter uncertainty, complemented by scenario analysis with stochastic dominance testing and Sobol sensitivity analysis. Projections indicate cumulative savings of $9.49 trillion (90% CI: $5.89-$13.69 trillion) over 2025-2039 across foreign exchange, alternative investments, and real estate markets. Three findings emerge. First, projection uncertainty is dominated by forex cost reduction parameters, establishing clear research priorities. Second, scenarios involving comprehensive institutional coordination first-order stochastically dominate fragmented experimentation, providing welfare justification for policy coordination that holds regardless of risk preferences. Third, calibrated adoption dynamics are consistent with historical diffusion patterns for financial technologies.

title: AI-Powered Corporate Governance
affiliations: Peking University - HSBC Business School, Peking University HSBC Business School and

detail.title: AI-Powered Corporate Governance
detail.abstract: We study how generative AI adoption by institutional investors reshapes corporate governance. Exploiting the November 2022 release of ChatGPT as a quasi-experimental shock to AI adoption costs, we show that firms with greater pre-shock exposure to machine-based investors experience significant valuation gains and strengthened governance, including increased CEO pay-performance and turnover-performance sensitivity, greater shareholder activism, and fewer financial restatements. These firms also undertake fewer but higher-quality acquisitions and produce fewer but more valuable patents, indicating improved investment efficiency in real decisions. We trace these effects to two complementary mechanisms. Generative AI enables machine-based investors to process idiosyncratic information at scale, shorten investment horizons, and coordinate trading, thereby strengthening exit-based discipline. At the same time, enhanced information processing facilitates coalition formation with activist investors, amplifying voice-based governance. Overall, AI-enhanced information processing by institutional investors strengthens governance and improves real economic outcomes.

title: A Comprehensive Survey on Prompting Strategies and Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Automated Financial Metrics Extraction
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and PICT Pune

detail.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Prompting Strategies and Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Automated Financial Metrics Extraction
detail.abstract: There is an exponential growth in unstructured data in finance these days, such as earnings reports and call transcripts, and regulatory filings too, and this is growing exponentially, making it difficult to manage manually. Hence, it is essential to have automated systems to obtain key metrics without wasting time. This survey is all about exploring the existing methods, especially large language models along with various prompting strategies and another technique called "Retrieval Augmented Generation" to obtain information about finance. The survey includes more than 30 papers, starting from traditional NLP methods, moving to neural networks, and finally to recent LLMs, along with various checks to see how they perform. The results are based on various datasets, including a few, such as "FinQA," which includes 8,281 pairs for question answering, "ConvFinQA," which includes 3,892 conversations and more than 14,000 questions within them, and "TAT-QA," which includes 16,552 questions within them. State of the art models achieve 58 to 62%, but human experts achieve 89 to 91%, and this 30% gap is what's left to be addressed. Some key issues arise, such as numerical multi-step reasoning, which is somewhat tricky, and combining all kinds of heterogeneous data sources, and how to best acquire appropriate domain expertise for finance. That's what it seems to be, and that's what's holding everything back. For anyone looking to combine natural language processing and finance tech, this is a good resource, even though some of it is a bit scattered in how it all ties together.

title: Repricing Algorithms and Consumer Data
affiliations: University of Rochester - Simon Business School

detail.title: Repricing Algorithms and Consumer Data
detail.abstract: This paper studies how the data available to a repricing algorithm shapes equilibrium prices and welfare in a differentiated product duopoly. I contrast two informational regimes: an algorithm that observes only the rival's price, and one that additionally observes the consumer's demand type. Without demand data, a repricing algorithm raises equilibrium prices above the Bertrand level by allowing the rival to act as a price leader. With demand data, this channel collapses and equilibrium prices fall below the Bertrand level. A faster algorithm amplifies whichever effect is operative. Under endogenous adoption, the two regimes again yield opposing conclusions. Without demand data, equilibrium adoption always harms consumers. With demand data, adoption is a dominant strategy that leaves both sellers worse off while consumers benefit. These results caution against treating algorithmic access to consumer data as uniformly anti-consumer, as restricting such access can harm rather than protect consumers.

title: The Problem Is Not "Socialism" but the Term Itself: A Theoretical Analysis of the Conceptual Incoherence of Socialist Ideas

detail.title: The Problem Is Not "Socialism" but the Term Itself: A Theoretical Analysis of the Conceptual Incoherence of Socialist Ideas

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract:
The aim of this article is to demonstrate the theoretical incoherence and practical futility of the longstanding public debate “Capitalism vs. Socialism”.


The paper offers a conceptual and theoretical analysis of the term “socialism” within the framework of Marx’s philosophical–economic theory. It argues that contemporary discussions of capitalism and socialism are distorted by entrenched terminological errors that were consolidated and institutionalised within the Soviet ideological model, whose influence continues to shape political and intellectual discourse today.


By drawing a systematic distinction between Marx’s scientific theory—comprising dialectical materialism, historical materialism, and political economy—and the ideological construct developed during the Soviet period and commonly known as Marxism, the author demonstrates that the concept of a “socialist social formation” is theoretically inconsistent and lacks any foundation within the framework of historical materialism.


The analysis shows that, according to Marx’s theoretical system, the type of social formation is determined by the mode of production and, therefore, by the type of labour employed. From this standpoint, both private and state ownership are capitalist in character when the production process is based on wage labour. Hence, the so-called “socialist” states of the twentieth century should be regarded as systems of absolute state capitalism—a form of capitalism in which the state is the sole and monopolistic owner of all means of production.


The article further argues that the modern use of the term “socialism” results from a semantic substitution: instead of denoting a theoretically invalid type of social formation, it now refers to a social function of the capitalist state—namely, redistributive policy within the capitalist economic system. Clarifying these distinctions enables a more accurate understanding of Marx’s theoretical legacy and shows that, unlike the ideological doctrine of Marxism, his philosophical–economic theory supports rather than rejects the principles of a free society: private property, free labour, and economic efficiency.

title: Geopolitical Shocks and Default Probabilities of European Firms: A Sectoral Heterogeneity Analysis

detail.title: Geopolitical Shocks and Default Probabilities of European Firms: A Sectoral Heterogeneity Analysis
detail.abstract: This paper estimates sector-specific sensitivities of European firms’ default probabilities to geopolitical risk shocks, providing empirical counterparts to δk in the reverse stress testing framework of Hurlin et al. (2026). Using Local Projections on a panel of 1,324 European firms from January 2021 to April 2026, I estimate impulse responses of the logit-transformed Bloomberg 5-year default probability to a one-standard-deviation shock in the standardized first difference of the Caldara and Iacoviello (2022) GPR Index. Results show strong crosssector heterogeneity. Consumer Staples and Consumer Discretionary display the largest, most persistent responses, exceeding 0.018 after four months; Industrials, Materials, and Health Care also respond positively. Energy and Communication Services remain insignificant, while Financials are positive but less sensitive. At industry-group level, Automobiles & Components drives Consumer Discretionary, while Banks and Insurance show similar patterns. Robustness checks confirm the findings, and estimated ˆδk,h help calibrate sector-level credit portfolio models.

title: The Ouroboros Threat: How AI Cannibalism Degrades Cyber Threat Intelligence

detail.title: The Ouroboros Threat: How AI Cannibalism Degrades Cyber Threat Intelligence

keywords: L86: Information and Internet Services; Computer Software
O33: Technological Change: Choices and Consequences; Diffusion Processes

detail.abstract:
This paper investigates the systemic degradation of Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) caused by the exponential rise of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and its impact on machine learning-based defensive infrastructures. As cybersecurity models increasingly learn from synthetic, machine-generated data rather than continuous human-generated inputs, they suffer from a systemic architectural flaw known as Model Autophagy Disorder (MAD), or "model collapse." Through mathematically grounded analysis, this paper demonstrates that this recursive training progressively erases statistical outliers from training datasets. Consequently, automated security tools become highly optimized for filtering routine noise but develop catastrophic blind spots to sophisticated, human-engineered Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs), non-linear social engineering attacks, and zero-day exploits. This intrinsic vulnerability is further compounded by active adversarial exploitation, including data poisoning and the proliferation of fake proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits.

After systematically evaluating existing mitigation strategies, algorithmic synthetic data filtering, Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) verification, and cryptographic data provenance this study concludes that no single technological solution can fully neutralize synthetic data pollution. Instead, the paper proposes the adoption of a Hybrid Zero-Trust Intelligence Architecture. This framework combines strict cryptographic data provenance (aligning with emerging C2PA, STIX 2.1, and OASIS standards) with targeted, human-led validation for high-stakes intelligence. Supported by a rigorous Return on Security Investment (ROSI) analysis, the proposed architecture provides a vital strategic roadmap for enterprises to restore threat visibility, ensure operational resilience, and remain viable within an increasingly stringent cyber insurance market

detail.title: Horticulture and Agricultural Income in India: Evidence from a State-level Panel Analysis

detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of horticultural output on agricultural income across Indian states. Using a balanced panel dataset of 28 states over the period 2015-16 to 2023-24 (N = 252), the study estimates a mixed-functional form fixed effects model to quantify the relationship between the value of horticultural production and crop sector income, proxied by Crops Gross State Value Added (Crops GSVA). Controlling for irrigation, rainfall, fertiliser consumption, cropping intensity, and agricultural credit, the results indicate a positive and statistically significant relationship between horticulture and agricultural income. The preferred specification yields an elasticity of 0.410, implying that a 10% increase in horticultural output is associated with a 4.1% increase in Crops GSVA within a state. The findings are robust across alternative specifications, including exclusion of northeastern states, omission of credit, and inclusion of time fixed effects. The results provide macro-level empirical evidence supporting the role of horticulture-led diversification as a driver of agricultural income growth in India.

title: NOP-EU Cross-System Organic Compliance Protocol: A Practitioner Framework for U.S. Organic Operators Navigating the December 2026 U.S.–EU Regulatory Transition

detail.title: NOP-EU Cross-System Organic Compliance Protocol: A Practitioner Framework for U.S. Organic Operators Navigating the December 2026 U.S.–EU Regulatory Transition

keywords: NOP-EU Cross-System Organic Compliance Protocol v2.0 organic certification

detail.abstract:
The December 2026 expiration of the United States-European Union Organic Equivalence Arrangement, combined with the European Union's structural transition from an equivalence regime to a compliance regime under Regulation (EU) 2018/848, represents the most significant operational change for U.S. organic exporters since the creation of the USDA National Organic Program.

This protocol synthesizes the regulatory architecture U.S. organic operators must navigate across two parallel regimes: the NOP under 7 CFR Part 205 and EU 2018/848. It identifies the specific product categories, documentation workflows, and certification requirements where the two frameworks diverge, and provides a structured reference for operators building export readiness.

The protocol addresses twelve operational sections: (1) food system resilience context and the federal policy framework; (2) scope and exclusions of the bilateral Arrangement; (3) the EU compliance-based framework under 2018/848; (4) wine sulfite handling under 7 CFR § 205.605 and EU organic wine rules; (5) the livestock antibiotic prohibition and its cross-system treatment; (6) the NOP Import Certificate (NOPIC) workflow under the Strengthening Organic Enforcement Final Rule, 88 Fed. Reg. 3548 (January 19, 2023); (7) SOE-era fraud prevention, supply-chain traceability, and recordkeeping requirements; (8) reconditioning procedures under both NOP and EU frameworks; (9) the EU Certificate of Inspection issued through the TRACES NT electronic platform; (10) three cross-system compliance scenarios drawn from grain-and-oilseed export, wine export, and non-covered product categories; (11) the integration of cross-system compliance with sustainable agriculture practice and federal conservation programs; and (12) a cross-standard compliance comparison matrix covering NOP, EU 2018/848, Naturland, and JAS. Version 2.0 includes comparative compliance tables and expanded cross-system compliance scenarios.

The intended audiences are U.S. organic producers planning first-time EU export or expanding existing channels; USDA-accredited certifying agents developing cross-standard competence; and cooperative managers coordinating compliance across multiple member operations.

Version 2.0 released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Companion DOI-registered version: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19722689

title: Organizational AI Discernment: The Missing Capability for AI Value Capture in Abundance Environments

detail.title: Organizational AI Discernment: The Missing Capability for AI Value Capture in Abundance Environments
detail.abstract: Organizations investing the most in artificial intelligence paradoxically can capture the least value per dollar spent. This paper introduces Organizational AI Discernment (OAD) as a new strategic capability required when technological abundance inverts traditional competitive constraints from resource acquisition to strategic evaluation. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory, absorptive capacity, and attention economy literature, this research argues that existing capability frameworks were built for scarcity environments and are insufficient when AI options, demos, and prototypes are effectively unlimited. OAD is conceptualized through three pillars: Signal Detection, Contextual Judgment, and Selection Discipline. A sequential mixed-methods research design is proposed to validate OAD as a distinct construct and test its moderating role in the relationship between AI investment and value capture. This research contributes a new theoretical construct, a diagnostic framework for practitioners, and a resolution to the AI investment paradox. It demonstrates that discernment infrastructure can determine AI value creation outcomes in abundance environments.

title: Substance Over Form: How Big Tech Licensing Agreements Are Acquisitions in Disguise.

detail.title: Substance Over Form: How Big Tech Licensing Agreements Are Acquisitions in Disguise.
detail.abstract: Between March 2024 and December 2025, four of the most powerful technology companies in the world spent approximately $24 billion acquiring their competitors. None of them called it that. Microsoft, Amazon, Google, and Nvidia each structured their transactions as non-exclusive licensing agreements combined with mass hiring events, preserving the legal independence of each target while absorbing its founding team, its core technology, and the competitive threat it represented. The law, built around the premise that acquisitions involve equity transfers, found nothing to review. This paper identifies these transactions as a structurally distinct and previously unexamined phenomenon, the reverse acqui-hire, and argues that the collective failure to regulate them stems from three compounding problems: existing valuation frameworks cannot fairly price deals that bundle intellectual property, human capital, and competitive foreclosure value into a single consideration that no party is required to disaggregate; the Hart-Scott-Rodino notification framework is architecturally blind to transactions that achieve acquisition-like outcomes without an equity transfer; and the failure of five regulatory authorities across three jurisdictions to exercise enforcement authority over any of these deals reflects not insufficient effort but a fundamental mismatch between the design of existing law and the structure of the transactions it failed to see. This paper proposes a framework grounded in the principle of substance over form, under which the economic character of a transaction, not its contractual label, determines its regulatory classification.

title: Interest Free Treasury Cash: The Treasury General Account's Foregone Interest

detail.title: Interest Free Treasury Cash: The Treasury General Account's Foregone Interest

keywords: Comparative or Joint Analysis of Fiscal and Monetary Policy/Stabilization
Financial Institutions and Services: Government Policy and Regulation

detail.abstract: The U.S. Treasury holds hundreds of billions of dollars in the Treasury General Account (TGA), a zero interest account at the Federal Reserve, while overnight rates remain well above zero. Since March 2022, that design choice has left $106.2 billion in nominal foregone interest on the table ($114.9 billion on a compound basis), using the Overnight Reverse Repurchase Agreement (ON RRP) rate as a conservative benchmark. An accounting identity derived from the U.S. Treasury and the Fed's joint accounting shows that every dollar of foregone interest either increases the Fed's remittances or reduces deferred asset accumulation. If the TGA were remunerated, the additional interest expense would have reduced Fed remittances by $16.8 billion and increased the deferred asset by $89.4 billion since March 2022. Conditional on an eventual Fed recovery, the Treasury's net present value cost is approximately zero, as foregone interest increases the Fed's net income. Instead, the primary impacts are on the timing of flows between the two institutions and reported Fed losses and government deficits. Projections for foregone interest from March 2026 through September 2035 add $377.4 billion under current rate expectations. The paper also considers policy alternatives to a zero rate TGA, and how other nations manage remuneration. The U.S. is the only major sovereign that holds an economically large, unremunerated balance.

title: Pyramids, Diamonds, and Oscillations: AI and the Structure of Internal Labor Markets
affiliations: Goethe University Frankfurt, HKU Business School, The University of Hong Kong, Faculty of Business and Economics, The University of Hong Kong,  and Goethe University Frankfurt

detail.title: Pyramids, Diamonds, and Oscillations: AI and the Structure of Internal Labor Markets
detail.abstract: AI is changing workplaces: it leads to higher individual productivity and faster learning. We model the effects of these changes on internal labor markets. We show that for productivity shocks, firms preserve the span in the long run: a pyramid remains a pyramid. In the short run, however, firms freeze junior hiring, temporarily transforming the pyramid toward a diamond. In the transition to the new steady state, firms may oscillate between pyramids and diamonds before settling. For learning shocks, the long-run span falls, potentially permanently shifting the firm from a pyramid to a diamond. These fluctuations create inequality between junior cohorts and affect firm value when human capital is firm-specific.

title: Bouwen wij economieën die ons ondermijnen? Een relationeel-ecologische herconceptualisering van economie als materiële infrastructuur van menswording en de institutionele voorwaarde voor duurzame ontwikkelingsruimte

detail.title: Bouwen wij economieën die ons ondermijnen? Een relationeel-ecologische herconceptualisering van economie als materiële infrastructuur van menswording en de institutionele voorwaarde voor duurzame ontwikkelingsruimte
detail.abstract:
Dit werk ontwikkelt een interdisciplinair kader waarin economie wordt begrepen als de materiële infrastructuur van menswording. In tegenstelling tot gangbare benaderingen die economie primair conceptualiseren als een autonoom domein van markten, groei en efficiëntie, wordt betoogd dat economische processen fundamenteel ingebed zijn in sociale, institutionele en ecologische structuren. Economie wordt daarmee hergedefinieerd als een relationeel en ecologisch proces van georganiseerde interdependentie, waarin de voorwaarden voor menselijke ontwikkeling worden geproduceerd, verdeeld en gereproduceerd.

Vertrekkend vanuit een relationeel-procesmatig mensbeeld analyseert het werk hoe economische ordening de toegang tot bestaanszekerheid, ontwikkelingsruimte en sociale stabiliteit structureert. Daarbij wordt aangetoond dat markten weliswaar belangrijke coördinatiemechanismen vormen, maar tegelijkertijd inherente beperkingen kennen, waaronder externaliteiten, machtsconcentratie en distributieve blindheid. Deze beperkingen impliceren dat economische uitkomsten niet louter het resultaat zijn van individuele keuzes, maar in hoge mate worden gevormd door institutionele kaders en machtsverhoudingen.

Het werk integreert inzichten uit de ecologische economie om te laten zien dat economische activiteit onlosmakelijk verbonden is met de biosfeer. Productie en consumptie worden opgevat als materiële doorstroomsystemen van energie en grondstoffen die afhankelijk zijn van de regeneratieve capaciteit van natuurlijke systemen. Dit leidt tot een kritische herbeoordeling van economische groei: groei wordt niet langer beschouwd als doel op zichzelf, maar als instrument dat slechts normatief gerechtvaardigd is voor zover zij bijdraagt aan de reproductie van sociale en ecologische voorwaarden voor menselijke ontwikkeling.

Daarnaast wordt aandacht besteed aan macro-economische dynamiek, mondiale interdependentie en digitalisering. Het werk laat zien hoe mondiale productieketens, financiële systemen en digitale infrastructuren nieuwe vormen van afhankelijkheid en machtsconcentratie creëren, die nationale instituties overstijgen en vragen om vormen van governance op meerdere schaalniveaus. In dit verband wordt het spanningsveld tussen schaal, legitimiteit en machtsasymmetrie in mondiale governance geanalyseerd.

De centrale bijdrage van dit werk ligt in de ontwikkeling van een normatief-analytisch kader waarin economische ordening wordt beoordeeld op haar vermogen om duurzame ontwikkelingsruimte te waarborgen. Deze ontwikkelingsruimte wordt opgevat als de samenhang tussen bestaanszekerheid, gelijkwaardigheid, autonomie en ecologische begrenzing. Het werk concludeert dat economie slechts duurzaam kan functioneren wanneer zij wordt ingericht als een corrigeerbaar systeem van wederzijdse afhankelijkheid, waarin institutionele structuren in staat zijn om externe effecten te internaliseren, machtsconcentratie te begrenzen en sociale en ecologische stabiliteit te ondersteunen.

Daarmee biedt het werk een alternatieve benadering van economische analyse, waarin economie niet wordt losgekoppeld van samenleving en natuur, maar wordt begrepen als een integraal onderdeel van de voorwaarden waaronder menselijke ontwikkeling mogelijk is.

detail.title:
DO CRYPTOCURRENCIES PRICE HAVE STRONG LONG TERM
RELATIONSHIP?
detail.abstract: This paper unearthed the long-term nexus among the most popular seven cryptocurrencies viz.-Ethereum, Bitcoin, Dogecoin, Cardano, Binance Coin, Tether, Ripple. The objective of the research was to study the long term relationship among various cryptocurrencies. The Autoregressive Distributed Lag and vector error correction model cointegration technique has been used to investigate this nexus between these cryptos. The research was based on five-year data collected between April, 2018 and 2023. The outcome revealed that there was a long-term relationship between cryptocurrencies. There have been three cointegrating relationships in our system. The direction for future studies would be to investigate the relationship with other financial avenues like stocks, mutual funds, gold, foreign exchange, etc.

title: The Patent Trap A Historical and Formal Analysis of Why the Patent System Fails Its Inventors

detail.title: The Patent Trap A Historical and Formal Analysis of Why the Patent System Fails Its Inventors
detail.abstract: This paper advances a historical and formal argument that the contemporary patent system does not, in general, help the inventor who creates the invention it is asked to protect. The argument is framed in terms of the Patent Trap: three interlocking structural constraintspre-filing solvency, maintenance solvency, and enforcement capacity-that together determine whether a given inventor can extract positive expected value from a granted patent. Eight historical case studies spanning 1871-2018 (Swan, Baird, Whittle, Flowers, Baylis; Meucci, the Wright Brothers, Farnsworth) motivate the analysis, which is then formalised. The Wealth Ceiling Theorem (Proposition 1) shows that for any inventor whose working capital falls below a critical threshold W*, expected net value from patent pursuit is bounded above, and for sufficiently low wealth is strictly negative, regardless of the gross commercial value of the invention. Two corollaries follow: on the monotonicity of the wealth ceiling in invention value, and on the resulting selection bias in commercialised inventions. An empirical calibration with parameters drawn from Walsh-Lee-Jung and Cohen-Nelson-Walsh demonstrates that for a UK individual inventor filing in three jurisdictions via investor-disclosure-financed capital, no finite invention value produces a positive expected return. The paper closes by specifying a four-condition financing architecture capable of neutralising the trap using existing financial and legal instruments.

title: Financial Liberalizations, Booms, and Crashes
affiliations: , Kiel Institute for the World Economy /Sciences Po Paris and Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Sloan School of Management

detail.title: Financial Liberalizations, Booms, and Crashes

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The views expressed here are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect the views of the Federal Reserve Board or the Federal Reserve System.

detail.abstract: Financial liberalization is often seen as a way to deepen credit markets and stimulate economic growth, but it may also fuel credit booms that end in crisis. We construct a new cross-country database of banking regulation policies covering 21 regulatory indicators for 18 advanced economies since World War II. We distinguish liberalizations that directly relax constraints on credit supply from broader financial reforms. Liberalizations that directly affect credit supply lead to substantial expansions in private credit. Credit expansion is concentrated in non-tradable sectors and is not accompanied by higher interest rates or credit spreads in the short run, consistent with an outward shift in credit supply. Real GDP rises over the following 2 to 4 years, but the gains are temporary. On average, GDP returns to trend in the medium run, and there is an increase in the risk of financial crisis and worse downside growth outcomes. Only liberalizations that directly expand credit supply generate these boom-bust dynamics. Based on these estimates, financial liberalization is welfare-improving for coefficients of relative risk aversion below 7.2, a moderately high value.

title: El diseño gráfico como estrategia de marketing sensorial y emocional en entornos educativos digitales: un estudio empírico sobre su impacto en la percepción y la intención de matrícula Diseñadora gráfica y especialista en Mercadeo

detail.title: El diseño gráfico como estrategia de marketing sensorial y emocional en entornos educativos digitales: un estudio empírico sobre su impacto en la percepción y la intención de matrícula Diseñadora gráfica y especialista en Mercadeo
detail.abstract: En el contexto de la creciente digitalización del sector educativo, las instituciones enfrentan el desafío de diferenciarse en entornos altamente competitivos. Este estudio analiza el impacto del diseño gráfico como herramienta de marketing sensorial y emocional en la percepción y la intención de matrícula de estudiantes potenciales. Se adopta un enfoque metodológico mixto con alcance descriptivo-correlacional, combinando un estudio de caso con un análisis cuantitativo basado en encuestas estructuradas aplicadas a 120 participantes. Los resultados evidencian una relación significativa entre los estímulos visuales, las respuestas emocionales y la intención de inscripción. Se concluye que el diseño gráfico estratégico influye de manera directa e indirecta en la toma de decisiones, consolidándose como un factor clave en el marketing educativo digital.

title: The Declaration of Independence as Kindling the American Culture of Reason-Giving

detail.title: The Declaration of Independence as Kindling the American Culture of Reason-Giving

publicationDetails.detailsText: Harvard Journal of Law & Public Policy Per Curiam (April 2026)
George Mason Legal Studies Research Paper No. LS No. 26-10
publicationDetails.journalName: Antonin Scalia Law School, George Mason University Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: As we search for the roots of the reason giving culture in American law and politics, it is important to examine the Nation’s birth certificate. The Declaration of Independence celebrates its semiquincentennial in 2026. Across 250 years, the study of the Declaration and its impact have, of course, been extensive. There is, however, a lesson to be drawn from the Declaration of Independence that has been underexplored: It was an exercise and exemplar of “reason giving,” arguably solidifying by example a custom and culture of reason giving in American law and politics. This Essay articulates the reasons why the Declaration of Independence should be credited with helping to firmly establish that culture and custom, and it explains the practical utility and legitimacy functions of reason giving against the backdrop of the very purposeful and direct appeal to reason giving in the Declaration—a design feature of the document to add to the legitimacy of the Founders’ claim to independence.

detail.abstract: This paper unearthed the long-term nexus among the most popular seven cryptocurrencies viz.-Ethereum, Bitcoin, Dogecoin, Cardano, Binance Coin, Tether, Ripple. The objective of the research was to study the long term relationship among various cryptocurrencies. The Autoregressive Distributed Lag and vector error correction model cointegration technique has been used to investigate this nexus between these cryptos. title: Privacy-Preserving Shelf-Edge Feedback Telemetry in Perfumery Retail: Planogram-Locked Voice-to-Tag Aggregates and Their Relationship to Sales

detail.title: Privacy-Preserving Shelf-Edge Feedback Telemetry in Perfumery Retail: Planogram-Locked Voice-to-Tag Aggregates and Their Relationship to Sales

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no potential conflicts of interest with respect to the research, authorship, and/or publication of this article.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Retail brands often lack timely, shelf-level feedback signals reflecting consumers' immediate reactions to products at the point of consideration. We develop a privacy-preserving shelf-edge telemetry system that converts ambient in-store speech into non-reconstructable semantic tags (e.g., "too sweet", "too strong", "freshness positive") using on-device keyword spotting and semantic normalization. The system is planogram-locked to a specific branded shelf segment and transmits only thresholded aggregate counts (k-threshold buckets) per time window. By design, the device stores no audio and retains no transcripts; only aggregates leave the shelf. We outline a field evaluation in perfumery retail across four stores and 28 branded shelves with linked daily sales. The empirical strategy uses shelf fixed effects, store-by-time controls, and promotion and price covariates to estimate associations and short-horizon predictive relationships between tag dynamics and sales outcomes. We also specify validation procedures for detection performance and sensitivity analyses over k to quantify privacy-utility trade-offs. The work contributes (i) a practical privacy-by-design architecture for real-time consumer insight in physical retail, (ii) a planogram-locking mechanism that improves attribution without identity tracking, and (iii) a replicable analytic template for linking non-identifying semantic telemetry to commercial outcomes in stores.

title: FINANCIAL-STRUCTURAL VULNERABILITY: How Private Equity Ownership Architecture Produces Consumer Harm in Essential Services

detail.title: FINANCIAL-STRUCTURAL VULNERABILITY: How Private Equity Ownership Architecture Produces Consumer Harm in Essential Services
detail.abstract: Consumer Culture Theory's existing vulnerability frameworks identify situational, environmental, and individual conditions as sources of consumer vulnerability but have not theorized how a provider's financial ownership architecture produces vulnerability in consumers before any individual market encounter. Drawing on Baker, Gentry, and Rittenburg's (2005) foundational vulnerability framework and Arnould and Thompson's (2005) Consumer Culture Theory, this paper proposes financial-structural vulnerability as a fourth condition type: vulnerability produced by the financial ownership architecture of the service provider, specifically through three mechanisms-lock-in amplification, invisible actor asymmetry, and compliance cost compression. We develop this construct through an empirical analysis of the U.S. portable moving and storage sector, comparing eight operators across ownership types (private equity-backed, pension-owned, founder-owned, and public company). Consumer satisfaction data across 8 operators reveals a consistent and substantial gap: PE-backed operators cluster at 1.4-2.1 on Trustpilot's 5-point scale while non-PE operators cluster at 4.3-4.8, a mean difference of 2.77 points across a combined review base of approximately 13,000 consumers. Safety quality data from the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration shows that the primary PE-backed operator exhibits a vehicle out-FINANCIAL-STRUCTURAL VULNERABILITY 2 of-service rate of 18.4%, compared to 8.2% for the pension-owned comparatormore than double. Critically, we show that leverage intensity alone does not predict these outcomes; the pension-owned comparator carries 7.17x net leverage yet maintains superior consumer outcomes, indicating that the mechanism is the specific incentive architecture of PIK preferred equity compounding rather than debt level per se. The paper extends CCT's vulnerability theory to the provider-side financial architecture and offers implications for marketplace regulation in financialized essential services.

title: A Deep Learning Approach to Heterogeneous Consumer Aesthetics in Fast Fashion
affiliations: Georgetown University - Department of Economics, Students

detail.title: A Deep Learning Approach to Heterogeneous Consumer Aesthetics in Fast Fashion
detail.abstract: Aesthetics drives product differentiation in industries such as fashion, interior decor, luxury goods, real estate and hospitality. However, visual differentiation is hard to encode in formal economic analysis. This paper develops a methodology to parse, process and model the aesthetic dimension and applies it to fast fashion. It works with millions of purchase records from H&M in the Netherlands, including product images, text descriptions, prices, and consumer demographics. I fine-tune Fashion CLIP embeddings with a three-tower approach that builds separate channels for product visuals and text, consumer history, and price, which makes downstream analysis tractable and scalable. The embeddings feed a latent-class deep demand system that captures price and taste sensitivities through deep nets, recovers rich substitution patterns, reveals meaningful heterogeneity, and performs much better than competing alternatives. Then, a supply-side inversion recovers sensible markups and costs and supports conduct tests and counterfactuals on sustainability practices. I also estimate machine learning hedonic pricing models that perform much better than competing alternatives. This model allows us to construct quality-adjusted price indices, make it possible to price completely new designs, and with an Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition reveal the underlying sources of price changes. Finally, a Poisson event study around the COVID-19 lockdown shows that the range of demand responses across embedding-based product and user clusters exceeds anything recoverable from simple text-based attributes or demographic labels alone. All these findings show that high-dimensional embeddings can be first class citizens in disciplined economic and statistical analysis. The methodology is portable to any market where products are differentiated along sensory dimensions that are hard to encode but meaningfully important for consumer choices.

title: A Design-Stage Diagnostic for Public Digital Investment

detail.title: A Design-Stage Diagnostic for Public Digital Investment
detail.abstract:
Governments now commit well over half a trillion US dollars a year to digital‑government and public‑sector ICT systems, yet similar technologies and budgets often produce sharply divergent trajectories: some initiatives consolidate into resilient, widely used services, while others stall, generate new risks or end in costly remediation. Conventional value‑for‑money (VfM) tools in public finance and audit—cost–benefit analysis, options appraisal, performance monitoring and ex post VfM studies—relate spending to outputs and outcomes, but offer limited visibility into whether a programme's design‑stage architecture makes those expectations plausible or likely to command sustained satisfaction and trust from citizens and front‑line staff. Building on target‑costing and whole‑life‑costing practice in construction and public investment, this paper argues that most cost and value in digital‑government portfolios are effectively committed at the design stage, and that VfM assessment must therefore engage explicitly with design‑stage capability configuration.

It introduces the Adaptive Digital Governance (AMDG) framework, a design‑stage diagnostic for public digital investment and VfM that profiles reforms along three dimensions—digital‑systems maturity, participatory‑learning capacity and resilience under stress—and compares these configurations to an empirically derived library of 111 digital‑government initiatives across 32 countries. The analysis applies AMDG in three steps: scoring and archetyping the 111 reforms, mapping their capability configurations, and constructing a structured review subset to examine whether high‑ and low‑scoring cases within the same archetype and domain display the expected governance and trajectory contrasts. It shows that infrastructure‑heavy configurations with weak learning and resilience capacities are systematically associated with more fragile, cost‑unstable and citizen‑dissatisfying trajectories than hybrid configurations that combine strong digital infrastructures with robust participatory and resilience capabilities, conditional on context. For finance ministries, treasuries, supreme audit institutions, sponsoring line ministries and donors, AMDG offers a practical, reproducible design‑stage diagnostic for bringing governance capabilities into ex ante screening, portfolio‑level risk mapping and piloted collaborations to safeguard value for money and governance quality in digital‑government investment.

title: Beyond the Commons Toward a Digital Common Heritage of Mankind Framework Algorithmic Enclosure of the Cognitive Commons and the Nagoya Analogy

detail.title: Beyond the Commons Toward a Digital Common Heritage of Mankind Framework Algorithmic Enclosure of the Cognitive Commons and the Nagoya Analogy

detail.abstract: The training of large generative models on the accumulated cultural, linguistic and intellectual output of humanity has been analysed, in the dominant Anglo-American and European legal debates, principally through the lens of copyright doctrine-fair use, transformative use, text and data mining exceptions. This article argues that copyright is the wrong instrument, operating at the wrong scale, for a structural transformation that exceeds it. What is occurring is not a succession of infringements of authors' rights but an algorithmic enclosure of the cognitive commons: the privatisation, through the monopolisation of computational capacity to extract latent value, of an intergenerational heritage produced collectively by humanity over millennia. The article develops a framework-the Digital Common Heritage of Mankind (DCHM)-that re-situates the question within the international law regime of the common heritage of mankind and within the access and benefit-sharing regime of the 2010 Nagoya Protocol. The Nagoya analogy is exact: pharmaceutical extraction of genetic resources and traditional knowledge from the Global South was met, in international law, with a binding regime requiring prior informed consent and equitable benefit-sharing. Generative AI extraction of the world's linguistic, cultural and intellectual heritage has been met, thus far, with no equivalent regime. The article proposes such a regime, grounded in four international legal instruments, enriched by analytical concepts drawn from Islamic jurisprudence on the waqf and the common resource (mushaʿ), articulated through the Indigenous Data Sovereignty literature on OCAP and CARE principles, and translated into an operational three-layer architecture spanning international governance, Indigenous data sovereignty, and national sovereign data licensing. The broader theoretical horizon is the shift from intellectual property as a framework protecting individual and corporate interests to cognitive sovereignty as a framework protecting the collective heritage of humanity.

detail.abstract: Retail analytics has shifted from back-office reporting toward continuous sensing of the customer journey in physical spaces (Roggeveen & Sethuraman, 2020). Yet firms still struggle to obtain timely, shelf-level indicators of consumer experience that are both operationally actionable and socially acceptable. In many categories especially perfumery purchase intent is shaped by immediate sensory impressions and by verbal descriptions exchanged between shoppers and advisors. Shoppers often articulate attributes (“too sweet,” “too strong,” “smells cheap,” “more fresh”) and usage contexts (“office,” “night out,” “gift”) at the shelf. Brands, however, typically learn about such perceptions through lagging channels: sales patterns, post-purchase surveys, returns, and online reviews. These channels can be delayed, biased toward vocal minorities, and poorly linked to specific in-store contexts.

title: Fashion Consumption among Women Aged 40 to 60: Behavior and Style Perspectives
affiliations: Universidade Regional de Blumenau, Universidade Regional de Blumenau and

detail.title: Fashion Consumption among Women Aged 40 to 60: Behavior and Style Perspectives
detail.abstract: The objective of this study is to analyze the factors that influence clothing consumption among aging women, aged between 40 and 60 years, as well as to understand the profile of B1-class women in this age group within the fashion market, based on the reality of Blumenau, Santa Catarina, Brazil. The research also seeks to relate the aging process to elements that impact the clothing preferences and needs of these consumers, in addition to examining the role of media in shaping and influencing their choices. This is a qualitative, descriptive study. Thirteen interviews were conducted with B1-class women, aged 40 to 60, residing in Blumenau. The main results indicate that bodily and psychological changes associated with aging and menopause directly affect their clothing choices, with a preference for garments that, in addition to offering comfort and aesthetics, help conceal certain body areas. Although they value fashion as a tool for self-esteem and social inclusion, most report difficulties in finding products that fully meet their needs and desires. The participants also express dissatisfaction with the underrepresentation of their age group in the media, highlighting the need for a more inclusive and realistic approach in the fashion market.

title: JAOGS™ v1.0 — Justice Automated Operational Governance Standard (Core)
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Indiana University, Indianapolis - Indiana University Indianapolis

detail.title: JAOGS™ v1.0 — Justice Automated Operational Governance Standard (Core)

keywords: Execution-Layer Governance Decision Observability Human-AI Interaction AI Governance Justice Systems Decision Traceability Institutional Decision-Making

detail.abstract:
JAOGS™ v1.0 (Justice Automated Operational Governance Standard) establishes a foundational governance standard for execution-layer decision environments in AI-supported justice systems.

While existing frameworks emphasize system performance, model accuracy, and algorithmic bias, JAOGS™ addresses a distinct and underexamined domain: how human decision-makers interpret and act upon system-generated outputs in real-world operational contexts.

This paper introduces the concept of the Decision Visibility Gap the unstructured and largely undocumented space between system-generated signals and institutional outcomes. Within this space, human judgment, discretion, and contextual conditions determine how decisions are formed and executed.

JAOGS™ defines the requirements, structural components, and alignment criteria necessary to document, trace, reconstruct, and evaluate decision-making processes at the execution layer. The standard provides a formal framework for making decision environments observable, accountable, and defensible without evaluating underlying system performance.

This work contributes a new governance paradigm for AI-supported justice systems, with implications for corrections, courts, supervision, and monitoring environments.

title: Workforce Management Inefficiency in U.S. Food and Agricultural Enterprises: The Hidden Cost Problem and a Proven ERP Implementation Framework

detail.title: Workforce Management Inefficiency in U.S. Food and Agricultural Enterprises: The Hidden Cost Problem and a Proven ERP Implementation Framework
detail.abstract: The U.S. food and agricultural sector faces a structural workforce management crisis that receives little systematic attention: the administrative inefficiency generated by fragmented, siloed human resources and payroll systems accumulated through decades of mergers, acquisitions, and organizational growth. With total U.S. agricultural labor expenses forecast at over $53 billion in 2025 (American Farm Bureau Federation, 2025), and with fruit and vegetable producers spending up to 40% of their total production expenses on labor alone (AFBF, 2025), the cost of managing that labor pool inefficiently represents a significant and addressable drag on sector productivity. This paper documents the scope of the problem, identifies its structural drivers-including the post-M&A fragmentation of HR systems, the administrative complexity of H-2A seasonal worker compliance, and the absence of integrated workforce management technology in a significant portion of mid-to-large agricultural enterprises-and presents a validated implementation framework based on the author's direct experience deploying ERP-integrated workforce management systems in agricultural chemical manufacturing. The paper concludes with a proposed application of this framework to U.S. food and agricultural enterprises and a model for measuring return on implementation investment.

title: WHEN EVALUATION BECOMES ILLEGITIMATE -A TYPOLOGY OF ENTITLEMENT FAILURES IN SOCIO-TECHNICAL SYSTEMS

detail.title: WHEN EVALUATION BECOMES ILLEGITIMATE -A TYPOLOGY OF ENTITLEMENT FAILURES IN SOCIO-TECHNICAL SYSTEMS

detail.abstract: Evaluation systems are foundational to socio-technical environments, yet they rely on a largely unexamined assumption: that evaluation inputs are inherently legitimate. This paper challenges this assumption by theorizing evaluative entitlement-the condition under which an actor is justified in evaluating a target within a specific domain. Rather than treating illegitimacy as a binary condition, the paper conceptualizes it as a structured space of failure modes with distinct system-level consequences. It develops a typology of three qualitatively distinct forms of entitlement failure: over-entitlement (authority without epistemic grounding), under-entitlement (epistemic grounding without authority), and mis-entitlement (authority and access applied outside legitimate domain). Each failure mode arises from a different configuration of evaluative authority, epistemic access, and domain alignment, and each produces a distinct form of signal distortion: noise inflation, signal omission, and signal inconsistency. The analysis reveals structural asymmetries: over-entitlement is visible and relatively corrigible, under-entitlement is invisible and harder to detect, and mis-entitlement is partially visible but most difficult to diagnose. A set of testable propositions are derived to guide empirical research across peer review, recruitment, platform rating, and AI-mediated evaluation systems. The paper shifts the focus of evaluation research from how inputs are processed to whether they should be admitted at all.

title: “The Role of AI Expert Systems and Robotics in Library Operations and development: a Comprehensive Analysis of Technological Integration in Modern Library Services.”

detail.abstract: This research examines the transformative impact of artificial intelligence expert systems and robotics on contemporary library operations. The study investigates how these technologies enhance service delivery, operational efficiency, and user experience in modern library environments. Through analysis of secondary data from recent implementations and case studies, this research identifies key applications including automated cataloguing, intelligent resource recommendation systems, robotic book handling, and AI-driven user support services. The findings reveal significant improvements in operational efficiency, with automated systems reducing cataloguing time by up to 60% and robotic shelving systems increasing accuracy rates to 99.2%. Expert systems demonstrate particular effectiveness in providing personalized recommendations and specialized research assistance, while robotics revolutionize physical collection management through RFID-enabled sorting and shelving processes. The research concludes that strategic integration of AI expert systems and robotics creates substantial value for library operations, though implementation requires careful consideration of staff training, infrastructure costs, and user acceptance factors. These technologies represent a paradigm shift toward intelligent, automated library services that enhance both operational capacity and user satisfaction while preserving the essential human elements of library science.

title: Strengthening Cybersecurity in Digital Oilfields: A Real-Time Risk Intelligence Framework for Protecting Critical Energy Infrastructure

detail.title: Strengthening Cybersecurity in Digital Oilfields: A Real-Time Risk Intelligence Framework for Protecting Critical Energy Infrastructure
detail.abstract: Oilfield digitalization has increased cybersecurity and operational risks as more systems rely on interconnection, real-time data acquisition, and industrial control technologies (Kumar et al. 2020; Humayed et al. 2017). Even with these advances, many digital oilfield environments remain devoid of comprehensive frameworks that combine cybersecurity awareness with real-time operational monitoring and decision-making capabilities. This paper introduces a real-time cybersecurity and risk intelligence framework designed to increase threat visibility, assist in anomaly detection, and facilitate better decision-making in digital oilfield systems. This framework unifies cybersecurity principles with operational workflows to allow continuous monitoring and structured risk interpretation. This approach is informed by real operational conditions and designed for deployment within live oilfield environments, supporting both field monitoring and executive-level decision processes. The framework offers a scalable model to strengthen cybersecurity resilience across critical energy infrastructure systems with further applications to digitally enabled industrial environments.

title: The Capital Governance Report: Structural Economic Misalignment in Legal Acquisition Systems

detail.title: The Capital Governance Report: Structural Economic Misalignment in Legal Acquisition Systems

The concepts described in this paper are based on independent structural analysis and applied research conducted across legal acquisition architectures. detail.abstract:
This paper analyzes structural economic misalignment in digital acquisition systems within professional service firms, with a focus on legal markets. It identifies a systematic disconnect between capital allocation and economic outcome, caused by the absence of mandate-level feedback within acquisition architectures.

While prevailing performance metrics — including cost per lead, conversion volume, and click-through rates — provide continuous operational visibility, they do not capture the relationship between capital deployed and mandate value realized. As a result, optimization systems converge toward activity-based signals rather than economic outcomes, producing increasing efficiency within a structurally incomplete objective function.

The analysis introduces two core concepts. The Activity-Signal Fallacy describes the assumption that observable activity metrics constitute valid proxies for economic outcome. Economic Leakage defines the continuous structural outflow of capital toward activity lacking verified linkage to realized mandate value.

The paper further examines the signal-chain architecture underlying legal acquisition systems and identifies the structural break between acquisition events and economic outcome data. It outlines the conditions required to establish a closed-loop system in which verified economic outcome is captured, structured, and returned to the allocation system.

The findings suggest that, in the absence of such infrastructure, professional service firms operate capital allocation systems that optimize for activity efficiency rather than capital efficiency, resulting in compounding misalignment over time.

title: NexVote -100% Direct Democracy through Informatics and AI

detail.title: NexVote -100% Direct Democracy through Informatics and AI
detail.abstract: In today's scenario, citizens are highly connected digitally but policy participation is still mostly indirect. NexVote is a civic technology platform built as a final-year engineering project to support direct, transparent, and discussion-driven community decision making. This paper presents the implemented architecture of NexVote: Angular 17 frontend, Node.js and Express backend, PostgreSQL with Knex migrations, a FastAPI AI microservice, and Solidity smart contracts on Ethereum Sepolia through a relayer model. The platform supports community creation, member-based proposal lifecycle, multilingual content assistance, AI summarization, semantic similarity checks, secure vote capture, quorum-aware finalization, and on-chain audit hashing. The paper also discusses trade-offs around privacy, moderation quality, and legal-operational constraints. Our contribution is an original and implementable reference design showing how informatics and AI can improve civic clarity, process integrity, and trust in digital governance participation.
