detail.abstract: In today's digital economy, mobile subscriber identifiers have transformed from a simple means of communication into a fundamental means of accessing digital assets. Nonetheless, in the current SIM card recycling life cycle, a system vulnerability, known as the "Residual Linkage" issue, arises when a mobile number is reassigned without de-linking it from the original user's financial and identity-related assets, leading to identity theft and financial fraud. This paper presents a de-linking framework, proposed as "Clean Slate Protocol, (also referred to as the Secure Mobile Identity Migration or SMIM framework), which uses the National Identity infrastructure for de-linking these assets. This model will ensure a synchronised state between Telecommunication Service Providers (TSPs) and Financial Institutions, thereby securing the digital identity lifecycle and respecting the "Right to be Forgotten" as enshrined in law.

title: Bans Without Control: India's Internet Paradox Why restricting websites has not reduced access and what it reveals about demand in a digital society

detail.title: Bans Without Control: India's Internet Paradox Why restricting websites has not reduced access and what it reveals about demand in a digital society
detail.abstract: This article examines the limits of website-blocking as a strategy of digital regulation in India. It argues that repeated restrictions on pornographic websites have not substantially reduced access, as users continue to rely on alternative domains, mirror sites, and indirect channels. The persistence of access despite regulation reveals a contradiction between formal control and practical outcomes. Drawing on patterns of online behavior, regional trends, and the role of low-cost internet, the article suggests that demand, rather than technical access alone, drives continued consumption. It further highlights how limited sex education, social stigma, and digital expansion shape this phenomenon. The article contends that a restriction-based approach, without addressing underlying social and educational factors, has limited effectiveness. It concludes that India’s experience reflects broader challenges of digital governance, where controlling access does not necessarily resolve the demand that sustains it. A more comprehensive approach combining regulation, education, and awareness is therefore needed.

title: Engage or Fade Away: Disciplinary Disparities in AI Research Across Business Schools

detail.title: Engage or Fade Away: Disciplinary Disparities in AI Research Across Business Schools

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None to declare.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This bibliometric study is a secondary analysis of research abstracts. IRB approval was not deemed necessary for this study
declarations.funderStatement: This research was not sponsored by a funding agency.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence threatens to transform, or displace, business disciplines that fail to engage with this paradigm shift. Using bibliometric analysis of 1,461,524 articles from 2,064 ABDC-ranked journals (2014-2025), we examine AI research engagement across seven business disciplines and document striking disparities: MIS demonstrates substantial engagement (27.2%) while Economics (3.6%), Accounting (4.3%), and Management (4.8%) show minimal integration despite significant automation exposure. Beyond measuring whether disciplines engage with AI, we introduce a novel two-dimensional embedding framework that distinguishes technical AI proximity from disciplinary integration. This analysis reveals critical nuance: while MIS leads in AI research quantity and technical sophistication, Finance leads in disciplinary integration (28.8% vs. 18.9% in the "Integrated AI" quadrant). Over half of MIS's AI research (53.2%) applies foundational AI methods, technically sophisticated but disconnected from traditional MIS concerns such as information systems design, user behavior, and organizational IT management. Accounting (78.1%) and Marketing (72.7%) primarily study AI as phenomenon rather than adopting it as methodology. Drawing on absorptive capacity theory, we theorize these patterns as potentially persistent rather than self-correcting. We introduce the shaper-consumer bifurcation, where disciplines below an engagement threshold are relegated to using AI tools designed without their expertise. All findings withstood eight robustness checks across journal tiers, geographic subsamples, and temporal specifications.

title: The Prestige-Innovation Mismatch: How Business School Rankings Obscure AI Research Leadership

detail.title: The Prestige-Innovation Mismatch: How Business School Rankings Obscure AI Research Leadership

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None to declare.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This bibliometric study is a secondary analysis of research abstracts. IRB approval was not deemed necessary for this study.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was not sponsored by a funding agency.

detail.abstract: Business school deans face an uncomfortable reality: the rankings that shape hiring decisions, resource allocation, and strategic positioning may be systematically blind to AI research leadership, the very capability that will define competitive advantage in the coming decade. Drawing on bibliometric analysis of 1.46 million articles (see Supplement A for full methodology) across 2,064 business journals (2014-2025), I construct an AI Leadership Index (AILI) measuring institutional research output, quality, technical sophistication, and citation impact. The findings reveal a striking prestige-innovation mismatch: of the top 20 institutions by AILI, only 4 appear in the UTD Top 100 Business School Research Rankings. Chinese technical universities dominate AI research leadership while remaining invisible to Western prestige systems. Critically, a sensitivity analysis examining departmental attribution reveals that only 15.7% of Core AI articles in business journals are confirmed to originate from business school departments, raising fundamental questions about what institutional rankings actually measure. I develop two theoretical frameworks, certification lag and pipeline absorptive capacity, explaining why evaluation systems optimized for stability become decoupled from fast-cycle innovation domains. The implications extend beyond academic positioning to doctoral training, faculty hiring, and the future of business education itself.

title: Generative AI in Higher Education: Academic Authorship, Validity, and the Transformation of Assessment

detail.title: Generative AI in Higher Education: Academic Authorship, Validity, and the Transformation of Assessment
detail.abstract:
This paper analyses how generative artificial intelligence is reshaping the requirements of academic authorship in higher education and explores the implications this development holds for a contemporary culture of assessment. It begins from the observation that generative systems can substantially accelerate scholarly work in areas such as structuring, drafting, and tutorial support, while simultaneously generating new risks for academic integrity, validity, and reliability.

To address this development, the paper develops the theoretical framework of functional tool indifference. What matters, on this view, is not the tool as such, but whether validity, traceability, and human responsibility are preserved throughout the scholarly process. On this basis, the paper proposes a distinction between a merely technical product and a human artefact. An AI-generated output becomes a human artefact attributable in scholarly terms only through the human act of validation – that is, through review, selection, revision, source checking, and responsible contextualization.

From this perspective, academic authorship shifts away from mere text production towards capacities of validation, verification, and judgement. For higher education, this entails the need for a transformed assessment culture that evaluates not only end products, but also processes of production, reflective performance, and the logic of evidentiary support. The paper therefore argues for a dual model of assessment based on process integrity and artefact validity, and for sustained AI governance that strengthens higher education institutions as sites of methodological, reflective, and validation competence.

title: Choke Points, Concentration, and Systemic Fragility: Theory, Evidence, and Policy Implications for Critical Minerals, Semiconductors, and Healthcare in an Age of Hyperglobalization

detail.title: Choke Points, Concentration, and Systemic Fragility: Theory, Evidence, and Policy Implications for Critical Minerals, Semiconductors, and Healthcare in an Age of Hyperglobalization
detail.abstract: Forty years of hyperglobalization have seeded choke points everywhere—from the Strait of Hormuz to Taiwan’s silicon fabs. Paul Krugman identifies the symptom; Nobel Lau reate Michael Spence identifies the cause: decentralized markets systematically under invest in resilience because its benefits, unlike those of efficiency, are non-appropriable network-wide public goods. We formalize both diagnoses. Modeling choke points as two-stage Leontief production networks, we show that processing-stage concentration— measured by the Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (HHI)—amplifies supply shocks into out sized price volatility. Drawing on Samuelson’s (1952) spatial price equilibrium frame work, we introduce the concept of incomparative advantages: developing countries hold comparative advantage in Stage 1 extraction while a single dominant nation (notably China) holds comparative advantage in Stage 2 processing, creating structural con centration that vertical integration could partially dissolve. Panel data for cobalt, lithium, and copper yield an instrumental-variables estimate of ˆβ = 0.612, confirm ing that processing-stage HHI causally raises price volatility. We extend the analysis to semiconductors, healthcare, financial infrastructure (SWIFT), and energy, ranking twelve global choke points by severity and likely disruption duration. Policy must choose among onshoring, international cooperation, and hybrid strategies—with coop eration cheaper but harder. Artificial intelligence amplifies near-term concentration risk while offering long-run resilience dividends through materials substitution and process acceleration.

title: The Helix Cyber Resilience Architecture: Articulating Human Formation, Operational Integration, and Governance Across the Cyber Resilience Lifecycle

detail.title: The Helix Cyber Resilience Architecture: Articulating Human Formation, Operational Integration, and Governance Across the Cyber Resilience Lifecycle

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is Co-Founder of DANRESA Cybersecurity and is involved in the development of the implementation ecosystem described in Section 9 of this paper (Cyber Heroes League, Be a Cyber Hero, Stay Cyber Aware, and Be a Cyber Leader). This paper presents a conceptual architecture intended for academic and professional discussion. The author declares no other financial or personal relationships that could have influenced the work presented.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This paper presents a conceptual architecture based on theoretical reasoning and observation of professional practice. It does not involve human participants, patient data, or experimental procedures requiring ethics committee approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The work was developed from the author's independent professional practice in cybersecurity.

detail.abstract:
This paper presents the Helix Cyber Resilience Architecture, a conceptual lifecycle-based architecture that articulates cyber resilience as a progressive capability developed across three interdependent dimensions: human formation, operational integration, and governance. Grounded in more than two decades of professional practice in cybersecurity and in sustained observation of how resilience emerges in real-world contexts, Helix proposes a structured perspective that complements established frameworks such as the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, the NICE Workforce Framework, the CSTA K-12 Standards, and ISACA COBIT.

The architecture is built upon foundational structures that sustain cybersecurity posture over time, organized into three interdependent maturity curves — formative, operational, and governance — unified by the common variable of the individual's maturity in relation to cyber risk exposure. A five-level model, transversal across the three curves and grounded in observable risk reduction, offers a structured means to describe progression from foundational exposure to architectural leadership. The paper further identifies critical transitions between curves as specific architectural elements, whose quality influences the structural continuity of cyber resilience across the lifecycle.

The approach emphasizes resilience as an evolving capability, built through practice, real-world exposure, and continuous progression. Rather than replacing established frameworks, Helix offers a complementary architectural lens that enables the progression of human and institutional maturity to be observed across the ecosystem of existing references. The paper also describes an implementation ecosystem currently under development, which operationalizes the architecture's principles in formative, operational, and governance contexts. This work constitutes an ongoing developmental model and is offered as an invitation to reflection, application, critique, and refinement by the academic and professional communities interested in the structural continuity of cyber resilience over time.

title: Computable Trust Architecture: A Formal Framework for Runtime AI Governance

detail.title: Computable Trust Architecture: A Formal Framework for Runtime AI Governance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. This research was conducted independently with no financial relationships with any organizations that could be perceived to have influenced the work.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The reference implementation and all associated development were self-funded by the author.

detail.abstract: The rapid deployment of AI systems in regulated domains has outpaced the governance frameworks designed to contain them. We present the Trust Computation System (TCS), a formal framework for runtime AI governance that quantifies trust as a computable, attributable, and policy-enforceable property of AI outputs. TCS defines the Trust Integrity Score (TIS) as a function of four governance dimensions, Boundedness (B), Attribution (A), Compliance (C), and Known (K), evaluated against a resolved policy configuration parameterized by risk tier r, action class a, and data acquisition connection type ct. Every evaluation produces a Trust Certificate: a tamper-evident, hash-chained, identity-attributed governance record suitable for regulatory examination. We introduce the Computable Trust Architecture (CTA) as a distinct category of AI governance infrastructure, present the formal mathematical specification, a reference implementation achieving 108 passing unit tests, controlled reference implementation evaluations across financial services and healthcare governance scenarios, and Trust Dynamics, a formal model of trust loss, adaptive governance, drift detection, and recovery. The framework addresses a structural gap in current AI governance: between policy documents that describe intended behavior and enforcement systems that guarantee it at the point of action.

title: Integrating UPnP technology with CAFM systems -automated device identification and device control in building operation and maintenance

detail.title: Integrating UPnP technology with CAFM systems -automated device identification and device control in building operation and maintenance
detail.abstract: Purpose-Modern buildings use intelligent automation for comfort, efficiency and sustainability, impacting their construction and operation. Although building automation (BA) operates via bus lines and is controlled by sensors and actuators, computer-aided facility management (CAFM) systems often handle data redundantly. Current standards fail to detail effective systems integration, with a noticeable gap in practical network models and solutions.The purpose of this paper is to design a network model that integrates building services and networks at the automation level. The goal is to enable the CAFM side to control all electrical loads (such as lighting, blinds, pumps), climate control (HVAC) and security monitoring. Design/methodology/approach-This paper explores the automatic discovery and integration of BA devices and centralized controls into CAFM systems, focusing on innovative networking models, system data provisioning, import functions and web operation. Established technologies such as Universal Plug and Play (UPnP) and Extensible Markup Language (XML) standards are utilized to develop new solutions. Findings-The paper introduces a solution with a database and software module enabling bidirectional webbased coupling via LAN. The UPnP standard was enhanced to include facility management (FM)-specific information for device communication. The prototype effectively controls devices through CAFM systems, setting a foundation for future improvements in web-based BA. These results are crucial for developing standards for automated data processing between CAFM systems and BA. Practical implications-This research benefits FM, especially in maintenance, operations, energy and compliance. In addition, the need for time-consuming on-site inspections to record device master data for maintenance management, in case of commissioning or changing facility service providers, can be eliminated. The principles of the developed software module enhance CAFM systems as high-performance building control tools. Originality/value-The paper adapts existing technologies for specific FM applications and integrates them for the first time into key FM processes.

title: <u>Shadow Node Theory v2.3.1: Scale Invariance in the Node Satellization Algorithm — Empirical Verification Across 502 Cases, Eleven Domains, and Thirty Orders of Magnitude of Temporal Scale</u>

detail.title: <u>Shadow Node Theory v2.3.1: Scale Invariance in the Node Satellization Algorithm — Empirical Verification Across 502 Cases, Eleven Domains, and Thirty Orders of Magnitude of Temporal Scale</u>
detail.abstract: This paper presents Shadow Node Theory v2.3.1 (SNT v2.3.1), a formal model of node satellization operating across three scales of systemic resolution — Micro (Atomic Node / individual), Meso (intra-national Fungal Network), and Macro (superorganism collision between nations and digital platforms). The central hypothesis holds that when two power nodes orbit in critical proximity, the node with greater accumulated advantage satellizes the historically dominant node through an algorithm whose dynamics follow a power law invariant to temporal scale and substrate: R(t) = a·t^b, where b is the satellization velocity parameter. SNT v2.3.1 delivers four empirical contributions: (1) formalization of the Triple-Resolution Systemic Model with distinct applicability conditions across scales; (2) N-body matrix verification with Mexican INEGI data (32 federal entities, b = −0.473, R² = 0.838, p < 0.001), revealing that the binary model underestimated Tlaxcala's satellization gradient by 9.3×; (3) operationalization of the Atomic Sovereignty Index (ASI) on behavioral data from 4,774 users and 409,287 events (HackerEarth 2026, precision = 1.0, zero false positives); and (4) a final corpus of 502 verified cases across 11 domains spanning 30 orders of magnitude of temporal scale — from digital behavioral cycles of hours to galactic merger timescales of billions of years. Three statistically robust findings emerge from the 502-case corpus. First, abrupt triggers produce significantly faster satellization than gradual ones (Mann-Whitney U = 24,802, p = 1.91 × 10⁻⁵, n = 486), a result stable across three successive corpus expansions from 57 to 114 to 502 cases. Second, institutional friction is the dominant predictor of satellization velocity across all substrates: domains without friction (biological invasion b_mean = +1.435; parasite-host b_mean = +1.148; planetary systems b_mean = +1.029) consistently produce b > 1, while high-friction domains (sovereign countries b_mean = −0.098; predator-prey b_mean = +0.102) produce b ≈ 0. Third, political sovereignty operates as a satellization brake mechanically equivalent to ecological mutual interdependence — both prevent definitive satellization by making complete node extinction destructive to the hub. This equivalence holds across 230 country pairs and 4 predator-prey systems spanning different substrates and temporal scales. The model is accompanied by eight falsifiability criteria (RC1–RC8), a four-step diagnostic protocol for real-world application, and a public replication package including scripts, data, and publication-quality figures (Zenodo DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19446521; GitHub: github.com/Inzainos/The-shadow-Node-Theory).

title: KNOW YOUR GROUND Canada's Strategic Imperatives and Red Lines for the 2026 CUSMA Review

detail.title: KNOW YOUR GROUND Canada's Strategic Imperatives and Red Lines for the 2026 CUSMA Review
detail.abstract:
Know Your Ground: Canada's Strategic Imperatives and Red Lines for the 2026 CUSMA Review

Canada enters the 2026 USMCA Joint Review — which opens July 1 under Article 34.7 and locks in the agreement's architecture for sixteen years — holding more undeployed leverage than at any point in a generation. This paper argues that Canada is misreading the negotiation it is in. The 2026 review is not a technical trade consultation. It is a strategic confrontation over the architecture of the North American economy through 2042, conducted with a counterpart whose policy objectives are no longer primarily economic. Budget Lab at Yale confirms that all 2025 tariffs make the U.S. economy persistently smaller. A government willing to impose self-harmful tariffs is pursuing a different objective. Canada's strategy must be calibrated to the game actually being played.

The paper draws on three analytical frameworks from the companion series — the five-scenario economic analysis in No Going Back, the legal architecture in The Exits Exist, and the digital sovereignty framework in Code Before Clause — and adds three dimensions those papers do not fully develop: the implications of the intangibles economy for what is actually at stake; the strategic challenge of negotiating with a partner that tolerates economic self-harm; and nine specific actions Canada must take before July 1.

The central finding is structural: a 15% tariff crosses an irreversibility threshold — confirmed independently by the Bank of Canada and CIGI — above which automotive platform reallocations occur on four-to-six-year production cycles that no subsequent tariff removal can undo. But the more consequential finding concerns the digital economy. CUSMA's Chapter 19 architecture enables asymmetric data extraction that Ciuriak estimates at approximately 0.9% of annual Canadian GDP in foregone growth — a cumulative 13.7% shortfall over 15 years. A status quo extension compounds that loss for sixteen additional years without reform.

The paper identifies Canada's non-negotiable red lines, maps five legal exits within CUSMA's own treaty architecture, and documents Canada's leverage portfolio across energy, critical minerals, pension fund holdings, agricultural retaliation, and digital governance. It argues that Canadian digital sovereignty is not merely a Canadian defensive interest but a U.S. strategic necessity under the 2025 National Security Strategy and AI Action Plan — and that this alignment creates a positive Canadian negotiating proposal, not only a defensive red line. Nine specific actions — including tabling a Digital Sovereignty Act, rebuilding the SAGIT sectoral advisory architecture, asserting Article 32.2 essential security jurisdiction, and publishing a critical minerals export control framework — can close the preparation gap before the July 1 window closes. The deficit is not legal authority. It is institutional capacity and strategic will.

title: What Cramer Holds vs What He Recommends: Signal-Time Features in 16,701 Mad Money Recommendations (2018-2024)

detail.title: What Cramer Holds vs What He Recommends: Signal-Time Features in 16,701 Mad Money Recommendations (2018-2024)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial or personal relationships that could be perceived to have influenced this study. The author had no business relationship with CNBC, James Cramer, or the subjects of the analysis when conducting this research, and was not employed to produce investment advice based on this work.

detail.abstract: We study 16,701 long stock recommendations from Jim Cramer's CNBC Mad Money (January 2018-December 2024) and ask which signal-time features and prior-disclosure states separate the recommendations that subsequently beat the S&P 500 from those that don't. Forward returns are measured at one-, three-, six-, and twelve-month horizons against the same-window return of the SPY ETF. Because Cramer frequently returns to the same names-NVDA alone is recommended 179 times-we first group repeated mentions into 5,459 continuous position sequences, then label each sequence by whether it contains an on-air Charitable Trust ownership disclosure, advisory hold language, or neither. Four signal-time features and sequence-level labels jointly structure forward performance in the 2018-2024 sample. Market capitalization, trailing 90-day return, and VIX regime are directly observable at recommendation time; engagement tier is used descriptively at the sequence level and operationally only when Cramer has disclosed ownership or hold advice in a prior episode. The sharpest single result is that the casual-buy underperformance is almost entirely a small-cap phenomenon. In the small-cap casualbuy cell, the unconditional one-year stock return is-11.9% versus SPY at +12.7%; outside crisis periods (VIX < 30), the corresponding market-neutral pair trade earns +28.7% per position (p < 0.0001) and remains profitable after typical short-selling costs. Beyond this we show that (i) the engagement-tier ordering portfolio > hold-recommendation > casual buy holds directionally and survives controls for size, momentum, and sector, (ii) Cramer's timing on his own Trust holdings is performance-dependent-he is more likely to mention a portfolio name after a recent run-up, and his return mentions on alreadyowned names after ≥15% prior drawdowns predict +24.7% one-year alpha, a pattern that is absent on similarly-drawn-down stocks he does not own, and (iii) the small-cap pair trade flips sign in crisis regimes (VIX ≥ 30), so the regime distinction is essential.

title: La Chispa: la caída de los Ingresos de los Jóvenes y las Manifestaciones de 2019
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Universidad del Desarrollo

detail.title: La Chispa: la caída de los Ingresos de los Jóvenes y las Manifestaciones de 2019
detail.abstract: Lo ocurrido en octubre de 2019 nos invita a reflexionar sobre cuáles podrían haber sido sus posibles causas. El fenómeno es complejo y requiere del análisis multidisciplinario. Desentrañar las múltiples razones que subyacen, no solo lo que gatilla las movilizaciones, sino también el descontento que lo antecede -muchas veces llamado "malestar"- es necesario para corregir errores y, al mismo tiempo, apreciar los múltiples logros que alcanzó Chile en las últimas décadas. En lo que sigue nos centraremos en lo que llamamos “la chispa” que incendió la pradera. Mencionaremos además otras posibles causas que son el objeto de análisis de nuestro esfuerzo. En este trabajo pondremos énfasis en la caída de los ingresos que sufrieron las generaciones más jóvenes en el mercado de trabajo. Dichos malos resultados, comparados con los buenos obtenidos por generaciones anteriores, dan pie a la hipótesis que las diferentes experiencias económicas de las generaciones generaron un sentimiento de malestar y frustración, que fue la chispa que desató el incendio. La hipótesis es que la situación fue el "pasto seco" que se fue acumulando y que fue encendida por "la chispa" del deterioro de los ingresos de las generaciones más jóvenes.

title: Information Thermodynamics of Data Markets

detail.title: Information Thermodynamics of Data Markets
detail.abstract: We apply the formalism of information thermodynamics to the economics of data markets. Starting from a constrained maximum-entropy principle on market-belief distributions, we derive an informational temperature τ (dollars per bit) as the Lagrange multiplier conjugate to the belief entropy and an informational free energy F I = U I-τS I whose non-equilibrium excess satisfies ∆F I = τ • D KL (P informed ∥ P public). Data extraction is modeled as a Szilard engine-the minimal realization of information-to-work conversion that every richer information-engine construction specializes. The Sagawa-Ueda (2010) generalized second law bounds the work extractable by an agent holding a measurement M of the market state X at ⟨W⟩ ≤ ∆F I + τ I(M; X); when M is shared across agents the bound does not additively replicate, producing data rivalry as a conservation law on extractable work. False information is a zero-mutual-information memory state whose expected work is nonpositive. Kinetic equations with three rates-diffusion κ, extraction γ, and context erosion λ-yield exponential depreciation of F I as a theorem. The Jarzynski equality ⟨e-W/τ ⟩ = e-∆F I /τ and Crooks fluctuation theorem P(+W)/P(-W) = e (W-∆F I)/τ apply without modification, converting τ into an estimable quantity from realized-profit distributions. A thermodynamic impossibility result follows: non-rival data with positive F I in a finite market would violate the generalized second law. The framework makes quantitative several features of data economies-depreciation, hoarding premia, exclusivity, and the irreversibility of extraction-that resist treatment within classical information economics, rational inattention, and real-options pricing of information goods.

reference: The (Im)materiality of Immigration Law, 58 COLUMBIA HUM. RTS. L. REV. __ (forthcoming 2026)
title: The (Im)materiality of Immigration Law

detail.title: The (Im)materiality of Immigration Law

publicationDetails.detailsText: The (Im)materiality of Immigration Law, 58 COLUMBIA HUM. RTS. L. REV. __ (forthcoming 2026)

detail.abstract:
Immigration law killed Renée Good, Alex Pretti, and many other noble souls last year, just as it has killed innumerable people on the move over the centuries. It has killed, maimed or stymied all these human beings by nurturing a lie: that migration is inherently harmful. By sorting, excluding, and expelling human beings, immigration law has constructed a false reality that sustains the commonsense that migration is dangerous and that violence in response to it is necessary and justified. Law here is not, primarily, responding to reality—it is staging it.

This Article exposes the prevailing belief that migration is inherently harmful as untrue and theorizes why it is nonetheless so entrenched. This conviction is deeply rooted because the work immigration law does for our society has little to do with the practical logistics of managing people on the move. Immigration law serves instead a more mystical purpose: legitimating and sustaining the status quo of the American social structure. While migration law imposes extraordinary, material violence on migrants—the jails, the expulsions, the deaths, the torn ties of family, friends and community—migration law’s actual purposes are immaterial—ineffable, emotional, and metaphysical. Migration law ultimately aims to produce the immaterial abstractions of “nation,” the superiority of “citizens” and “heritage Americans,” and to carry water for capitalism.

If this is the real work of immigration law—to deploy legal violence on “others” to produce the superiority of citizens and capital—is it legitimately law at all? Does it deserve the honor? Or is it rather the rawest kind of power cannibalizing the rule of law’s legitimacy? The ICE occupation of Minneapolis has made the answer plain for all to see. What should follow from this fact? I argue that in a world that took the rule of law and constitutional provisions—like birthright citizenship—more seriously, immigration law wouldn’t be law at all since its immaterial purposes violate too many precepts of law’s rule.

title: Price Transmission Resilience in China's Photovoltaic Supply Chain: Evidence under Geopolitical Risk
affiliations: , University of Auckland Business School and University of Auckland

detail.title: Price Transmission Resilience in China's Photovoltaic Supply Chain: Evidence under Geopolitical Risk
detail.abstract: This study examines price transmission across three manufacturing segments of the photovoltaic supply chain: upstream polysilicon, midstream solar cells, and downstream modules. We further investigate how geopolitical risk and other macroeconomic factors interact with this internal transmission mechanism. Prior research has extensively examined PV-related equity markets, firm performance and policy impacts, yet spot price dynamics across the physical production chain have received less attention. To address this gap, we use Chinese weekly spot market price data from July 2021 to February 2026, capturing a complete cycle from acute shortage to structural overcapacity. The methodology combines dynamic conditional correlation modeling, frequency-domain connectedness analysis, and a vector autoregression framework augmented with exogenous variables including geopolitical risk, the oil price, exchange rate, and global supply chain pressure. The results show that, first, price discovery runs counter to the physical production sequence: cell-to-polysilicon Granger causality is highly significant, and by week 16 the cell segment accounts for 32.95% of polysilicon's forecast-error variance. In comparison, the reverse direction explains only 2.30%. Second, connectedness is regime-dependent. Total connectedness ranges from 19.73% in calm periods to 31.45% during high-volatility episodes such as the 2021–2022 supply shortage, when modules also became significant upstream transmitters before retreating as overcapacity set in after mid-2023. Third, geopolitical risk does not significantly enter the price transmission system. The USD/CNY exchange rate and global supply chain pressure enter the system selectively via the polysilicon segment, leaving cell and module pricing unaffected. These findings reveal a demand-informed rather than cost-driven pricing structure in the PV industry, suggesting that stabilization policies targeting midstream cell pricing may prove more effective than interventions aimed at upstream raw materials.

title: Oil Laundering How did Russian Oil Circumvent the European Union’s Embargo?
affiliations: Gakushuin University and Institute of Developing Economies (IDE-JETRO)

detail.title: Oil Laundering How did Russian Oil Circumvent the European Union’s Embargo?
detail.abstract: The European Union’s embargo on Russian crude and refined oil from 2022 may have unintentionally enabled the indirect entry of Russian oil into sanctioning EU markets through third-country refining, a process commonly described as “oil laundering.” To provide formal evidence of this mechanism, this paper examines whether Russian crude oil was rerouted to non-sanctioning countries—specifically China, India, Turkey, Singapore, and the United Arab Emirates—and whether these “laundromat” countries subsequently increased exports of refined petroleum products to the EU. Using a gravity-model framework and event-study analysis, we show sharp and synchronized shifts in trade flows consistent with laundering behavior. Imports of Russian crude oil into laundromat countries remained stable before 2022 but surged dramatically afterward, rising by 5,360% in 2023 and 10,894% in 2024. In parallel, EU imports of refined petroleum products from these same countries show no pre-embargo trend but a substantial increase by 105% in 2023 and 59% in 2024. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that China and India served as the most prominent intermediaries, while other sanctioning countries—such as the United States, Canada, Australia, and Japan—exhibited no comparable increases. Placebo tests confirm that EU members exempt from the embargo did not increase refined-product imports from laundromat countries. Because the EU’s 2022 embargo unintentionally facilitated indirect entry of Russian oil through third-country refining, these findings highlight the need for more comprehensive downstream product regulations and improvement of traceability mechanisms in sanction design.

title: Geopolitical Energy Shocks, Safe Havens, and Sovereign Bond Markets Evidence from the 2026 U.S.–Israeli Conflict with Iran

detail.title: Geopolitical Energy Shocks, Safe Havens, and Sovereign Bond Markets Evidence from the 2026 U.S.–Israeli Conflict with Iran
detail.abstract: Geopolitical conflicts in major energy-producing regions generate shocks that propagate through global energy markets and financial systems. This paper examines how the 2026 U.S.–Israeli conflict with Iran affected sovereign bond yields across countries with differing energy exposures. Because the conflict occurred in a region central to global oil supply expectations, the episode provides a useful setting to study how geopolitical energy shocks transmit to financial markets through oil price channels and global capital flows.Using daily sovereign yield data for sixteen countries and an event-window panel framework, the analysis evaluates how energy price shocks, safe-haven capital flows, and global financial conditions shape sovereign yield responses across countries and maturities. The results reveal heterogeneous yield adjustments across countries. Safe-haven sovereign markets experience smaller increases in yields during the conflict, consistent with flight-to-safety dynamics. Economies with greater dependence on imported energy also exhibit smaller increases in long-term yields once global benchmark rates are controlled for, suggesting that the growth effects of energy price shocks dominate inflationary pressures in sovereign bond markets.These results highlight the importance of energy-market disruptions as a source of sovereign risk transmission and underscore the role of sovereign bond markets in absorbing geopolitical energy shocks.

title: The Inversion Error: Why Scaling Cannot Fix What Architecture Got Wrong

detail.title: The Inversion Error: Why Scaling Cannot Fix What Architecture Got Wrong

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests. No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: The current generation of large language models (LLMs) has compressed the entire symbolic output of human civilization into a single synthesizable architecture. What it has not accomplished, and what no amount of scaling will supply, is the structural foundation that makes symbolic cognition safe, coherent, and genuinely useful in a physical world. This structural absence, the Inversion Error, is a failure of integration between the high-level symbolic reasoning of the Transformer and the foundational enactive constraints of the physical world. It manifests as three discrete, reproducible, and diagnosable failure modes: Continuity, Gravity and Physics, and Reversibility of Thought. A structured pilot study, the Spaghetti Table Protocol, administered across three leading multimodal systems produces an aggregate score of 4 out of a possible 30 on a three-pillar diagnostic rubric, confirming the Inversion Error as a reproducible Class Failure of current transformer architectures rather than a model-specific artifact. The Parametric AGI framework proposes three formally specifiable, sparsely-gated Attention Mechanism modifications to the Transformer architecture: the Somatic Engine, the Gravity Engine, and the Episodic Buffer Engine. Situated within the neuro-symbolic AI research program, the engines encode symbolic physical constraints as differentiable priors within the attention mechanism itself, enforced during the forward pass rather than as post-hoc corrections, introducing class-level intensional constraints into what is currently a set-level extensional architecture. Trained through Reinforcement Learning from Physical Feedback (RLPF) rather than human preference ratings, they address the structural gap between statistical pattern and physical constraint. The framework is grounded in abductive reasoning and AI system design understood as theory-building in Peter Naur's sense: a structural condition diagnosed from the socio-technical designer's vantage point, visible from outside the engineering system and invisible from within. This paper is simultaneously a diagnostic contribution, a solution architecture proposal, and a collaboration invitation to the mathematical and ML research communities for formal engine specification, to the AI safety research community for corrigibility and inner alignment engagement, and to foundation model and world model development teams pursuing physical grounding for development-level access to active training environments.

title: Monetary transmission in the WAEMU: Separating the liquidity and rate channels

detail.title: Monetary transmission in the WAEMU: Separating the liquidity and rate channels
detail.abstract: WAEMU banks collect deposits equivalent to a large share of GDP yet extend private credit at rates far below comparator regions, despite two decades of accommodative monetary policy. Standard analyses misdiagnose this gap by treating the BCEAO's two instruments-the policy rate (price) and weekly refinancing auctions (quantity)-as a single monetary stance. We separate their effects using a panel of seven member states, exploiting within-year crosscountry variation in refinancing, a shift-share diagnostic, and a natural experiment from the 2012 reserve requirement cut. We find that while the policy rate is largely decoupled from banking outcomes and the real economy, refinancing quantity reaches the real economy precisely where the policy rate fails. Refinancing has a powerful and persistent downward effect on lending rates and an immediate impact on credit volumes. Gains to bank profitability are delayed. Furthermore, we document that the aggregate correlation between refinancing and sovereign bond accumulation reflects the region's prudential architecture and fiscal dominance, rather than a causal supply-push. The deposit-credit gap is thus not a monetary failure, but a reflection of the institutional setup where liquidity flows most easily to sovereign instruments.

title: Répression, vie chère et gouvernement par l'opacité au Mali

detail.title: Répression, vie chère et gouvernement par l'opacité au Mali
detail.abstract: Cette note analyse la séquence politique, sociale et médiatique observée au Mali entre le 18 et le 24 avril 2026. Elle avance que des événements en apparence dispersés-maintien en détention du journaliste Youssouf Sissoko, préavis de grève dans l'enseignement supérieur, déguerpissements à Bamako, hausse des prix des carburants, tensions humanitaires dans le Nord, remaniement du Conseil national de Transition et repositionnements diplomatiques-relèvent d'une même logique de gouvernement. En mobilisant la théorie de l'inversion morale d'État, la littérature sur l'autoritarisme légal et les travaux récents sur la digitalisation du débat public malien, la note montre que le régime militaire convertit des coûts politiques et sociaux en preuves de souveraineté. La contrainte est présentée comme ordre, l'opacité comme prudence patriotique, et la souffrance ordinaire comme le prix admissible de la refondation. Sur le plan méthodologique, l'analyse repose sur un croisement raisonné de sources institutionnelles, d'organisations de défense des droits, d'agences de presse et de médias maliens, tout en écartant les récits insuffisamment corroborés. La conclusion soutient que la crise malienne est désormais indissociablement une crise de vérité publique et une crise de performance étatique.

detail.abstract:
Archival Digital Edition of the original 1998 article published in the Suffolk Transnational Law Review. This article examines the World Trade Organization Dispute Settlement Understanding (DSU) and argues for a stronger and more enduring implementation framework for the multilateral trading system.

Developed during the 1995–1998 formative period and published at the start of the DSU/WTO tipping point, this article was one of the few very early statements of the broader promise and practical significance of an emerging “everything WTO / DSU” world. Methodologically, the article combined close reading, use, and analysis of the original DSU document and its text with validation through discussions, interviews, and contemporaneous practitioner, legal, diplomatic, and policy sources, including Ambassador Harlan Cleveland, U.S. Trade Representative leadership and context, and lawyers and leaders from other countries. Its relevance today is even clearer in hindsight: the WTO now has 166 members out of around 200 countries worldwide today, and its framework covers 98% of world trade. In that sense, the article addressed not a marginal mechanism, but the rise of a near-universal trade architecture with real enforcement teeth.

The paper was significantly shaped by interviews and discussions with Ambassador Harlan Cleveland and grounded in contemporaneous U.S. trade-policy realities of the period, including Mickey Kantor and Charlene Barshefsky’s testimony on the enforcement gap. In approach, balance, reach, and timing, it stands as one of the few very early statements of the broader promise and practical significance of the emerging WTO/DSU order.

This is a historically significant work originally published in 1998 and republished in digital archival form in 2026 to preserve the original publication, restore access, support accurate citation, and document an early contribution to a framework that later became globally significant.

detail.abstract: This analysis evaluates the fiscal and policy implications of extending unemployment insurance benefits for striking workers in Oregon from ten weeks to twenty-six weeks. Drawing on policy projections, comparative state approaches, and unemployment insurance expenditure data, the paper assesses both anticipated budgetary impacts and potential effects on collective bargaining dynamics. Findings suggest that extending benefit duration would likely represent a minimal share of total unemployment insurance expenditures while providing increased financial stability for workers during labor disputes. The analysis also considers concerns regarding prolonged strikes and system strain, concluding that the policy change would modestly rebalance bargaining power without significantly disrupting the unemployment insurance system.

detail.abstract: Fooltopia: The Modern-Day Utopia is a structured satirical exploration of a hypothetical global condition in which all nations voluntarily adopt a "No First Aggression" doctrine for a defined period. The work unfolds across five interconnected volumes, each examining systemic and behavioural consequences arising from the sustained absence of conflict. Through poster-style micro-narratives and thematic progression, the paper highlights the paradoxical dependencies of modern systems on frictionincluding geopolitics, institutional relevance, media cycles, criminal justice structures, and interpersonal dynamics. As the narrative advances from pre-treaty anticipation to post-treaty stillness, the satire probes whether absolute peace, when prolonged, may itself generate instability or existential ambiguity. This work is not predictive but exploratory, intended to stimulate reflection on whether human systems are structurally conditioned to rely on opposition in order to function.

title: Beyond the Paycheque: Why Employees Stay Despite Below-Market Compensation -A Multi-Theoretical Framework

detail.title: Beyond the Paycheque: Why Employees Stay Despite Below-Market Compensation -A Multi-Theoretical Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This is an independent academic paper. No external funding was received, and the author has no financial or personal relationships with any organisations that could have influenced the findings presented.

detail.abstract: A persistent assumption in human resource management holds that compensation is the primary determinant of employee retention. Yet empirical evidence consistently challenges this view. Gallup's 2024 State of the Global Workplace data reveals that pay and benefits account for only 11 per cent of departure reasons, while engagement, culture, and wellbeing account for 68 per cent combined. This paper examines the psychological and structural factors that explain why employees remain in organisations offering below-market compensation, drawing on a multi-theoretical framework comprising Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory (1959), Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs (1943), Vroom's Expectancy Theory (1964), Social Exchange Theory (Blau, 1964), the Psychological Contract (Rousseau, 1989), and the concept of Job Embeddedness (Mitchell et al., 2001). The paper argues that employee retention is a fundamentally multi-dimensional phenomenon, driven by a complex interplay of intrinsic motivators-including meaningful work, recognition, autonomy, and growth-and structural factors such as organisational belonging, perceived career investment, psychological safety, and the costs of leaving. The paper further engages with the contemporary phenomenon of the 'Great Stay' (2024-2025), in which declining quit rates reflect not merely loyalty but a complex mixture of economic caution, job embeddedness, and what Gallup terms 'the Great Detachment'. The paper concludes with a holistic retention framework and practical recommendations for organisational leaders and HR practitioners.

title: The Virtue of Sparsity in Complexity
affiliations: University of Ottawa - Telfer School of Management and Telfer School of Management, University of Ottawa

detail.title: The Virtue of Sparsity in Complexity
detail.abstract: Sparsity or complexity? In modern high-dimensional asset pricing, these are often viewed as competing principles: richer feature spaces appear to favor complexity, while economic intuition has long favored parsimony. We show that this tension is misplaced. We distinguish capacity sparsity-the dimensionality of the candidate feature space-from factor sparsity-the parsimonious structure of priced risks-and argue that the two are complements: expanding capacity enables the discovery of factor sparsity. Revisiting the benchmark empirical design of Didisheim et al. (2025) and pushing it to higher complexity regimes, we show that nonlinear feature expansions combined with basis pursuit yield portfolios whose out-of-sample performance dominates ridgeless benchmarks beyond a critical complexity threshold. The evidence shows that the gains from complexity arise not from retaining more factors, but from enlarging the space from which a sparse structure of priced risks can be identified. The virtue of complexity in asset pricing operates through factor sparsity.

title: The Contract Clause and the Corporation
affiliations: George Mason University - Antonin Scalia Law School and University of Illinois College of Law (deceased)

detail.title: The Contract Clause and the Corporation

keywords: Trustees of Dartmouth College v. Woodward

detail.abstract:
The legal treatment of the corporation stands at a major crossroad. Historically, courts and legislatures have viewed corporations as concessions or creatures of the state, essentially governed by legal rules. This view owes much to the franchise and special chartering origins of the corporation. Yet market forces have long since freed the corporation from the control of state legislators, and the corporation can now safely be viewed as fundamentally contractual. This shift has been documented by a generation of economists who have studied the intricate web of contracts that comprises the modern corporation. Nevertheless, the concession or franchise view persists in modern legislation and judicial decisions. The corporate form, and business organizations generally, cannot fully achieve their potential until they escape the shackles of the regulatory approach.

The conflicting views of the corporation have constitutional significance. Article I, section 10 of the Constitution states: “No State shall . . . pass any . . . Law impairing the Obligations of Contracts.” This provision was a significant legal predicate for the economic success of this country because it preserved efficient arrangements by private citizens from unnecessary state interference. It is time now to extricate this important constitutional principle from its recent relative disuse and use it to ensure the stability of internal corporate arrangements. In this Article we demonstrate how the contract clause can be applied to several different types of changes in state corporation law.

This Article demonstrates that the contract clause can and should play a central role in controlling state manipulation of corporate law. Because corporate law is fundamentally contractual, the state should do no more than enforce these contracts and provide standard forms to reduce transaction costs. As long as the law goes no further than this, the parties to corporations will tend to reach efficient arrangements. To the extent the law interferes with these arrangements, the results will be suboptimal. The appropriate answer to this problem is not more regulation at the federal level, since this will only add another layer of interference with private arrangements. Rather, laws that interfere with private arrangements in effect at the time of the enactment should be held invalid under the contract clause.

Part I discusses the contractual theory of the corporation, and not only establishes an essential predicate for application of the contract clause, but also shows why the contract clause must occupy a central role in fostering the development of optimal corporate arrangements. Part II discusses the function and scope of the contract clause, as well as the general considerations underlying application of the contract clause to the corporate contract. Part II specifies the conditions under which state statutory changes in the corporate contract amount to a violation of the contract clause. Such changes include state antitakeover statutes and revisions in the standard of care owed by directors in the wake of Smith v. Van Gorkum.

title: From Models to Decision Architectures: Structural Trends and Emerging Failure Topologies in Modern AI Systems

detail.title: From Models to Decision Architectures: Structural Trends and Emerging Failure Topologies in Modern AI Systems

keywords: Germany Version: SSRN Working Paper Date: 2026

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems are increasingly deployed as components within complex sociotechnical decision infrastructures rather than as isolated predictive models. Evaluation frameworks, however, remain largely model-centric: they focus on improving the accuracy, robustness, or fairness of individual models. This paper argues that a growing class of failures cannot be explained at the model level. Instead, they emerge from interactions between components inside AI-driven decision architectures, where perception, prediction, optimization, and control modules interact across organizational and technical boundaries. We propose a shift in analytical perspective from models to decision architectures. The paper introduces a conceptual framework that identifies recurrent failure topologies arising from subsystem interaction, governance misalignment, and feedback dynamics. Drawing on examples from autonomous systems, healthcare, finance, and public administration, we show how structurally similar failure patterns emerge across domains despite differences in models and datasets. The framework contributes three elements: (1) a taxonomy of architecture-level failure modes, (2) a cross-sector analytical lens for understanding systemic AI failures, and (3) a foundation for governance and auditing approaches that focus on decision processes rather than isolated models. By reframing AI safety as a property of decision architectures, the paper highlights a critical gap in current evaluation paradigms and suggests directions for future research in AI governance and system design.

detail.abstract: Employees' productivity in Nigerian public sector is known to be relatively low compared with those of their counterparts in other developing and developed countries. The above phenomenon has been linked to poor reward and benefit system management. Most employees experience low level of motivation in their workplaces due to several factors, such as, low morale, job dissatisfaction, and general lack of work incentives. It is in this context that the article examined various reward and benefit system management as means of staff productivity in Edo State Ministry of Education, using a qualitative research methods, that depended on the judgmental sampling technique, and a sample size of 20 respondents, as well as, the application of both primary and secondary method of data collection. In addition, the textual analysis techniques was applied in the analysis of both the primary and secondary data collected for the study. Findings from the study revealed that there is inadequate provision of reward to staff of Edo State Ministry of Education (ESME). Also, the research found that the administration of monetary rewards to staff of Edo State Ministry of Education is not adequate for enhancement of their productivity, amongst others. The article recommended that the government should make provision for enhanced monetary and non-monetary rewards to employees of ESME to ensure staff productivity and achievement of a better service delivery; the administration of rewards and benefit systems in ESME should be implemented in accordance to employees' performance in the workplace to encourage hard working staff, and to also, discourage laziness among employees; among others.

title: Instrumental Variable Analysis Without Structural Equations
affiliations: , , University College London, University College London, Cornell University - Cornell Tech NYC and

detail.title: Instrumental Variable Analysis Without Structural Equations
detail.abstract: We consider efficient inference on least-squares solutions to inverse problems as a way to avoid having to assume exact solutions exist. Such assumptions are substantive and not innocuous and their failure may well imperil inference when we impose them on the statistical model. Our approach instead allows to conduct inference on a quantity that is defined regardless of solutions existing and coincides with the usual estimands when they do. For the case of instrumental variables, this means we can motivate the analysis with structural models but these do not need to hold exactly for the statistics to actually go through as well.

title: Unpacking PropTechs and IoT ecosystems: European insights with a novel business model taxonomy

detail.title: Unpacking PropTechs and IoT ecosystems: European insights with a novel business model taxonomy

keywords: Digital transformation Paper type Academic paper

detail.abstract: Purpose-PropTechs and IoT ecosystems are essential for transforming buildings into smart buildings to improve sustainability, optimise processes and transform the user experience of buildings. To gain insight into PropTechs, we develop a business model taxonomy of PropTechs offering solutions for the smart built environment. The paper also provides insights into the PropTech landscape and how to encourage the adoption of PropTech solutions. Design/methodology/approach-We use an iterative, multi-method approach that includes a systematic literature review, an analysis of 90 PropTechs from Germany, Austria and Switzerland and 14 expert interviews. Findings-The taxonomy comprises 16 dimensions, grouped into Value Proposition, Value Architecture, Value Network and Value Finance. Other findings highlight the growing importance of PropTechs in the real estate industry. Building owners are responsible for proactively adopting digital strategies to ensure adaptability, longterm value and sustainable retrofits. Similarly, PropTechs should engage service providers at an early stage and support product viability through vertical integration. Practical implications-The taxonomy provides practitioners with a structured framework to analyse and differentiate PropTechs while helping them identify complementary solutions that contribute to a robust ecosystem. Originality/value-This research offers a comprehensive and systematic foundation-previously lacking-for advancing knowledge of PropTechs and the technological evolution of buildings, thereby facilitating deeper understanding and supporting theory development.

title: Strategic Alignment of Total Rewards: An IPPO Model Approach to Individualized Compensation and Benefits

detail.title: Strategic Alignment of Total Rewards: An IPPO Model Approach to Individualized Compensation and Benefits
detail.abstract: Traditional Human Resource Management (HRM) practices frequently rely on standardized compensation and benefit structures, fundamentally ignoring the deep psychological and philosophical variations among employees. Based on the IPPO Model (Interest + Personality + Philosophy = Outcomes), this paper proposes a novel framework for designing individualized compensation, benefit, and reward packages. By systematically aligning financial and nonfinancial rewards with an employee's vocational interests, behavioral traits, and foundational philosophy of work, organizations can significantly improve engagement, mitigate burnout, and extend organizational tenure. This paper introduces the concept of Philosophically Calibrated Total Rewards (PCTR)a reward architecture in which compensation structures are designed not merely to incentivize performance but to resonate with the individual's deepest understanding of what work is for. Drawing on the established literature of compensation theory, motivational psychology, and the IPPO Model's three-layer architecture, the paper operationalizes a Total Rewards Alignment Protocol (TRAP) that enables HR practitioners to construct individualized reward menus aligned to each employee's Interest, Personality, and Philosophy profile. The paper further develops the IPPO Reward Compatibility Matrix, a diagnostic instrument for identifying reward misalignment patterns and their organizational consequences, and demonstrates the application of the PCTR framework across the full HRM lifecyclefrom compensation offer design through performance management, internal mobility, and leadership retention. It concludes with a structured agenda for empirical research required to validate the framework's predictive claims.

detail.abstract: Fumigation is a critical phytosanitary practice widely employed in international trade to ensure the integrity of agricultural commodities and animal feed shipments. However, the application of fumigants introduces a complex regulatory and operational dimension by transforming otherwise non-hazardous cargo into dangerous goods under international maritime regulations. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of fumigated cargo transport units classified under UN 3359 within the framework of the International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Code. It explores the regulatory requirements, operational challenges, and safety risks associated with fumigated cargo, with a particular focus on export operations originating from major agricultural economies such as Brazil. Drawing from real-world logistics practices, this study highlights systemic gaps in compliance, documentation inconsistencies, and the critical role of technical expertise in mitigating operational risks. The findings emphasize the need for enhanced regulatory awareness, crossfunctional coordination, and standardized procedures to ensure safe and efficient maritime transport of fumigated cargo.

title: The Impact of Formal and Informal Institutions on Stock Market Reactions to Divestment Announcements: A Meta-Analysis
affiliations: Northumbria University and University of Vaasa

detail.title: The Impact of Formal and Informal Institutions on Stock Market Reactions to Divestment Announcements: A Meta-Analysis
detail.abstract: This study examines how institutional factors and cultural characteristics influence stock market reactions to divestment announcements. Drawing upon agency and institutional theories, we posit that divestment announcements in countries with stronger shareholder protection generate higher positive returns than divestments in countries with weaker shareholder protection. Furthermore, we contend that stock market reactions to divestment announcements tend to be negative in countries with a long-term orientation culture or high levels of corruption. To test these hypotheses, we conduct a meta-analysis of 144 primary studies with 202 effect sizes and 90,449 firm-level observations. The results indicate that, in general, divestments result in a strong positive stock market reaction. Furthermore, our findings suggest a positive moderation effect of a stable regulatory environment on the relationship between stock market reactions to divestments. While stock market reactions to divestments are negative in countries with a long-term cultural orientation, they tend to be positive in environments with higher external corruption.

detail.abstract: The U.S. Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025 (CLARITY Act, H.R. 3633) 2 establishes a formal regulatory framework for digital assets by defining oversight between the SEC and CFTC. Although presented as domestic reform, its implications extend globally, shaping how financial systems interpret and integrate digital assets. Building on the already enacted GENIUS Act (July 2025) 3 , the framework moves stablecoins closer to regulated financial instruments, enabling them to compete with traditional bank deposits and accelerate blockchain-based payments. This paper analyzes the Act's impact on global banking through its effects on deposits, cross-border payments, and tokenized financial infrastructure. Focusing on emerging markets, particularly India, it argues that U.S. regulatory clarity increasingly functions as a global reference point, influencing compliance, innovation, and financial flows. While the framework introduces efficiency and access, it also raises risks including deposit displacement, regulatory arbitrage, and growing reliance on U.S.-anchored systems. The paper concludes that the CLARITY Act represents not just regulatory clarity, but a directional shift in global finance toward systems where traditional banking and blockchain-based infrastructure operate in parallel.

title: Management of Public and Private Sector Enterprises in Bangladesh: A Comparative Study During 1971-2011

detail.title: Management of Public and Private Sector Enterprises in Bangladesh: A Comparative Study During 1971-2011
detail.abstract: The management practices of private and public sector enterprises of Bangladesh have been continually improving since the independence of the country. From the inception of the country in 1971, there was a highly disorganized management in both the public and private sectors. However, it has now been reached to a reasonable shape that can be claimed as moderate management practices like other developing countries of the world. Observation shows that a rapid development in the management of private sector has been occurred since early 1990s. In 2000, there has been a substantial change and modification in management practices of the private sector enterprises in Bangladesh due to shifting focus of the government from public to private sector. The reasons can be attributed by the development of information technology and introduction to the privatization policy of the enterprises. This study shows that the development of management practices followed an upward trend in Bangladesh. The higher the development in private sector management is inducing the higher development of public sector management in Bangladesh.

title: Risk Management in Heterogeneous Regulatory Environments: A Framework for Interpretable Compliance

detail.title: Risk Management in Heterogeneous Regulatory Environments: A Framework for Interpretable Compliance
detail.abstract:
This paper examines a recurring issue in cross-border financial regulation: institutions applying identical regulatory requirements are often assessed differently across jurisdictions. The paper argues that this inconsistency is primarily driven by differences in interpretation rather than deficiencies in regulation.

It introduces the concept of interpretation risk and proposes an Interpretable Compliance Framework (ICF), which structures compliance into control objectives, evidence standards, and escalation thresholds. The framework enables institutions to make their compliance approach explicit, documented, and reviewable.

Using examples from AML and KYC practice, the paper demonstrates how differences in evidence expectations and risk tolerance lead to inconsistent supervisory outcomes. The proposed approach improves auditability and predictability without requiring changes to existing regulatory frameworks.

title: Legal Form and Corporate Outcomes: Evidence from the Societas Europaea *
affiliations: Université Paris-Dauphine, PSL Research University, Université Paris-Dauphine, PSL Research University and Léonard de Vinci Pôle Universitaire

detail.title: Legal Form and Corporate Outcomes: Evidence from the Societas Europaea *
detail.abstract: We examine firms' adoption of the Societas Europaea (SE), a supranational corporate form introduced in 2004, to study how legal structure affects corporate decisions and shareholder outcomes. At the end of 2024, SE companies accounted for more than 25% of the EURO STOXX 50 index. Adopters are more likely to be family-controlled firms with higher operating growth and market performance. Following adoption, firms attract greater foreign investor ownership and increase their cross-border acquisitions outside Europe, which is consistent with signaling a global identity. However, markets react negatively to SE implementation, except when headquarters relocation accompanies the change, and postadoption information asymmetry increases. Our evidence suggests that while the SE structure enhances contractual flexibility and global positioning, it also gives considerable latitude to CEOs and blockholders, with uncertainty about subsequent decisions and their consequences for shareholders.

detail.abstract: Using the Taro Yamane formula, a sample of 400 respondents was drawn through stratified random sampling to capture departmental and hierarchical diversity. A structured questionnaire, validated through expert assessment and pilot-tested for reliability (Cronbach's alpha: 0.715-0.789), assessed five dimensions of organisational learning; individual learning, team learning, knowledge acquisition, knowledge sharing, and organisational memory, alongside operational performance. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and linear regression in SPSS version 24 at the 5% significance level. Findings showed a significant and positive relationship between all dimensions of organisational learning and operational performance (𝑅 2 = 0.469). Knowledge acquisition was the strongest predictor (𝛽 = 0.895, 𝑝 < 0.001), followed by individual learning, knowledge sharing, and team learning. The results highlight the importance of structured knowledge development, continuous skill improvement, and collaborative learning in enhancing service efficiency, reducing operational errors, and improving customer satisfaction in Nigerian banks. The study recommends that bank management embed formal knowledge acquisition systems, promote cross-functional learning mechanisms, and strengthen organisational memory to support sustained operational effectiveness.

title: Machine Learning Forecasts of Asymmetric Betas Using Firm-Specific Information
affiliations: University College Dublin, University College Dublin and University College Dublin

detail.title: Machine Learning Forecasts of Asymmetric Betas Using Firm-Specific Information
detail.abstract: We demonstrate that machine learning methods provide a powerful framework for modelling conditional asymmetric risk. Using a large cross-section of US stocks and a comprehensive set of firm characteristics, we show that allowing for nonlinearities significantly increases the out-of-sample performance across a wide range of asymmetric beta measures and forecasting horizons. Trading frictions, followed by characteristics related to intangibles, momentum and growth, emerge as the most important drivers of future risk dynamics. Reconstructing CAPM beta from forecasts of asymmetric beta components indicates that a more granular decomposition of systematic risk yields a more accurate representation of market beta. We also find that incorporating conditional beta forecasts into discounted cash flow models that account for the term structure of betas enhances equity valuation accuracy. Finally, we show that the statistical outperformance of conditional betas translates into economically significant benefits for market-neutral portfolio investors.

detail.abstract:
Software quality assurance now operates under faster release cadences, richer browser interfaces, API-heavy architectures, and growing pressure for developers to participate in quality work earlier. The market is not empty: major tools and platforms already provide established capabilities in browser automation, API testing, cross-browser infrastructure, low-code authoring, and model-based orchestration. The persistent problem is combinational rather than absolute. Many teams still need several properties at once: readable suites, separate handling of business data, unified Web and API scenario thinking, visible step-level evidence, user-controlled artifact retention, low-friction developer onboarding, and a handoff path into ordinary source code without deep vendor dependence.

This paper identifies several persistent workflow gaps in the current QA automation landscape-ranging from artifact ownership to first-day developer accessibility and presents WebSureQTool as a proposed design response.

WebSureQTool implements a local-first architecture that prioritizes:

  1. Readability: Human-readable YAML suites for cross-role collaboration.
  2. Data Discipline: Separate handling of scenario logic from reusable CSV-backed datasets and row-based CSV/JSON data tables.
  3. Portability: A reduced-lock-in handoff path into standard Java/JUnit or C#/NUnit source code through baseline code generation and export.

The paper argues that a developer-friendly, local-first orchestration layer can reduce clerical maintenance and improve evidence transparency without surrendering long-term asset ownership. By targeting a sub-10-minute first-run experience, the proposed design enables ordinary web and UI developers to participate in quality work earlier in the feature lifecycle.

detail.abstract: This paper defines Trajectory Engineering. It is the set of methods, infrastructures, and governance arrangements required to observe, model, and intervene on the propagation of disease and health through time. The unit of analysis is three interacting domains: biological, environmental, and cultural. The scale is the population; the resolution is the individual. The paper identifies three failure modes that a planetary health infrastructure must overcome — observation without intervention, reductionism without context, and systems without substrate. It proposes a financial instrument, the Health Trajectory Benefit, capable of funding root-cause interventions across generational timescales. It proposes a governance architecture, federated sovereignty, to make the data commons legitimate. The political philosophy underneath it, EcoDemocracy, is one I first sketched in surgical residency in 1989. This prospectus is intended to open, not close, the research and implementation program anchored by the Health 4.0 platform and Doctor AI architecture. The actuarial methodology, the governance compact, and the pilot cohorts names here are deliverables of the program, not of this document.

detail.abstract: The contemporary global economic landscape is characterized by heightened volatility, stemming from geopolitical tensions, technological disruptions, and systemic shocks. This reality necessitates a paradigm shift from traditional risk management towards the cultivation of strategic resilience. This article investigates the constitutive elements of strategic resilience within complex economic systems, positing it as a dynamic capability integral to sustainable competitive advantage and macroeconomic stability. The research employs a mixed-methodology framework, combining a systematic literature review of global scholarship with a qualitative analysis of strategic narratives from leading multinational corporations and national economic policies across the OECD and emerging economies. The purpose is to deconstruct the multi-level architecture of resilienceoperational, strategic, and systemic-and to evaluate the efficacy of various managerial and governance instruments in fostering it. The analysis reveals that resilience is not merely a defensive capacity but a proactive function, predicated on strategic agility, cognitive flexibility, redundant resource allocation, and adaptive governance structures. A key finding is the critical role of meta-governance in orchestrating resilience across public and private sector boundaries, particularly in managing transboundary crises. The study concludes by proposing an integrated framework for resilience assessment, highlighting the socioeconomic impact of resilient design in mitigating welfare losses during disruptions. The practical value lies in providing policymakers and corporate strategists with a structured approach to diagnose resilience gaps and implement coherent capacitybuilding initiatives.
