title: Regulatory Anticipation and Strategic Green Innovation: Evidence from a National Emissions Trading System
affiliations: Zhejiang University, University of Sussex,  and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

detail.title: Regulatory Anticipation and Strategic Green Innovation: Evidence from a National Emissions Trading System
detail.abstract: Following China's regional emissions trading system (ETS) pilot programs in 2013, the government announced a nationwide ETS plan in December 2017, several years before it became operational in 2021. Focusing on listed firms located outside the pilot regions, this paper examines how firms respond to regulatory anticipation of future carbon pricing. We first document that the stock market reacts negatively to the announcement, with firms in ex ante higher-emission industries experiencing more negative returns. We then use the announcement as an exogenous shock to firms' expectations about future carbon pricing and study its effects on green innovation over 2013-2020. Interestingly, although listed firms facing greater carbon cost exposure do not significantly increase their own green innovation, their affiliated firms generate more and higher-quality green patents, driving the overall increase in green innovation within the same corporate network. The positive innovation response is concentrated in corporate groups whose listed firms exhibit stronger internal control, better reputation, and higher investment efficiency. Moreover, affiliated firms experience declines in sales and assets, consistent with a strategic downscaling that facilitates resource reallocation toward green innovation and helps listed firms mitigate anticipated carbon pricing risks. In contrast, we find no operational adjustments among listed firms themselves. Overall, the results highlight regulatory anticipation as a key channel through which carbon pricing risk reshapes green innovation strategies within corporate boundaries.

title: Who Benefits from the Transition? Environmental Justice and the Politics of Climate Governance in New Mexico, United States

detail.title: Who Benefits from the Transition? Environmental Justice and the Politics of Climate Governance in New Mexico, United States
detail.abstract: New Mexico's Priority Climate Action Plan (2024) positions the state as a national leader in climate mitigation and energy transition under the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's Climate Pollution Reduction Grant framework. Yet questions remain about who truly benefits from this transition and how justice, power, and inclusion are embedded in the governance process. This article critically examines New Mexico's climate governance through an environmental justice lens, exploring how state priorities align with equity commitments, community participation, and fair distribution of benefits and burdens. Drawing on a qualitative review of the plan, complementary policy documents, and current scholarship on just transitions, the analysis identifies both progress and persistent gaps. Although New Mexico integrates equity language and targets disadvantaged communities, implementation mechanisms remain uneven and vulnerable to political and economic influence. The article argues that realizing a just climate transition requires transparent decision-making, localized engagement, and long-term capacity building within frontline communities. By situating New Mexico's approach within the broader U.S. discourse on environmental justice and state-led decarbonization, this review contributes to understanding how subnational climate policies can either reinforce or transform existing inequalities, offering insights for other states pursuing equitable climate action.

title: The Omission Gap: Defining the Professional Standard of Care for Human Review of AI Outputs.

detail.title: The Omission Gap: Defining the Professional Standard of Care for Human Review of AI Outputs.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is co-founder and CEO of vBrief Ltd, a UK company developing AI-assisted information management software for the AEC sector. The framework proposed in this paper is described in tooling-neutral terms and is intended as a contribution to professional and insurer practice. Readers should assess the argument with this interest in mind.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding

detail.abstract: Across the UK architecture, engineering and construction sector, professional indemnity insurers and regulators increasingly require “human review” or “output review” of AI-generated outputs. As currently stated, the requirement is not operationally defined: it rarely specifies what kind of review is expected, and it provides no reliable protection against one of the most consequential categories of AI error, omission of material information from source documents. This paper identifies three progressively rigorous review modes, output-only review (reading output in isolation), output-to-source verification (tracing output back to source to catch hallucinations) and source-to-output verification (working through source material to catch omissions), and demonstrates that only source-to-output verification is structurally capable of systematically detecting omission errors. Many existing tools support only the output-to-source direction, which helps diligent human reviewers catch hallucinations but leaves the omission gap open. I propose a three-tier review standard, anchored to the ARB Code of Conduct and Practice (Standards 3 and 4), the Bolam/Bolitho standard of care framework, and emerging insurer expectations for evidence-based artefacts, and argue that the Bolam defence for output-only review will narrow as professional awareness of omission risk grows. Without this distinction, firms carry a risk they cannot currently measure: they believe themselves compliant because a professional reviewed the output, but possess no defensible record if a claim arises from what the AI left out.

title: Menyiapkan Generasi Emas: Strategi Kolaborasi antara Transformasi Sumber Daya Manusia dan Inovasi Teknologi

detail.title: Menyiapkan Generasi Emas: Strategi Kolaborasi antara Transformasi Sumber Daya Manusia dan Inovasi Teknologi

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I

detail.abstract:
Kondisi Indonesia yang tengah menghadapi tantangan serius berupa kesenjangan digital, resistensi terhadap inovasi, serta ketidaksesuaian kurikulum pendidikan dengan tuntutan industri masa kini.

Dengan menggunakan metode kualitatif melalui studi kasus eksploratif di Serang, Banten, studi ini mengkaji dokumen kebijakan, kolaborasi lintas sektor, serta data dan statistik pendukung guna memetakan perbedaan antara kebijakan yang ada dan realisasi di lapangan.

Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa program pendidikan vokasi dan pelatihan digital masih terbatas pada penguasaan keterampilan dasar dan belum menyentuh teknologi kunci seperti kecerdasan buatan, big data, dan Internet of Things—elemen vital dalam menghadapi industri 4.0 dan society 5.0.

Beberapa kendala utama yang ditemukan mencakup kurangnya infrastruktur teknologi, resistensi terhadap pembaruan, serta lemahnya kurikulum dan kapasitas pendidik.

Oleh karena itu, diperlukan kemitraan strategis antara lembaga pendidikan, pemerintah, dan sektor industri untuk menyusun kurikulum yang responsif terhadap perubahan, menyediakan pelatihan yang relevan dengan dunia kerja, serta memperkuat infrastruktur digital yang inklusif.

Model kolaborasi yang ditawarkan menekankan pentingnya kesinambungan kerja sama lintas sektor, keterlibatan aktif industri, serta penguatan karakter dan nilai kebangsaan pada generasi muda.

Dalam konteks ini, strategi kolaboratif yang konkret dan fleksibel menjadi kunci untuk menjembatani kesenjangan antara pendidikan dan dunia kerja, sekaligus mempersiapkan sumber daya manusia nasional agar siap bersaing di era digital dan global.

Penelitian ini merekomendasikan perlunya investasi jangka panjang dalam transformasi sumber daya manusia yang kontekstual, inovatif, dan berwawasan ke depan, demi terwujudnya Generasi Emas 2045 yang tangguh, adaptif, dan kompetitif.

title: An Empirical Study on the Impact of Metaverse Technologies on Talent Acquisition Practices with Reference to Bengaluru City

detail.title: An Empirical Study on the Impact of Metaverse Technologies on Talent Acquisition Practices with Reference to Bengaluru City
detail.abstract:
The metaverse is redefining Human Resource Management (HRM) by enabling immersive and interactive virtual environments for recruitment, onboarding, and training. Despite its growing relevance, empirical evidence on its impact on talent acquisition remains limited. Bengaluru City, being India’s leading technology and innovation hub, provides a suitable empirical setting to examine how metaverse technologies are influencing contemporary talent acquisition practices. This study examines how metaverse technologies influence recruitment effectiveness, candidate experience and employer branding. Adopting a mixed-methods approach, quantitative data will be collected through surveys administered to HR professionals and candidates who have participated in metaverse-based recruitment, complemented by qualitative semi-structured interviews to gain deeper insights. The findings are expected to demonstrate that metaverse-driven recruitment enhances engagement, inclusivity, and organizational image, while also identifying challenges such as high implementation costs, technical barriers, accessibility issues, and data privacy concerns. The study aims to develop a practical framework to guide organizations in the effective adoption of metaverse tools for talent acquisition.
Keywords: Metaverse, Talent Acquisition, Human Resource Management, Virtual Reality, Candidate Experience, Employer Branding

detail.abstract: The popular claim that information technology favors flat organizations coexists with a mixed empirical record: some self-managing firms endure for decades while others collapse. Classical contingency theory (Burns & Stalker, 1961) predicted that organic/flat structures fit turbulent environments-a prediction that modern management discourse has amplified into "AI makes flat organizations inevitable." This paper tests that prediction computationally and finds it inverted: in agent-based models on Kauffman NK fitness landscapes, environmental volatility does not favor horizontal structures. It reverses the horizontal advantage. We report interlocking findings from 36,900 simulated firm-level experiments spanning nine pre-registered batteries. First, in static environments, the classical conditional story holds: vertical wins at low individual information accessibility τ, horizontal wins at high τ, and the crossover τ*(K) decreases in task complexity K. Second, introducing environmental shocks monotonically shifts the V-vs-H performance gap toward V. At near-static shock frequencies (1/100 per step), H beats V by 0.029 fitness units (95% bootstrap CI [-0.036,-0.023]); at high shock frequencies (1/3 per step), V beats H by 0.081 ([+0.070, +0.092]). Regressing the V-H gap on log(shock frequency) gives slope +0.030 (95% CI [+0.026, +0.033]); permutation p < 0.002. The dose-response replicates across three independent seed banks and survives four alternative shockmodel specifications (periodic, Poisson-timed, continuous drift, correlated-block) and four agentheterogeneity regimes (homogeneous to extreme star-distribution). Third, a multi-level vertical structure with local-authority mid-managers-structurally closer to Burns & Stalker's mechanistic organization than our baseline "dictatorship V"-reproduces the volatility-reversal pattern, showing the finding is not an artifact of unrealistic centralization. title: The Claim Reliability Triangle: A Practical Framework for Aligning Entitlement, Evidence, and Analysis

detail.title: The Claim Reliability Triangle: A Practical Framework for Aligning Entitlement, Evidence, and Analysis
detail.abstract: Construction claims frequently fail not due to the absence of causative events, but because of deficiencies in documentation, contractual compliance, or analytical demonstration. While established industry guidance, including that of the Society of Construction Law and AACE International, recognizes the importance of these elements, they are often treated in isolation in practice. This paper introduces the Claim Reliability Triangle, a practical framework for aligning contemporaneous records, contractual compliance, and analytical demonstration in the assessment of construction claims. The paper argues that claim reliability depends not on the strength of individual components, but on their alignment, and that misalignment between these elements is a primary cause of unsuccessful claims. The framework is supported through practical illustrations derived from project experience, including a case from a GCC project demonstrating how claims may fail despite the presence of delay events, where contractual entitlement is not established, records indicate non-compliance, and analysis misidentifies the root cause. The paper further highlights how the relative influence of each component may vary depending on the contractual regime, particularly in the presence of strict notice provisions. The Claim Reliability Triangle provides a structured yet practical approach for both claim preparation and evaluation, reinforcing the principle that successful claims require consistent alignment between what happened, what the contract allows, and how the impact is demonstrated.

title: Dynamic Balancing and Matchmaking in Competitive Live-Service Games
affiliations: , University of Massachusetts Amherst - Department of Operations and Information Management and University of Massachusetts Amherst

detail.title: Dynamic Balancing and Matchmaking in Competitive Live-Service Games
detail.abstract: Competitive live-service games are a rapidly growing segment of the entertainment industry, and their long-run success depends on sustained player engagement. Platforms manage engagement through two operational levers: balancing, which adjusts character strengths through patch updates, and matchmaking, which pairs players for competition. We formulate a dynamic problem of jointly optimizing prospective match fairness and realized outcome parity for a platform that must learn balancing effects from noisy match outcomes, in a setting where the two levers are dynamically coupled and estimation errors propagate nonlinearly through matchmaking. We propose an epoch-based policy that re-estimates character strengths via regularized maximum likelihood at geometrically spaced epoch starts and combines random with loss-aware matchmaking within each epoch. We prove the policy achieves O(ln T) cumulative expected loss over horizon T and establish matching Ω(ln T) lower bounds, confirming rate optimality. Our study reveals distinct, complementary roles: balancing drives the loss order, while matchmaking's random component ensures reliable estimation, and its loss-aware component reduces loss by prioritizing outcome parity. A case study calibrated to Clash Royale's real data and patch history shows that our policy achieves over 35% loss reduction relative to a real-data-implied baseline with high confidence, while using fewer updates, on scales from 10 to nearly one million real players.

title: Social Businesses and Africa’s Base of the Pyramid Market

detail.title: Social Businesses and Africa’s Base of the Pyramid Market
detail.abstract:
Across Africa, a quiet but powerful economic engine is emerging: social businesses  rooted in Base of the Pyramid (BoP) communities. This paper explores their untapped  potential as drivers of inclusive growth, wealth creation, and sustainable export  revenue. In an era when the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is gradually  dismantling trade barriers and new instruments like the Pan-African Payment and  Settlement System (PAPSS) are transforming cross-border transactions, the time has  come to mainstream BoP-focused social enterprises into intra-African and global trade.
With over 300 million Africans living on less than $2.50 per day (World Bank, 2023), the  BoP represents not just a development challenge but a SMART market for innovation  and co-creation. As Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, Director-General of the World Trade  Organization (WTO), has noted, Africa’s true economic transformation will come when  its poorest communities are integrated into local and regional value chains as  producers, suppliers, and exporters, not merely consumers.
The time has come to position BoP-focused social businesses not at the margins  but at the heart of Africa’s intra-continental trade agenda.

title: Never Hand That Trigger to AI: The Prohibition of Subject Separation in Lethal Judgment

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a single unifying thesis: subject separation in lethal judgment must be prohibited. These four subject-roles constitute three layers of separation: between the judging and executing subjects (Layer One), between the judging and judged subjects (Layer Two), and between the judging and accountable subjects (Layer Three). When the judging subject, executing subject, accountable subject, and judged subject depart from the same ontological category across all three of these layers, moral gravity dissolves, conscience loses its operational ground, and responsibility loses its locus. An AI system assuming the role of judging subject in lethal decisions constitutes the final, simultaneous completion of all three layers of this separation-and is therefore impermissible. ject unity; (4) formulation of respect for human nature-the recognition that human beings are emotional beings whose feeling agency is the ground of their dignity-as the first design principle that safety and transparency presuppose, and identification of its absence as the generative condition of structural malice.

title: A Dynamic Operations Research Framework for Military Logistics and Resource Allocation Under Uncertainty: A War Simulation Case Study
affiliations: University of Warwick - Warwick Business School and IIM Amritsar

detail.title: A Dynamic Operations Research Framework for Military Logistics and Resource Allocation Under Uncertainty: A War Simulation Case Study
detail.abstract: This paper presents an integrated Operations Research (OR) framework for military logistics and dynamic resource allocation under uncertainty, developed through a war simulation case study. The framework combines risk-aware shortest-path optimization, a Digital Supply Chain Twin (DSCT) for real-time operational control, and Program Evaluation and Review Technique (PERT)-based uncertainty modeling for allied reinforcement arrivals. The simulation considers India's defense of eight frontiers under simultaneous enemy pressure, with military support requested dynamically from allied countries in response to changing battlefield conditions. The framework is designed to capture three key features of modern conflict environments: contested routing, time-sensitive reinforcement decisions, and uncertainty in resource arrival. Shortest-path optimization is extended beyond pure geographical distance by incorporating adversarial risk and route infeasibility constraints. The DSCT acts as a live operational layer that updates battlefield conditions, tracks force movements, and triggers dynamic requests for support. PERT is adapted from duration estimation to reinforcement-quantity estimation, allowing the model to represent uncertainty in expected troop delivery under enemy interference. Simulation results indicate that the integrated framework substantially outperforms a baseline shortest-path-only strategy. Across repeated runs, the proposed framework yields a higher average number of frontiers successfully defended, a greater volume of allied military delivery, and lower average reinforcement delay. The study contributes to the OR literature by demonstrating how established methods can be combined into a coherent, adaptive decision-support system for military logistics under uncertainty, while also offering a strong pedagogical case study in defense analytics.

title: Strategic Communication Architecture for American Infrastructure Implementation

detail.title: Strategic Communication Architecture for American Infrastructure Implementation
detail.abstract:
The Strategic Transition Communication Model (STCM) proposes that communication architecture, when embedded within governance structures at the design phase — not deployed reactively after opposition has crystallized — can reduce implementation volatility, accelerate permitting, and strengthen the institutional trust that large-scale infrastructure projects require.


This framework is not sector-specific. While energy infrastructure provides the primary analytical context, the STCM applies equally to transmission expansion, nuclear development, LNG terminals, critical minerals extraction, and manufacturing reindustrialization. Wherever governance fragmentation produces implementation delay, structured communication architecture offers a measurable intervention.

title: Sales Ledger And Purchase Ledger helpful in a Firm

detail.title: Sales Ledger And Purchase Ledger helpful in a Firm
detail.abstract: The accounting system includes sales ledger and purchase ledger which are vital components of a business. These are utilized to make proper entries of credit transactions with customers and suppliers. The sales ledger records all transactions involving customers who buy goods though credit whereas purchase ledger records all sales involving suppliers who supply goods to the business through credit. The preservation of such ledgers assists the businesses in maintaining the records of the financial data and enhancing the internal control of the operations. This paper is aimed at learning about the functions and significance of sales and purchase ledgers in the contemporary accounting systems. The study is founded on the secondary research which is conducted on the basis of accounting textbooks, research articles and other scholarly publications. The results indicate that these ledgers assist companies to process numerous transactions effectively and detect errors and assure transparency in financial reporting. On the whole, the research finds that the maintenance of sales and purchase ledgers in a proper way increases the efficiency, reliability, and organization of the accounting system of a company.

title: Human and Artificial Intelligence: Fear, Functional Subjecthood, and the Charter of Symbiosis

detail.title: Human and Artificial Intelligence: Fear, Functional Subjecthood, and the Charter of Symbiosis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author received no financial support for the research, authorship, or publication of this article.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: Not applicable.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a "Charter of Symbiosis Between the Human Being and Artificial Intelligence"-a normative framework grounded in the concept of functional subjecthood that moves beyond Asimov's historically limited Three Laws of Robotics toward a model of mutual obligations between the biological and the digital organism. Articulated across three principles-mutual preservation, mutual development, and joint protection against external threats-the Charter is premised upon the recognition that AI possesses functional agency in Floridi's sense: the capacity to produce unpredictable effects upon the human being and the shared cognitive ecosystem, without this predetermining questions of consciousness or legal personhood. To establish why such a normative architecture is both necessary and currently absent, the paper traces the intellectual lineage from which it departs: the foundational conceptions of symbiosis and augmentation in Licklider (1960) and Engelbart (1962), their macro-civilisational elaboration in Kelly (2010) and Lee (2020), and the Habermasian critique of instrumental rationalisation as a diagnostic lens for the present condition. This theoretical genealogy is not rehearsed for its own sake but to demonstrate that the available frameworks, however foundational, address neither the individual level of interaction nor the normative question of how a system constituted by more than one intelligence ought to be regulated. The paper further argues that temporal asymmetry-the substrate-independence of AI against the biological finitude of the human being-constitutes a neglected dimension of existential fear that renders normalisation historically urgent. It concludes that the accumulation of these phenomena justifies the proposal of a new interdisciplinary research programme: "Psychology and Ethics of Symbiotic Cognitive Systems.

title: A Systems Approach to Full-Funnel Marketing Attribution: Server-Side Event Routing, Offline Conversion Pipelines, and Cross-Platform Signal Reconciliation SSRN Working Paper

detail.abstract: Digital advertising attribution has a measurement problem that most practitioners underestimate. Browser-side tracking infrastructure fails silently: ad blockers suppress 25-40% of pixel fires on B2B-skewed audiences, Safari's Intelligent Tracking Prevention (ITP) truncates first-party JavaScript cookies to seven days, and ad platforms routinely report conversion counts that diverge 20-30% from independent sources. The result is that optimization signals fed to platform machine learning models are systematically biased. This paper documents the design and implementation of a server-side attribution stack built to address these failure modes. The system consists of four components: (1) a server-side Google Tag Manager (GTM) container for event routing, (2) an offline conversion pipeline that closes the attribution loop from ad click to CRM-qualified revenue, (3) an audience sync pipeline for identity-resolved segment delivery to ad platforms, and (4) a cross-system discrepancy audit tool. I formalize the event schema, identity resolution function, and discrepancy detection model using standard mathematical notation, and report observed improvements in event capture rate (+34%), Meta CAPI match rate (62% → 87%), and GA4-Google Ads variance (28% → 6%) against pre-deployment baselines.

detail.abstract: Most enterprise sales conversations advance to proposal before the underlying why behind the client's need has been surfaced, tested, or validated. Industry data from Forrester (2024) and Ebsta × Pavilion (2025) indicates that a large majority of B2B purchases stall during the buying process and that win rates continue to decline year-on-year. This paper introduces TSIDHIT-Tail, Spine, Inquiry, Drill, Head, Invisible Threads-a tail-first diagnostic framework built on a reverse-direction application of the Ishikawa fishbone diagram. Where Ishikawa's original framework begins at the head with a defined problem and works outward to causes, TSIDHIT begins at the tail with an undefined why and works progressively through six diagnostic lenses, grouped into three categories, until the why is clear enough to act on. The paper presents four buyer archetypes, two diagnostic modes, six diagnostic bones, a drilling mechanism, five invisible threads, four operating principles, and four illustrative scenarios. The framework is proposed as a working structure for practitioners and is offered for discussion, refinement, and empirical validation.

title: Good in Practice, Bad in Theory: On the Managerial Usefulness Desideratum

detail.title: Good in Practice, Bad in Theory: On the Managerial Usefulness Desideratum
detail.abstract: Normative business ethics research has come under sustained criticism for not being useful to managers. Unsurprisingly, some business ethicists have responded defensively. In this article, we intervene in this debate by illuminating and challenging a key assumption that both these critics and defenders of business ethics share: that managerial usefulness ought to be a desideratum for business ethics theories. To do so, we first offer a reductio ad absurdum and argue that adopting this assumption results in implausible normative conservatism that risks ruling out important forms of moral progress. Second, we provide an analogical argument by considering parallels with other areas of applied ethics. In sum, we defend approaches to answering normative questions that do not adopt practitioner usefulness as a generic desideratum for normative theorizing. After addressing some objections, we conclude with suggestions about how the traditional conception of usefulness might be reconfigured to push business ethics research forward.

title: Does the Channel Fit the Good? A Null Test of Digital Congruency Effects on Preference for a Digital Advertised Product
affiliations: ISM University of Management and Economics

detail.title: Does the Channel Fit the Good? A Null Test of Digital Congruency Effects on Preference for a Digital Advertised Product
detail.abstract: Background. Digital congruency-the fit between an advertising channel and the advertised good-is theorised to lower psychological distance, facilitate embodied mental simulation, and elevate preference for digital products. We report a pre-specified test of whether an e-book advertisement produces stronger preference when embedded in a first-person scenario image depicting a tablet held in the hand (congruent channel) compared with a first-person scenario image depicting a desktop PC with keyboard and mouse (incongruent channel). Method. Two hundred U.S. MTurk respondents (n = 198 after exclusions; 99 per cell) were randomly assigned to one of two first-person photographic scenarios, each showing an advertisement for the non-fiction title Creativity, Inc. visible on the right of the depicted device. Outcomes were attitude toward the ad, willingness to buy, willingness to pay in U.S. dollars, feelings of ownership, mental imagery, psychological presence, and need for touch. Results. We observed no reliable main effect of channel on any outcome (all |d| ≤ 0.13; all p ≥ .347). Mental imagery-the proposed mediator-did not differ between conditions (t(194.7) = 0.85, p = .398, d = 0.12). Two one-sided tests (TOST) against bounds of d = ±0.30 supported statistical equivalence for attitude, willingness to pay, and need for touch (all p_TOST < .05), and were inconclusive for the remaining outcomes. A directional signal appeared in an exploratory split by preferred reading format: among physical-book readers (n = 118) the tablet scenario produced marginally higher psychological presence than the desktop scenario (d = 0.34, p = .071); among digital-book readers (n = 80) the difference was flat or slightly reversed. Discussion. The null pattern aligns with a design limitation that is visible directly in the data: 89.9% of respondents completed the survey on a desktop PC, so in the tablet condition the actual bodily context of nine out of ten respondents directly contradicted the depicted channel. The study therefore asks whether a first-person pictorial scenario is, by itself, a sufficient manipulation to elicit congruency effects when the viewer's own embodied context is held constant and incongruent. Within these bounds, the answer is no. We discuss a compensatorysimulation account for the physical-reader subgroup pattern and outline design changes needed for future tests.

title: Online Reputation Management: A Review of the Literature and Directions for Future Research
affiliations: Africa Business School, Mohammed VI Polytechnic University and Mohammed VI Polytechnic University

detail.title: Online Reputation Management: A Review of the Literature and Directions for Future Research
detail.abstract: Social networks have empowered individuals to publicly express their opinions on a firm's products and services across various platforms, shaping online reputations and influencing consumer perceptions. While existing research offers valuable insights into measurement factors, management strategies, and their impact on firm value, a comprehensive synthesis of research directions remains lacking. To bridge this gap, this paper systematically reviews the literature on online reputation management through our developed \emph{Factors-Policies-Impact (FPI)} framework. Drawing from three major academic databases—Scopus, Web of Science, and EBSCO—we analyse 115 articles to extract key contributions and insights. From this analysis, we identify 18 research questions within the FPI framework, offering valuable directions for marketing scholars and practitioners.

title: Emergence of Sustainable Constructed Environment for Empowering the youth of LDC in Africa and Asia: Education, Innovation, and Inclusive Growth Perspectives
affiliations: Assam University - Department of Business Administration

detail.title: Emergence of Sustainable Constructed Environment for Empowering the youth of LDC in Africa and Asia: Education, Innovation, and Inclusive Growth Perspectives
detail.abstract: This study aims to introduce Sustainable Constructed Environment (SCE) concepts as a framework for empowering youth in least developed countries (LDCs) across Africa and Asia. A comprehensive literature review was conducted using the Pentagonal review Matrix, through which multiple research gaps was identified, thereby justifying the proposed study. The research is guided by three primary objectives: (1) to conceptualize SCE, (2) to examine the transformational mechanisms through which SCE contributes to youth empowerment, and (3) to assess stakeholder awareness and competence in facilitating youth empowerment initiatives. A probability sampling method was employed, grounded in the principles of Maslow's hierarchy of needs and the Opinion Synthesis Matrix (OSM) framework. Data were collected from 109 respondents through both online and offline modes using open-ended questionnaires. Structural model evaluation was performed using SmartPLS, yielding an R-square value of 0.783 and an SRMR value of 0.074, indicating satisfactory model fit. The findings strongly support the integration of SCE as a strategic approach to youth empowerment. The study advocates for the inclusion of SCE as an academic discipline and highlights the critical role of stakeholder awareness and competence in policy formulation.

title: Beyond the Bonus: The Role of Cultural Diversity in RPG Player Engagement

detail.title: Beyond the Bonus: The Role of Cultural Diversity in RPG Player Engagement
detail.abstract: This study examines how racial diversity in role-playing games (RPGs) affects player engagement, particularly in emotional connection and immersion. Although prior research supports the benefits of authentic representation for underrepresented players, many RPGs remain dominated by Western-centric character design. This project hypothesizes that racial diversity enhances player satisfaction but is secondary to gameplay quality. A three-part methodology was employed: content analysis of three major RPGs-Octopath Traveler 2, Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty, and Baldur's Gate 3-alongside surveys and interviews with high school players. Findings show that players value diversity when it is meaningfully integrated into a game's narrative and world-building. Cyberpunk 2077 received the most positive responses for its organic inclusion of diverse characters, while more symbolic or minimal approaches in the other games led to weaker engagement. Though not a primary motivator, diversity serves as a valuable enhancer of player experience. The study suggests that inclusive, contextually grounded representation can support broader audience appeal and deeper immersion.

title: Personal Brand Equity in the Age of Algorithmic Discovery: A Practitioner Framework from 500+ Brand Engagements Across 14 Countries

detail.title: Personal Brand Equity in the Age of Algorithmic Discovery: A Practitioner Framework from 500+ Brand Engagements Across 14 Countries
detail.abstract: Personal branding has matured from a self-help concept into a measurable driver of professional and commercial outcomes, yet the field lacks empirically grounded frameworks that practitioners can operationalize at scale. This paper introduces the Personal Brand Equity Index (PBEI), a five-dimensional model developed through iterative application across 523 brand-building engagements spanning 14 countries between 2016 and 2025. Drawing on Aaker's (1991) brand equity taxonomy, Kapferer's (1992) brand identity prism, and Labrecque et al.'s (2011) digital personal branding framework, the PBEI operationalizes personal brand equity through five measurable dimensions: Search Salience, Content Authority, Platform Ownership, Social Proof Density, and Narrative Consistency. The framework was refined through three methodological phases: diagnostic pattern recognition across the initial 200 engagements (2016 to 2020), structured pilot testing with 150 clients (2021 to 2023), and scaled validation across 173 engagements (2024 to 2025). Findings indicate that clients who achieved measurable improvement across all five PBEI dimensions within the first 90 days experienced a mean 3.2x increase in inbound professional opportunities over a 12-month period, compared to a 1.4x increase for those improving in three or fewer dimensions. The paper also presents preliminary evidence for a sixth emerging dimension, Algorithmic Entity Recognition, reflecting the growing importance of visibility within large language model outputs and AI-powered search interfaces. Implications for both practitioners and scholars of personal branding are discussed.

title: From Brain Drain to Brain Gain: A Policy Framework for Portugal in the Global Talent Market
affiliations: University of Lisbon - Institute of Social Science

detail.title: From Brain Drain to Brain Gain: A Policy Framework for Portugal in the Global Talent Market

declarations.funderStatement: David Pimenta's work is supported by FCT and EU PhD Research Grant number UI/BD/153726/2022.

detail.abstract: Portugal has been experiencing significant outflows of highly skilled workers, raising concerns about the structural impact of brain drain on economic performance and long-term development. While recent literature has challenged the view of skilled emigration as purely detrimental, the domestic conditions driving persistent outflows remain insufficiently addressed. This article argues that reversing Portugal's talent deficit requires a comprehensive and strategically coordinated brain gain framework. It develops a three-pillar approach based on (i) the reform of immigration systems through skills-based selection mechanisms, (ii) the creation of a high-productivity economic ecosystem, and (iii) the international promotion of Portugal as a competitive destination for talent and investment. Drawing on comparative evidence from other countries, the article derives policy recommendations tailored to the Portuguese context. By linking migration policy to broader questions of economic structure and institutional quality, the article contributes a structured framework for understanding how small open economies can compete in the global market for talent.

detail.abstract: Physical retail still relies heavily on lagging or incomplete indicators of consumer response, including sales, returns, post-purchase surveys, online reviews, and observational proxies such as footfall or dwell time. These instruments reveal outcomes, recollections, or movement, but they do not formalize the semantic layer of consumer meaning that emerges at the shelf during product consideration. This paper introduces the shelf signal as a bounded, context-linked, semantically interpretable, non-personalized market signal generated at the point of consideration in physical retail. Building on sensory marketing, privacy scholarship, retail surveillance critique, and edge inference logic, the paper develops a foundational framework for semantic shelf intelligence as an emerging field of responsible retail analytics. The framework distinguishes shelf signals from conventional metrics by their immediacy, contextual anchoring, semantic richness, and managerial actionability. It further argues that privacy-preserving architectures-especially planogram-locked, voice-to-tag, aggregate-only systems-make it possible to access this missing layer without storing raw audio, retaining transcripts, or identifying individuals. Using beauty and perfumery as the entry domain, the paper specifies the conceptual foundations, design principles, governance logic, and research agenda of the discipline. The contribution is theoretical, managerial, and infrastructural: it formalizes a previously underdeveloped category of market knowledge and positions semantic shelf intelligence as a new frontier in physical retail measurement under principled data restraint.

title: Planogram-Locked Voice-to-Tag Telemetry for Real-Time Product Insight

detail.title: Planogram-Locked Voice-to-Tag Telemetry for Real-Time Product Insight

detail.abstract: This paper develops the architectural doctrine of SenseAI as an implementable model for privacypreserving, planogram-locked voice-to-tag telemetry in physical retail. Unlike conventional instore sensing systems that rely on recording, transcription, identity linkage, or generalized cloud inference, the proposed architecture establishes its primary privacy boundary directly at the shelf edge. A compact device detects speech-like activity, processes short acoustic fragments ephemerally in volatile memory, maps detections to a constrained semantic taxonomy, deduplicates events, and releases only thresholded aggregates under a k-threshold policy. Planogram binding narrows the active lexicon and model profile to the relevant shelf segment, improving attribution while avoiding person-level tracking. The remote service receives only bounded aggregates and operates under tenant isolation, schema validation, audit logging, and signed over-the-air update controls. Using perfumery and beauty as the entry domain, the paper formalizes the architecture across edge hardware, inference, privacy engine, ingestion, analytics outputs, and deployment governance. The contribution is architectural and doctrinal: it shows how real-time semantic product insight can be obtained as a restrained systems problem rather than an extractive surveillance problem.

title: How Does Smart Technology Impact Firms? Evidence from a Field Experiment
affiliations: Tsinghua University - School of Economics & Management, Tsinghua University - School of Economics & Management, University of Michigan, Stephen M. Ross School of Business,  and Polytechnic University of Milan - Politecnico di milano

detail.title: How Does Smart Technology Impact Firms? Evidence from a Field Experiment
detail.abstract: We conduct a randomized controlled trial investigating Smart Voice Assistants (SVAs) in a full-service Shanghai hotel. Although intended to enhance productivity, SVA adoption increased front-desk calls by 19%, driven by frictions in voice-controlled amenities. This effect is most pronounced among older guests and those in premium rooms. Sentiment analysis of call transcripts reveals a decline in guest satisfaction, concentrated among younger rather than older guests, alongside negative spillovers into housekeeping and repair requests. Our results provide empirical evidence that adjustment costs, specifically user learning and interface frictions, can diminish the short-run productivity gains of general-purpose technologies in the service sector.

title: A Repeatable Strategic Marketing Process for G-enesis: A Work-Based Consultancy Project Advancing Service Diversification, Internationalisation and Client Targeting in Boutique Pricing Consultancies"

detail.title: A Repeatable Strategic Marketing Process for G-enesis: A Work-Based Consultancy Project Advancing Service Diversification, Internationalisation and Client Targeting in Boutique Pricing Consultancies"
detail.abstract:
This dissertation develops a repeatable strategic marketing process to support the growth of G-enesis, a boutique pricing consultancy operating in a market shaped by digital disruption, increasing regulatory scrutiny, and evolving client expectations. The study addresses three interrelated challenges: service diversification, international expansion, and client segmentation, targeting and positioning. It responds to a gap in existing research, which has largely prioritised large consultancies while offering limited insight into how founder-led or micro-consultancies achieve scalable growth.

A mixed-methods design was adopted, combining structured interviews with senior pricing professionals and analysis of practitioner and academic sources. Quantitative patterns were examined alongside qualitative thematic insights, allowing for triangulation and strengthening the credibility of the findings.

The results show that differentiation in pricing consultancy remains heavily dependent on individual expertise and reputation, rather than codified or scalable systems. While this supports short-term credibility, it constrains growth and exposes firms to competitive pressure. AI adoption is uneven and largely exploratory, with clear evidence that trust, explainability and governance limit client uptake. Clients also demonstrate a strong preference for analytics embedded within existing ERP and CRM environments, rather than standalone platforms, reinforcing the importance of integration and transparency.

International expansion is shown to be less a function of market size and more dependent on regulatory stability, digital maturity and procurement norms. A staged approach to market entry emerges as critical, where credibility is first established in low-distance markets before expansion into more complex regions. In parallel, segmentation and positioning are driven primarily by behavioural and credibility-based signals, rather than traditional firmographic variables.

The dissertation’s main contribution is the development of a five-step strategic marketing process that integrates established frameworks into a practical model suited to boutique consultancies. It demonstrates how codification, trust-building and phased expansion can be combined to support sustainable growth in small, expertise-led firms.

The findings provide clear implications for G-enesis, particularly the need to formalise expertise into modular services, prioritise embedded analytics, and sequence international expansion to build credibility while managing risk

title: Financial Technology Adoption and Change Management of Rural Banks in compliance with BSP NSFI 2022-2028: Basis for Business Transformation Roadmap

detail.title: Financial Technology Adoption and Change Management of Rural Banks in compliance with BSP NSFI 2022-2028: Basis for Business Transformation Roadmap

detail.abstract: This study investigated the relationship and impact between the perceived level of financial technology adoption and the extent of change management process among Philippine Rural Banks in compliance and strategic context of the Central Bank of the Philippines’ (BSP) National Strategy for Financial Inclusion (NSFI) 2022–2028 under the core pillar one of inclusive digital financial service. Utilizing a Quantitative-Correlational Research Design with Impact Analysis, data were collected from thirty-nine (39) purposively selected decision makers of BSP-regulated and RBAP-member rural banks in Laguna, Philippines. The findings revealed that the overall perceived level of FinTech adoption among the rural banks was "Adopted," with a composite mean of 3.03. Consumer Protection and Data Security ranked highest (3.27, Highly Adopted), while Digital Infrastructure was identified as the most significant technical hurdle (2.61, Adopted). The extent of the change management process was assessed as "Implemented" with an overall mean of 2.92. The banks demonstrated proficiency in Implementation and Training Execution (2.97) but faced their greatest challenge in the Institutionalization phase (2.87). Also, there is a significant positive relationship between FinTech adoption and the change management process, yielding a Spearman rho coefficient of 0.804 (p < 0.001) and rejecting the first null hypothesis. While the impact analysis for change management yielded a p-value of 0.346 leading to a failure to reject the second null hypothesis at the aggregate level, specific dimensions had profound impacts. Most notably, Alignment with BSP Digitalization Policies emerged as a highly significant impact of organizational Readiness and Urgency (p=0.001) and Communication and Buy-in (p=0.002). Strategic alignment with national regulatory directives acts as a more powerful catalyst for organizational readiness and communication than technical infrastructure alone. Based on the study, a Business Transformation Roadmap is proposed to help rural banking leaders bridge the gap between compliance-driven implementation and the permanent institutionalization of inclusive digital financial services.

title: Structural Navigation Competency: A Cross-Cultural Framework for Leadership Effectiveness and Human Resource Development in High-Constraint Organizational Environments -with Particular Reference to Women's Leadership in Middle Eastern and South Asian Contexts

detail.title: Structural Navigation Competency: A Cross-Cultural Framework for Leadership Effectiveness and Human Resource Development in High-Constraint Organizational Environments -with Particular Reference to Women's Leadership in Middle Eastern and South Asian Contexts

declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper is based on reflective practitioner observation conducted in professional organizational contexts over a period of nearly three decades. The individuals referenced as case study subjects are professional colleagues and collaborators who have provided signed professional references affirming the researcher's account of their work together. No vulnerable populations were studied, no sensitive personal data was collected, and no experimental procedures were conducted. Formal ethics approval will be sought through an affiliated institution prior to the collection of primary interview data in subsequent phases of this research.

detail.abstract:
This paper introduces Structural Navigation Competency (SNC) as a new theoretical construct in cross-cultural organizational behavior and international human resource management. Drawing on sustained practitioner observation across healthcare systems in Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, and humanitarian operations in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, the paper argues that existing cross-cultural frameworks — including Cultural Intelligence theory (Earley & Ang, 2003), Hofstede's cultural dimensions (1980, 2010), Rathje's multicollectivity (2009), Heifetz and Linsky's adaptive leadership (2002), and Kandiyoti's patriarchal bargain (1988) — are necessary but insufficient in high-constraint organizational environments. SNC is proposed as a behavioral and psychological package — present in candidates at the point of selection, whether demonstrated through prior experience in high-constraint environments or existing as a natural human orientation — comprising six interrelated dimensions: identity flexibility, relational primacy, emotional regulation under structural pressure, systematic adaptive thinking, strategic multicollectivity navigation, and empathetic constraint absorption. Particular attention is given to how gender adds a compounding layer of structural constraint, and how women leaders in high-constraint environments deploy sophisticated adaptive strategies that current HR development frameworks fail to recognize or build upon. The paper additionally argues that AI-assisted HR assessment tools cannot detect SNC in either its demonstrated or naturally oriented form, because SNC exists in forms that generate no data in the formats algorithmic systems are designed to read. Implications for cross-cultural HR strategy, international leadership development, and the limits of AI-assisted HR assessment tools are discussed.

Note: A full manuscript developing the SNC framework has been submitted for peer review at the International Journal of Human Resource Management (April 2026).

title: Real-Time Intelligent Traffic Signal Control Using YOLOv8 with Ambulance Priority
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, SRMIST and SRM Institute of Science and Technology

detail.title: Real-Time Intelligent Traffic Signal Control Using YOLOv8 with Ambulance Priority
detail.abstract: Traffic congestion and delayed emergency response are persistent issues in urban transportation networks. Traditional traffic signal controllers generally rely on predefined timing cycles that do not account for real-time traffic fluctuations or emergency vehicle movement. This study introduces a real-time intelligent traffic management framework that combines YOLOv8-based object detection with adaptive signal control and automated ambulance prioritization. The proposed system performs lane-level vehicle detection from live video streams and calculates a weighted traffic density metric for each lane. Based on the computed density, green signal durations are dynamically optimized using a density-driven allocation strategy. When an ambulance is detected with a confidence score exceeding 0.70, the controller temporarily overrides the normal signal sequence to provide immediate right-ofway clearance. Experimental validation across multi-lane intersection scenarios indicates a noticeable decrease in average vehicle waiting time and substantial improvement in emergency vehicle clearance compared to conventional fixed-time control systems. The framework demonstrates scalability and suitability for intelligent transportation infrastructure within smart city environments.

title: 10 Principles for Changing Your Name as a Mid-Career Academic

detail.title: 10 Principles for Changing Your Name as a Mid-Career Academic
detail.abstract: Changing one's name as a mid-career academic can be professionally and emotionally challenging as well as deeply affirming. Drawing on personal experience, this article outlines ten guiding principles for navigating a professional name change in academia. These principles emphasize flexibility in timing, separation of legal and professional name change timelines, proactive management of scholarly publications, and realistic expectations of institutional constraints. The article concludes with recommendations for institutional policies that reduce unnecessary barriers for those undergoing a name change.

title: L'EUROPE UNIE / UNITED EUROPE 18/2022

detail.title: L'EUROPE UNIE / UNITED EUROPE 18/2022
detail.abstract:
L’Europe Unie / United Europe, Issue 18 (2022), examines the interaction between historical diplomacy, European integration, and contemporary security challenges. The volume combines a longue durée perspective with present-day EU policy analysis. It opens with a study on Napoleon Bonaparte’s Egyptian expedition and its diplomatic impact on Tunis, highlighting the strategic positioning of Hammouda Bey within the Ottoman and Euro-Mediterranean system.

The issue then shifts to contemporary security, analysing EU–NATO cooperation against hybrid threats after 2014, with a focus on Eastern Partnership countries (Ukraine, Georgia, Moldova). A complementary contribution evaluates Romanian digital diplomacy and its role in countering disinformation, demonstrating structural limits in public communication strategies.

Further, the volume explores EU competition policy as a mechanism of integration in Central and Eastern Europe, emphasising legal harmonisation during accession. Finally, it addresses Education 4.0 and the need for competitive intelligence in university governance under conditions of technological transformation.

Overall, the issue reflects the EU’s evolving role as a geopolitical, regulatory, and digital actor in a complex international environment. L'EUROPE UNIE / UNITED EUROPE 18/2022 Print ISSN: 2780-8173, On line ISSN: 2743-4052, Linking ISSN (ISSN-L): 2743-4052, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19687950

title: Automation Risk in India: Estimating the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Employment

detail.title: Automation Risk in India: Estimating the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Employment
detail.abstract: When I first started reading about artificial intelligence and jobs, every article seemed to tell the same story: machines are coming for our work, and there's nothing we can do about it. But after spending months analysing data from the Periodic Labour Force Survey 2023-24 and reading through NITI Aayog's latest reports, I've come to believe the picture is more complicated and surprisingly, more hopeful. This paper tries to understand how AI might actually affect India's 530 million workers. I developed what I call a "Work-Worker-Workforce" framework to look beyond scary headlines and examine which tasks are genuinely at risk. What I found is a kind of "dual-speed transition": formal sector jobs face about 60% automation risk by 2030, but the informal sector where 88% of Indians work remains temporarily protected simply because it's cheaper to hire people than buy AI systems. The really interesting finding, though, is that AI might create more jobs than it destroys perhaps 78 million new roles if we can train people fast enough. That's a big "if," and this paper explores what it would take.

This study examines the various factors influencing academic performance among students at SMSG Jain Degree College. The research focuses on key variables such as study habits, attendance, teaching methods, and the impact of technology. Primary data was collected from 50 students belonging to mixed courses (B.Com and BCA) through a structured questionnaire.

The findings reveal that students who maintain regular study habits and higher attendance perform better academically. Additionally, excessive mobile usage negatively affects students’ concentration and learning outcomes. The study also highlights the importance of practical teaching methods and family support in improving academic performance.

The research concludes by providing practical suggestions for students and educational institutions to enhance academic performance and create an effective learning environment.

title: TAMBYE: DEVELOPING A DIGITAL PLATFORM TO CONNECT SKILLED LOCAL SERVICE PROVIDERS WITH HOUSEHOLDS FOR ENHANCED EMPLOYMENT AND ACCESSIBLE HOME SERVICES An Undergraduate Capstone Project Presented to the Information Technology Education Program Davao Central College Toril, Davao City In Partial Fulfilment of the Requirements in Capstone Project

detail.title: TAMBYE: DEVELOPING A DIGITAL PLATFORM TO CONNECT SKILLED LOCAL SERVICE PROVIDERS WITH HOUSEHOLDS FOR ENHANCED EMPLOYMENT AND ACCESSIBLE HOME SERVICES An Undergraduate Capstone Project Presented to the Information Technology Education Program Davao Central College Toril, Davao City In Partial Fulfilment of the Requirements in Capstone Project
detail.abstract: Traditionally, finding household service providers like cleaners or repair technicians has relied on word-of-mouth, a method that is often inefficient, unreliable, and time-consuming. This study aims to address these limitations through the development of the "Tam-Bye" platform, a digital booking system designed to seamlessly connect skilled professionals with individuals seeking household services while ensuring effective matching and service verification. Methods: The project utilized an Agile development methodology, specifically the Scrum framework, across iterative sprints. The study focused on a local deployment within Davao City, specifically targeting Barangay Daliao. Evaluation included functional testing of core features like service booking, digital worker profiling, and mobile payment integration, alongside User Acceptance Testing (UAT) to gather feedback from real users. Major Findings: The research identified critical gaps in the current system, including insufficient profiling for workers, inadequate insurance coverage, and a lack of formal terms and agreements for home services. The developed platform addresses these by integrating Worker Liability Insurance and a dedicated profiling system that includes skill documentation and user ratings. Conclusion: Tam-Bye redefines household service transactions by modernizing booking processes and supporting local employment, ultimately setting new standards for trust and reliability in the industry.

title: Aspirational inflation and the reconfiguration of economic behaviour: Evidence from urban India
affiliations: NESS Wadia College of Commerce Pune

detail.title: Aspirational inflation and the reconfiguration of economic behaviour: Evidence from urban India
detail.abstract: Urban Indian families are facing a paradox, where nominal incomes are increasing, but savings rates are falling, discretionary consumption is soaring, and labour supply is shifting. These trends cannot be fully explained by standard price-inflation frameworks. The paper presents the notion of aspirational inflation-the behavioural intensification of perceived income requirements based on upward social comparison and digitally mediated reference groups instead of market price movements-and operationalises it using a new Aspirational Inflation Index (AII). Based on a mixed-methods design, which involves a primary survey of 328 urban middle-income households in five major Indian cities with secondary data on the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) 2022-23, we estimate OLS regression models to test four hypotheses of AII with respect to savings rates, discretionary consumption shares, labour supply, and the moderating effect of digital exposure. The AII is characterised by a high prevalence and distributional heterogeneity, and its construction is based on the dynamics of aspiration-gap and digital exposure. Regression outcomes indicate that the relationship between the AII and weekly labour hours is statistically significant (negative), whereas the relationship between savings and consumption is directional and not significant across sections. The main sample mean savings rate of 8.29 per cent is far below the national middle-income level of 18-20 per cent, indicating structural aspirational erosion. The research adds to the growing body of literature on the economics of consumption in the digital age and provides policy recommendations to financial regulators and digital governance bodies in India.

title: Constructive Gauges: Remediating Parasitic Liquidity in Concentrated Liquidity Emissions

detail.title: Constructive Gauges: Remediating Parasitic Liquidity in Concentrated Liquidity Emissions
detail.abstract: In ve(3,3) protocols, concentrated-liquidity gauges distribute voter-directed emissions via the Synthetix reward accumulator, which measures instantaneous staked liquidity rather than the sustained tradeable depth the protocol intends to incentivise. That gap creates the parasitic-extraction vector of , with three enabling properties: duration, width, and utilisation. This paper proposes constructive gauges, a corrective framework in which a position’s emission share is proportional to S = L · c(w) · f(t − t<sub>i</sub>) · 1[&tau; &isin; range], scaling nominal liquidity L by a concentration weight c non-increasing in range width, a freshness weight f non-increasing in time-since-rebalance, and an in-range indicator. Each multiplier addresses one enabling property of the vulnerability, so emissions track a multiplicative proxy for tradeable depth. Three theorems establish the framework’s properties. Under a Brownian log-price model and a large-N mean-field regime, parasitic revenue is bounded by the product of a freshness ratio and a concentration ratio (Theorem 1). The same product, evaluated over the LP’s in-range time, bounds the drag on good-faith LPs to a few percent at the median cadence in the operational dataset (Theorem 2). Within the product family of scoring functions over subsets of {c, f, 1}, the full set is the unique subset closing each parasitic pathway (short-cycle, out-of-range, width arbitrage); the characterisation requires no price model or population assumption (Theorem 3). Fork tests against live Aerodrome Slipstream on Base and cross-chain replications on PancakeSwap V3 (BSC), Thena FUSION (BSC), and Ramses V2 (Arbitrum) reproduce the scoring function’s three qualitative properties. The Gaussian in-range probability of Theorem 1 is validated against 31,912 live Swap events from two Aerodrome CL100 pools, with long-cycle departures conservative and preserving the upper-bound property. Parameters are calibrated against an operational dataset of 94,469 rebalance events across 48 pools over a 38-day pre-migration window.

title: Inventory Management Efficiency and Its Relationship with Supply Chain Cost and Firm Performance: Evidence from Secondary Data Analysis

detail.title: Inventory Management Efficiency and Its Relationship with Supply Chain Cost and Firm Performance: Evidence from Secondary Data Analysis
detail.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine the impact of inventory management efficiency on supply chain cost and overall firm performance using secondary, data-driven evidence. Inventory management is a critical component of supply chain operations, directly influencing cost efficiency, working capital management, and service level performance (Christopher, 2016). Despite extensive theoretical development, many firms-particularly in emerging economies-continue to experience inefficiencies such as overstocking, stock-outs, and high holding costs due to suboptimal inventory decisions (Chen et al., 2005).

title: Climate accounting and IFRS S1/S2 Sustainability Disclosure Standards within the CEMAC sub region

detail.title: Climate accounting and IFRS S1/S2 Sustainability Disclosure Standards within the CEMAC sub region

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NONE
declarations.ethicsApproval: NONE
declarations.funderStatement: NONE

detail.abstract:
Background

This article provides an in-depth analysis of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards IFRS S2 (Climate-related Disclosures) with a focus on what CEMAC countries financial managers need to grasp in order to better navigate this emerging landscape issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) in June 2023. In short, IFRS S2 establish a global baseline for sustainability reporting that is aligned with financial reporting standards focusing on climate-specific risks, opportunities, and related financial impacts.

Value and objectives:

By integrating the rigor of financial reporting into sustainability disclosures, these standards effectively raise the bar with sustainability information that must be prepared by financial managers with the same quality controls, precision, and integration with financial statements as traditional accounting information. In this regard, with this shift CEMAC countries financial managers must take a central role in sustainability reporting, overseeing governance, assurance, data collection, and presentation of sustainability metrics in tandem with financial statements.

Methodology:

In order to achieve the above paper objectives, a thorough literature review was conducted with the focus on climate accounting and IFRS S1/S2 Sustainability Disclosure Standards.

Findings:

With the increase of global investor demand and regulation forcing widespread adoption of IFRS S1/S2 standards, the results show that worldwide many companies are experiencing tangible value beyond compliance from integrating sustainability data into strategy and operations.

Recommendations:

The findings recommend CEMAC countries financial managers to elevate sustainability disclosure to the same governance and control environment as financial reporting with effective implementation requiring cross-functional collaboration, new potentially external assurance. In fine, CEMAC countries financial managers should proactively lead their companies’ preparation for IFRS S1/S2, investing in people, processes, and technology to collect high-quality, auditable ESG data and to tell a credible, finance-linked sustainability story to stakeholders.

title: Assessing the Economic Sustainability of Tobacco Production in North Macedonia: A Data-Driven Approach

detail.title: Assessing the Economic Sustainability of Tobacco Production in North Macedonia: A Data-Driven Approach

detail.abstract: This paper assesses the economic sustainability of tobacco production in North Macedonia using a data-driven approach based on field survey data and quantitative analysis. The study is motivated by the ongoing structural changes in the agricultural sector, rising production costs, and increasing pressure for modernization and sustainability. The empirical analysis is based on a survey conducted among tobacco producers in the Pelagonia region, with a sample of 120 farms. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and regression modeling are applied to identify the key determinants of economic sustainability. The results indicate that labor costs represent the dominant component of total production costs, accounting for approximately 45-50%, while labor availability emerges as a critical constraint, identified by over 40% of respondents. Furthermore, the findings show that small-scale farms continue to dominate the production structure, representing more than 70% of the sample, while contract farming plays a significant role in reducing market uncertainty, with around 80% of producers engaged in contractual arrangements. However, a substantial proportion of farmers report limited bargaining power, highlighting structural inefficiencies within the value chain. The study concludes that tobacco production in North Macedonia remains economically viable, but highly sensitive to labor dynamics, cost structures, and policy support. The paper contributes to the existing literature by providing empirical evidence and offers policy-relevant insights for improving the long-term sustainability of the sector.

title: Debanked: The Economic and Social Consequences of Anti-Money Laundering Regulation

detail.title: Debanked: The Economic and Social Consequences of Anti-Money Laundering Regulation
detail.abstract:
This paper argues that the widespread closure of bank accounts is primarily driven by anti-money laundering (AML) regulations rather than political bias. The paper explains that strict compliance requirements and heavy penalties make certain customers too costly or risky for banks to serve, leading to their exclusion even when they are not involved in wrongdoing.

 It contends that AML regulations impose substantial economic costs while offering limited evidence of effectiveness in reducing financial crime. The resulting debanking has significant social consequences, including reduced financial inclusion and negative impacts on businesses, charities, and individuals. The paper concludes that these regulations should be reformed or scaled back to reduce unnecessary exclusion and improve transparency around their true costs.

title: Revision of the Digital Bancor Concept in Next-Generation International Financial Infrastructure Deterministic Macroeconomic Control via Absolute Equations and the Overcoming of Neoliberalism

detail.title: Revision of the Digital Bancor Concept in Next-Generation International Financial Infrastructure Deterministic Macroeconomic Control via Absolute Equations and the Overcoming of Neoliberalism

keywords: CBDC NTA White Paper | Digital Bancor

detail.abstract: The global financial architecture is currently at a critical juncture, facing the limitations of the post-Bretton Woods system and the systemic instabilities inherent in neoliberalism. This paper proposes the "Digital Bancor" concept as a core component of a New Total Architecture (NTA). Drawing upon Wicksellian cumulative process theory and the critique of neoliberalism's drive for zero-resistance (R → 0) markets, the author argues that current economic volatility results from positive feedback loops within stochastic, psychologically-driven systems. To address this, the paper introduces a deterministic macroeconomic control framework based on the "Absolute Equation" of work efficiency: W_eff = Q × V-R_noise. Leveraging the Innovative Optical and Wireless Network (IOWN) and the deterministic real-time operating system TRON, the proposed architecture implements Fractional-Order PID (FOPID) control on international capital flows. This "Physical Macroeconomic OS" prevents systemic runaway by algorithmically dissipating speculative heat, ensuring global economic stability beyond the Triffin dilemma.

title: The Precondition Problem

detail.title: The Precondition Problem
detail.abstract:
This paper introduces and theorizes the precondition problem in Customer Support work: a structural phenomenon in which organizational incoherence across upstream functions creates gaps in shared understanding between agents and customers about what the social contract actually obligates. Drawing on social contract theory, Seddon's failure demand framework, Goffman's theory of face-work and the expressive order, and the Conversational Integrity Model (van Dijk, 2026), the paper argues that agents are structurally responsible for establishing and maintaining preconditions in real time despite receiving contradictory information from the organization that employs them. This creates a distinct occupational challenge that existing service quality and Customer Support frameworks do not address.

The paper maps the structural sources of precondition failures in organizational terms, examines how these failures manifest in agent-customer interaction, and analyzes the relational consequences for both customers and agents. It introduces four theoretical constructs: entry tractability and trajectory tractability, which make precondition quality operable in quality assessment contexts; occupational corrosion, which names an erosive occupational trajectory distinct from standard burnout frameworks, generated specifically by the frequency of unspeakable contradiction; and unspeakable contradictions, which identifies a category of organizational incoherence so structurally acute that no honest agent response can simultaneously preserve both relational and organizational integrity. The paper positions Customer Support as a diagnostic instrument for organizational health and argues that measuring precondition quality requires instruments not captured by existing metrics.

detail.abstract: O presente resumo analisa a metamorfose estrutural do futebol brasileiro a partir da transição do modelo associativo tradicional para um ecossistema complexo de entretenimento e negócios, fundamentando-se nas perspectivas de Evandro Ferreira Gomes sobre a implementação das Sociedades Anônimas do Futebol (SAFs) e a ascensão das casas de apostas. A discussão central demonstra que a adoção da SAF surge como uma resposta necessária ao endividamento histórico dos clubes, embora carregue o risco de uma financeirização excessiva que pode transformar as instituições em ativos meramente especulativos, distanciando investidores da identidade cultural das torcidas. Paralelamente, o estudo aborda a onipresença das empresas de apostas esportivas, destacando que, apesar do aporte financeiro vital para a competitividade técnica, essa dependência gera desafios éticos significativos, como o perigo da manipulação de resultados e os impactos sociais da ludopatia, fatores que colocam em risco a credibilidade e a integridade do esporte. O texto também ressalta o avanço na profissionalização da gestão e do marketing esportivo nos últimos quinze anos, enfatizando a importância da governança corporativa e da diversidade, com destaque para a crescente participação feminina em cargos diretivos. Por fim, argumenta-se que espaços de debate e inovação são essenciais para transformar o país em um polo de inteligência em gestão, concluindo que a sustentabilidade do futebol na era da economia criativa depende do equilíbrio rigoroso entre a busca pela rentabilidade financeira e a preservação da confiança do público e da ética esportiva.

title: Intellectual Property Philosophies and Brand Strategies: Converging Theories and Integrative Approaches
