detail.abstract: This research extends the examination of intellectual property (IP) law by delving into its intricate relationship with branding in the contemporary marketplace. Building on foundational philosophical theories such as John Locke's Labour Theory, Hegelian Personality Theory, and utilitarianism, the study explores how these theories influence both the legal frameworks and strategic dimensions of branding. Branding is positioned as a vital form of intellectual capital that transcends trademarks and logos, embodying corporate identities and fostering emotional connections with consumers. The research investigates the alignment of IP philosophies with branding objectives, highlighting the role of IP law in protecting and promoting brand identities. Furthermore, the study examines the Economic Theory of IP, emphasizing its impact on innovation and creativity in brand development, alongside the Theory of Social Good, which considers brands’ contributions to societal welfare and cultural richness. The Democratic Theory and Theory of Justice are also explored to understand brand equity and equitable access to cultural symbols. Through real-world case studies, the research demonstrates the practical linkages of IP philosophies on branding strategies, illustrating the balance between creator rights and the public interest, as well as the ethical considerations in brand protection and development. This exploration reveals the dynamic interplay between legal and philosophical frameworks, offering a nuanced understanding of how IP law and branding collectively shape the global marketplace and cultural landscape.

title: What Every AI Job Study Gets Wrong: A Framework for Predicting How Much AI Will Actually Transform Each Occupation

detail.title: What Every AI Job Study Gets Wrong: A Framework for Predicting How Much AI Will Actually Transform Each Occupation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is employed by Microsoft Corporation, which develops and sells AI products including Microsoft 365 Copilot. The analysis and opinions in this paper are the author's own and do not represent the views of Microsoft. The framework was developed independently and no funding was received for this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: n/a
declarations.funderStatement: n/a self funded

detail.abstract:
Existing research on AI's labor market impact focuses predominantly on exposure—measuring which occupations' tasks AI can technically perform. While valuable, exposure metrics alone cannot predict which occupations will actually experience transformation, because they ignore the institutional, economic, regulatory, and social barriers that mediate technology adoption.

Massenkoff and McCrory (2026) empirically demonstrate that actual AI adoption remains a fraction of theoretical capability: in Computer and Mathematical occupations, AI could theoretically handle 94% of tasks, yet professional usage covers only 33%. A similar gap exists across virtually every occupation category but is not uniform—Management and Healthcare show larger gaps while Office and Administrative Support shows a smaller one. Existing studies document this gap without offering a framework to explain why it exists or predict how it will close.

This paper argues that convergence will be highly uneven and occupation-specific, and in some cases the gap will persist indefinitely. I introduce the PRIME framework—five categories of deployment barriers (Policy, Resources, Inertia, Market acceptance, Error tolerance)—that collectively explain why AI capability does not translate uniformly into adoption. Each category encompasses multiple sub-dimensions, forming a comprehensive taxonomy of adoption friction.

Applying PRIME across 22 major U.S. occupation categories (121 sub-occupations, 150+ million workers), I generate transformation predictions using a three-axis model: AI Capability (current), AI Capability (predicted, 3–5 years), and composite PRIME barriers. Results map to four levels—Radical Restructuring, Significant Transformation, Moderate Transformation, and Minimal Change—describing how extensively each occupation's tasks will incorporate AI. This paper predicts how occupations will transform—not whether employment will rise or fall, which depends on market demand outside the framework's scope.

The analysis reveals that occupations with identical exposure scores face divergent futures (judges and paralegals share similar AI capability scores but face opposite trajectories), and that the exposure–adoption gap is a structural feature of high-barrier occupations, not a temporary lag. Early empirical evidence from independent sources is consistent with the framework's predictions. The framework is grounded in practitioner observation of enterprise AI deployment and is offered as a theoretical contribution with an explicit call for empirical validation.

title: AI Applications in Supply Chain Optimization for Enhancing Business Efficiency

detail.title: AI Applications in Supply Chain Optimization for Enhancing Business Efficiency
detail.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into supply chain management represents a paradigm shift in how modern enterprises achieve operational excellence and competitive advantage. This paper examines the transformative potential of AI technologies in optimizing supply chain processes, from demand forecasting to logistics coordination. Through systematic analysis of machine learning algorithms, predictive analytics, and automation systems, this research demonstrates how AI driven solutions enable organizations to reduce costs, improve forecasting accuracy, accelerate decision-making, and enhance customer satisfaction. Drawing upon empirical evidence from industry leaders including Amazon, Walmart, and Unilever, the study illustrates tangible outcomes of AI implementation while acknowledging critical challenges such as data quality constraints, integration complexities, and ethical considerations. The findings indicate that AI-powered supply chains achieve 15-20% reduction in logistics costs and 35-50% improvement in forecast accuracy compared to traditional approaches. This paper concludes with strategic recommendations for organizations embarking on digital transformation journeys, emphasizing the necessity of phased implementation, robust data infrastructure, and continuous learning frameworks to maximize return on investment and sustain long-term competitive positioning in increasingly volatile global markets.

title: TRANSITIONING PROPERTY REGISTRATION IN INDIA: A COMPARATIVE AND STAKEHOLDER-CENTRIC ANALYSIS OF THE REGISTRATION BILL, 2025 VIS-À-VIS THE REGISTRATION ACT, 1908

detail.title: TRANSITIONING PROPERTY REGISTRATION IN INDIA: A COMPARATIVE AND STAKEHOLDER-CENTRIC ANALYSIS OF THE REGISTRATION BILL, 2025 VIS-À-VIS THE REGISTRATION ACT, 1908
detail.abstract: The legal framework governing property registration in India continues to be anchored in the Registration Act, 1908, a statute designed for a vastly different socioeconomic and administrative context. While the Act has historically served as a mechanism for recording transactions and providing evidentiary value, its reliance on manual processes, fragmented record systems, and a presumptive title regime has rendered it increasingly inadequate in addressing modern challenges such as fraud, delays, and transactional opacity. In response, the Draft Registration Bill, 2025 proposes a significant shift towards a technology-driven registration system, introducing provisions for digital registration, integration with land records, and enhanced identity verification mechanisms. However, this paper argues that the transition to a digital framework, while necessary, is not sufficient in itself to resolve the deeper structural deficiencies embedded within the existing system. The Bill does not fully address persistent concerns relating to title uncertainty, data protection, digital exclusion, and the constitutional balance between the Union and the States in matters of land governance. Through a critical analysis of the proposed reforms, this study highlights the gap between technological advancement and legal certainty. The paper concludes that although the Registration Bill, 2025 represents an important step towards modernisation, its effectiveness will ultimately depend on the incorporation of robust safeguards, institutional coordination, and an inclusive implementation strategy that goes beyond digitisation to ensure transparency, accessibility, and trust in property transactions.

title: MEMBINA JAMBATAN MERENTASI LAUT CHINA SELATAN: ANALISIS NARATIF PERBANDINGAN AMALAN TERBAIK KESATUAN SEKERJA BORNEO UTARA (SABAH) DAN SARAWAK DALAM ERA KECERDASAN BUATAN

detail.title: MEMBINA JAMBATAN MERENTASI LAUT CHINA SELATAN: ANALISIS NARATIF PERBANDINGAN AMALAN TERBAIK KESATUAN SEKERJA BORNEO UTARA (SABAH) DAN SARAWAK DALAM ERA KECERDASAN BUATAN
detail.abstract: Perkembangan pesat kecerdasan buatan (Artificial Intelligence, AI) telah mengubah landskap pekerjaan global dan mencabar peranan tradisional kesatuan sekerja. Kajian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis amalan terbaik kesatuan sekerja di Sabah dan Sarawak melalui pendekatan analisis naratif perbandingan dalam konteks era AI. Kajian ini menggunakan data sekunder daripada jurnal akademik dan laporan organisasi antarabangsa untuk menilai tahap adaptasi teknologi, strategi perlindungan pekerja dan kekuatan institusi kesatuan sekerja di kedua-dua wilayah. Dapatan menunjukkan bahawa kesatuan sekerja di Sarawak lebih tersusun dalam sektor formal dan lebih proaktif dalam mengadaptasi teknologi, manakala di Sabah lebih menekankan pendekatan komuniti dalam memperkukuh kesedaran pekerja. Kajian ini menekankan kepentingan kerjasama antara wilayah sebagai satu bentuk "jambatan" strategik bagi meningkatkan keberkesanan kesatuan sekerja dalam menghadapi cabaran digitalisasi.

title: Concept of Decision Making in Team Behavior: A Literature Review on Structures, Voice Centralization, and Consensus

detail.title: Concept of Decision Making in Team Behavior: A Literature Review on Structures, Voice Centralization, and Consensus
detail.abstract:
This paper discusses the concept of decision making in team behavior. The 
background of the problem is that modern organizations increasingly rely on teams 
as their main decision making unit, but many teams still struggle to manage their 
collective decision making process. The research questions in this paper include 
what are the forms of decision making in teams, what factors affect the quality of 
team decisions, and what are the practical implications of these theories for 
organizations. The purpose of this paper is to identify the forms of decision making 
in teams, analyze the factors that affect the quality of team decisions, and formulate 
practical implications for organizations. The benefits of this paper consist of 
theoretical benefits, which are to enrich the study of organizational behavior 
especially about team decision making, and practical benefits, which are to provide 
guidance for managers and team leaders in managing the decision making process 
more effectively. The method used is literature study by analyzing eight Scopus
journal articles published between 2024 and 2025. The results show that there are 
four forms of decision making in teams: unanimous, voting, lead entrepreneur, and 
delegation. The factors that affect the quality of team decisions include the chosen 
decision structure, the process of centralizing voice on competent members, the 
level of consensus achieved, and the extent to which team members are involved in 
the process. Research also finds that participation in decision making has a positive 
impact on organizational commitment, organizational citizenship behavior, and 
group cohesion. The conclusion of this paper is that no single decision structure is 
always best, centralizing voice on competent members is beneficial as long as it is 
not excessive, healthy consensus must consider the variation of opinions, and team 
involvement is very important especially in crisis situations.

title: MAKE YOUR MOVE: IMPLEMENTING A SMART DIGITAL BOOKING AND MARKETPLACE SOLUTION TO EMPOWER CLIENTS, BEAUTY PROFESSIONALS, AND LOCAL ENTREPRENEURS An Undergraduate Capstone Project Presented to the Information Technology Education Program Davao Central College Toril, Davao City In Partial Fulfilment of the Requirements in Capstone Project

detail.title: MAKE YOUR MOVE: IMPLEMENTING A SMART DIGITAL BOOKING AND MARKETPLACE SOLUTION TO EMPOWER CLIENTS, BEAUTY PROFESSIONALS, AND LOCAL ENTREPRENEURS An Undergraduate Capstone Project Presented to the Information Technology Education Program Davao Central College Toril, Davao City In Partial Fulfilment of the Requirements in Capstone Project
detail.abstract: Beauty services have long been a cultural staple, yet traditional booking methods remain largely manual, leading to inefficiencies such as long wait times and scheduling conflicts. This study aims to modernize these transactions by developing "Make Your Move," a digital booking system designed to address limited review options, overlapping schedules, and improper documentation. The research followed an Agile Scrum methodology and included a pilot deployment at YanYan Parlor to test system functionality. Data was collected through User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and surveys involving 19 customer respondents, including debutantes and students. The major findings revealed a 100% review capture rate, a 94.74% Net Promoter Score (NPS), and a reduction in booking errors to just 5%. The study concludes that integrating digital tools into local beauty services significantly enhances operational efficiency, transparency, and customer trust.

title: Superjustice: Law in the Age of Artificial Intelligence — Introduction
affiliations: Victoria University of Wellington  and University of Toronto - Faculty of Law

detail.title: Superjustice: Law in the Age of Artificial Intelligence — Introduction

publicationDetails.detailsText: Superjustice: Law in the Age of Artificial Intelligence (Oxford University Press, 2026). ISBN: 978019899

detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming legal systems worldwide, yet the prevailing frameworks for integrating AI into legal systems remain inadequate. Current approaches often underestimate AI’s emerging capabilities while permitting unstructured, haphazard adoption. This book introduces Superjustice: a paradigm for leveraging AI to make legal systems more accessible, efficient, participatory, and equitable. Drawing on developments in large language models (LLMs), machine learning, natural language processing, and data-driven governance, the book argues that the growing disconnect between technological progress and legal stasis presents both extraordinary risk and a moment of opportunity for fundamental legal transformation.

The book proceeds in three parts. Part I establishes the conceptual foundations. It first identifies ten structural ailments of centralized legal systems, which we call the “Ten Pillars of Legal Dysfunctionality.” It then develops hybrid models of decentralized legal governance. It also explores how data-driven approaches, including personalized law, can help move legal systems from gridlock toward dynamism.

Part II turns to implementation. It examines the evolving relationship between human judgment and AI capabilities in adjudication and revisits the human-in-the-loop principle. It also introduces the concept of “Justice as a Service.” It then analyzes implications for legal education, professional roles, and the democratization of legal knowledge.

Part III adopts a systemic perspective. It first examines the future of justice work, including emerging professional roles, AI-augmented adjudication, and changing legal business models. It then presents CRISPR-J—Cost-effective, Rapid, Inclusive, Smart, Predictive, and Resilient Justice—as a design framework for AI-enabled legal systems. Finally, it introduces a Dynamic Challenges Matrix for analyzing the technical, human, governance, and societal dimensions of legal transformation.

Throughout, the book engages with concerns regarding algorithmic transparency, AI bias and hallucination, data privacy, the digital divide, and the preservation of procedural justice and institutional legitimacy. It calls for a proactive approach that seizes the opportunity to redesign legal systems to better advance human flourishing. This Introduction sets out the book’s thesis, situates it within current debates on AI and law, and maps the full argument. The table of contents for the complete book is included.

Samuel I. Becher and Benjamin Alarie, Superjustice: Law in the Age of Artificial Intelligence (Oxford University Press, 2026); https://global.oup.com/academic/product/superjustice-9780198991908.

title: EVENTWISE: DEVELOPMENT OF AN INTEGRATED EVENT PLANNING AND COORDINATION MANAGEMENT INFORMATION SYSTEM An Undergraduate Capstone Project Presented to the Information Technology Education Program Davao Central College Toril, Davao City In Partial Fulfilment of the Requirements in Capstone Project

detail.title: EVENTWISE: DEVELOPMENT OF AN INTEGRATED EVENT PLANNING AND COORDINATION MANAGEMENT INFORMATION SYSTEM An Undergraduate Capstone Project Presented to the Information Technology Education Program Davao Central College Toril, Davao City In Partial Fulfilment of the Requirements in Capstone Project
detail.abstract:
The event planning industry relies heavily on effective communication, collaboration, and timely coordination among event planners, clients, and vendors to ensure successful event execution. However, many event planning processes, particularly in Davao City, still depend on fragmented and manual communication methods such as phone calls, text messages, and emails. These practices often result in poor communication, limited collaboration, and inadequate updates for clients, leading to delays, misunderstandings, and reduced client satisfaction. This study aimed to design and develop EventWise, an integrated event planning and coordination management information system that addresses these challenges by centralizing communication, task management, and real-time updates in a single digital platform.

 

The study employed a descriptive developmental research design. System requirements were gathered through interviews and observations involving event planners and clients. A survey questionnaire was conducted among 30 respondents, consisting of event planners and event clients in Davao City, to evaluate the system’s usability, functionality, and effectiveness. The survey instrument was validated through expert validation by information technology professionals and event management practitioners to ensure reliability and content validity.

 

The results indicated that EventWise significantly improved communication efficiency, collaboration frequency, and the timeliness of client updates. Respondents rated the system highly in terms of usability, real-time coordination, and overall effectiveness in addressing communication gaps during the event planning process. Findings also showed an increase in client engagement and satisfaction due to improved transparency and progress tracking.

 

In conclusion, EventWise proved to be an effective digital solution for enhancing event planning and coordination. The system demonstrates the potential of integrated management information systems in improving operational efficiency, stakeholder collaboration, and client satisfaction in the local event planning industry.

title: The Role of Organizational Citizenship Behavior in Enhancing Employee Self-Development: A Review from an Organizational Behavior Perspective

detail.title: The Role of Organizational Citizenship Behavior in Enhancing Employee Self-Development: A Review from an Organizational Behavior Perspective
detail.abstract: This study examines the role of Organizational Citizenship Behavior (OCB) in enhancing employee self-development from an organizational behavior perspective. OCB refers to discretionary behavior beyond formal job requirements that contributes to organizational effectiveness. Using a literature review approach, this study explores how OCB supports experiential learning, skill improvement, proactive attitudes, and social competence development. The findings indicate that employees who engage in OCB tend to gain broader work experiences and strengthen their interpersonal and professional capabilities. The study also finds that the relationship between OCB and self-development is reciprocal, as development activities may also reflect citizenship behavior. However, the positive impact of OCB depends on supportive organizational conditions, including leadership, mentoring, and organizational climate. Overall, OCB can enhance employee selfdevelopment and serve as a strategic mechanism for sustainable human resource development.

title: Efficiency of Municipal Waste Sorting Infrastructure under Regulatory and Market Variability: An Integrated Framework

detail.title: Efficiency of Municipal Waste Sorting Infrastructure under Regulatory and Market Variability: An Integrated Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is affiliated with a company operating in the waste management sector. The study is of a conceptual and analytical nature and does not promote any specific technological solutions.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
This study addresses the problem of evaluating the efficiency of municipal waste sorting infrastructure under conditions of regulatory and market variability. Existing approaches typically assess performance either in purely economic terms or within single-dimensional frameworks, which limits their ability to capture interactions between technological performance, system conditions, and multiple categories of outcomes.

To address this limitation, the study develops and applies an integrated analytical framework linking system variability (S), technological effectiveness (T), and adaptive capacity (A). Integrated efficiency is defined as the relationship between aggregated effects and total inputs, evaluated relative to system-dependent benchmarks.

The framework is applied through a structured scenario-based analysis, including the introduction of deposit-refund systems, the absence or instability of extended producer responsibility mechanisms, and changes in waste stream morphology.

The results demonstrate that regulatory and market variability systematically disrupts the alignment between system conditions and technological configuration, leading to a deterioration of integrated efficiency. This decline is driven by simultaneous reductions in economic and environmental effects and increases in resource intensity. Adaptive capacity is identified as a key mechanism enabling the system to stabilise performance and partially restore efficiency under changing conditions.

The study contributes by reconceptualising efficiency as a dynamic and system-conditioned property, and by providing a framework that integrates economic, environmental, and social dimensions without assuming their full substitutability. The proposed approach offers a basis for evaluating and designing waste management infrastructure under conditions of system variability.

title: Analysis of Leadership Styles and Their Impact on Individual and Group

detail.title: Analysis of Leadership Styles and Their Impact on Individual and Group
detail.abstract: The style of leadership is widely acknowledged as a vital element affecting both individual and collective behavior within organizations. This paper intends to examine how varying leadership styles impact attitudes, effectiveness, and interactions among members of an organization. Using established theories such as transformational, transactional, and ethical leadership, this research takes a conceptual view to investigate behavioral results at both the individual and group levels. At the individual level, leadership affects psychological empowerment, motivation, and job satisfaction. At the group level, leadership influences communication patterns, team cohesion, and overall effectiveness. The results indicate that leadership styles that prioritize inspiration, participation, and ethical principles generally yield more favorable outcomes compared to rigid or transactional styles. Consequently, organizations should embrace flexible leadership strategies to improve both individual growth and group performance.

title: Transformational Leadership and Organizational Climate as Predictors of OCB

detail.title: Transformational Leadership and Organizational Climate as Predictors of OCB
detail.abstract: Organizational Citizenship Behavior (OCB) has been recognized as a key factor in modern organizational effectiveness. However, the fundamental question of how a healthy organizational behavior ecosystem particularly transformational leadership (TL) and organizational climate (OC) shapes OCB remains debated. This paper aims to reconstruct the understanding of this relationship through a critical review of various empirical studies across the SME, education, banking, hospital, and public service sectors. Using Social Exchange Theory, Transformational Leadership Theory, and Social Bond Theory as foundations, this paper identifies that TL and OC consistently exert a positive influence on OCB. Nevertheless, this relationship is not linear; job satisfaction, affective commitment, and dispositional factors such as self efficacy and locus of control act as significant mediators or moderators. Contradictory findings regarding the role of organizational commitment as a mediator which failed in certain collectivist cultural contexts highlight the importance of contextual sensitivity. This paper also critiques common methodological weaknesses and introduces a warning about "citizenship pressure" as a potential dark side of OCB. In conclusion, good organizational behavior leads to OCB conditionally, not deterministically.

title: Principles of Research Methodology Concepts & Applications

detail.title: Principles of Research Methodology Concepts & Applications
detail.abstract: A lucid framework connecting established concepts with practical steps, Principles of Research Methodology: Concepts & Applications takes the reader through each phase of research: defining a problem, exploring existing literature, devising an effective plan, gathering relevant data, analyzing the findings and presenting conclusions. It underscores the importance of aligning the research question with relevant theory and methodology, thereby instilling confidence in the validity of research results. Additionally, it examines the ethics inherent in research and explores forward - looking approaches, such as the use of artificial intelligence and research based on data. This comprehensive textbook is a must - read for any student, faculty or professional involved in designing, executing or evaluating research within any academic field. It presents the fundamental tools required to conduct efficient, reliable and significant research.

title: Understanding Theories Inorganizational behavior

detail.title: Understanding Theories Inorganizational behavior
detail.abstract: Organizational Behavior (OB) is a field of study that examines how individuals and groups behave within an organization and how these behaviors influence organizational performance. This paper aims to explore and understand several key theories in organizational behavior, including classical theory, human relations theory, contingency theory, and modern organizational behavior approaches. These theories are important because they provide different perspectives in explaining how employees think, feel, and act in the workplace. The discussion in this paper shows that organizational behavior has developed from a focus on efficiency to a more human-centered and flexible approach. By understanding and combining these theories, organizations can improve employee performance, motivation, and overall effectiveness. Therefore, the study of organizational behavior is essential for students, managers, and organizations in facing today's dynamic work environment.

title: Organizational Behaviour and Group Dynamics: An Integrative Analysis of Individual, Group, And Organizational Processes in Organizational Behaviour Courses

detail.title: Organizational Behaviour and Group Dynamics: An Integrative Analysis of Individual, Group, And Organizational Processes in Organizational Behaviour Courses
detail.abstract: This paper explores the relationship between organizational behaviour and group dynamics by integrating five key sources that address individual behaviour, group decision-making, social perception, and organizational practices. The findings indicate that organizational behaviour is shaped by complex interactions between psychological, social, and structural factors. While individual behaviour forms the foundation, group dynamics significantly influence decision quality, particularly through processes such as groupthink and vigilance. Additionally, social perceptions of groups affect interpersonal relationships, and a gap exists between theoretical knowledge and actual organizational practices. Therefore, an integrative and critical approach is necessary to fully understand and effectively manage organizational behaviour and group dynamics in contemporary organizations.

title: New Paternalism Meets Older Wisdom
affiliations: Mercatus Center at George Mason University

detail.title: New Paternalism Meets Older Wisdom
detail.abstract: This paper explores the convergence between contemporary “new paternalism”, particularly behavioural interventions such as nudges, and longstanding philosophical traditions that have historically justified guidance-oriented governance. It argues that while new paternalism presents itself as a novel, empirically grounded approach rooted in behavioural economics, many of its core principles echo older forms of moral and political thought, emphasising human fallibility, bounded rationality, and the legitimacy of structured choice environments. By comparing modern policy tools with insights from classical philosophy and earlier governance frameworks, the paper highlights both continuities and tensions, especially concerning autonomy, legitimacy, and the role of the state. Ultimately, it contends that integrating older ethical wisdom can both deepen the normative foundations of new paternalism and expose its limitations, encouraging a more reflective and balanced application in public policy.

title: Pay Range Disclosure Laws and the Gender Pay Gap
affiliations: University of Pittsburgh - Katz Graduate School of Business and University of Pittsburgh - Katz Graduate School of Business

detail.title: Pay Range Disclosure Laws and the Gender Pay Gap
detail.abstract: Many state and local governments in the United States have implemented pay transparency laws requiring employers to disclose pay ranges in job postings. These policies are intended to reduce wage inequality by limiting pay secrecy and strengthening workers’ ability to negotiate compensation, particularly for groups historically subject to underpayment. This study empirically evaluates the impact of pay range disclosure laws on the gender pay gap. Exploiting the staggered adoption of mandatory pay disclosure requirements across U.S. states, we use a difference-in-differences research design using individual-level wage data from the American Community Survey (ACS). We find that the gender pay gap declines significantly following the implementation of mandatory pay range disclosure laws. The reduction is larger in settings where workers have greater potential bargaining power and in labor market segments in which women are more likely to be underpaid previously. We also document an increase in female labor force participation and employ Heckman selection models to address concerns that the observed narrowing of the pay gap is driven by changes in workforce composition. In contrast, we find no comparable effects for pay transparency laws that require pay disclosure only upon employee request. Overall, the findings provide evidence on the effect of mandatory pay range disclosure legislation on the gender pay gap and have important implications for policymakers.

title: The Dynamics of Exchange Rates and Their Impact on International Trade Performance in Emerging Economies Virga

detail.title: The Dynamics of Exchange Rates and Their Impact on International Trade Performance in Emerging Economies Virga
detail.abstract: Exchange rates play a crucial role in international finance by influencing trade flows, investment decisions, and economic stability. This study aims to analyze the impact of exchange rate fluctuations on international trade performance in emerging economies. The research employs a qualitative descriptive approach using secondary data obtained from international financial institutions, academic journals, and economic reports. The findings indicate that exchange rate volatility significantly affects export competitiveness, import costs, and trade balance. A depreciation of the domestic currency tends to boost exports but increases import costs, while appreciation may reduce export competitiveness. However, the effectiveness of exchange rate movements depends on economic structure, trade elasticity, and government policies. Therefore, appropriate exchange rate management and macroeconomic stability are essential to optimize trade performance.

title: From Output to Authority: Bridging the Decision Authority Gap in AI-Enabled Organizations through the DAG Framework

detail.title: From Output to Authority: Bridging the Decision Authority Gap in AI-Enabled Organizations through the DAG Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of Interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: Self

detail.abstract: The accelerated integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into organizational decision-making has fundamentally reshaped how information is generated, interpreted, and executed. While existing research has extensively examined AI performance, ethics, and human-AI collaboration, limited attention has been paid to the structural transition from AI-generated outputs to formally authorized decisions. This paper introduces the concept of the Decision Authority Gap (DAG)-a critical disconnect between output generation and decision ownership in AI-enabled environments. Drawing on perspectives from organizational theory, governance, and behavioral decision-making, the study proposes the DAG Framework, a fourlayer model comprising AI Output, Human Interpretation, Decision Authority, and Execution. The framework identifies the Decision Authority Layer as the 2 | P a g e central point of failure, where the absence of explicit ownership leads to accountability diffusion, unverified execution, and systemic risk. To bridge theory and practice, the paper introduces the Decision Authority Implementation Matrix (DAIM), a structured tool that enables organizations to audit and redesign AI-mediated decision processes. Supported by theoretical propositions and cross-sectoral illustrations in hiring, financial decisionmaking, and higher education admissions, the study demonstrates how authority ambiguity undermines both decision quality and governance integrity. By reframing AI adoption as a challenge of decision architecture rather than technological capability, this paper contributes a novel and actionable perspective to the discourse on responsible AI. The findings have implications for organizational leaders, policymakers, and researchers seeking to restore accountability and strengthen decision-making in increasingly automated environments.

title: How Exchange Rates Affect Import and Export Activities

detail.title: How Exchange Rates Affect Import and Export Activities
detail.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of exchange rates on import and export activities in international trade. Exchange rates are a key component in international finance because they determine the value of one currency relative to another, which directly affects the price of goods and services traded across countries. Changes in exchange rates can influence trade performance, investment decisions, and overall economic stability. This research uses a qualitative approach through a literature review method. Data are collected from books, academic journals, and reliable sources related to international finance. The analysis is conducted descriptively to explain the relationship between exchange rate fluctuations and trade activities. The results show that when a currency depreciates, exports tend to increase because domestic goods become cheaper for foreign buyers. However, imports become more expensive, which can increase production costs and inflation. Conversely, when a currency appreciates, imports become cheaper but exports decrease due to higher prices in global markets. In conclusion, exchange rates play an important role in shaping international trade. Stable exchange rates are necessary to support balanced trade and sustainable economic growth.

title: The Sovereign Duration Regulatory Blind Spot: Why Capital Adequacy Ratios Understate Systemic Risk During Monetary Tightening

detail.title: The Sovereign Duration Regulatory Blind Spot: Why Capital Adequacy Ratios Understate Systemic Risk During Monetary Tightening
detail.abstract: The world's financial system is currently experiencing the most extreme tightening cycle of monetary policy in 40 years; however, despite Capital Adequacy Ratios suggesting that banking systems remain well-capitalized, the failure of Silicon Valley Bank in 2023 highlighted a significant measurement gap in the global regulatory framework. This paper addresses the primary problem: that all sovereign debt securities are classified as "risk-free" under the Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) risk-weighting framework, while disregarding both the duration of risk and mark-tomarket losses. We propose a corrective measure, the Duration-Adjusted Capital Adequacy Ratio (DACAR), which requires banks to deduct a fraction of the unrealized losses on their Held-to-Maturity (HTM) sovereign bond portfolios, with the fraction determined by a continuous measure of monetary policy tightness. This measure, α, scales the adjustment based on the deviation of the policy rate from its long-term average. Using Brunnermeier and Sannikov's amplification model (2014) to calibrate the threshold, we present an econometric strategy to validate the predictive power of this measure via a Panel Logit Model with a Policy Interaction Term that isolates duration exposure based on the α-activation threshold. Additionally, this paper describes the theoretical and empirical basis for reforming the Basel III framework.

title: Misspecification Loss in Inventory Systems with Correlated Demand
affiliations: , The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, University of Illinois at Chicago - College of Business Administration and

detail.title: Misspecification Loss in Inventory Systems with Correlated Demand
detail.abstract: We study a periodic-review inventory system with positive lead time and correlated demand. While most inventory models assume independent demand for tractability, this simplification may lead to model misspecification in practice. We consider a decision maker who implements a myopic base-stock policy based on a misspecified i.i.d. model, while the true demand follows a stationary Gaussian AR(1) process. We derive closed-form expressions for the optimal policy under the true model and for the cost of the misspecified policy, and quantify misspecification loss via a competitive ratio. Our results show that longer lead times do not necessarily amplify misspecification loss. In particular, when demand exhibits positive correlation, increasing the lead time can attenuate the impact of misspecification. At the same time, this misspecification becomes increasingly consequential when backlog penalties are high. Under positive correlation, underestimation of uncertainty leads to persistent understocking and substantial losses, whereas under negative correlation, misspecification induces overstocking and the resulting loss is less sensitive to stockout penalties. Overall, the cost of using a simplified demand model depends not only on demand variability, but also on whether demand exhibits persistence or reversal over time and the relative costs of backlog versus excess inventory.

title: A Mathematical Framework for Quantifying Opportunities, Calculating Chances, and Predicting Future Outcomes in Real-Life Decision Making

detail.title: A Mathematical Framework for Quantifying Opportunities, Calculating Chances, and Predicting Future Outcomes in Real-Life Decision Making
detail.abstract: Human beings make hundreds of decisions daily, yet the cognitive tools most people employ remain largely intuitive, emotionally driven, and systematically biased. This concept paper introduces The Possibilities Formula (TPF) — a structured mathematical framework that quantifies opportunity, weighs probabilistic outcomes, and guides rational decision-making across real-life domains including career planning, entrepreneurship, education, relationships, and financial choices. Drawing from probability theory, expected utility, Bayesian inference, and scenario modelling, TPF translates subjective life choices into measurable Possibility Scores. The paper presents the core formula, twelve derived sub-formulas, the SCORE operationalisation protocol, three-scenario composite scoring, five detailed case studies with real statistics, a comparative table of advantages, and a rigorous appraisal of limitations with directions for future empirical research. Historical milestones in decision science from Pascal (1654) to Kahneman and Tversky (1979) contextualise TPF within its intellectual lineage.

title: "WE ARE ALL HERD ANIMALS": COMMUNITY AND ORGANIZATIONALITY IN COWORKING SPACES

detail.title: "WE ARE ALL HERD ANIMALS": COMMUNITY AND ORGANIZATIONALITY IN COWORKING SPACES
detail.abstract: This paper develops an understanding of coworking spaces as organizational phenomena. Based on an ethnography of betahaus in Berlin, we demonstrate how coworking spaces not only provide a sense of community but also pattern the work activities of their members. We theorize this finding by drawing on the emergent literature on organizationality. Our contribution is twofold. First, we challenge current understandings of coworking spaces as neutral containers for independent work. Instead, we show how coworking incorporates the disposition of becoming organizational. That is, coworking spaces can frame and organize work and may even provide a basis for collective action. Second, we add to research on organizing outside traditional organizations by drawing attention to the complex and shifting interplay of formal and informal relationships in such settings. In so doing, we inform current debates about new forms of organization and organizing.

title: Interpretive Drift: Demanding a New Kind of Leader in a World That No Longer Stabilizes

detail.title: Interpretive Drift: Demanding a New Kind of Leader in a World That No Longer Stabilizes
detail.abstract:
Interpretive drift — the silent erosion of alignment between an organization’s governing premises and the emerging logic of what creates value — is the defining leadership challenge of a world that no longer stabilizes. Its defining feature is not speed but concealment: it operates while performance remains acceptable, driven by the same success that makes it undiscerned within the prevailing logic. The central mechanism is this: as governing premises are validated through repeated success, organizations progressively convert the capacity to think — to interrogate those premises — into the capacity to execute within them. By the time misalignment erodes results, the organization has lost the very capacity needed to revise its assumptions. Artificial intelligence does not introduce this dynamic. It structurally accelerates it, reinforcing governing logic with a speed and apparent rigor that no previous technology approached.

The dominant model of leadership — recognize disruption, mobilize change — was built for environments that stabilized between disruptions long enough for reactive adjustment to succeed. It fails under interpretive drift not because leaders are inattentive but because the sequence it depends on has inverted: the most consequential choices are made not when change is mobilized, but during the preceding interval of apparently sound performance. By the time misalignment is visible, those choices have already foreclosed much of the response space.

What this inversion reveals is the need for a different kind of leader — one defined not primarily by the ability to respond to disruption, but by the capacity to question and revise governing premises while they are still producing acceptable results, and to act on that judgment before evidence compels it. This capability cannot be sustained through individual judgment alone. It requires an organizational architecture that preserves the capacity to think throughout structural consolidation rather than allowing it to be consumed by execution.

This paper argues that what the environment now requires is not a better version of the reactive model but a categorically different organizational architecture — one designed to continuously surface and test governing premises before misalignment erodes results. The 4D Performance Engine — Direction, Design, Disciplines, and Development — specifies that architecture. Its differentiation from existing synthesis frameworks rests on a single claim: the four failure modes it addresses do not operate independently. They share a common structural root in the thinking/execution displacement that consolidation produces, and they compound rather than add. No combination of individually sound interventions counteracts a compounding system. The architecture works because it targets the root, not the symptoms — preserving the organizational capacity to think throughout consolidation, so that when governing premises must be revised, the capacity to revise them has not been consumed by the efficiency gains of executing within them. Six behavioral principles specify how leaders enact this architecture in practice.

In a world that no longer stabilizes, the capacity to continuously revise governing premises before misalignment erodes results becomes a decisive source of competitive advantage for those who build it before others recognize the need.

title: Organizational Architecture Theory (OAT) A Framework for Designing Organizational Outcomes through Structural Coherence

detail.title: Organizational Architecture Theory (OAT) A Framework for Designing Organizational Outcomes through Structural Coherence

keywords: Organizational Design; Management Theory; Systems Thinking; Organizational Performance; Organizational Architecture; Outcome Engineering; Organizational Coherence; Structural Alignment; Organizational Systems

detail.abstract: Organizational performance remains persistently constrained by a structural disconnect between intended objectives and actual outcomes. Despite the widespread adoption of management frameworks, performance systems, and process optimization methodologies, organizations continue to experience recurring inefficiencies, misalignment, and unpredictability in results. This paper introduces Organizational Architecture Theory (OAT), a conceptual and applied framework that redefines the causal mechanisms underlying organizational performance. OAT posits that outcomes are not primarily the result of execution quality, but the emergent product of underlying organizational architectures. In this perspective, organizations are understood as outcome-generating systems whose results are determined by the coherence of their structural configuration.

title: Decluttering Unconscious Bias In Entrepreneurship

detail.title: Decluttering Unconscious Bias In Entrepreneurship
detail.abstract:
Clarity is a design choice. It’s time to start building for real.

In the high-stakes world of entrepreneurship, "vision" is often celebrated as a founder’s greatest gift. But what if that vision is actually an invisible filter, distorting your perception of the market, your team, and your potential for success?

In the book Decluttering Unconscious Bias in Entrepreneurship, Deepu Sebastian provides a technical manual for the "Conscious Entrepreneur." Moving beyond typical diversity lectures, this book explores how cognitive noise leads to catastrophic strategic errors and why brilliant startups often fail—not from a lack of speed, but from moving with massive momentum in the wrong direction.

Drawing on twenty years of global experience and the principles of decision theory, Deepu Sebastian offers practical tools to:

  • Identify the "Validation Illusion" that masks market realities.

  • Break the "Culture Fit" trap to build teams of windows, not mirrors.

  • Create "Speed Bumps" in decision-making to outpace unconscious bias.

Stop building on mirages. Strip away the mental clutter and transform your leadership from a series of reactive impulses into a robust, intentional process. This book is the essential guide for any leader ready to see the world—and their business—as it truly is.

title: WORKING PAPER | PHILOSOPHY OF WORK AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE Beyond Augmentation Why Artificial Intelligence Requires a Cognitive and Educational Refoundation of Work

detail.title: WORKING PAPER | PHILOSOPHY OF WORK AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE Beyond Augmentation Why Artificial Intelligence Requires a Cognitive and Educational Refoundation of Work
detail.abstract: In recent years, research on the impact of artificial intelligence on work has progressively abandoned the narrative of substitution in favor of the augmentation paradigm. Recent studies from MIT Sloan (Loaiza and Rigobon, 2025), McKinsey & Company (2025) and Pearson (2026) show with increasing consistency that value derives not from the technology itself, but from the quality of the human-AI system designed within organizations. This convergence represents a significant advance in the debate, yet conceals a structural limitation: its focus remains confined to the organizational and corporate dimension, presupposing that the individual enters the working system already endowed with the cognitive capacities necessary to interact productively with artificial systems. This paper proposes an alternative and complementary thesis: artificial intelligence requires not only a transformation of work, but a cognitive and educational refoundation of the human being that precedes entry into the productive world. Through a comparative analysis of major technological transitions and the introduction of the concept of velocity asymmetry, we argue that continuous corporate training represents a transitional and structurally insufficient solution. The true competitive advantage lies not in the ability to adopt AI tools, but in the quality of human thought that guides the dialogue with artificial cognitive systems. When this thought is absent or deactivated, AI does not solve the problem: it amplifies it.

title: Meta-Capacity as a Constraint-Based Framework for Explaining Performance Gaps in Complex Systems

detail.title: Meta-Capacity as a Constraint-Based Framework for Explaining Performance Gaps in Complex Systems
detail.abstract:
While modern management obsessively accumulates structural resources, it remains blind to the physics of their accessibility. This paper presents a formal diagnostic framework based on the Meta-Capacity (MC) Equation, proving that systemic failure is rarely a result of resource scarcity, but a direct consequence of internal 'clogs'—Structural Blockages (EB) and Resource Dissipation (IE). By operationalizing the Capacity-Access Gap, this work provides leaders with a surgical tool to unlock latent potential without further resource expansion.
Across cognitive, organizational, and socio-technical systems, a persistent and poorly explained phenomenon is the mismatch between structural resources and realized performance. Existing approaches in behavioral science, organizational theory, and systems research primarily explain performance in terms of resource availability, adaptive capacity, or regulatory mechanisms. However, they provide limited conceptual tools for explaining why substantial structural potential often remains only partially accessible in practice. This paper introduces meta-capacity as a system-level parameter that captures the accessible portion of structural capacity under internal constraint conditions. A distinction is made between structural capacity (SC) as latent potential and meta-capacity (MC) as functionally accessible capacity. The difference between these two dimensions is formalized as the capacity-access gap (CAG), which reflects the extent to which internal constraints reduce effective system functioning. The framework identifies recurrent system states-aligned, constrained, and compensatory-and shows how persistent accessibility gaps can lead to compensatory dynamics, including externalization of functions, dependency formation, and structural fragility. In contrast to resource-based explanations, the model suggests that increasing resources without addressing accessibility constraints may fail to improve performance and may, under certain conditions, increase systemic instability. The paper provides a diagnostic framework for distinguishing between resource scarcity and accessibility constraints, offering a basis for more effective decision-making across system levels. By reframing system performance as a function of accessible rather than total capacity, the framework introduces a new perspective on how latent potential can be unlocked and system stability improved. This framework represents one formalization of a broader research program on metacapacity across system levels.

title: Quantifying Retail Inventory Loss: A Combined Shrinkage and Stockout Analytics Framework for Distribution Centers

detail.title: Quantifying Retail Inventory Loss: A Combined Shrinkage and Stockout Analytics Framework for Distribution Centers
detail.abstract:
Retail distribution centers face significant financial exposure from two primary inventory loss mechanisms: shrinkage and stockouts. While existing literature addresses these challenges independently, few frameworks quantify their combined financial impact at the warehouse level using open-source analytics tools. 

  

This study presents an end-to-end retail inventory analytics pipeline built using PostgreSQL, Python, and Power BI across 183,000 simulated daily transactions spanning five distribution centers and 100 SKUs over twelve months. 

  

Key findings identify $163.9M in stockout losses and $385,625 in shrinkage losses  

revealing distinct warehouse performance profiles. From the research, two distribution centers demonstrate elevated shrinkage rates exceeding 9% while Atlanta and Los Angeles centers experience demand-driven stockout losses driven by insufficient inventory replenishment. 

  

A running inventory window function methodology is introduced for precise stockout detection representing an improvement over simple daily flow proxies. Findings suggest targeted loss prevention strategies should differ by warehouse profile rather than applying uniform interventions across the distribution network.

An inverse relationship is identified between warehouse shrinkage rates and 

stockout lost revenue suggesting these mechanisms operate as competing loss mechanisms sharing the same inventory pool.

title: Behavioral Drift in Deployed AI Systems: A Practitioner Position Paper on Contested Classification

detail.title: Behavioral Drift in Deployed AI Systems: A Practitioner Position Paper on Contested Classification
detail.abstract: Stakeholders may not share the same criteria for judging whether a behavioral drift event in a deployed AI system constitutes improvement or degradation. This paper proposes a taxonomy distinguishing adaptive, degenerative, and ambiguous drift types, and argues that contested classification often arises from this underlying objective function problem. These categories require opposite responses. The critical problem is detecting and classifying drift and achieving agreement that a given instance is positive-a problem that is simultaneously technical and organizational. The taxonomy and argument are developed from practitioner observation and presented as a hypothesis warranting formal investigation, not as validated theory. The contribution of this paper is conceptual rather than empirical: it proposes a way to classify contested drift events and to locate the governance problem that follows detection.

title: The Frog and Scorpion: A Conceptual Framework for Emergent Cooperation Under Constraint

detail.title: The Frog and Scorpion: A Conceptual Framework for Emergent Cooperation Under Constraint
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a conceptual framework that reinterprets the frog-and-scorpion allegory as a model of emergent cooperation between opposing forces under constraint. Drawing on dialectical theory, complexity science, cooperative game theory, conflict resolution research, and selected cognitive science concepts, the framework argues that destructive opposition is not always fixed; under certain conditions, systems with sufficient regulatory capacity can transform reactive conflict into higher-order coordination. The paper maps the allegory's core elements onto functional roles in complex adaptive systems, distinguishes conceptual claims from illustrative analogies, and develops a set of testable propositions concerning response flexibility and cooperative outcomes. Rather than treating allegory as evidence, the paper uses allegory as a heuristic device for organizing insight across biological, organizational, and societal domains. The result is a more disciplined interdisciplinary model suitable for future empirical refinement and practical application in mediation, organizational design, and systems thinking.

title: Beyond the water cooler: Leading multicultural teams and navigating challenges in a digital workplace—A perspective of SMEs in Singapore

detail.title: Beyond the water cooler: Leading multicultural teams and navigating challenges in a digital workplace—A perspective of SMEs in Singapore
detail.abstract: With the increasing prominence of virtual teams, the digital workplace has introduced unique challenges and opportunities for leaders and team members alike. This study focuses on investigating the significant leadership challenges encountered by managers of multicultural virtual teams within Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Singapore. The central goal is to propose actionable recommendations aimed at improving team performance and collaboration in such settings. To achieve this objective, qualitative data were gathered through semi-structured online interviews with business leaders responsible for managing diverse teams across various sectors. The thematic analysis uncovered substantial cultural communication barriers, as well as challenges in trust and relationship-building, which were intensified by the absence of physical interaction in virtual environments. The key findings underline the critical importance of enhancing cultural awareness, fostering effective communication, and strategically utilizing digital platforms for collaboration. This research emphasizes the significance of adaptive leadership in effectively managing multicultural virtual teams. Furthermore, it suggests future directions for exploring the impacts of digital platforms, enhancing leadership training effectiveness in virtual environments, and monitoring longitudinal changes.

title: Supply Chain Sales & Operations Planning Playbook A Comprehensive Step-by-Step Framework for Supply Chain Professionals

detail.title: Supply Chain Sales & Operations Planning Playbook A Comprehensive Step-by-Step Framework for Supply Chain Professionals

keywords: approximately $400 million in line-haul transportation cost savings
a comprehensive KPI reference guide covering 15 supply chain performance metrics with world-class benchmarks

detail.abstract:
Supply chain disruptions of the 2020s — including the COVID-19 pandemic, the global semiconductor shortage, and ongoing geopolitical volatility — have exposed critical vulnerabilities in how organizations plan and manage their supply chains. At the center of these vulnerabilities is a failure of integrated planning: the inability to align demand, supply, financial, and operational decisions into a single coherent management process. Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP) is the process designed to close this gap — yet fewer than 15% of organizations worldwide operate S&OP at a mature level, leaving the majority exposed to preventable disruptions, excess inventory, stockouts, and avoidable costs estimated in the trillions of dollars annually.

This playbook presents a comprehensive, practitioner-validated S&OP framework developed from direct operational experience at Amazon.com Services LLC (78 North American fulfillment centers, 100+ million Prime customers), Moderna Inc. (COVID-19 vaccine and cancer vaccine supply chains), and Goodbaby International (global manufacturing). The framework consists of eight integrated process steps — data foundation, statistical demand forecasting, demand review, supply review, financial integration, pre-S&OP resolution, executive decision-making, and performance measurement — organized into a monthly planning cycle with a 16-week strategic horizon.

The playbook introduces an AI/ML-driven network design and demand-supply visibility methodology validated at national scale. Implementation across Amazon's North American fulfillment network produced a 6% improvement in inventory placement accuracy, approximately $400 million in line-haul cost savings, and a 25% year-over-year improvement in inventory spread — confirmed publicly by Amazon CEO Andy Jassy on the Q3 2024 earnings call.

Real-world case studies are drawn from nine organizations: Procter & Gamble, Cisco Systems, Unilever, Johnson & Johnson, Amazon, Moderna, Walmart, Ford Motor Company, and the U.S. Department of Defense. A 24-month implementation roadmap, 15-metric KPI reference guide, and analysis of the ten most common S&OP failures are included as practical tools for supply chain practitioners worldwide.

title: Emotion Regulation as a Psychological Buffer Against Work Stress in Organizational Settings

detail.title: Emotion Regulation as a Psychological Buffer Against Work Stress in Organizational Settings
detail.abstract: Work stress remains one of the most influential psychological factors affecting employee performance, engagement, and health in modern organizations. Employees across industries face increasing emotional demands due to digital transformation, hybrid work systems, and intensified performance expectations. Emotion regulation, defined as the ability to monitor and modify emotional responses, explains why individuals under similar work pressure experience different stress outcomes. This paper integrates foundational theories of emotion regulation and emotional intelligence with real organizational data drawn from widely cited workplace well-being reports. Evidence from corporate publications frequently referenced in academic research demonstrates how emotional processes influence stress, burnout, and psychological safety. The discussion highlights how organizational context strengthens or weakens employees' ability to regulate emotions effectively. The paper concludes that emotion regulation must be treated as a strategic competency within organizational behavior and human resource development.

title: Organizational Behaviour and Group Dynamics: An Integrative Analysis of Individual, Group, And Organizational Processes in Organizational Behaviour Courses

detail.title: Organizational Behaviour and Group Dynamics: An Integrative Analysis of Individual, Group, And Organizational Processes in Organizational Behaviour Courses
detail.abstract: This paper explores the relationship between organizational behaviour and group dynamics by integrating five key sources that address individual behaviour, group decision-making, social perception, and organizational practices. The findings indicate that organizational behaviour is shaped by complex interactions between psychological, social, and structural factors. While individual behaviour forms the foundation, group dynamics significantly influence decision quality, particularly through processes such as groupthink and vigilance. Additionally, social perceptions of groups affect interpersonal relationships, and a gap exists between theoretical knowledge and actual organizational practices. Therefore, an integrative and critical approach is necessary to fully understand and effectively manage organizational behaviour and group dynamics in contemporary organizations.

title: ANALYSIS OF THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN INDIVIDUAL BEHAVIOR ELEMENT AND WORK BEHAVIOR

detail.title: ANALYSIS OF THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN INDIVIDUAL BEHAVIOR ELEMENT AND WORK BEHAVIOR
detail.abstract: This study aims to analyze the relationship between individual behavior elements and employee work behavior within organizations. The research uses a qualitative descriptive approach with a literature review method, drawing data from academic journals, books, and previous studies related to organizational behavior. The findings show that individual behavior elements, such as personality, motivation, and attitude, have a significant influence on how employees perform their tasks, interact with others, and respond to workplace challenges. In addition, factors such as ability, diversity, and knowledge sharing also play an important role in shaping work behavior and supporting innovative work behavior. The results indicate that these factors are interconnected and collectively influence employee performance and organizational outcomes. Employees with positive individual characteristics, supported by strong abilities and collaborative work environment, tend to perform better and contribute more to innovation. Therefore, organizations are encouraged to pay attention not only to technical competencies but also to behavioral and psychological aspects in order to create a more productive, innovative, and adaptive work environment.

title: BASIC CONCEPTS OF ORGANIZATIONAL BEHAVIOR AND MANAGERIAL IMPLICATIONS IN IMPROVING ORGANIZATIONAL

detail.title: BASIC CONCEPTS OF ORGANIZATIONAL BEHAVIOR AND MANAGERIAL IMPLICATIONS IN IMPROVING ORGANIZATIONAL
detail.abstract: This study aims to examine the basic concepts of organizational behavior and its implications for organizational effectiveness. Organizational behavior is a field of study that focuses on understanding individual and group behavior within an organization and how it influences overall performance. This research uses a literature review method based on two academic journals to analyze key concepts such as motivation, leadership, and organizational culture. The findings indicate that organizational behavior plays a significant role in improving employee performance and organizational effectiveness. Factors such as motivation, leadership style, and organizational culture greatly influence individual and group behavior. In addition, interdisciplinary approaches from psychology and sociology contribute to a deeper understanding of organizational dynamics. In conclusion, a comprehensive understanding of organizational behavior enables managers to make better decisions, manage human resources effectively, and create a productive work environment. Therefore, organizational behavior is essential for achieving organizational goals and maintaining long-term success.

title: From Control Governance to Learning Governance: Reciprocal Oversight and Upward Learning

detail.title: From Control Governance to Learning Governance: Reciprocal Oversight and Upward Learning
detail.abstract: Oversight is typically understood as a hierarchical mechanism for monitoring compliance, evaluating performance, and enforcing accountability. This article argues that such a control-centered view is incomplete because it underexplains whether oversight enables superordinate actors to learn from subordinate experience and revise the goals, indicators, rules, and expectations they impose. To address this gap, the article introduces the concept of reciprocal oversight, defined as an oversight process that combines downward inspection with upward learning. It further distinguishes between control governance and learning governance, showing how oversight can either generate defensive compliance or support institutional adaptation. The article develops the mechanisms linking indicator pressure, field knowledge, protected disclosure, and the learnability of superiors to governance outcomes. It argues that governance becomes more adaptive when oversight findings inform revision as well as judgment. In this sense, good governance requires not only answerability from below but also learning from below.

title: What Happens When Responsiveness Meets Organizational Accountability Costs? Toward a Typology of Distorted Responsiveness in Public Agencies

detail.title: What Happens When Responsiveness Meets Organizational Accountability Costs? Toward a Typology of Distorted Responsiveness in Public Agencies
detail.abstract: This article develops a typology of distorted responsiveness in public organizations and explains how organizational conditions shape each type. Although responsiveness is widely regarded as a core normative value, research shows that responsiveness does not necessarily lead to meaningful problem resolution. This study conceptualizes responsiveness as varying across forms. Drawing on scholarship on accountability, grievance redress, and street-level bureaucracy, it introduces the concept of organizational accountability costs to capture the risks and burdens associated with substantive response. It then develops a twodimensional framework based on substantive problem-solving and organizational absorption of accountability costs, generating four types: symbolic, procedural, frontline-burdened, and responsible responsiveness. The article further argues that managerial political capacity enables organizations to absorb these costs and shift responsiveness toward more effective forms. By integrating typology and mechanism, the study offers a framework for diagnosing distorted responsiveness and identifying pathways toward a more responsible response.

title: Leadership Role in Organization

detail.title: Leadership Role in Organization
detail.abstract: This study examines the role of leadership in organizations by reviewing existing literature on leadership concepts, theories, and practices. The main objective is to understand how leadership influences organizational effectiveness and performance. The study is based on a qualitative approach using a literature review method, focusing on key leadership theories such as trait theory, behavioral theory, and transformational leadership.

This study explores the fragility of multi-tier supply networks in the automotive and pharmaceutical sectors, examining the ripple e!ects of geopolitical shocks and pandemics. By employing a Bayesian network simulation to calculate conditional probabilities of disruptions, the research maps

complex supplier dependencies and introduces a

The findings demonstrate that dynamic visibility and

bu!ers and structural redundancy in maintaining

true operational resilience.

title: Strategic Risk-Taking: Information Systems Design and the Formation and Enactment of Perceived Risk under Strategic Paradox

detail.title: Strategic Risk-Taking: Information Systems Design and the Formation and Enactment of Perceived Risk under Strategic Paradox

declarations.funderStatement: WHU - Otto Beisheim School of Management: Financing of field study Hanns-Seidel-Stiftung: Scholarship during field study

detail.abstract:
Dominant models conceptualize perceived risk as a probabilistic judgment and risk propensity as a direct dispositional driver of strategic risk-taking, implicitly assuming stable evaluative processes across decision makers and contexts. These assumptions systematically mispredict strategic action under conditions of strategic paradox—where competing demands must be attended to simultaneously and the organization’s future is at stake—by leaving unexplained how perceived risk—while expressed as probability judgments—is formed and enacted.

This study contributes to strategic risk-taking theory. First, it shifts the focus from stable evaluation to the formation and enactment of perceived risk under conditions of strategic paradox. We provide empirical evidence consistent with the view that perceived risk—while expressed as probability judgments—is formed and enacted through an affective–cognitive schema integration process. Second, building on this microfoundational account, our empirical evidence further indicates that risk propensity functions as an experience-based sensitivity that regulates how perceived risk translates into strategic action, rather than as a direct dispositional driver of strategic risk-taking. Third, extending this perspective, our model results indicate that risk propensity and ideological orientations are rooted in shared affectively valenced experience structures emerging through affective–cognitive schema integration, helping to explain their association with strategic behavior.

title: Teaching Activity-Based Costing in Hospitality Through the Profitability Reinterpretation Framework

detail.title: Teaching Activity-Based Costing in Hospitality Through the Profitability Reinterpretation Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is affiliated with MonsoonSIM, which is referenced in this teaching note as the illustrative simulation environment. No external sponsor influenced the content of this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper is conceptual and pedagogical in nature and does not report research involving human participants, patient data, or identifiable personal data. Ethics approval was therefore not required.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this work.

detail.abstract: Activity-Based Costing (ABC) is widely recognized as a useful approach for improving cost visibility, yet learners often struggle to appreciate its practical relevance in service and hospitality contexts. Unlike many product-based settings, service operations rely heavily on human effort, physical capacity, supporting resources, and fluctuating demand, making profitability difficult to interpret through simplified costing views. This teaching note introduces the Profitability Reinterpretation Framework (PRF), a conceptual model explaining how learners move from a revenue-led view of service performance toward a more activity-based understanding of profitability. Using a simulation-based hospitality context, the note shows how learners can reinterpret apparent profitability by tracing resource consumption, activity burden, and managerial implications. In the present case, the illustrative setting is implemented through MonsoonSIM, although the framework is intended to be transferable to other service-learning environments. The note is conceptual and pedagogical in nature and is intended for educators in management accounting, hospitality, business, and related disciplines seeking to make costing more visible through experiential learning.

title: Carbon-Aware Supplier Selection: Integrating Cost, Risk, and Emissions in Procurement Decisions

detail.title: Carbon-Aware Supplier Selection: Integrating Cost, Risk, and Emissions in Procurement Decisions

Global supply chains face unprecedented pressure to
balance economic e!ciency with environmental
sustainability and operational resilience. As
Carbon-Aware Supplier Selection: Integrating Cost, Risk, and Emissions in Procurement Decisions 
enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems evolve,
organizations are increasingly seeking to embed
environmental, social, and governance (ESG) metrics
directly into procurement decision-making. This
